## Answer

### Main idea

The PostgreSQL 17 [planner](../../../glossary.md#planner) turns one analyzed and rewritten query into one executable plan. Its entry point, `planner()`, hands the `Query` to `standard_planner()` unless an extension installed `planner_hook`, and returns a [PlannedStmt](../../../glossary.md#plannedstmt) ([planner.c#planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L274-L285)).

The planner does not try whole plans one by one. It first builds a working model of the query and rewrites it into an equivalent shape that is easier to optimize. Then it builds candidate [paths](../../../glossary.md#path) bottom up: several ways to scan each table, to join each pair of inputs, and to group, sort and limit. Each path carries an estimated row count and an estimated [cost](../../../glossary.md#cost) ([pathnodes.h#Path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1622-L1669)).

Paths compete as they are built. `add_path()` keeps a new path only when no existing path of the same relation beats it on cost, sort order, row count, parameterization and parallel safety, and it throws away the old paths the new one beats ([pathnode.c#add_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L361-L373)). At the end, `standard_planner()` takes the cheapest final path, turns it into a [plan tree](../../../glossary.md#plan-tree) with `create_plan()`, fixes its references, and packs it into the `PlannedStmt` ([planner.c#standard_planner-finish](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L415-L422), [planner.c#standard_planner-setrefs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L525-L533)).

Two facts shape everything else in this tutorial:

- **Every choice rests on estimates.** Row counts come from stored [statistics](../../../glossary.md#statistics) and from the table's current file size, and costs come from formulas over those rows ([costsize.c#set_baserel_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5250-L5268)). A wrong estimate can make a slow plan look cheapest, and the planner never learns from the run.
- **The executor runs the plan it is given.** It adapts only inside decisions the plan already made: it splits a hash table into batches, prunes partitions whose bounds a parameter excludes, launches fewer workers than planned when none are free, and compiles expressions only when a JIT provider is loaded. Each chapter's "Planning versus execution" section lists the boundaries for its mechanism.

The running query Q1 shows the whole pipeline at work. The planner estimated 3,019 pending orders, 200 western customers and 302 joined rows, and chose a hash join, a sort and a limit. The run found 3,019, 200 and 290 rows (Measured, E1.2).

#### The pipeline at a glance

```text
SQL text
 |
 [A] pg_parse_query ............... raw parse tree (RawStmt)
 [B] parse analysis + rewriter .... list of Query trees (views expanded, rules applied)
 [C] pg_plan_query -> planner() ... planner_hook, or standard_planner()
 |
 standard_planner
 |-- [D] tuple_fraction: all rows (0), or cursor_tuple_fraction for a cursor
 |-- [E] subquery_planner (runs again for every subquery level)
 |     |-- preprocess: CTEs, MERGE to join, sublinks to joins, SQL-function inlining,
 |     |   subquery pull-up, UNION ALL flattening, row marks, expressions
 |     |   (constant folding), HAVING to WHERE, outer-join reduction
 |     `-- grouping_planner
 |           |-- LIMIT/OFFSET adjust tuple_fraction
 |           |-- set operation? -> plan_set_operations
 |           |-- otherwise query_planner -> make_one_rel:
 |           |     base rels + quals + equivalence classes + join removal
 |           |     -> scan paths per table -> join search (dynamic programming or GEQO)
 |           `-- upper steps: projection, grouping, window, DISTINCT, ORDER BY,
 |                 then LockRows, Limit, ModifyTable -> final relation's paths
 |-- [F] cheapest final path (fraction-aware) -> create_plan: Path tree -> Plan tree
 |-- [G] SS_finalize_plan (parameters) -> set_plan_references (flat range table, Var fix-up)
 `-- [H] PlannedStmt: plan, range table, subplans, dependencies, parallelModeNeeded, jitFlags
 |
 [I] portal and executor run the plan
```

- [A] [postgres.c#exec_simple_query-parse](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1071), [postgres.c#pg_parse_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L616-L630)

### How to read this tutorial

Each chapter follows the same order. It starts with the main idea, the values the mechanism uses and a logic map. A step-by-step walkthrough follows, then how alternatives become eligible and are compared, and then exceptions. Formulas and worked examples, planning versus running, lifecycle events, regression tests and a causal summary close the chapter. Chapters 1 and 2 give the vocabulary the others use, so read them first.

Numbers on this page come in three kinds, and the page always says which:

| Label | What it is | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| Estimated by the planner | a cost or row count printed by plain `EXPLAIN` | the planner's model, before anything runs |
| Measured | an actual row count, a counter, a catalog value or a byte count | `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` with timing off, catalog queries, `pg_prepared_statements`, `pg_stat_statements` |
| Derived | arithmetic on quoted inputs | the formula shown next to it |

Every measured or estimated number comes from one isolated server built from the pinned checkout by the script under [Measurement Script](#measurement-script). Each experiment has a label such as E4.2, and the script prints that label above the statements that produce it. No wall-clock time is ever recorded, so every number repeats exactly on this platform.

Some experiments change a planner setting to expose an alternative the planner would not choose, for example `enable_hashjoin = off` to see the merge join it rejected. Those are marked **forced setting**. A forced plan shows what an alternative costs; it is not a recommendation.

### The running schema and queries

The script builds a small shop database. Every value comes from a deterministic hash of the row number, so each run produces the same data, and `ANALYZE` reads every row, so the statistics are exact and repeatable.

| Table | Rows | Pages | What makes it interesting |
|---|---|---|---|
| `customers` | 2,000 | 22 | `region` is skewed 40/30/20/10 %; `country` depends on `region` (two per region); 20 % of `email` values are NULL |
| `orders` | 30,000 | 226 | 30 % of orders belong to 20 large customers (ids 1-20); `status` is about 85 % shipped, 10 % pending, 5 % cancelled; `ordered_at` rises with `id`, so it is perfectly correlated with the heap order; `amount` is uniform from 0 to 999.99; `note` is 95 % NULL |
| `items` | 90,000 | 574 | three lines per order; half the lines sell one of ten popular products |
| `events` | 600,000 | 6,819 | large enough for a parallel plan at default settings; a BRIN index on `at` |
| `places`, `docs`, `accounts` | 20,000, 20,000, 1,000 | 167, 187, 7 | points for GiST and SP-GiST, tag arrays for GIN, a row-level security fixture |
| `orders_r` | 30,000 | 20 for March | the orders range-partitioned by month, plus a default partition |
| `orders_h`, `items_h` | 30,000, 90,000 | | hash-partitioned four ways on the join key |
| `wide_p` | 25,600 | | 256 hash partitions, for planning-overhead measurements |
| `ledger` | 10,000 | 28 per child | legacy inheritance with `CHECK` constraints |

Row and page counts are Measured, E0.1. The permanent indexes are `customers_pkey`, `orders_pkey`, `orders_customer_id_idx`, `orders_ordered_at_idx`, `items_pkey (order_id, line_no)`, `items_product_id_idx` and `events_at_brin`; experiments that need another index create it inside a transaction and roll it back.

Four running queries recur through the chapters:

```sql
-- Q1: pending orders of western customers, largest first
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_q1 */ c.name, o.id, o.amount
  FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'pending'
 ORDER BY o.amount DESC
 LIMIT 5;

-- Q2: revenue of pending orders per region, over three tables
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_q2 */ c.region, count(*) AS lines, sum(i.qty * i.price) AS revenue
  FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.id
 WHERE o.status = 'pending'
 GROUP BY c.region;

-- Q3: customers without a cancelled order, written two ways
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_q3 */ * FROM customers c
 WHERE c.id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled');
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_q3 */ * FROM customers c
 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'cancelled');

-- Q4: a write that joins
UPDATE /* wiki_pqt_q4 */ orders o SET amount = o.amount * 1.1 FROM customers c
 WHERE c.id = o.customer_id AND c.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'pending';
```

The script runs Q1 in E1.1 to E1.3, E16.2 and E16.3, Q2 in E8.1, Q3 in E9.4, and Q4 only inside `EXPLAIN` (E13.3) or against a disposable copy inside a rolled-back transaction (E13.11). These statements belong to a disposable teaching database; do not run Q4 against data you care about.

### Chapter 1. Follow one query

#### 1.1 Main idea

A SQL string passes through four stages before a single row comes back. The [grammar](../../../glossary.md#grammar) turns text into a raw [parse tree](../../../glossary.md#parse-tree). Parse analysis turns that tree into a `Query`. The [rewriter](../../../glossary.md#rewriter) expands views and rules into one or more `Query` trees. Then the planner turns each `Query` into a PlannedStmt, which the [executor](../../../glossary.md#executor) runs inside a [portal](../../../glossary.md#portal) ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-parse](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1071), [postgres.c#exec_simple_query-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1195-L1199), [postgres.c#exec_simple_query-portal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1221-L1240)).

This matters because each stage sees a different object and can change a different thing. A view is gone before the planner starts, because the rewriter already replaced it with its query. The planner never sees SQL text, only `Query` nodes. And the executor never sees `Query` nodes, only the finished plan tree.

The surprising part is that "planning" is not one fixed step. The same query is planned differently for a cursor than for a plain `SELECT`. And a [utility command](../../../glossary.md#utility-command) such as `EXPLAIN` or `CREATE TABLE AS` carries a query inside it, which is planned only when the utility runs. This chapter follows Q1 through every boundary with experiments E1.1 to E1.7 ([E1.1](#measurement-script)).

#### 1.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| raw parse tree (`RawStmt`) | One statement as the grammar saw it, with no catalog lookups yet | `raw_parser()` called from `pg_parse_query()` ([postgres.c#pg_parse_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L616-L626)) | current: built from this string only | parse analysis |
| `Query` | An analyzed statement: [range table](../../../glossary.md#range-table), join tree, target list, clauses, `commandType` | `transformStmt()` ([analyze.c#transformStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L340-L416), [parsenodes.h#Query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L117-L176)) | current: resolved against the catalogs at this moment | rewriter, then planner |
| rewritten `Query` list | Zero or more queries after rules and views are applied | `QueryRewrite()` ([rewriteHandler.c#QueryRewrite](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L4556-L4596)) | current: view definitions read now | planner, one call per query |
| `cursorOptions` | Bit flags that tell the planner how the plan will be used, such as `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` and `CURSOR_OPT_FAST_PLAN` | the caller: `exec_simple_query()`, the `DECLARE` grammar, `EXPLAIN` and others ([parsenodes.h#CURSOR_OPT](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L3281-L3291)) | parameter | `standard_planner()` |
| `boundParams` | Parameter values known at planning time, or NULL | the plan cache, which passes them on to `pg_plan_queries()` ([plancache.c#BuildCachedPlan-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L967-L971)); NULL in the simple protocol ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1198-L1199)) | parameter | constant folding and selectivity |
| `tuple_fraction` | The fraction of the result the caller expects to fetch; 0 means all rows | `cursor_tuple_fraction` for a fast-start cursor, else 0 ([planner.c#standard_planner-tuple-fraction](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L387-L413)) | parameter (setting) | choice of the final path |
| `PlannedStmt` | The planner's output: plan tree, flat range table, dependency lists, JIT flags | `standard_planner()` ([planner.c#standard_planner-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L537-L562), [plannodes.h#PlannedStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L46-L100)) | stored for the life of the portal or cache entry; its costs are estimates | executor, plan cache |
| portal and `QueryDesc` | The runtime container for one execution | `CreatePortal()`, `PortalStart()` ([pquery.c#PortalStart-QueryDesc](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/pquery.c#L495-L517)) | current: bound to a snapshot and destination | `ExecutorStart()`, `ExecutorRun()` |

Two similar-looking values come from different places. `cursorOptions` is fixed by the caller before planning starts, while `tuple_fraction` is derived from it inside the planner, and a `LIMIT` can change it again later ([planner.c#grouping_planner-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1352-L1367)).

#### 1.3 Logic map

```text
SQL text (simple protocol message)
|
+-- [A] pg_parse_query: grammar -> list of RawStmt (no catalog access)
|
+-- for each RawStmt:
|     [B] snapshot needed? -> push a transaction snapshot for analysis and planning
|     [C] parse analysis (transformStmt)
|           optimizable (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE) -> Query with a real commandType
|           DECLARE / EXPLAIN / CREATE TABLE AS / CALL -> CMD_UTILITY Query that holds an analyzed inner query
|           anything else -> CMD_UTILITY Query wrapping the raw statement
|     [D] rewrite: CMD_UTILITY? -> pass through unchanged
|                  otherwise QueryRewrite: rules, then views -> RTE_SUBQUERY
|     [E] pg_plan_queries, per Query:
|           CMD_UTILITY -> wrapper PlannedStmt, no planning
|           otherwise pg_plan_query -> planner() -> planner_hook or standard_planner()
|                 standard_planner: parallel feasibility, tuple_fraction,
|                 subquery_planner -> best path -> create_plan -> set_plan_references
|                 -> PlannedStmt (+ jitFlags)
|     [F] pop snapshot; CreatePortal; PortalStart -> ExecutorStart (or utility run later)
|     [G] PortalRun -> executor, or ProcessUtility for a utility statement
|           a utility that contains a query (EXPLAIN, CTAS, DECLARE, COPY (query), REFRESH)
|           rewrites and plans that inner query now, through pg_plan_query
```

- [A] [postgres.c#pg_parse_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L616-L626)
- [B] [postgres.c#exec_simple_query-snapshot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1166-L1170), [postgres.c#pg_plan_query-snapshot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L896-L901)
- [C] [analyze.c#transformStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L340-L416)
- [D] [postgres.c#pg_rewrite_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L820-L829), [rewriteHandler.c#ApplyRetrieveRule-subquery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L1869-L1886)
- [E] [postgres.c#pg_plan_queries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L977-L1010), [planner.c#planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L274-L285), [planner.c#standard_planner-core](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L415-L422), [planner.c#standard_planner-setrefs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L520-L535)
- [F] [postgres.c#exec_simple_query-portal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1211-L1240), [pquery.c#PortalStart-QueryDesc](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/pquery.c#L495-L517)
- [G] [postgres.c#exec_simple_query-run](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1279-L1289), [pquery.c#PortalRunUtility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/pquery.c#L1125-L1160), [explain.c#ExplainOneQuery-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L489-L490), [createas.c#ExecCreateTableAs-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/createas.c#L291-L303), [portalcmds.c#PerformCursorOpen-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/portalcmds.c#L80-L92), [copyto.c#BeginCopyTo-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/copyto.c#L518-L520), [matview.c#refresh_matview_datafill-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/matview.c#L398-L412)

#### 1.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: raw parsing

Input: the SQL text of one protocol message. `exec_simple_query()` calls `pg_parse_query()`, which runs `raw_parser()` and returns one `RawStmt` per statement ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-parse](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1071), [postgres.c#pg_parse_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L616-L626)). This stage reads no catalogs, because it must work even in an aborted transaction ([postgres.c#pg_parse_query-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L603-L614)). Output: a list of raw trees, which the loop then handles one at a time.

##### Step 2: snapshot and parse analysis

Input: one raw tree. Decision: does analysis need a [snapshot](../../../glossary.md#snapshot)? If so, `exec_simple_query()` pushes one ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-snapshot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1166-L1170)). The planner needs it too, because it may call user-defined functions ([postgres.c#pg_plan_query-snapshot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L896-L901)).

Parse analysis then calls `transformStmt()`. Optimizable statements become a `Query` whose `commandType` is `CMD_SELECT`, `CMD_INSERT` and so on. `DECLARE CURSOR`, `EXPLAIN`, `CREATE TABLE AS` and `CALL` get special handling, and every other statement is wrapped in a `CMD_UTILITY` `Query` ([analyze.c#transformStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L340-L416)). Output: one `Query`. When query identifiers are enabled, analysis also computes the [jumbled](../../../glossary.md#query-jumbling) query ID and calls `post_parse_analyze_hook` ([analyze.c#parse_analyze_fixedparams](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L121-L127)).

##### Step 3: rewriting

Input: the analyzed `Query`. Decision: a utility `Query` passes through unchanged; any other goes to `QueryRewrite()` ([postgres.c#pg_rewrite_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L820-L829)). `QueryRewrite()` first applies non-`SELECT` rules, which can produce several queries, then applies view expansion to each result ([rewriteHandler.c#QueryRewrite](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L4572-L4596)).

View expansion replaces the view's range-table entry in place. The entry becomes an `RTE_SUBQUERY` that holds the view's query, while the view's OID stays in the entry so that the view can be locked and its permissions checked ([rewriteHandler.c#ApplyRetrieveRule-subquery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L1869-L1886)). Output: a list of `Query` trees in which no view reference remains.

##### Step 4: planning

Input: each rewritten `Query`. `pg_plan_queries()` gives a utility statement a dummy `PlannedStmt` with `commandType = CMD_UTILITY` and calls `pg_plan_query()` for everything else ([postgres.c#pg_plan_queries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L977-L1010)). `pg_plan_query()` calls `planner()`, which calls `planner_hook` if an extension set one ([hook](../../../glossary.md#hook)) and `standard_planner()` otherwise ([postgres.c#pg_plan_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L891-L912), [planner.c#planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L274-L285)).

`standard_planner()` creates the per-invocation state, `PlannerGlobal` ([planner.c#standard_planner-glob](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L301-L326)). It then decides whether parallel plans are allowed at all. The caller must pass `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK`, and the statement must be a `SELECT` without data-modifying `WITH`. Also, `max_parallel_workers_per_gather` must be above zero, and the query must contain nothing parallel-unsafe ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L365)).

It then sets `tuple_fraction` and calls `subquery_planner()`, which does all the real work described in chapters 2 to 13 ([planner.c#standard_planner-core](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L387-L416)). The result is a set of candidate paths for the final [upper relation](../../../glossary.md#upper-relation). `standard_planner()` picks one with `get_cheapest_fractional_path()` and turns it into a plan tree with `create_plan()` ([planner.c#standard_planner-core](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L418-L422)). Chapter 14 follows the rest: parameter finalization, `set_plan_references()` and the assembly of the `PlannedStmt`.

##### Step 5: portal and execution

Input: the list of `PlannedStmt`s. The simple protocol pops the planning snapshot, creates an unnamed portal, and starts it ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-portal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1211-L1240)). For a single `SELECT`, `PortalStart()` builds a `QueryDesc` and calls `ExecutorStart()` ([pquery.c#PortalStart-QueryDesc](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/pquery.c#L495-L517)). `ExecutorStart()` turns the plan tree into a tree of runtime state nodes ([execMain.c#InitPlan-ExecInitNode](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L959)). `PortalRun()` then fetches all rows ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-run](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1279-L1289)).

The planning snapshot is not reused for execution. The source says reusing it would let execution see a snapshot taken before the tables were locked ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-snapshot-pop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1201-L1212)).

##### Step 6: utilities that contain a query

A utility statement is not planned in step 4. `PortalRunUtility()` hands it to `ProcessUtility()` ([pquery.c#PortalRunUtility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/pquery.c#L1125-L1160), [utility.c#ProcessUtility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/utility.c#L499-L525)). Five utilities then rewrite and plan the query they carry, each through `pg_plan_query()`:

| Utility | Where it plans | `cursorOptions` it passes |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPLAIN` | `ExplainOneQuery()` ([explain.c#ExplainOneQuery-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L489-L490)) | `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` for a plain query ([explain.c:343](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L343)); the cursor's own options for `EXPLAIN DECLARE` ([explain.c#ExplainOneUtility-declare](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L565-L583)) |
| `CREATE TABLE AS`, `SELECT INTO`, `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` | `ExecCreateTableAs()` ([createas.c#ExecCreateTableAs-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/createas.c#L291-L303)) | `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` |
| `DECLARE CURSOR` | `PerformCursorOpen()` ([portalcmds.c#PerformCursorOpen-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/portalcmds.c#L80-L92)) | the grammar's options, which always include `CURSOR_OPT_FAST_PLAN` ([gram.y#DeclareCursorStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L12605-L12614)) |
| `COPY (query) TO` | `BeginCopyTo()` ([copyto.c#BeginCopyTo-analyze](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/copyto.c#L451-L453), [copyto.c#BeginCopyTo-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/copyto.c#L518-L520)) | `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` |
| `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` | `refresh_matview_datafill()` ([matview.c#refresh_matview_datafill-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/matview.c#L398-L412)) | `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` |

`CREATE EXTENSION` and `ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE` plan too: they run each statement of the extension script through `pg_analyze_and_rewrite_fixedparams()` and `pg_plan_queries()` ([extension.c#execute_sql_string-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/extension.c#L911-L916)).

`PREPARE` and `EXECUTE` are also utilities, but they go through the plan cache instead ([prepare.c#PrepareQuery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L87-L127), [prepare.c#ExecuteQuery-GetCachedPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L193)). The extended protocol does the same for every statement: `exec_parse_message()` builds a cached plan source and `exec_bind_message()` asks it for a plan ([postgres.c#exec_parse_message-cache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1509-L1555), [postgres.c#exec_bind_message-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L2024-L2046)). Functions written in SQL or PL/pgSQL, and [SPI](../../../glossary.md#spi) callers, plan their embedded queries on their own schedule. Chapter 14 covers all of these.

#### 1.5 Eligibility and comparison

The planner does not pick a plan by total cost alone. It picks the path whose cost is lowest for the fraction of rows the caller will fetch. `get_cheapest_fractional_path()` returns the cheapest-total path when `tuple_fraction` is 0 and otherwise compares every path's fractional cost ([planner.c#get_cheapest_fractional_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6533-L6559), [pathnode.c#compare_fractional_path_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L115-L132)).

For a fast-start path to be compared at all, it must survive the earlier pruning of paths. Every relation marks `consider_startup` true only when `tuple_fraction` is above zero, so cheap-startup paths are kept only when the caller wants part of the result ([relnode.c#build_simple_rel-consider_startup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L210-L211), [relnode.c:707](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L707)).

Which statements can be planned in parallel is decided once, at the top, before any path exists ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L365)). `DECLARE CURSOR` never sets `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` ([gram.y#DeclareCursorStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L12605-L12614)), so a cursor's query is always planned without parallel paths.

#### 1.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Transaction is in the aborted state | Only `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` pass; other statements fail before analysis ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-aborted](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1139-L1145)) | nothing is planned |
| Several statements in one simple-protocol message | They run in one implicit transaction block ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-implicit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1088-L1096)) | each is still analyzed, planned and run in turn |
| A utility statement | `pg_plan_queries()` makes a wrapper `PlannedStmt` without calling the planner ([postgres.c#pg_plan_queries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L988-L1002)) | only the utilities in step 6 plan a query, later |
| `EXPLAIN CREATE TABLE AS` for a table that already exists | `ExplainOneUtility()` checks existence first and prints a dummy group ([explain.c#ExplainOneUtility-ctas-exists](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L543-L557)) | no planning happens |
| A rule rewrites one statement into several | `QueryRewrite()` returns a list and each entry is planned separately ([rewriteHandler.c#QueryRewrite](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L4572-L4596)) | one message can yield several plans |
| `planner_hook` is set | `planner()` calls the hook instead of `standard_planner()` ([planner.c#planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L280-L283)) | an extension can wrap or replace planning (chapter 15) |
| The planner modifies its input | `standard_planner()` scribbles on the `Query` ([planner.c#planner-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L270-L271)) | callers that plan twice, such as the plan cache, copy the tree first ([plancache.c#BuildCachedPlan-copy](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L941-L952)) |
| A scrollable cursor whose plan cannot run backward | `standard_planner()` adds a Material node on top ([planner.c#standard_planner-scroll](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L424-L432)) | the cursor can move backward at the cost of materializing rows |

#### 1.7 Formulas and worked examples

##### Reading Q1's plan (E1.1, E1.2)

Estimated by the planner, E1.1, and measured, E1.2 (actual rows, timing off):

```text
 Limit  (cost=663.46..663.48 rows=5 width=24) (actual rows=5 loops=1)
   ->  Sort  (cost=663.46..664.22 rows=302 width=24) (actual rows=5 loops=1)
         Sort Key: o.amount DESC
         Sort Method: top-N heapsort  Memory: 25kB
         ->  Hash Join  (cost=49.50..658.45 rows=302 width=24) (actual rows=290 loops=1)
               Hash Cond: (o.customer_id = c.id)
               ->  Seq Scan on orders o  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=3019 width=14) (actual rows=3019 loops=1)
                     Filter: (status = 'pending'::text)
                     Rows Removed by Filter: 26981
               ->  Hash  (cost=47.00..47.00 rows=200 width=18) (actual rows=200 loops=1)
                     Buckets: 1024  Batches: 1  Memory Usage: 19kB
                     ->  Seq Scan on customers c  (cost=0.00..47.00 rows=200 width=18) (actual rows=200 loops=1)
                           Filter: (region = 'west'::text)
                           Rows Removed by Filter: 1800
```

Each line of [EXPLAIN](../../../glossary.md#explain) output is one plan node. The two numbers in `cost=` are the estimated startup and total cost, `rows` is the estimated output, and `width` the estimated average row width in bytes ([plannodes.h#Plan-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L125-L135)). The `actual` figures come from running the plan. Here every scan estimate matches its actual count, and the join estimate of 302 rows is close to the 290 actual rows. The `Sort Method` and `Memory` lines are decided while running, not by the planner (chapter 10).

##### Fractional cost for a cursor (E1.7)

Define `S` as a path's startup cost, `T` as its total cost, and `f` as `tuple_fraction`. The cost compared is:

```text
fractional cost = S + f * (T - S)        for 0 < f < 1
fractional cost = T                      for f = 0 or f >= 1
```

This is `compare_fractional_path_costs()` ([pathnode.c#compare_fractional_path_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L115-L132)). In practical terms, a path that starts cheaply wins when the caller will stop early.

Estimated by the planner, E1.7. The top node of the plain query `SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.id`:

```text
 Hash Join  (cost=901.00..2611.28 rows=90000 width=62)
```

The top node of the same query under `DECLARE c1 CURSOR FOR`:

```text
 Merge Join  (cost=0.58..5886.64 rows=90000 width=62)
```

Derived, with `cursor_tuple_fraction = 0.1` (E1.7 shows the setting):

| Path | `S` | `T` | Cost at `f = 0` | Cost at `f = 0.1` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hash Join | 901.00 | 2611.28 | 2611.28 | 901.00 + 0.1 × 1710.28 = 1072.03 |
| Merge Join | 0.58 | 5886.64 | 5886.64 | 0.58 + 0.1 × 5886.06 = 589.19 |

At `f = 0` the hash join is cheaper, so the plain query uses it. At `f = 0.1` the merge join is cheaper, because a hash join must read all of `orders` into its hash table before returning its first row. The `DECLARE` grammar sets `CURSOR_OPT_FAST_PLAN`, and that flag is what switches `tuple_fraction` to `cursor_tuple_fraction` ([gram.y#DeclareCursorStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L12610-L12611), [planner.c#standard_planner-tuple-fraction](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L388-L408)).

##### A view disappears before planning (E1.4, E1.5)

Estimated by the planner, E1.4. The view `pending_orders` adds `status = 'pending'`, and the plan shows only a scan of `orders` with both conditions:

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=676.75..676.76 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..676.00 rows=301 width=0)
         Filter: ((amount > '900'::numeric) AND (status = 'pending'::text))
```

Measured, E1.5. The `debug_print_parse`, `debug_print_rewritten` and `debug_print_plan` settings log each tree. The script keeps only boundary markers from those logs, one per line (`s01-debug.txt`); `...` marks a cut. The markers for the view query read, in order:

```text
marker e1_5_view_query
parse tree:
{QUERY
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 0
:inh true
:relkind v
...
rewritten parse tree:
{QUERY
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 1
{QUERY
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 0
:inh true
:relkind r
...
plan:
{PLANNEDSTMT
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
:parallelModeNeeded false
:jitFlags 0
{AGG
{SEQSCAN
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 1
:subquery <>
:inh false
:relkind v
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 0
:inh false
:relkind r
...
```

`commandType 1` is `CMD_SELECT` and `rtekind 0` and `1` are `RTE_RELATION` and `RTE_SUBQUERY` ([nodes.h#CmdType](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L262-L274), [parsenodes.h#RTEKind](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1023-L1036)). So the parse tree still names the view (`relkind v`), and the rewritten tree holds it as a subquery over the table (`relkind r`).

The plan section shows exactly one Agg node above one SeqScan node, the same shape E1.4 printed. Its flat range table still lists the view, now with its subquery cleared (`:subquery <>`), beside the table itself. `set_plan_references()` clears that field but records the view's OID, so the plan still depends on the view (chapter 14; [setrefs.c#add_rte_to_flat_rtable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L547-L549), [setrefs.c#add_rte_to_flat_rtable-relationOids](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L564-L578)). The three logs come from `pg_rewrite_query()` and `pg_plan_query()` ([postgres.c#pg_rewrite_query-debug](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L813-L815), [postgres.c#pg_rewrite_query-debug-rewritten](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L877-L879), [postgres.c#pg_plan_query-debug](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L960-L961)).

##### A utility that plans its inner query (E1.6)

Estimated by the planner, E1.6. `EXPLAIN CREATE TABLE pending_copy AS SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending'` prints the plan of the inner `SELECT` only:

```text
 Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=3019 width=40)
   Filter: (status = 'pending'::text)
```

This comes from `ExplainOneUtility()`, which rewrites the inner query and hands it to `ExplainOneQuery()` with `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` ([explain.c#ExplainOneUtility-ctas](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L559-L563)).

#### 1.8 Planning versus execution

| Decided while planning | Decided or adapted while executing |
|---|---|
| Plan shape, join order and methods, estimated costs and rows ([planner.c#standard_planner-core](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L415-L422)) | actual row counts, sort method and memory, hash batches (E1.2) |
| Whether parallel plans are allowed at all ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L365)) | how many workers actually start (chapter 12) |
| `jitFlags`, from the plan's total cost ([planner.c#standard_planner-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L564-L587)) | whether any code is compiled, which needs a JIT provider (chapter 12) |
| The query inside a utility, but only when the utility runs ([pquery.c#PortalRunUtility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/pquery.c#L1125-L1160)) | the utility's own effects, such as creating a table |
| Which relations the plan references ([planner.c#standard_planner-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L549-L557)) | the snapshot the rows are read with: a new one, not the planning snapshot ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-snapshot-pop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1201-L1212)) |

#### 1.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| A simple-protocol statement finishes | its `Query` and `PlannedStmt` live in `MessageContext` or a per-statement context ([postgres.c#exec_simple_query-contexts](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1172-L1193)) | freed with the context | the next execution parses, analyzes, rewrites and plans again |
| `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` changes a view | old view query | new view query in the catalog | the next rewrite reads the view's rule from the relation cache and expands the new definition ([rewriteHandler.c#fireRIRrules-rd_rules](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L2128-L2143), [rewriteHandler.c#ApplyRetrieveRule-subquery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L1869-L1886)) |
| A setting such as `cursor_tuple_fraction` changes | old value | new value, session scope (`PGC_USERSET`, [guc_tables.c#cursor_tuple_fraction](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3787-L3796)) | the next planning uses it |
| A statement is prepared (`PREPARE`, extended protocol) | no cache entry | a cached plan source in the plan cache ([prepare.c#PrepareQuery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L87-L127), [postgres.c#exec_parse_message-cache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1509-L1555)) | later executions may reuse a plan (chapter 14) |

#### 1.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- `EXPLAIN` of `DECLARE` and scroll cursors, including the Material node added for backward scans: [portals.sql#scroll-cursor-plans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/portals.sql#L569-L582).
- `EXPLAIN` of `CREATE TABLE AS` and `SELECT INTO`: [select_into.sql#explain-analyze-ctas](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_into.sql#L99-L104); parallel plans under `CREATE TABLE AS`: [write_parallel.sql:17](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/write_parallel.sql#L17).
- Planning counts per statement, via `pg_stat_statements` with `track_planning`: [planning.sql#replan-counting](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/sql/planning.sql#L10-L27).
- Explicit test absence: no regression test sets `cursor_tuple_fraction` or turns on `debug_print_parse`, `debug_print_rewritten` or `debug_print_plan`; E1.5 and E1.7 are this page's own evidence for those behaviors.

#### 1.11 Causal summary

1. SQL text: the grammar builds raw trees without touching the catalogs.
2. Analysis resolves names into a `Query`; the rewriter replaces views with subqueries.
3. The caller's `cursorOptions` decide whether parallel plans are allowed and set `tuple_fraction`.
4. `standard_planner()` builds paths, keeps the one cheapest for that fraction, and turns it into a `PlannedStmt`.
5. A portal runs it under a fresh snapshot.
6. A utility that contains a query plans that query only when the utility runs, and the simple protocol repeats every stage on every execution.

### Chapter 2. Understand the planner's working model

#### 2.1 Main idea

The planner works on three layers of objects. At the bottom is the analyzed `Query` and its expression trees, which say what to compute. In the middle is a search space: one [RelOptInfo](../../../glossary.md#reloptinfo) per relation, join or later processing step, each holding candidate paths. At the top is the output: a plan tree wrapped in a PlannedStmt ([optimizer/README#Paths-and-Join-Pairs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/README#L20-L42)).

This matters because almost every later chapter is about one move between these layers. Transformations rewrite the `Query` (chapter 3). Estimation fills in sizes on `RelOptInfo`s (chapter 4). Path generation adds `Path`s and throws most of them away (chapters 5 to 13). Plan creation turns the survivors into `Plan` nodes (chapter 14).

The surprising part is that a join is not a path between two tables but a relation of its own. There is exactly one `RelOptInfo` for the join of `{customers, orders}`, however it is built, and the different ways to build it are its paths ([optimizer/README#Paths-and-Join-Pairs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/README#L28-L42)). This chapter names the structures with Q1 as the example and uses E1.3, E1.5 and E16.3.

#### 2.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Query` | What to compute: range table, join tree, target list, clauses ([parsenodes.h#Query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L117-L176)) | parse analysis and the rewriter | current; the planner modifies it in place ([pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L177-L180)) | every planning stage |
| `PlannerGlobal` (`glob`) | State shared by all query levels of one `planner()` call: subplans, the flat range table, dependency lists, parallel flags ([pathnodes.h#PlannerGlobal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L95-L166)) | `standard_planner()` ([planner.c#standard_planner-glob](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L301-L326)) | current, for this planning run only | `set_plan_references()`, the `PlannedStmt` |
| [`PlannerInfo`](../../../glossary.md#plannerinfo) (`root`) | State for one query level: its `Query`, relation arrays, [equivalence classes](../../../glossary.md#equivalence-class), join constraints, upper relations ([pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L195-L211), [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-simple_rel_array](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L223-L232), [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-ec-joininfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L313-L340), [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-upper_rels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L412-L419)) | `subquery_planner()`, once per `Query`, with `query_level` and `parent_root` ([planner.c#subquery_planner-root](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L641-L649)) | current, for this planning run only | all of `query_planner()` and `grouping_planner()` |
| [`Relids`](../../../glossary.md#relids) | A set of range-table indexes, stored as a `Bitmapset` ([pathnodes.h#Relids](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L26-L30), [bitmapset.h#Bitmapset](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/bitmapset.h#L49-L56)) | built from range-table indexes | current | identifies relations, joins, clause needs |
| `RelOptInfo` | One base relation, join relation or processing step, with its size estimates and candidate paths ([pathnodes.h#RelOptInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L853-L898), [pathnodes.h:938-944](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L938-L944)) | `build_simple_rel()`, `build_join_rel()`, `fetch_upper_rel()` ([relnode.c#build_simple_rel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L192-L215), [relnode.c#fetch_upper_rel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L1469-L1500)) | `pages` and `tuples` mix stored statistics with the current file size; `rows` is an estimate (chapter 4) | path generation, joins, costing |
| [`IndexOptInfo`](../../../glossary.md#indexoptinfo) | What the planner knows about one usable index: size, columns, operator families, capabilities, cost function ([pathnodes.h#IndexOptInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1107-L1160), [pathnodes.h#IndexOptInfo-am-fields](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1189-L1206)) | `get_relation_info()`, which skips invalid indexes ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-invalid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L256-L283)) | stored catalog data plus current index size | index path generation (chapter 7) |
| `Path` | One way to produce a `RelOptInfo`'s rows, with estimated rows, startup and total cost, sort order and parameterization ([pathnodes.h#Path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1622-L1669)) | the `create_*_path()` functions | estimate | `add_path()`, then `create_plan()` |
| `ParamPathInfo` | Shared data for all paths that need values from the same outer relations ([pathnodes.h#ParamPathInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1556-L1586)) | parameterized path builders | estimate (`ppi_rows`) | nested-loop joins (chapter 8) |
| [`PathTarget`](../../../glossary.md#pathtarget) | The expressions a path returns, with their cost and width ([pathnodes.h#PathTarget](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1529-L1549)) | `reltarget` of each relation, upper-level targets | estimate (cost, width) | projection, plan target lists |
| `RestrictInfo` | One [qual](../../../glossary.md#qual) with its cached cost, selectivity and the relations it needs ([pathnodes.h#RestrictInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2560-L2600), [pathnodes.h#RestrictInfo-caches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2647-L2657)) | qual distribution (chapter 3) | clause is current; selectivity and cost are cached estimates | scans, joins, estimation |
| `EquivalenceClass`, [`PathKey`](../../../glossary.md#pathkey) | Sets of expressions known equal, and sort orders defined over them ([pathnodes.h#EquivalenceClass](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1380-L1400), [pathnodes.h#PathKey](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1464-L1475)) | `equivclass.c`, `pathkeys.c` | current | derived clauses, ordering, merge joins |
| [`SpecialJoinInfo`](../../../glossary.md#specialjoininfo) | The minimum relation sets an outer, semi or anti join needs on each side ([pathnodes.h#SpecialJoinInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2892-L2913)) | `deconstruct_jointree()` | current | join legality (chapter 8) |
| [`PlaceHolderVar`](../../../glossary.md#placeholdervar) | An expression that must be computed below an outer join and may become NULL above it ([pathnodes.h#PlaceHolderVar](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2749-L2801)) | subquery pull-up | current | target lists above outer joins |
| `varnullingrels` ([nullingrels](../../../glossary.md#nullingrels)) | The outer joins that can turn a column reference into NULL at that point of the query ([primnodes.h#Var](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L218-L220), [primnodes.h#Var-varnullingrels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L269-L274)) | parse analysis and the planner | current | clause placement, equivalence reasoning |
| `AppendRelInfo` | Maps a parent's columns to one child's, for inheritance and `UNION ALL` ([pathnodes.h#AppendRelInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2930-L2990)) | appendrel expansion (chapter 11) | current | child scans under Append |
| `Plan`, `PlannedStmt` | The executable tree: each node's costs, rows, width, target list and quals; and the statement-level wrapper ([plannodes.h#Plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L119-L172), [plannodes.h#PlannedStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L46-L100)) | `create_plan()` and `standard_planner()` | stored; costs and rows are copies of estimates | the executor, the plan cache |

Two pairs are easy to confuse. `pages` and `tuples` on a `RelOptInfo` are inputs read before planning, while `rows` is the planner's estimate after the relation's conditions are applied ([pathnodes.h#RelOptInfo-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L647-L652)). And a `Path` omits what the executor needs while a `Plan` omits what only the planner needs, which is why the two trees are separate ([optimizer/README#Paths-and-Join-Pairs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/README#L20-L26)).

#### 2.3 Logic map

The structures form a pipeline. Each arrow says what one structure hands to the next.

```text
Query (range table, jointree, targetList, clauses)                                   [A]
  |  subquery_planner makes one PlannerInfo per Query level;
  |  all levels share one PlannerGlobal                                              [B]
  v
PlannerInfo
  |- simple_rel_array[rti] -> base RelOptInfo (+ IndexOptInfo list for tables)       [C]
  |- join_rel_list         -> join RelOptInfo, one per set of Relids                 [D]
  |- upper_rels[kind]      -> upper RelOptInfo per processing step (UPPERREL_*)      [E]
  |- eq_classes, join_info_list (SpecialJoinInfo), placeholder_list, append_rel_list [F]
  v
RelOptInfo.pathlist: Paths compared by add_path; set_cheapest picks winners          [G]
  |  the final upper rel (UPPERREL_FINAL) holds the candidate whole-query paths
  v
best Path --create_plan--> Plan tree --set_plan_references--> PlannedStmt            [H]
```

- [A] [parsenodes.h#Query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L117-L176)
- [B] [planner.c#subquery_planner-root](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L641-L649), [pathnodes.h#PlannerGlobal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L83-L95)
- [C] [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-simple_rel_array](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L223-L232), [relnode.c#build_simple_rel-get_relation_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L335-L341)
- [D] [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-join_rel_list](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L271-L296)
- [E] [pathnodes.h#UpperRelationKind](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L65-L81), [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-upper_rels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L412-L419)
- [F] [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-ec-joininfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L313-L340), [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-appendrels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L358-L374)
- [G] [pathnode.c#add_path-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L361-L398), [pathnode.c#set_cheapest](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L242-L253)
- [H] [planner.c#standard_planner-core](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L418-L422), [planner.c#standard_planner-setrefs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L520-L535)

#### 2.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: one PlannerInfo per query level

Input: a `Query`. `subquery_planner()` creates a `PlannerInfo` for it, links it to the shared `PlannerGlobal`, and records its level: 1 at the top, one more for each nested subquery ([planner.c#subquery_planner-root](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L641-L649)). Output: `root`, the object that nearly every planner function takes as its first argument ([pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L173-L188)). Consequence: a sub-`SELECT` that is not flattened gets its own `root` and its own complete planning pass (chapter 9).

##### Step 2: one RelOptInfo per base relation

Input: the range table. For each entry that is scanned, `build_simple_rel()` makes a `RelOptInfo` whose `relids` is a one-member set ([relnode.c#build_simple_rel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L192-L215)). For a table it calls `get_relation_info()`, which reads the size, the indexes and other catalog facts ([relnode.c#build_simple_rel-get_relation_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L335-L341)). An index that is not valid is skipped there, so no later step ever sees it ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-invalid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L256-L267)). Output: `simple_rel_array[rti]`, indexed by range-table index ([pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-simple_rel_array](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L223-L232)).

The `RelOptKind` field says what the relation is: a base relation, a join, an "other member" such as a partition, or an upper relation ([pathnodes.h#RelOptKind](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L819-L851)). Members of an inheritance tree or a `UNION ALL` are "other rels": they are planned individually, and their parent gets an Append of their paths ([pathnodes.h#RelOptInfo-comment-otherrels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L617-L628)).

##### Step 3: clauses become RestrictInfos

Input: the `WHERE` and `JOIN ... ON` conditions. The planner wraps each ANDed condition in a `RestrictInfo`. It records the relations the clause references (`clause_relids`) and needs (`required_relids`), whether it is a pseudoconstant, and its [security level](../../../glossary.md#security-barrier). It also caches the clause's [selectivity](../../../glossary.md#selectivity) and cost ([pathnodes.h#RestrictInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2560-L2600), [pathnodes.h#RestrictInfo-caches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2647-L2657)). Output: conditions attached to base relations or kept as join conditions (chapter 3). Consequence: a clause's selectivity is computed once and reused by every path that applies it.

##### Step 4: joins and later steps are relations too

Input: the set of base relations. A join `RelOptInfo` is identified by the union of its members' `Relids`, plus the range-table indexes of any outer joins computed below it ([pathnodes.h#RelOptInfo-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L604-L615)). Every later step — grouping, window functions, `DISTINCT`, ordering, the final result — is an upper relation named by an `UPPERREL_*` kind ([pathnodes.h#UpperRelationKind](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L65-L81), [relnode.c#fetch_upper_rel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L1456-L1500)). Output: one place per step to collect alternative paths.

##### Step 5: paths compete inside each relation

Input: a new `Path`. `add_path()` keeps it only if no existing path is at least as good on every axis: cost, sort order, rows, the outer relations it needs, and parallel safety. It also deletes old paths that the new one beats ([pathnode.c#add_path-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L361-L373)). `set_cheapest()` then records the cheapest-startup and cheapest-total paths, and fails with "could not devise a query plan" if none survived ([pathnode.c#set_cheapest](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L242-L253)). Output: a short list of non-dominated paths per relation. Chapter 5 shows the comparison rules in numbers.

##### Step 6: expressions and parameters

The clauses and target lists are expression trees. Their leaves are `Var` nodes (column references), `Const` nodes and `Param` nodes. Operators and function calls are `OpExpr` and `FuncExpr` nodes that name the operator or function and list their arguments ([primnodes.h#Var](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L247-L294), [primnodes.h#FuncExpr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L746-L771), [primnodes.h#OpExpr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L813-L840)).

A `Param` has four kinds. `PARAM_EXTERN` values come from outside the plan, such as `$1`. `PARAM_EXEC` values pass between plan nodes, for example from a nested loop's outer row to its inner scan. The two sub-select kinds are turned into `PARAM_EXEC` during planning ([primnodes.h#ParamKind](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L338-L371)). The planner records the type of every `PARAM_EXEC` slot in `glob->paramExecTypes` ([pathnodes.h#PlannerGlobal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L137-L138)).

##### Step 7: from Path to Plan

Input: the winning path of the final upper relation. `create_plan()` walks the path tree and builds a `Plan` node for each path node ([createplan.c#create_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L322-L350)). The `Plan` keeps the estimated costs, rows and width, plus the target list, quals, child links and parameter sets the executor needs ([plannodes.h#Plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L119-L172)). Output: the plan tree that chapter 14 finishes.

#### 2.5 Eligibility and comparison

Structures decide what is even considered. A relation that has no `RelOptInfo` has no paths. An index absent from `indexlist`, because it is invalid or not yet usable, never produces an index path ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-invalid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L256-L281)). A join between two relation sets exists only if a `RelOptInfo` for their union is built, which the join search does only for legal, useful pairs (chapter 8).

Comparison always happens inside one `RelOptInfo`, never across relations. Two paths for `{customers, orders}` compete with each other, but a path for `{orders}` never competes with one for the join ([pathnode.c#add_path-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L405-L412)). Parameterized paths are treated as unordered, so they cannot win on sort order ([pathnode.c#add_path-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L381-L386)).

#### 2.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A relation ends with no surviving path | `set_cheapest()` raises "could not devise a query plan for the given query" ([pathnode.c#set_cheapest](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L252-L253)) | planning fails; in practice some path, such as a sequential scan, is always available |
| A path is dominated but is also the child of a bitmap path | `add_path()` does not free an `IndexPath`, because a `BitmapHeapPath` may point to it ([pathnode.c#add_path-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L405-L412)) | memory is kept for index paths |
| An upper relation | Most `RelOptInfo` fields are unused; only path fields matter ([relnode.c#fetch_upper_rel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L1465-L1467)) | size fields there are not table sizes |
| A partitioned index | `IndexOptInfo` copies no access-method capabilities for it ([pathnodes.h#IndexOptInfo-am-fields](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1189-L1192)) | it serves as a uniqueness proof, not as a scan path ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L108-L113)) |
| Planner objects are printed but not read back | `PlannerInfo` and `PlannerGlobal` carry `no_copy_equal, no_read` ([pathnodes.h#PlannerGlobal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L97), [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L197)) | they live only during planning; a `PlannedStmt` can be serialized, which parallel query relies on ([execParallel.c#ExecSerializePlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execParallel.c#L216), [execParallel.c:1250](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execParallel.c#L1250)) |

#### 2.7 Formulas and worked examples

##### Q1's structures (E1.3)

Q1's range table has `customers c` and `orders o`, so there are two base `RelOptInfo`s and one join `RelOptInfo` for their union. Above them sit two upper relations, `UPPERREL_ORDERED` for the sort and `UPPERREL_FINAL`, whose paths get the `Limit` ([planner.c#grouping_planner-upper](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1750-L1766), [planner.c#grouping_planner-final](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1805-L1815)). Estimated by the planner, E1.3 (`VERBOSE` prints each node's output columns):

```text
 Limit  (cost=663.46..663.48 rows=5 width=24)
   Output: c.name, o.id, o.amount
   ->  Sort  (cost=663.46..664.22 rows=302 width=24)
         ...
         ->  Hash Join  (cost=49.50..658.45 rows=302 width=24)
               Output: c.name, o.id, o.amount
               Inner Unique: true
               Hash Cond: (o.customer_id = c.id)
               ->  Seq Scan on public.orders o  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=3019 width=14)
                     Output: o.id, o.customer_id, o.status, o.ordered_at, o.amount, o.note
                     Filter: (o.status = 'pending'::text)
               ->  Hash  (cost=47.00..47.00 rows=200 width=18)
                     Output: c.name, c.id
```

The mapping from structure to output:

| Structure | In Q1 | Visible in E1.3 as |
|---|---|---|
| base `RelOptInfo` for `orders`, with `RestrictInfo` `status = 'pending'` | 3,019 estimated rows | the `Seq Scan on public.orders` line and its `Filter` |
| join `RelOptInfo` for `{c, o}` | one relation, many candidate paths | the one surviving path, `Hash Join` |
| `RestrictInfo` for `o.customer_id = c.id` | a join clause | `Hash Cond` |
| `PathTarget` of the join | the three output columns | `Output: c.name, o.id, o.amount` |
| upper relations `UPPERREL_ORDERED` and `UPPERREL_FINAL` | `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 5` | `Sort`, and the `Limit` on the final relation's path |

The `width=14` on the orders scan and `Output` of six columns look inconsistent, but they come from different layers. The width is the planner's estimate for the columns the query needs, while the six-column output list is a plan-creation choice that returns the whole table row to avoid a projection step ([createplan.c#create_scan_plan-physical-tlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L629-L643)). The hash side instead asked for a narrow list, because a Hash node stores its input rows ([createplan.c#create_hashjoin_plan-tlists](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L4767-L4778)).

##### How big is the working model? (E16.3)

Measured, E16.3. `EXPLAIN (MEMORY)` reports the memory the planner allocated while planning Q1, from a context created just for that measurement ([explain.c#standard_ExplainOneQuery-memory](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L469-L499)):

```text
 Planning:
   Memory: used=41kB  allocated=64kB
```

All of these structures live in the caller's [memory context](../../../glossary.md#memory-context), recorded as `root->planner_cxt` ([planner.c:649](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L649)). So the planner's memory is released with the statement, not kept between executions, unless the plan cache copies the finished plan (chapter 14).

#### 2.8 Planning versus execution

| Planner structure | What the executor gets instead |
|---|---|
| `Path`, `RelOptInfo`, `PlannerInfo` | nothing; they are discarded after `create_plan()` and `set_plan_references()` |
| `Var` with a range-table index | a `Var` that points at an input tuple slot: `OUTER_VAR`, `INNER_VAR` or `INDEX_VAR` ([primnodes.h#Var-special-varnos](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L206-L239)) |
| `PARAM_EXEC` slots | `paramExecTypes` in the `PlannedStmt`, which sizes the executor's parameter array ([plannodes.h#PlannedStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L93)) |
| estimated `rows` and costs | copied into `Plan.plan_rows` and the cost fields; the executor does not use them to change strategy, and EXPLAIN prints them ([plannodes.h#Plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L125-L135)) |

#### 2.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subquery_planner()` starts a query level | no `PlannerInfo` | a new `root` with empty lists ([planner.c#subquery_planner-root](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L641-L681)) | the level plans independently |
| `add_path()` accepts a better path | old paths in `pathlist` | dominated paths removed and freed ([pathnode.c#add_path-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L370-L373)) | later joins see only survivors |
| `set_cheapest()` runs | unsorted winners | `cheapest_startup_path`, `cheapest_total_path` set ([pathnode.c#set_cheapest](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L242-L260)) | parent joins build on these |
| Planning ends | planner structures in the caller's context | only the `PlannedStmt` is kept by the caller | a new planning run rebuilds everything |
| A node definition changes in source | old struct layout | `gen_node_support.pl` regenerates the copy, equal, out, read and query-jumbling functions and `nodetags.h` from the node headers ([gen_node_support.pl#queryjumblefuncs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/gen_node_support.pl#L1246-L1249), [Makefile#node_headers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/Makefile#L37-L63), [Makefile#node-support-stamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/Makefile#L73-L88), [gen_node_support.pl header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/gen_node_support.pl#L1-L16)) | a build implication only; `pg_node_attr` markings decide which functions exist ([nodes.h#pg_node_attr-list](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L40-L70)) |

The generated node support dates from commit `964d01ae90` ("Automatically generate node support functions"), and outer-join-aware Vars (`varnullingrels`) from `2489d76c49` ("Make Vars be outer-join-aware"). The v17 history places both before the 17 development cycle began, so neither is new in 17.

#### 2.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- There is no test of these structures as such. They are exercised by every planner test; the plans in `join.sql`, `subselect.sql` and `aggregates.sql` show their effects.
- Explicit gap: the page's E1.5 capture shows range-table kinds only as enum numbers, and nothing in the regression suite prints `PlannerInfo` or `RelOptInfo` contents. `debug_print_plan` prints the `PlannedStmt` only ([postgres.c#pg_plan_query-debug](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L960-L961)).

#### 2.11 Causal summary

1. A `Query` enters, and each query level gets a `PlannerInfo`, all sharing one `PlannerGlobal`.
2. Every scanned table becomes a base `RelOptInfo` filled from the catalogs, every join a `RelOptInfo` named by its set of members, and every later step an upper `RelOptInfo`.
3. Conditions become `RestrictInfo`s that cache their estimates.
4. Paths compete inside each relation through `add_path()`, and the survivor of the final upper relation becomes a `Plan` tree.
5. Only the `PlannedStmt` outlives planning, so everything else is rebuilt the next time the query is planned.

### Chapter 3. Transform the query safely

#### 3.1 Main idea

The planner does not search for paths on the query as you wrote it. Before any path exists, `subquery_planner()` ([planner.c#subquery_planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L629-L631)) rewrites the query tree into an equivalent form that is easier to plan. It folds constants, inlines simple SQL functions and flattens subqueries and views into the outer query. It turns `EXISTS` and `IN` into joins and weakens outer joins that cannot produce NULL rows. Finally it files every `WHERE` condition at the lowest place where it can run.

This matters because the result often looks nothing like the SQL. A `LEFT JOIN` shows up as an inner Hash Join, a join disappears, an `IS NOT NULL` vanishes, and a view becomes a plain table scan. Each rewrite is guarded by a correctness rule: strictness protects NULL semantics, [volatility](../../../glossary.md#function-volatility) protects side effects, [collation](../../../glossary.md#collation) protects comparisons, and [leakproofness](../../../glossary.md#leakproof-function) protects [row-level security](../../../glossary.md#row-level-security). A rewrite that would break a rule is skipped, never approximated.

The chapter's evidence is E3.1 to E3.13 in stage s03, plus the view expansion of E1.4 and E1.5 in stage s01.

#### 3.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Query` tree (`jointree`, `rtable`, `targetList`, `havingQual`) | The analyzed and rewritten statement, see parse tree | The parser and rewriter; the planner edits it in place ([prepjointree.c:885-886](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L885-L886)) | Current in-memory state of this planning run | Every later step, ending in `query_planner()` ([planner.c:1553](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1553)) |
| `PlannerInfo` (`root`) | Per-query-level planner state, created once per `Query` ([planner.c#subquery_planner-root](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L641-L646)) | `subquery_planner()` | Current state | Holds `qual_security_level`, `hasPseudoConstantQuals`, `eq_classes` and `join_info_list` ([pathnodes.h:495](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L495), [pathnodes.h:503-504](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L503-L504), [pathnodes.h:314](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L314), [pathnodes.h:340](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L340)) |
| `RangeTblEntry.securityQuals`, `security_barrier`, `lateral` | Policy quals, the barrier-view flag, and `LATERAL` marking on a range table entry ([parsenodes.h:1112-1113](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1112-L1113), [parsenodes.h:1246-1250](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1246-L1250)) | The rewriter: view expansion sets `security_barrier`, and row-level security prepends policy quals ([rewriteHandler.c:1875-1877](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L1875-L1877), [rewriteHandler.c:2305-2312](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L2305-L2312)) | Stored in the tree before planning | Pull-up refusal, pushdown safety, qual ordering |
| `RestrictInfo` | One ANDed condition plus planning flags: `is_pushed_down`, `pseudoconstant`, `leakproof`, `security_level`, `required_relids` ([pathnodes.h#RestrictInfo](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2560-L2598)) | Built while `deconstruct_jointree()` distributes quals | Current state | Scans, joins, equivalence classes, gating Result nodes |
| `RelOptInfo``.baserestrictinfo`, `joininfo`, `baserestrict_min_security` | A relation's one-table conditions, its join conditions, and the lowest security level among them ([pathnodes.h:979-985](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L979-L985)) | `distribute_restrictinfo_to_rels()` | Current state | Path generation in chapters 6 to 8 |
| `RelOptInfo.notnullattnums` | Column numbers declared `NOT NULL` ([pathnodes.h:926-930](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L926-L930)) | Read from `pg_attribute.attnotnull` when the relation is opened ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-notnull](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L165-L184)) | Stored catalog state, read at planning time | The 17 `IS [NOT] NULL` rewrite (E3.8) |
| `EquivalenceClass` | A set of expressions proven equal, with `ec_has_const` when one member is a constant ([pathnodes.h:1380-1393](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1380-L1393)) | Mergejoinable equalities found during distribution | Derived current state | Derived restrictions and join clauses (E3.7), pathkeys |
| `SpecialJoinInfo` | An outer, semi or anti join that limits legal join orders ([pathnodes.h:2888-2901](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L2888-L2901)) | `deconstruct_jointree()` | Current state | Join removal, [semi join](../../../glossary.md#semi-join-and-anti-join) reduction, chapter 8 |
| `pg_proc` flags: `provolatile`, `proisstrict`, `proconfig`, `prosecdef`, `procost`, `prosqlbody` | Function properties that decide folding, inlining and cost | Catalog, read through the syscache during planning ([clauses.c#evaluate_function-volatility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4495-L4507), [clauses.c#inline_function-showstoppers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4587-L4598)) | Stored catalog state | Constant folding and [SQL function inlining](../../../glossary.md#sql-function-inlining) |
| `boundParams` | Parameter values the caller of `planner()` supplied | `PlannerGlobal.boundParams` ([clauses.c#eval_const_expressions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2261-L2274)) | Parameters | Folded into constants only when flagged constant, or during estimation ([clauses.c#eval_const_expressions_mutator-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2494-L2498)) |

Two similar-looking values come from different places. `notnullattnums` is catalog state that a later `ALTER TABLE` can change, while a `RestrictInfo`'s `pseudoconstant` flag is derived from the query text in this planning run only. The first can go stale in a cached plan; the second cannot.

#### 3.3 Logic map

The map follows one query level from the rewriter's output to the distributed quals. Each line names the step, its condition, and what it hands on. The bracketed keys index the citations under the block.

```text
Rewritten Query for one level (views already replaced by subqueries)
|
+-- [A] WITH list?            yes -> each CTE is inlined or planned as an initplan (chapter 9)
+-- [B] MERGE?                yes -> target and source become an outer join (chapter 13)
|       FROM empty?           yes -> a dummy RTE_RESULT entry is added
+-- [C] EXISTS / ANY sublinks at top level of WHERE or JOIN/ON?
|                             yes, and convertible -> semi join or anti join (chapter 9)
+-- [D] set-returning SQL function in FROM, inlinable?
|                             yes -> it becomes a subquery RTE
+-- [E] subquery or view RTE "simple" (no aggregates, LIMIT/OFFSET, DISTINCT,
|       security barrier, volatile output...)?
|                             yes -> its tables and quals merge into this level
|                             no  -> it stays a subquery, planned separately
+-- [F] simple UNION ALL?     yes -> an append relation (chapter 10)
+-- [G] expression preprocessing on every expression:
|       join aliases flattened -> constants folded, SQL functions inlined
|       -> quals canonicalized -> constant IN-lists marked hashable
|       -> remaining SubLinks become SubPlans -> outer Vars become Params
+-- [H] HAVING clause without aggregates, volatile functions or SubPlans?
|                             yes -> moved (or copied) into WHERE
+-- [I] outer join with a strict upper qual on its nullable side?
|                             yes -> reduced to an inner join, or to an anti join
+-- [J] grouping_planner -> query_planner:
      deconstruct_jointree files each qual:
        no Vars, not volatile           -> pseudoconstant: gating Result
        one relation                    -> baserestrictinfo
          IS NOT NULL on NOT NULL column -> dropped      (17)
          IS NULL on NOT NULL column     -> constant FALSE: relation empty (17)
        several relations               -> joininfo
        mergejoinable equality          -> EquivalenceClass
        security qual                   -> tagged with its security level
      then: EC-derived restrictions, useless left joins removed,
            unique semi joins made inner, OR restrictions extracted
      [K] at plan creation: quals ordered by security level, then cost
```

- [A] [planner.c#subquery_planner-ctes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L690-L695)
- [B] [planner.c#subquery_planner-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L697-L706)
- [C] [planner.c#subquery_planner-sublinks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L708-L715), [prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L427-L453)
- [D] [planner.c#subquery_planner-functions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L717-L723), [prepjointree.c#preprocess_function_rtes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L889-L925)
- [E] [planner.c#subquery_planner-pullup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L725-L729), [prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1661-L1709), [prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-end](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1772-L1784)
- [F] [planner.c#subquery_planner-union-all](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L731-L738)
- [G] [planner.c#preprocess_expression](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1156-L1202), [planner.c#preprocess_expression-sublinks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1204-L1250)
- [H] [planner.c#subquery_planner-having](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1041-L1100)
