#### 3.4 Step by step

##### Step 1. Start a level and settle the CTEs and special statements

Input: one rewritten `Query`. `subquery_planner()` builds a fresh `PlannerInfo` for it and records its nesting level, so a subquery gets its own `root` with a `parent_root` link ([planner.c#subquery_planner-root](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L641-L646)). It then asks `SS_process_ctes()` to inline or separately plan each `WITH` query ([planner.c#subquery_planner-ctes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L690-L695)); chapter 9 covers that decision. A `MERGE` becomes a join, and an empty `FROM` gets a dummy `RTE_RESULT` entry, so later code needs fewer special cases ([planner.c#subquery_planner-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L697-L706)).

Views never reach this step as views. The rewriter has already turned a view's range-table entry into a subquery entry ([rewriteHandler.c:1869-1877](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L1869-L1877)). E1.5 shows it: the parse tree holds an entry with `:rtekind 0 ... :relkind v`, and the rewritten tree holds `:rtekind 1` with the view's `Query` inside.

Measured, E1.5 (markers filtered from the debug_print_parse and debug_print_rewritten logs, s01-debug.txt):

```text
marker e1_5_view_query
parse tree:
{QUERY
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 0
:inh true
:relkind v
:inh true
rewritten parse tree:
{QUERY
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 1
{QUERY
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
{RANGETBLENTRY
:rtekind 0
:inh true
:relkind r
...
```

##### Step 2. Turn sublinks into joins before anything is flattened

`pull_up_sublinks()` looks only at the top level of `WHERE` and `JOIN ... ON`, walking through `AND` nodes and stopping at anything else ([prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks_qual_recurse-and](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L830-L859)). It must run first, because a pulled-up sublink becomes a join that the next steps may flatten further ([planner.c#subquery_planner-sublinks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L708-L715)). The rules for `IN`, `EXISTS` and `NOT EXISTS`, and why `NOT IN` is left alone, are in chapter 9.

##### Step 3. Inline set-returning SQL functions in FROM

`preprocess_function_rtes()` first folds the constants in each function call in `FROM`. It then asks `inline_set_returning_function()` whether the call can be replaced by the function's body. On success the entry becomes a subquery entry, which the next step may flatten ([prepjointree.c#preprocess_function_rtes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L889-L925)).

The function must be SQL-language, `SETOF`, not `STRICT`, not `VOLATILE`, not `SECURITY DEFINER`, and have no `SET` clause ([clauses.c#inline_set_returning_function-showstoppers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L5158-L5180)). E3.3 shows both outcomes. `orders_of(77)` became a Bitmap Heap Scan on `orders` with the function's `customer_id = 77` as an index condition. The PL/pgSQL twin stayed a Function Scan with the default 1,000-row guess, filtered to 333 rows.

Estimated by the planner, E3.3:

```text
 Bitmap Heap Scan on orders  (cost=4.36..38.20 rows=5 width=40)
   Recheck Cond: (customer_id = 77)
   Filter: (amount > '500'::numeric)
...
 Function Scan on orders_of_plpgsql  (cost=0.25..12.75 rows=333 width=96)
   Filter: (amount > '500'::numeric)
```

##### Step 4. Flatten simple subqueries and views

`pull_up_subqueries()` walks the join tree and merges each "simple" subquery into the current level ([prepjointree.c#pull_up_subqueries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L936-L946)). After a [pull-up](../../../glossary.md#subquery-pull-up), the subquery's tables join the outer query's join search, and its quals join the outer quals. E1.4 shows the effect on a view: one Seq Scan on `orders` carries both the view's `status = 'pending'` and the outer `amount > 900`.

`is_simple_subquery()` decides eligibility ([prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1661-L1709), [prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-end](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1772-L1784)). A subquery with set operations, aggregates, window functions, set-returning functions in the target list, `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, `ORDER BY`, `DISTINCT`, `LIMIT`, `OFFSET`, `FOR UPDATE` or its own `WITH` stays separate ([prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-features](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1676-L1701)). So does a security-barrier view ([prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-barrier](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1703-L1709)), and a subquery whose output list calls a volatile function ([prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-volatile](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1772-L1781)).

A subquery that stays separate can still receive outer quals, one qual at a time. `set_subquery_pathlist()` pushes a qual down unless the subquery has `LIMIT` or `OFFSET`, or the qual references an unsafe output column ([allpaths.c#set_subquery_pathlist-pushdown](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2530-L2603), [allpaths.c#subquery_is_pushdown_safe](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3582-L3590)). That is why `OFFSET 0` works as an optimization fence. In E3.4b the fenced subquery reads all 30,000 rows and filters above them, while the plain subquery becomes a primary-key lookup:

Estimated by the planner, E3.4b:

```text
 Index Scan using orders_pkey on orders  (cost=0.29..8.30 rows=1 width=40)
   Index Cond: (id = 42)
...
 Subquery Scan on s  (cost=0.00..901.00 rows=1 width=40)
   Filter: (s.id = 42)
   ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..526.00 rows=30000 width=40)
```

E3.9 separates two cases in one query. The subquery's `random()` output blocks pull-up, so a Subquery Scan remains. The qual `s.id = 5` still went down and became an index condition, while `s.r < 0.5` stayed above, because it references the volatile column ([allpaths.c#check_output_expressions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3707-L3741), [allpaths.c#qual_is_pushdown_safe-point5](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3928-L3943)).

##### Step 5. Preprocess every expression

`subquery_planner()` runs `preprocess_expression()` over the target list, `RETURNING`, every `WHERE` and `JOIN ... ON` qual, `HAVING`, window offsets, `LIMIT`, `ON CONFLICT` and `MERGE` parts, and expressions inside range-table entries ([planner.c#subquery_planner-expressions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L862-L895), [planner.c#subquery_planner-rte-expressions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L955-L1018)). The order inside `preprocess_expression()` matters, because each stage prepares the input of the next ([planner.c#preprocess_expression](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1156-L1202), [planner.c#preprocess_expression-sublinks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1204-L1250)):

1. Join alias variables become base-table variables ([planner.c:1175-1180](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1175-L1180)).
2. `eval_const_expressions()` folds constants, expands default and named arguments, and flattens nested `AND`/`OR` ([planner.c:1182-1202](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1182-L1202)).
3. A qual is canonicalized, which applies the inverse OR distributive law to pull terms common to every `OR` branch out of the `OR` ([planner.c:1207-1210](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1207-L1210), [prepqual.c#canonicalize_qual](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepqual.c#L270-L293), [prepqual.c#process_duplicate_ors](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepqual.c#L508-L517)).
4. `IN` lists of constants may be marked for hashed lookup at run time ([planner.c:1217-1225](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1217-L1225)).
5. Remaining sublinks become [SubPlans](../../../glossary.md#subplan), and references to outer query levels become `Param` nodes ([planner.c:1227-1238](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1227-L1238)).
6. A qual becomes an implicit-AND list ([planner.c:1246-1247](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1246-L1247)).

[Constant folding](../../../glossary.md#constant-folding) evaluates a function call only when all its arguments are constants and it is immutable. A stable function is folded only in estimation mode ([clauses.c#evaluate_function-constant-inputs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4487-L4507)). A strict function with a constant-NULL argument becomes NULL even if its other arguments vary ([clauses.c#evaluate_function-strict-null](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4477-L4485)). E3.1 shows `id = 2 + 3` as `Index Cond: (id = 5)` and `abs(-500)` as `'500'::numeric`. `now()` is stable, so it stays in the plan and runs at execution.

When a call cannot be evaluated, `simplify_function()` tries the function's [support function](../../../glossary.md#planner-support-function) and then inlining ([clauses.c#simplify_function](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4079-L4158)). Scalar inlining needs an SQL function without `SECURITY DEFINER` or a `SET` clause, whose body is a single `SELECT expression` ([clauses.c#inline_function-showstoppers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4587-L4598), [clauses.c#inline_function-simple-select](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4704-L4732)). The body may not be more volatile than the function, and a strict function's body must be strict ([clauses.c#inline_function-volatility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4777-L4794)). In E3.2 `big_amount(amount)` became `amount > '900'::numeric`, while `big_amount_pinned`, identical except for `SET search_path`, stayed a function call.

##### Step 6. Move HAVING conditions to WHERE when that is safe

A `HAVING` condition without aggregates, volatile functions or SubPlans moves into `WHERE` when the query has plain grouping, so it filters rows before grouping. With grouping sets it stays in `HAVING`. Without any `GROUP BY`, a copy goes to `WHERE` and the original stays, which lets a variable-free condition become a gating Result ([planner.c#subquery_planner-having](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1041-L1100)). Chapter 10's E10.12 shows the move.

##### Step 7. Reduce outer joins

`reduce_outer_joins()` looks for a strict qual above an outer join that rejects NULLs from the join's nullable side. Such a qual discards every null-extended row, so the [outer join](../../../glossary.md#outer-join) produces nothing that survives, and it can be an inner join ([prepjointree.c#reduce_outer_joins-strict](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L2896-L2914)). The same pass turns `LEFT JOIN ... WHERE inner.col IS NULL` into an anti join when the join clause is strict, and flips `RIGHT JOIN` into `LEFT JOIN` ([prepjointree.c#reduce_outer_joins-anti](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L2915-L2928)).

E3.5 shows the difference between the two places a condition can live. With `WHERE o.status = 'pending'`, the plan is an inner Hash Join. With the same condition inside `ON`, the rows without a match must still appear, so the plan keeps an outer join (a Hash Right Join, which is the left join with its inputs swapped).

##### Step 8. File each qual at the lowest level that can evaluate it

`grouping_planner()` calls `query_planner()` ([planner.c:1553](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1553)). There, `deconstruct_jointree()` scans the join tree, builds `SpecialJoinInfo` entries for outer joins, and hands each qual to `distribute_qual_to_rels()` ([initsplan.c#deconstruct_jointree](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L722-L739)). The qual's set of referenced relations decides its home:

- No relations and no volatile function: the qual is a pseudoconstant. It is marked for a gating Result node placed as high as possible ([initsplan.c#distribute_qual_to_rels-pseudoconstant](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2285-L2318)). E6.11 shows `One-Time Filter: (now() > ...)` above a bitmap scan.
- A mergejoinable equality that is not an outer-join clause goes to the equivalence-class machinery instead of a relation's list ([initsplan.c#distribute_qual_to_rels-ec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2504-L2509)).
- One relation: the qual joins that relation's `baserestrictinfo`. Several relations: it joins each relation's `joininfo` ([initsplan.c#distribute_restrictinfo_to_rels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2876-L2915)).

In 17, `add_base_clause_to_rel()` inspects a one-relation qual before storing it. `IS NOT NULL` on a `NOT NULL` column that no outer join can null is dropped; `IS NULL` on such a column becomes constant `FALSE` ([initsplan.c#add_base_clause_to_rel-nulltest](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2652-L2685), [initsplan.c#expr_is_nonnullable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2703-L2730)). Join clauses get the same check ([joininfo.c#add_join_clause_to_rels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/joininfo.c#L98-L125)). A constant-`FALSE` restriction makes the relation provably empty, so it gets a dummy path ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1602-L1621), [allpaths.c#set_rel_size-dummy](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L363-L377)), which becomes a Result with `One-Time Filter: false` ([createplan.c#create_append_plan-empty](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1236-L1253)). E3.8:

Estimated by the planner, E3.8, for `count(*)` under `WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL` on the `NOT NULL` column:

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=601.00..601.01 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..526.00 rows=30000 width=0)
```

Under `WHERE customer_id IS NULL` on the same column:

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=0.00..0.01 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Result  (cost=0.00..0.00 rows=0 width=0)
         One-Time Filter: false
```

Under `WHERE note IS NOT NULL` on a nullable column:

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=529.72..529.73 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..526.00 rows=1488 width=0)
         Filter: (note IS NOT NULL)
```

The first scan has no `Filter` line at all, and its cost equals an unfiltered scan.

The rewrite was committed in the 17 development cycle as `b262ad440e`, which removes redundant `IS [NOT] NULL` quals using `NOT NULL` column declarations. `3af7040985` then limited it for inheritance parents, whose children may have different `NOT NULL` constraints ([initsplan.c#add_base_clause_to_rel-inheritance](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2637-L2652), [inherit.c:909-914](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L909-L914)).

##### Step 9. Security quals keep their place

Policy quals and security-barrier quals carry a security level. `process_security_barrier_quals()` gives successive policy lists increasing levels, and ordinary `WHERE` quals get `qual_security_level`, the highest level of all ([initsplan.c#deconstruct_distribute-where-level](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L1150-L1158), [initsplan.c#process_security_barrier_quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L1258-L1311), [planner.c#subquery_planner-security-level](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L793-L801)). A qual is marked leakproof only if it passes no Var to a non-leakproof function ([restrictinfo.c:138-146](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/restrictinfo.c#L138-L146), [clauses.c#contain_leaked_vars](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L1258-L1273)).

When the plan is built, `order_qual_clauses()` sorts a node's quals by security level, then by cost. A leakproof qual that costs under ten times `cpu_operator_cost` is treated as level 0 and may run first ([createplan.c#order_qual_clauses-leakproof](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L5348-L5393)). E3.11 shows both rules. As `pqt_reader`, `balance > 5000` runs before the policy's `owner = CURRENT_USER`. Its operator is leakproof ([pg_proc.dat:435](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_proc.dat#L435)), so it counts as level 0. It also costs one `cpu_operator_cost` against two for the policy qual, whose `CURRENT_USER` is charged one more ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-cost-1](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4895-L4902)). `leaky(id)` runs after the policy qual, even though `leaky` is declared almost free, because it is not leakproof.

Estimated by the planner, E3.11 (as pqt_reader):

```text
 Seq Scan on accounts  (cost=0.00..24.50 rows=125 width=20)
   Filter: ((balance > 5000) AND (owner = CURRENT_USER))
 Seq Scan on accounts  (cost=0.00..22.00 rows=83 width=20)
   Filter: ((owner = CURRENT_USER) AND leaky(id))
```

A security-barrier view works differently: it is never pulled up (Step 4), and a qual containing a leaky function is not pushed into it ([allpaths.c#set_subquery_pathlist-leaky](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2521-L2528), [allpaths.c#qual_is_pushdown_safe-leaky](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3872-L3875)). E3.10 shows `leaky(id)` filtering above a Subquery Scan for the barrier view, but inside the scan filter, first, for the plain view. The leakproof `id = 42` still reaches the index through the barrier.

##### Step 10. Derive, remove and extract after distribution

With all quals filed, `query_planner()` runs four clean-ups in order ([planmain.c#query_planner-cleanups](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planmain.c#L195-L258)):

1. `generate_base_implied_equalities()` turns each equivalence class with a constant into `member = constant` restrictions ([optimizer/README#EquivalenceClasses-const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/README#L712-L721)). In E3.7, `c.id = 42` and `o.customer_id = c.id` gave `Index Cond: (customer_id = 42)` on `orders`, and no join clause remained.
2. `remove_useless_joins()` deletes a left join to a single relation that is provably unique on the join clause and whose columns nothing above uses ([analyzejoins.c#join_is_removable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/analyzejoins.c#L176-L240)). Uniqueness needs a unique, immediate, non-partial index ([analyzejoins.c#rel_supports_distinctness](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/analyzejoins.c#L840-L873)). E3.6 shows `orders LEFT JOIN customers` reduced to a Seq Scan on `orders` when no `customers` column is selected.
3. `reduce_unique_semijoins()` turns a semi join whose inner side is unique for the join clauses into an inner join ([analyzejoins.c#reduce_unique_semijoins](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/analyzejoins.c#L749-L826)); see E8.7.
4. `extract_restriction_or_clauses()` copies one-relation `OR` restrictions out of a join `OR` clause, so a scan can filter early ([orclauses.c#extract_restriction_or_clauses](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L32-L75)). Step 11 walks through it.

##### Step 11. Extract one-table OR conditions from a join OR

A condition such as `(c.region = 'west' AND o.amount > 990) OR (c.tier = 'gold' AND o.amount < 5)` references both tables, so Step 8 files it as a join clause. No scan could use it. `extract_restriction_or_clauses()` examines each base relation's `OR` join clauses. For every arm of the `OR`, it collects the parts that mention only that relation; if every arm has such a part, their `OR` is a valid restriction for that relation alone ([orclauses.c#extract_or_clause-contract](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L144-L154), [orclauses.c#extract_restriction_or_clauses-loop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L100-L120)). A part qualifies only if it mentions exactly that relation, is not pseudoconstant and calls no volatile function ([orclauses.c#is_safe_restriction_clause_for](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L126-L142)).

The new clause is redundant: the original `OR` stays as a join clause and is still checked when the join is formed. The extraction exists for two reasons. First, the scan can drop rows before the join, and the new clause may even become an index condition ([orclauses.c#extract_restriction_or_clauses-purpose](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L40-L51)). Second, the scan's row estimate now counts only rows that can pass. The planner adds the clause only when its selectivity is at most 0.9, because a weaker filter costs more than it saves ([orclauses.c#consider_new_or_clause-threshold](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L284-L299)).

Counting the same condition twice would underestimate the join. So `consider_new_or_clause()` divides the original `OR` clause's cached selectivity by the new clause's selectivity. The join's estimate then stays about what it would have been without the extra clause ([orclauses.c#consider_new_or_clause-selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L301-L344)). E3.13 shows both extracted clauses and the full `OR` kept as the Hash Join's `Join Filter`:

Estimated by the planner, E3.13:

```text
 Hash Join  (cost=56.85..734.07 rows=47 width=8)
   Hash Cond: (o.customer_id = c.id)
   Join Filter: (((c.region = 'west'::text) AND (o.amount > '990'::numeric)) OR ((c.tier = 'gold'::text) AND (o.amount < '5'::numeric)))
   ->  Seq Scan on orders o  (cost=0.00..676.00 rows=465 width=14)
         Filter: ((amount > '990'::numeric) OR (amount < '5'::numeric))
   ->  Hash  (cost=52.00..52.00 rows=388 width=15)
         ->  Seq Scan on customers c  (cost=0.00..52.00 rows=388 width=15)
               Filter: ((region = 'west'::text) OR (tier = 'gold'::text))
```

The `orders` scan passes an estimated 465 of 30,000 rows to the join instead of all of them, and the `customers` scan 388 of 2,000. Both extracted selectivities are far below the 0.9 threshold: 465 / 30,000 = 0.0155 and 388 / 2,000 = 0.194 (derived).

#### 3.5 Eligibility and comparison

Most transformations are not priced. The planner applies them whenever they are legal, because each one is assumed never to make the plan worse. The exceptions are listed in the last column.

| Transformation | Eligible when | Refused when | Compared by cost? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Constant folding | All arguments constant and function immutable; or strict with a NULL argument ([clauses.c#evaluate_function-rules](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4477-L4507)) | Returns a set or `record`; stable or volatile outside estimation ([clauses.c:4447-4464](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4447-L4464)) | No |
| Scalar SQL function inlining | SQL function whose body is one `SELECT expression` ([clauses.c#inline_function-simple-select](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4704-L4732)) | `SECURITY DEFINER`, `SET` clause, returns a set or `record`, body more volatile than the function ([clauses.c#inline_function-showstoppers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4587-L4598), [clauses.c#inline_function-volatility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4777-L4794)) | No |
| Set-returning SQL function inlining | SQL, `SETOF`, not strict, not volatile ([clauses.c#inline_set_returning_function-showstoppers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L5158-L5180)) | Any showstopper in that list | No |
| Subquery pull-up | `is_simple_subquery()` passes ([prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1661-L1709), [prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-end](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1772-L1784)) | Aggregates, `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`, `DISTINCT`, `ORDER BY`, security barrier, volatile outputs | No |
| Qual pushdown into a kept subquery | `subquery_is_pushdown_safe()` and `qual_is_pushdown_safe()` pass ([allpaths.c#subquery_is_pushdown_safe](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3582-L3590)) | `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`; SubPlans in the qual; leaky qual into a barrier view; unsafe output columns ([allpaths.c#qual_is_pushdown_safe](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3855-L3930)) | No |
| HAVING to WHERE | No aggregates, volatile functions or SubPlans ([planner.c#subquery_planner-having-code](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1072-L1100)) | Any of those, or grouping sets | No: a heuristic keeps SubPlans in `HAVING` |
| Outer join reduction | A strict upper qual rejects the nullable side's NULLs ([prepjointree.c#reduce_outer_joins-nullable-side](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L2910-L2913)) | The qual sits in `ON`, or is not strict | No |
| `IS [NOT] NULL` removal (17) | Simple Var, `NOT NULL` column, not nullable by an outer join ([initsplan.c#expr_is_nonnullable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2703-L2730)) | Row expressions, clone quals, non-partitioned inheritance parents ([initsplan.c#restriction_is_always_true](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2743-L2768)) | No |
| Left-join removal | Single inner relation, unique for the clause, columns unused above ([analyzejoins.c#join_is_removable-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/analyzejoins.c#L186-L240)) | Inner columns needed above; no suitable unique index | No |
| OR restriction extraction | Every arm of a join `OR` has a part that mentions only this relation, not volatile ([orclauses.c#is_safe_restriction_clause_for](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L126-L142)) | An arm has no such part; extracted selectivity above 0.9 ([orclauses.c#consider_new_or_clause-threshold](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L284-L299)) | Only the 0.9 threshold; the original `OR` is always kept |
| CTE inlining | Chapter 9 rules | Chapter 9 rules | Only through the user's `MATERIALIZED` choice |

What the transformations change is which alternatives chapters 6 to 8 can later compare. A pulled-up view lets the join search reorder its tables; a kept subquery is planned alone and joined as a unit. A dropped `IS NOT NULL` removes a filter cost; a derived `customer_id = 42` creates an index path that the original join clause could not use at scan level.

#### 3.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A stable function such as `now()` in a qual | Not folded at planning time; kept as an expression ([clauses.c#evaluate_function-volatility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4495-L4507)) | E3.1: the qual is evaluated at execution, and still usable as an index condition |
| A volatile function in a subquery's output list | Pull-up refused; quals on that column not pushed down ([prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-volatile](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1772-L1781)) | E3.9: a Subquery Scan with a Filter stays in the plan |
| A pseudoconstant qual inside a lower join domain | Evaluated at its syntactic level, not hoisted to the top ([initsplan.c#distribute_qual_to_rels-join-domain](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2302-L2313)) | The gating Result sits lower in the tree |
| A variable-free qual attached to an outer join's `ON` | Evaluated at the join, never used as a gating qual ([initsplan.c:2287-2292](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2287-L2292)) | Preserves outer-join semantics |
| A volatile variable-free qual | Evaluated at its original level, not marked pseudoconstant ([initsplan.c:2293-2298](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2293-L2298)) | It runs once per row, as written |
| A join `OR` clause with an extractable one-table part | The part is added as a restriction and the `OR` is kept at the join; the `OR`'s cached selectivity is divided by the part's ([orclauses.c#consider_new_or_clause-selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/orclauses.c#L301-L344)) | E3.13: scans filter early; the join estimate is not reduced twice. The division adjusts only the inner-join selectivity, so outer-join estimates can be off |
| A leaky equality with security level above zero | Not turned into an equivalence class ([equivclass.c#process_equivalence-leaky](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/equivclass.c#L95-L101)) | No derived clauses from it; it stays an ordinary qual |
| A qual whose collation differs from an index's | The index cannot serve it ([indxpath.c#IndexCollMatchesExprColl](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L39-L41)) | E3.12: `COLLATE "C"` against a column using the database default collation (also C here) falls back to a Seq Scan |
| An inheritance parent with an `IS NULL` qual | The parent's inh=true entry keeps the qual; the check reruns per child ([initsplan.c#add_base_clause_to_rel-inheritance](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2637-L2652), [inherit.c:909-914](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L909-L914)) | Children with different `NOT NULL` constraints stay correct |
| A view the user may not read | The planner checks view permissions early, before estimation could read the base tables' statistics ([planner.c#subquery_planner-view-acl](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L817-L847)) | An `ERROR` at planning time, not at execution |
| Nondeterministic collations | Not measurable here: the build has no ICU | A verification gap; see Open Questions |

#### 3.7 Formulas and worked examples

Terms: `relpages` and `reltuples` are the table's stored page and row counts ([reltuples and relpages](../../../glossary.md#reltuples-and-relpages)); `seq_page_cost` is 1, `cpu_tuple_cost` 0.01 and `cpu_operator_cost` 0.0025 (measured, E5.1). A function's per-row cost is `procost × cpu_operator_cost` ([plancat.c#add_function_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2133-L2134)). An SQL or PL function gets `procost = 100` unless declared otherwise ([functioncmds.c:1232-1240](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/functioncmds.c#L1232-L1240)).

Inlining changes both the cost and the row estimate of E3.2. Inputs, measured in E4.1: `orders` has `relpages = 226` and `reltuples = 30000`.

| Quantity | Inlined `amount > 900` | Not inlined `big_amount_pinned(amount)` |
|---|---|---|
| Page cost | 226 × 1 = 226 | 226 |
| Row cost | 30,000 × 0.01 = 300 | 300 |
| Qual cost per row | 1 operator × 0.0025 | 100 × 0.0025 = 0.25 |
| Qual cost total (derived) | 30,000 × 0.0025 = 75 | 30,000 × 0.25 = 7,500 |
| Scan total, derived | 601 | 8,026 |
| Scan total, estimated (E3.2) | `601.00` | `8026.00` |
| Rows, estimated (E3.2) | `2993`, from the histogram (chapter 4) | `10000` = 30,000 × 0.3333333, the default for a boolean function without a support function ([plancat.c#function_selectivity-default](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2045-L2053)) |

The fence of E3.4b is priced the same way. A Subquery Scan adds `cpu_tuple_cost` plus its filter's cost for each input row ([costsize.c#cost_subqueryscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1490-L1518)): 526 + 30,000 × (0.01 + 0.0025) = 526 + 375 = 901, the `901.00` estimated. The unfenced query costs `8.30`, because the qual reached `orders_pkey`.

#### 3.8 Planning versus execution

| Decided at planning time | Decided or evaluated at execution time |
|---|---|
| Which subqueries and views are merged, which joins are reduced or removed, which quals are dropped | Nothing is re-decided: the plan's shape is fixed |
| Immutable calls are replaced by constants (E3.1) | Stable calls such as `now()` run at execution, once per evaluation |
| A pseudoconstant qual is placed in a gating Result | The Result evaluates it once, before fetching any row, and returns nothing if it is false ([nodeResult.c#ExecResult-constant-qual](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeResult.c#L78-L91)) |
| Qual order inside each node, by security level then cost | The executor evaluates the list in that order |
| A bound parameter becomes a constant only if its caller flagged it constant ([clauses.c#eval_const_expressions_mutator-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2494-L2498)) | Otherwise the `Param` is read at execution; chapter 14 covers custom and generic plans |

#### 3.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP NOT NULL` | `notnullattnums` includes the column | The next planning reads the new `attnotnull` ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-notnull](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L165-L184)) | `IS NOT NULL` is no longer dropped; chapter 14 covers cached plans |
| `ALTER FUNCTION ... VOLATILE` or `... SET` | The function was folded or inlined | It is no longer folded or inlined | Inlined functions are recorded as plan dependencies, so cached plans are invalidated ([clauses.c:4885-4890](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4885-L4890), [clauses.c:2241-2244](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2241-L2244)) |
| `DROP` of the unique index used for join removal | The left join was removed | The join is kept | The planner reads the index list on every planning run ([analyzejoins.c#rel_supports_distinctness-unique-index](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/analyzejoins.c#L850-L862)) |
| `ALTER VIEW ... SET (security_barrier)` | The view is pulled up | The view stays a subquery | The rewriter reads the option at each rewrite ([rewriteHandler.c:1877](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L1877)) |
| `CREATE POLICY`, `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, or a different role | No policy quals | Policy quals with security levels | The rewriter adds them per statement; plans record a role dependency ([setrefs.c:3629-3631](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3629-L3631)) |

| `IS [NOT] NULL` on `NOT NULL` columns (17) | [predicate.sql#restriction-clauses](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/predicate.sql#L5-L34) |
| Join removal | [join.sql#join-removal](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/join.sql#L1980-L1995) and the cases to line 2260 |

Gaps: no test comment at the pin names plain outer-join reduction to an inner join; E3.5 demonstrates it. OR restriction extraction is covered by `join.sql` and by E3.13. Nondeterministic collations need ICU, which this build lacks, so their effect on transformations is not measured.

#### 3.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: a rewritten query, with views already turned into subqueries.
2. Transformation: `subquery_planner()` settles CTEs, turns top-level `EXISTS`/`IN` into joins, inlines SQL functions and flattens simple subqueries and views.
3. Transformation: every expression is folded, canonicalized and stripped of sublinks; `HAVING` quals move down; outer joins weaken where strict quals allow.
4. Interaction: `deconstruct_jointree()` files each qual at its lowest home, drops or falsifies `IS [NOT] NULL` on `NOT NULL` columns, and routes equalities into equivalence classes.
5. Observed result: derived constants add restrictions and useless left joins vanish, so the plan shows fewer joins and more pushed-down conditions than the SQL suggests.
6. Refresh: a changed `NOT NULL` flag, function volatility, index or policy changes the outcome at the next planning run.

### Chapter 4. Estimate rows and widths

#### 4.1 Main idea

Every cost in the next chapter is a price per page or per row, so the planner must first guess how many rows each step produces and how wide they are. It does not scan the table while planning; the one exception, an index probe for a column's current minimum or maximum, comes in step 4. It multiplies a table's estimated row count by the selectivity of each condition, the fraction of rows expected to pass, and it takes those fractions from compact per-column summaries that `ANALYZE` stored earlier ([costsize.c#set_baserel_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5256-L5275)).

Three facts surprise most readers. The table's row count is not the stored `reltuples`; it is the stored rows-per-page density times the table's current file size ([tableam.c:711-747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L711-L747)). Conditions on different columns are multiplied as if independent, unless an extended statistics object says otherwise ([clausesel.c#clauselist_selectivity-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L66-L71)). And when a summary is missing, fixed default fractions such as 0.005 and 1/3 stand in for it ([selfuncs.h:33-56](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/selfuncs.h#L33-L56)). The experiments are E4.1 to E4.15 in [the measurement script](#measurement-script); E16.5 shows how one wrong estimate spreads through a join.

#### 4.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pg_class.relpages`, `reltuples` (reltuples and relpages) | page count and live-row count when last measured | written in place by `VACUUM`, `ANALYZE` and `CREATE INDEX` ([analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-relstats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L630-L646), [index.c#index_update_stats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2797-L2803)) | stored; `reltuples = -1` means never measured | the density `reltuples / relpages` ([tableam.c:712-713](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L712-L713)) |
| current file size in pages | how many pages the table has now | `RelationGetNumberOfBlocks()` at planning time ([tableam.c#table_block_relation_estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L654-L667)) | current state | multiplied by the density to give the row count ([tableam.c:747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L747)) |
| `RelOptInfo.pages`, `tuples`, `allvisfrac` (RelOptInfo) | the planner's size estimate for one relation | `get_relation_info()` calls `estimate_rel_size()` ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L196-L203)) | estimate, mixing the current file size with stored density | row estimates and every scan cost |
| `pg_statistic` row per column (statistics) | `stanullfrac`, `stawidth`, `stadistinct`, [most-common values and histogram](../../../glossary.md#most-common-values-and-histogram), [correlation](../../../glossary.md#correlation) | computed by `ANALYZE` from a sample of rows ([analyze.c#acquire_sample_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1128-L1156)) | stored; exact only when the sample covers the table | the selectivity functions below; `correlation` only by index cost estimation, chapter 5 ([selfuncs.c#btcostestimate-correlation](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7182-L7198)) |
| extended statistics data ([extended statistics](../../../glossary.md#extended-statistics)) | ndistinct, functional dependencies and multi-column MCV lists for a set of columns | `CREATE STATISTICS`, filled by the next `ANALYZE` | stored | `clauselist_selectivity()` and `estimate_num_groups()` ([extended_stats.c#statext_clauselist_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/statistics/extended_stats.c#L1994-L2030)) |
| statistics target (`default_statistics_target`, per-column `SET STATISTICS`) | how many MCV entries and histogram buckets to keep | setting and column option | parameter | sample size `300 x target` ([analyze.c#std_typanalyze-minrows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1872-L1894)) |
| default selectivities | fixed guesses when no statistics apply | `DEFAULT_EQ_SEL` 0.005, `DEFAULT_INEQ_SEL` 1/3, `DEFAULT_NUM_DISTINCT` 200 and others ([selfuncs.h:33-56](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/selfuncs.h#L33-L56)) | parameter compiled into the server | restriction and join estimates |
| `RelOptInfo.rows` | rows expected after the relation's own conditions | `tuples x clauselist_selectivity()`, clamped ([costsize.c#set_baserel_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5256-L5275)) | estimate | scan costs, join sizes, and every node above |
| width | average bytes per output row | sum of column `stawidth` values, or a per-type guess ([costsize.c#set_rel_width-columns](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6169-L6188)) | estimate from stored statistics | memory and spill decisions for sorts and hashes (chapter 5) |
| `pg_proc.prorows`, support function | rows a set-returning function returns | the catalog, or a planner support function ([plancat.c#get_function_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2155-L2198)) | stored parameter, or computed from the call | function scan sizes |

Two similar pairs are easy to confuse. `relpages` is a stored page count, while `RelOptInfo.pages` is the file's size now, raised to 10 pages for a never-measured table (step 2). And `pg_statistic` holds stored summaries of a sample, while the row counts in `EXPLAIN` are estimates computed from them at planning time.

#### 4.3 Logic map

```text
ANALYZE, an earlier and separate command                                   [A]
  sample up to 300 x statistics-target rows
  -> pg_statistic: null fraction, width, n_distinct, MCV list, histogram, correlation
  -> pg_class: relpages, reltuples (written in place)
        |
Planning one base relation                                                  [B]
  pages  = current file size (at least 10 if never measured)
  density = reltuples / relpages          if reltuples >= 0 and relpages > 0
          = usable page bytes x fillfactor / estimated row width   otherwise
  tuples = density x pages
        |
rows = tuples x clauselist_selectivity(relation's conditions)                  [C]
  one condition           -> clause_selectivity
  several, one relation,
  extended statistics     -> multi-column MCV list first, then dependencies    [D]
  the rest                -> multiply, except "x > a AND x < b": hisel + losel - 1
        |
  each condition, by kind                                                   [E]
    column = constant   -> eqsel: MCV frequency if the constant is an MCV,
                           else (1 - MCV total - null fraction) / (other distinct values)
    column < constant   -> scalarltsel: MCV part + histogram part (interpolated)
    column IS NULL      -> null fraction
    LIKE 'prefix%'      -> pattern tested against histogram entries
    boolean function    -> support function, else 0.3333333
    no usable statistics-> default constant
  rows = clamp_row_est(tuples x selectivity): rounded, at least 1              [F]
        |
width = sum of column average widths                                         [G]
        |
join:  rows = outer x inner x FK selectivity x join-clause selectivity         [H]
       (semi, anti and outer joins adjust this; eqjoinsel matches MCV lists)
grouping: groups = product of n_distinct per relation, clamped,                [I]
          or the extended ndistinct value when one covers the columns
```

- [A] [analyze.c#std_typanalyze-minrows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1872-L1894), [analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-targrows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L484-L513), [analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-relstats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L630-L646)
- [B] [plancat.c#get_relation_info-size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L196-L203), [tableam.c#table_block_relation_estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L654-L667), [tableam.c:712-747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L712-L747)
- [C] [costsize.c#set_baserel_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5256-L5275), [clausesel.c#clauselist_selectivity_ext](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L117-L156)
- [D] [extended_stats.c#statext_clauselist_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/statistics/extended_stats.c#L1994-L2030), [clausesel.c#range-pairs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L269-L293)
- [E] [selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-mcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L398-L437), [selfuncs.c#scalarineqsel-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L695-L716), [selfuncs.c#nulltestsel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1708-L1738), [like_support.c#patternsel_common-histogram](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/like_support.c#L678-L716), [plancat.c#function_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2044-L2053)

- [H] [costsize.c#calc_joinrel_size_estimate-switch](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5504-L5539), [selfuncs.c#eqjoinsel_inner-mcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L2461-L2475), [selfuncs.c#eqjoinsel_inner-total](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L2576-L2603), [selfuncs.c#eqjoinsel_inner-nomcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L2606-L2634)
