#### 4.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: ANALYZE summarizes a sample

Input: a table and its statistics targets. `std_typanalyze()` asks for `300 x attstattarget` sample rows per column, a size chosen from a histogram-error bound in the source comment ([analyze.c#std_typanalyze-minrows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1872-L1894)). The table's sample size is the largest such request across its columns, index expressions and statistics objects ([analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-targrows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L484-L513)).

Decision: `acquire_sample_rows()` picks random blocks and then random rows from them. When the table is smaller than the sample, it reads every row ([analyze.c#acquire_sample_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1128-L1156)). The running schema relies on this: every table's sample covers the whole table, so the stored statistics are exact and repeat on every run.

Calculation: `compute_scalar_stats()` sorts the sample and derives the summaries. The MCV list keeps the values with the highest counts; a value with the same count as the last kept one does not displace it, so ties keep the values that sort first ([analyze.c#compute_scalar_stats-mcv-track](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2503-L2528)). The number of distinct values uses the Haas and Stokes estimator, and a count above 10 % of the table is stored as a negative fraction so that it scales with the table ([analyze.c#compute_scalar_stats-ndistinct](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2562-L2612)).

The histogram takes evenly spaced values from the sorted non-MCV values, so each bucket holds about the same number of rows ([analyze.c#compute_scalar_stats-histogram](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2694-L2700), [analyze.c#compute_scalar_stats-histogram-spacing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2764-L2789)). Correlation compares each value's sorted position with its physical position ([analyze.c#compute_scalar_stats-correlation](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2825-L2842)). A column's `n_distinct` option overrides the computed value ([analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-n_distinct](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L563-L574)).

Output: `pg_statistic` rows, and `relpages`, `reltuples` and `relallvisible` written into [pg_class](../../../glossary.md#pg_class) ([analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-relstats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L630-L646)). Consequence: the planner now reads summaries of the table as it was when `ANALYZE` ran.

##### Step 2: the planner sizes the table from the file

Input: the relation being planned. `get_relation_info()` calls `estimate_rel_size()`, which hands a heap to the table access method ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L196-L203), [plancat.c#estimate_rel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1065-L1078)).

Decision and calculation: `table_block_relation_estimate_size()` reads the current file size. If `reltuples` and `relpages` hold a measurement, density is `reltuples / relpages`. Otherwise it divides the usable page bytes, scaled by the table's fillfactor, by an estimated row width, with integer division. Either way, tuples are density times current pages, rounded ([tableam.c:712-747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L712-L747)). For a heap, the usable bytes are `BLCKSZ` minus the page header and the per-row overhead is the aligned tuple header plus one line pointer ([heapam_handler.c:2099-2102](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/heapam_handler.c#L2099-L2102)).

A table that was never measured, has fewer than 10 pages and has no inheritance children is treated as 10 pages, so a plan cached while it is small does not assume it stays tiny ([tableam.c:674-699](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L674-L699)). `allvisfrac` is `relallvisible / current pages`, not scaled up ([tableam.c:749-760](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L749-L760)).

Output: `pages`, `tuples` and `allvisfrac` on the `RelOptInfo`. Consequence: rows added since the last `ANALYZE` are counted, because the file grew, but only at the old density (E4.11).

##### Step 3: find statistics for each expression

Input: one side of a condition, for example `orders.status`. `examine_variable()` looks up the column's `pg_statistic` row through the [syscache](../../../glossary.md#syscache), unless `get_relation_stats_hook` supplies one ([selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5367-L5396)). For an expression such as `amount * 2`, it looks for an [expression index](../../../glossary.md#expression-index) or an extended statistics object on the same expression, because `ANALYZE` stores statistics for those too ([selfuncs.c#examine_variable-expression-stats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5134-L5160), [selfuncs.c#examine_variable-extended-expression](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5270-L5280)).

Decision: the statistics are data, so they are guarded. If the user may not read every row of the column, because of privileges, a security barrier view or row-level security, only a leakproof operator may see them ([selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable-acl](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5398-L5419), [selfuncs.c#statistic_proc_security_check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5818-L5833)). Otherwise the estimator falls back to its defaults.

##### Step 4: estimate each condition

Input: one qual. `clause_selectivity_ext()` dispatches on its node type. An operator clause calls the operator's restriction estimator from `pg_operator.oprrest` (E15.2 lists several); a `NullTest` calls `nulltestsel()`; a boolean function asks its planner support function or uses 0.3333333 ([clausesel.c#clause_selectivity_ext-opclause](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L831-L862), [clausesel.c#clause_selectivity_ext-nulltest](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L898-L917), [plancat.c#function_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2044-L2053)).

Equality with a constant, `eqsel()` and `var_eq_const()`: a unique index makes it `1/tuples`. Otherwise an MCV match returns that value's stored frequency. A non-MCV constant gets the remaining non-null fraction divided by the number of other distinct values, and never more than the rarest MCV ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-unique](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L331-L334), [selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-mcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L398-L437)). With no statistics it returns `1 / n_distinct`, which is `1/200` for a large table with nothing known ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-nostats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L441-L449), [selfuncs.c#get_variable_numdistinct-defaults](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5930-L5966)).

Comparison with a constant, `scalarineqsel()`: it adds the frequencies of MCVs that satisfy the condition, then applies the histogram fraction to the remaining non-null, non-MCV rows ([selfuncs.c#scalarineqsel-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L673-L716)). `ineq_histogram_selectivity()` finds the bucket by binary search and interpolates linearly inside it ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-bucket](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1169-L1172), [selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-interpolate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1220-L1273)).

When that search touches the first or last histogram entry, the planner asks a plain [B-tree](../../../glossary.md#b-tree) index on the column for the current minimum or maximum, the endpoint probe ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-endpoints](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1086-L1136), [selfuncs.c#get_actual_variable_range-index-choice](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6170-L6239)). Without such a value, it keeps the fraction at least `0.01 / (number of buckets)` away from 0 and from 1 ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-clamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1325-L1343)).

`LIKE` with at least 100 histogram entries tests the pattern against the histogram entries directly, skipping the first and last. With 10 to 99 entries it blends that count with a prefix heuristic, and with fewer it uses the heuristic alone. The result is kept between 0.0001 and 0.9999 ([like_support.c#patternsel_common-histogram](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/like_support.c#L678-L716), [selfuncs.c#histogram_selectivity-count](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L866-L882)). The frequencies of matching MCVs are then added ([like_support.c#patternsel_common-mcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/like_support.c#L718-L734)). Output: one selectivity per condition.

##### Step 5: combine the conditions and clamp

Input: the list of selectivities. If the conditions all refer to one table that has extended statistics, `statext_clauselist_selectivity()` first estimates as many as it can with a multi-column MCV list, and then with functional dependencies ([clausesel.c#clauselist_selectivity_ext](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L141-L156), [extended_stats.c#statext_clauselist_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/statistics/extended_stats.c#L1994-L2030)).

The rest are multiplied, which assumes independence. A lower and an upper bound on the same column form a range instead, estimated as `hisel + losel - 1` plus the null fraction, or `DEFAULT_RANGE_INEQ_SEL` if either side was a default ([clausesel.c#range-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L73-L91), [clausesel.c#range-pairs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L269-L293)).

Calculation and output: `rows = clamp_row_est(tuples x selectivity)`. `clamp_row_est()` rounds to an integer, raises anything at or below one row to 1, and replaces NaN and absurd values with `1e100` ([costsize.c#clamp_row_est](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L202-L218), [costsize.c:117](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L117)). Consequence: a plan never shows `rows=0` for an ordinary relation, even when the estimate is far below one (E5.6).

##### Step 6: estimate the width

`set_rel_width()` adds up the average width of each output column: the column's `stawidth` from `pg_statistic` through `get_attavgwidth()` when present, otherwise a guess from its type through `get_typavgwidth()` ([costsize.c#set_rel_width-columns](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6169-L6188)). Consequence: the width feeds the byte estimates of sorts, hashes and materializations, which decide whether they fit in [work_mem](../../../glossary.md#work_mem) (chapter 5).

##### Step 7: estimate join sizes

Input: two relations' row estimates and the join's conditions. `calc_joinrel_size_estimate()` first lets `get_foreign_key_join_selectivity()` take any conditions that match a foreign key; for inner and outer joins each such key contributes `1 / (referenced table's rows)` ([costsize.c#calc_joinrel_size_estimate-fk](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5423-L5442), [costsize.c#get_foreign_key_join_selectivity-rule](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5744-L5752)). For a semi-join or anti-join whose inner side is the referenced table, the key contributes that table's `rows / tuples` instead ([costsize.c#get_foreign_key_join_selectivity-semi](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5723-L5740)).

The remaining conditions go through `clauselist_selectivity()`, which calls each operator's join estimator from `pg_operator.oprjoin` (E15.2 lists several), or uses 0.5 when an operator has none ([clausesel.c#clause_selectivity_ext-opclause](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L831-L862), [plancat.c#join_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1991-L2019)). For `=`, `eqjoinsel()` matches the two MCV lists value by value when both exist; without them it uses `1 / max(n_distinct1, n_distinct2)` times the non-null fractions ([selfuncs.c#eqjoinsel_inner-mcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L2461-L2475), [selfuncs.c#eqjoinsel_inner-total](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L2576-L2603), [selfuncs.c#eqjoinsel_inner-nomcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L2606-L2634)). The join type then decides the formula, including the outer-join, semi-join and anti-join variants shown in [4.7](#47-formulas-and-worked-examples) ([costsize.c#calc_joinrel_size_estimate-switch](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5504-L5539)).

##### Step 8: estimate the number of groups

`estimate_num_groups()` multiplies the distinct counts of the grouped columns of each relation. An extended ndistinct statistic replaces the product when it covers the columns ([selfuncs.c#estimate_num_groups-per-rel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L3644-L3677)). With more than one column, the product is clamped to a tenth of the relation's rows, but never below the largest single count ([selfuncs.c#estimate_num_groups-clamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L3685-L3707)). If the relation's own conditions keep only part of it, a formula for drawing rows at random scales the count down ([selfuncs.c#estimate_num_groups-restriction](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L3709-L3754)). The result is capped at the input rows ([selfuncs.c#estimate_num_groups-final](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L3766-L3777)).

##### Step 9: size non-table relations

A function in `FROM` returns `prorows` rows unless its support function answers a `SupportRequestRows` ([plancat.c#get_function_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2155-L2198), [clauses.c#expression_returns_set_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L286-L308)). `CREATE FUNCTION` sets `prorows` to 1000 for a set-returning function unless `ROWS` says otherwise ([functioncmds.c#CreateFunction-defaults](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/functioncmds.c#L1241-L1247)). Subqueries, CTEs, `VALUES` lists and tuplestores have their own size functions, covered in chapters 6 and 9.

#### 4.5 Eligibility and comparison

For estimation, "eligibility" means which estimator is allowed to answer. The planner does not compare estimates against each other; it uses the first source that applies, in this order.

| Question asked | Source that answers, if eligible | Eligibility condition | Fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| Several conditions on one table | extended MCV list, then dependencies | a statistics object covers at least two of the conditions' columns or expressions ([extended_stats.c#statext_clauselist_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/statistics/extended_stats.c#L1994-L2030), [extended_stats.c#choose_best_statistics](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/statistics/extended_stats.c#L1219-L1293)) | per-condition product |
| `column = constant` | MCV frequency | the constant equals a stored MCV ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-mcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L398-L405)) | remaining fraction / other distinct values |
| `column < constant` | histogram | a histogram sorted by a compatible operator and the same collation ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1066-L1074)) | half of the non-MCV rows ([selfuncs.c#scalarineqsel-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L700-L713)) |
| any statistic at all | `pg_statistic` | a row exists and the security check passes ([selfuncs.c#statistic_proc_security_check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5818-L5833)) | default constants |
| join size | foreign key | the query's equality conditions match every column of a foreign key, and this join holds all of them ([initsplan.c#match_foreign_keys_to_quals-full](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L3344-L3351), [costsize.c#get_foreign_key_join_selectivity-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5689-L5697)) | the operators' join estimators, such as `eqjoinsel` |

Estimates do enter comparisons indirectly. Every path of one relation shares that relation's `rows`, so the choice between a sequential scan and an index scan never depends on different row guesses for the same table ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L299-L303)). The exception is a [parameterized path](../../../glossary.md#parameterized-path), whose extra join conditions give it its own smaller row count ([costsize.c#get_parameterized_baserel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5286-L5310)).

#### 4.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Table never analyzed (`reltuples = -1`) | density from type widths; no MCV or histogram; `=` uses 1/200 and `<` uses 1/3 ([tableam.c:714-745](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L714-L745), [selfuncs.c#scalarineqsel-nostats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L669-L671)) | E4.10: 14,464 rows estimated for 10,000; `y = 3` estimated 72 for 1,000 |
| Rows added since `ANALYZE` | counted through the file size at the old density ([tableam.c:711-747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L711-L747)); the histogram does not know the new values | E4.11: `x > 10000` estimated 2 rows for 10,000 |
| New maximum and a plain B-tree on the column | the endpoint probe reads the live maximum ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-endpoints](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1086-L1136)) | E4.11c: the same condition estimated 198 after the index existed |
| Condition on an expression with no statistics | defaults: `<` and `>` 1/3, `=` via `DEFAULT_NUM_DISTINCT` ([selfuncs.c#scalarineqsel-nostats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L669-L671), [selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-nostats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L441-L449)) | E4.14: 10,000 and 10 rows; an expression index gives the expression its own statistics |
| Dependent columns | independent product ([clausesel.c#clauselist_selectivity-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L66-L71)) | E4.6: 10 estimated for 98 until `CREATE STATISTICS` |
| No read access to all rows and a non-leakproof operator | statistics withheld ([selfuncs.c#statistic_proc_security_check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5818-L5833)) | default estimates for that condition |
| Constant is `NULL` | selectivity 0 for a strict operator ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-null](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L306-L310)) | clamped to one row |
| Unique index on the column | `1 / tuples` for equality ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_const-unique](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L331-L334)) | one-row estimates |
| Boolean function without a support function | 0.3333333 ([plancat.c#function_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2044-L2053)) | E5.5: 1,006 rows from 3,019 |
| Histogram fraction within 0.01 of a bucket from 0 or 1, no endpoint value | clamped to `0.01 / buckets` or `1 - 0.01 / buckets` ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-clamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1325-L1343)) | E4.11: 0.0001 of the table |
| `IS NULL` without statistics | `DEFAULT_UNK_SEL` 0.005 ([selfuncs.c#nulltestsel-defaults](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1748-L1760)) | small constant guess |
| Foreign key columns contain NULLs | not derated ([costsize.c#get_foreign_key_join_selectivity-nulls](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5704-L5711)) | join estimate can be too high |
| Parameter instead of a constant (generic plans, parameterized scans) | `var_eq_non_const()`: non-null fraction / n_distinct ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_non_const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L500-L527)) | E5.9 inner scan: an estimated 15 rows per customer (30000 / 2000), an average over skewed data |

#### 4.7 Formulas and worked examples

Terms: `N` is the relation's estimated tuples; `nullfrac`, `n_distinct`, MCV values and frequencies and histogram bounds come from `pg_stats` (E4.1); `sumcommon` is the total frequency of the MCV list; `s` is a selectivity. Estimated values below come from plain `EXPLAIN`, measured values from `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` actual rows or catalog queries, and derived values from arithmetic shown here.

The stored inputs, measured in E4.1:

```text
  relname  | relpages | reltuples | relallvisible
 orders    |      226 |     30000 |           226
...
   attname   | null_frac | avg_width | n_distinct  | correlation  | n_mcv | n_hist
 amount      |         0 |         6 | -0.86506665 | -0.003046035 |   100 |    101
 customer_id |         0 |         4 |        2000 |  0.014051536 |   100 |    101
 id          |         0 |         4 |          -1 |            1 |       |    101
 note        |    0.9504 |        10 |           1 |            1 |     1 |
 ordered_at  |         0 |         8 |          -1 |            1 |       |    101
 status      |         0 |         8 |           3 |    0.7369488 |     3 |
...
 status  | {shipped,pending,cancelled} | {0.8490667,0.10063333,0.0503}
```

The inputs of the two `customer_id` estimates, measured in E4.4b:

```text
  freq_of_7  | least_mcv_freq | n_mcv | mcv_total_freq | n_distinct | null_frac
 0.015266667 |  0.00056666665 |   100 |     0.34976697 |       2000 |         0
```

| Condition (experiment) | Formula | Derived | Estimated by the planner | Measured actual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status = 'pending'` (E4.2) | `N x freq(pending)` | 30000 x 0.10063333 = 3018.99, rounded to 3019 | 3019 | 3019 |
| `customer_id = 7`, an MCV (E4.4, E4.4b) | `N x freq(7)` | 30000 x 0.015266667 = 458.00001, rounded to 458 | 458 | 458 |
| `customer_id = 500`, not an MCV (E4.4, E4.4b) | `N x (1 - sumcommon - nullfrac) / (n_distinct - n_mcv)`, capped at the rarest MCV | 30000 x (1 - 0.34976697 - 0) / (2000 - 100) = 10.2668, rounded to 10; the selectivity 0.000342 is below the cap 0.00056666665 | 10 | 12 |
| `note IS NOT NULL` (E4.5) | `N x (1 - nullfrac)` | 30000 x 0.0496 = 1488 | 1488 | 1488 |
| `amount < 250` (E4.3, E4.1b, E4.1c) | `N x ((1 - nullfrac - sumcommon) x histfrac + mcv_part)` | 30000 x (0.989166678 x 0.2453876 + 0.0087999925) = 7545.9, rounded to 7546; steps below | 7546 | 7542 |

Rounding is `clamp_row_est()`'s `rint()`, round half to even, on the unrounded product ([costsize.c#clamp_row_est](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L202-L218)).

The `amount < 250` estimate combines the MCV list and the histogram. Its inputs, measured in E4.1b and E4.1c:

```text
 bucket_lower_index | lower_bound | upper_bound | n_bounds
                 25 |      244.59 |      254.56 |      101
...
 n_mcv | mcv_total_freq | mcv_freq_below_250
   100 |    0.010833322 |       0.0087999925
```

1. MCV part: `mcv_selectivity()` adds the frequencies of the MCVs below 250, 0.0087999925 ([selfuncs.c#scalarineqsel-mcv](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L677-L686)).
2. Non-MCV fraction: `1 - nullfrac - sumcommon` = 1 - 0 - 0.010833322 = 0.989166678 ([selfuncs.c#scalarineqsel-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L695-L716)).
3. Histogram position: 250 lies in bucket 25 of 100, between 244.59 and 254.56. Linear interpolation gives `binfrac` = 5.41 / 9.97 = 0.542628, so `histfrac` = (24 + 0.542628) / 100 = 0.2454263 ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-interpolate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1220-L1273)).
4. Strict inequality: for `<` the planner subtracts the estimated share of rows equal to 250, `1 / (n_distinct - n_mcv)`. Here n_distinct = 0.86506665 x 30000 = 25952 after rounding, so the share is 1 / 25852 = 0.0000387 and `histfrac` becomes 0.2453876 ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-eqsel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1195-L1216), [selfuncs.c:1315-1316](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1315-L1316), [selfuncs.c#get_variable_numdistinct-defaults](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5951-L5955)).
5. Combine: 0.989166678 x 0.2453876 + 0.0087999925 = 0.2515292, and 30000 x 0.2515292 = 7545.9, rounded to 7546. Without step 4 the product is 7547.0, so the equality correction decides the last digit.

The MCV list is lopsided. It covers only about 325 rows (0.010833322 x 30000), but 81 % of its frequency lies below 250, although `amount` is uniform. That follows from the tie rule in `compute_scalar_stats()`. A candidate enters a full MCV list only with a count strictly greater than the smallest tracked count, and an equal count is placed after the tracked ones. So among values with equal counts, those that sort first stay ([analyze.c#compute_scalar_stats-mcv-track](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L2503-L2528)).

Missing and stale statistics, E4.10 and E4.11 (`fresh` holds two `int` columns):

| Step | Inputs (measured) | Formula | Derived | Estimated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| never analyzed | `relpages 0`, `reltuples -1`; the file had 64 pages (the later `ANALYZE` recorded `relpages 64`) | density = (8192 - 24) / (4 + 4 + 24 + 4) = 8168 / 36 = 226, integer division; rows = 226 x 64 | 14464 | 14464 |
| `y = 3`, no statistics | `1 / DEFAULT_NUM_DISTINCT` | 14464 / 200 = 72.3 | 72 | 72 (actual 1000) |
| `x < 100`, no statistics | `DEFAULT_INEQ_SEL` | 14464 x 0.3333 = 4821.3 | 4821 | 4821 (actual 99) |
| after `ANALYZE`, then 10,000 more rows | `relpages 64`, `reltuples 10000`, current pages 108 | density = 10000 / 64 = 156.25; rows = 156.25 x 108 | 16875 | 16875 (actual 20000) |
| `x > 10000`, no index | the histogram still ends at 10000 (E4.11b); `x` is unique, so there is no MCV part | the search passes the last bound, so the fraction is 0; with no index to supply a live maximum it is raised to 0.01 / 100; 16875 x 0.0001 = 1.6875 | 2 | 2 (actual 10000) |
| same, after `CREATE INDEX fresh_x_idx` | `relpages 108`, `reltuples 20000` (E4.11c); bounds 9900 and 10000 (E4.11b) | tuples = 20000 / 108 x 108 = 20000; the probe replaces the last bound 10000 by the live 20000, so 10000 falls in the last bucket: `binfrac` = 100 / 10100 = 0.0099010, `histfrac` = (99 + 0.0099010) / 100 = 0.9900990; `>` takes 1 - 0.9900990 = 0.0099010; 20000 x 0.0099010 = 198.02 | 198 | 198 (actual 10000) |

The width model's 226 rows per page is not the problem: the later `INSERT` stored 10,000 rows in 44 new pages, about 227 per page (E4.11). The overestimate comes from the file size, because 10,000 rows at 226 per page need 45 pages, but the file had 64. `CREATE TABLE AS` inserts through a bulk-insert state, and with one each file extension adds as many pages as all earlier ones together, up to 64: 1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 pages ([createas.c#intorel_startup-bistate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/createas.c#L554-L561), [hio.c#RelationAddBlocks-sizing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/hio.c#L300-L307), [hio.c#RelationAddBlocks-remember](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/hio.c#L409-L429)). This explanation is derived, not measured ([Open Questions](#open-questions)).

E4.11b and E4.11c print the inputs of the last two rows. The histogram was built before the `INSERT`, so it still ends at 10000, and its last three bounds are 9800, 9900 and 10000. `CREATE INDEX` then rewrote the table's `relpages` and `reltuples` from the build. So the planner's table estimate rose from 16,875 to 20,000 rows (derived: 20000 / 108 x 108) without an `ANALYZE` ([index.c#index_update_stats-read](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2851-L2856), [index.c#index_update_stats-apply](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2912-L2929)). With a live endpoint the small-fraction clamp no longer applies, only the ordinary 0 to 1 bound ([selfuncs.c#ineq_histogram_selectivity-clamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L1325-L1343)).

Measured, E4.11b and E4.11c:

```text
 n_bounds |    last_bounds
      101 | {9800,9900,10000}
...
 relpages | reltuples
      108 |     20000
```

Estimated by the planner (`rows=`) and measured (`actual rows=`), E4.11 and E4.11c:

```text
 Seq Scan on fresh  (cost=0.00..318.94 rows=2 width=8) (actual rows=10000 loops=1)
   Filter: (x > 10000)
...
 Index Scan using fresh_x_idx on fresh  (cost=0.29..12.75 rows=198 width=8) (actual rows=10000 loops=1)
   Index Cond: (x > 10000)
```

Two dependent columns, E4.6. Region `west` is 10 % of customers and country `PT` is 4.9 % (measured in E4.1), and every `PT` customer is in `west`, because the schema draws `PT` only for `west`.

Estimated and measured, E4.6: the filter and the grouping, then the statistics object after `CREATE STATISTICS customers_geo (dependencies, ndistinct, mcv)` and `ANALYZE`, then the filter and the grouping again:

```text
 Seq Scan on customers  (cost=0.00..52.00 rows=10 width=56) (actual rows=98 loops=1)
...
 HashAggregate  (cost=57.00..57.32 rows=32 width=16) (actual rows=8 loops=1)
...
 customers_geo   | {"3, 4": 8} | {"4 => 3": 1.000000}
...
 Seq Scan on customers  (cost=0.00..52.00 rows=98 width=56) (actual rows=98 loops=1)
...
 HashAggregate  (cost=57.00..57.08 rows=8 width=16) (actual rows=8 loops=1)
```

Derived: independence gives 2000 x 0.1 x 0.049 = 9.8, rounded to 10. The groups estimate multiplies 4 regions by 8 countries, 32, which is under the clamp of 2000 / 10 = 200. After `ANALYZE`, the object records that column 4 (`country`) determines column 3 (`region`) with degree 1.0, and that the pair has 8 distinct combinations. Both estimates become exact.

Joins, E4.7 and E4.8b, use the `calc_joinrel_size_estimate()` formulas:

| Join type | Formula for rows |
|---|---|
| inner | `outer x inner x fkselec x jselec` |
| left | `max(outer x inner x fkselec x jselec, outer) x pselec` |
| full | `max(that product, outer, inner) x pselec` |
| semi | `outer x fkselec x jselec` |
| anti | `outer x (1 - fkselec x jselec) x pselec` |

Here `fkselec` is the foreign-key selectivity and `jselec` the selectivity of the join's own conditions. `pselec` is that of pushed-down conditions, such as `WHERE` conditions evaluated at an outer join, which apply after it; an inner join counts all its conditions in `jselec` ([costsize.c#calc_joinrel_size_estimate-pselec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5444-L5490), [costsize.c#calc_joinrel_size_estimate-switch](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5504-L5539)).

| Join (experiment) | Derived | Estimated | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orders JOIN customers` on the foreign key (E4.7) | 30000 x 2000 x (1/2000) | 30000 | 30000 |
| same, with `c.region = 'west'` (E4.7) | 30000 x 200 x (1/2000): the key uses the table's raw row count | 3000 | 2923 |
| `items JOIN products`, no foreign key; `products.id` unique, so no MCV list; `items.product_id` holds all 500 ids (E4.8) | 90000 x 500 x 1/max(500, 500) | 90000 | 90000 |
| `items a JOIN items b ON b.product_id = a.product_id`, skewed, both MCV lists (E4.8b, forced serial) | MCV-to-MCV matching, not reproduced here | 209172402 | 209193990 |

Other estimates:

| Case (experiment) | Derived | Estimated | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GROUP BY customer_id` (E4.9) | `n_distinct` = 2000 | 2000 | 2000 |
| `generate_series(1, 250)` (E4.12) | the support function computes `floor((finish - start + step) / step)` = floor((250 - 1 + 1) / 1) = 250 ([int.c#generate_series_int4_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/int.c#L1655-L1672)) | 250 | not run |
| `unnest(ARRAY[1,2,3,4])` (E4.12) | the support function reads the array length, 4 ([arrayfuncs.c#array_unnest_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/arrayfuncs.c#L6356-L6366)) | 4 | not run |
| PL/pgSQL set-returning function, default and `ROWS 50` (E4.12) | no support function, so `prorows` ([plancat.c#get_function_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2155-L2198)) | 1000 and 50 | not run |
| `name LIKE 'customer 01%'` (E4.13, E4.13b) | the 101 bounds fall every 20 names; of the 99 tested (first and last skipped), bounds 6 to 10, `customer 0100` to `customer 0180`, match: 2000 x 5 / 99 = 101.01 | 101 | 100 |
| `amount * 2 > 1000`, then with an expression index and `ANALYZE` (E4.14) | 30000 x 1/3; then the expression's own histogram | 10000, then 14923 | 14919 |

The `LIKE` row uses the histogram entries themselves, because the column has at least 100 of them; `name` is unique, so there is no MCV part ([like_support.c#patternsel_common-histogram](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/like_support.c#L678-L716), [selfuncs.c#histogram_selectivity-count](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L866-L882)). The bounds around the prefix, measured in E4.13b:

#### 4.8 Planning versus execution

The planner copies each path's row estimate into the plan node's `plan_rows` ([createplan.c#copy_generic_path_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L5410-L5418)). `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` prints that estimate beside the executor's count, which is the rows counted per loop, `ntuples / nloops` ([explain.c#ExplainNode-rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1807-L1858)). The count stays in the executor's instrumentation, which the planner does not read. Only `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM` and index builds change the stored inputs (section 4.9).

The executor does adapt around a wrong estimate in local ways, because it decides from the rows that actually arrive. A sort switches to disk when its tuples no longer fit in memory ([tuplesort.c#tuplesort_puttuple_common-spill](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/sort/tuplesort.c#L1276-L1293)). A hash join doubles its batches when its table outgrows the memory limit ([nodeHash.c#ExecHashTableInsert-grow](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeHash.c#L1691-L1698)). A hash aggregate enters spill mode at its limit ([nodeAgg.c#hash_agg_check_limits](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L1856-L1874)). E5.3 and E5.4b in chapter 5 show the sort and the aggregate spilling under a small `work_mem`.

The plan shape, however, stays fixed. E16.5 shows the consequence: the independence error of E4.6 makes the planner expect 10 customers instead of 98, so it expects 150 joined rows instead of 1,008 and picks a nested loop. The inner scan's `actual rows=10` is the average over its 98 loops.

Estimated by the planner (`rows=`) and measured (`actual rows=`), E16.5:

```text
 Nested Loop  (cost=4.00..492.46 rows=150 width=20) (actual rows=1008 loops=1)
   ->  Seq Scan on customers c  (cost=0.00..52.00 rows=10 width=18) (actual rows=98 loops=1)
         Filter: ((region = 'west'::text) AND (country = 'PT'::text))
   ->  Bitmap Heap Scan on orders o  (cost=4.00..43.90 rows=15 width=10) (actual rows=10 loops=98)
```

#### 4.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ANALYZE` (or [autovacuum](../../../glossary.md#autovacuum)'s analyze, once changed rows exceed `autovacuum_analyze_threshold + scale_factor x reltuples`) | old or no `pg_statistic` rows | new summaries from a fresh sample; `relpages`, `reltuples`, `relallvisible` rewritten in place ([analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-relstats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L630-L646), [autovacuum.c#relation_needs_vacanalyze-analyze](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/postmaster/autovacuum.c#L3076-L3095)) | every later plan uses the new summaries; chapter 14 covers cached plans |
| [VACUUM](../../../glossary.md#vacuum) | old `relpages`, `reltuples`, `relallvisible` | updated in place by `vac_update_relstats()`; column statistics only when `ANALYZE` runs too ([vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1369-L1408)) | new density and visible fraction |
| `CREATE INDEX` | table's `pg_class` values | `relpages`, `reltuples`, `relallvisible` from the build, written in place even if the transaction later aborts ([index.c#index_update_stats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2797-L2803), [index.c#index_update_stats-nontransactional](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2877-L2885)) | E4.11c: stored `reltuples` became 20,000, so the derived table estimate rose from 16,875 to 20,000; the endpoint probe became possible |
| `INSERT` or `COPY` without `ANALYZE` | file of `n` pages | file grows | row count scales with the file at the old density ([tableam.c:711-747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L711-L747)); histograms and MCVs stay old (E4.11) |
| `CREATE STATISTICS` | no multi-column knowledge | an empty statistics object | nothing changes until the next `ANALYZE` builds its data ([analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-extstats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L604-L606)); E4.6 |
| `ALTER TABLE ... SET STATISTICS` or `SET (n_distinct = ...)` | current target or computed n_distinct | a new target or override; a target of 0 makes `ANALYZE` skip the column | applies at the next `ANALYZE` ([analyze.c#examine_attribute-target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1015-L1030), [analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-n_distinct](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L563-L574)) |
| Table created but never measured | `reltuples = -1` | unchanged until the first measurement | width-based density, 10-page minimum, defaults (E4.10) |

#### 4.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- Extended statistics estimates are checked row for row by `check_estimated_rows()`, which compares an estimate with the actual count ([stats_ext.sql#check_estimated_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/stats_ext.sql#L9-L28)), for ndistinct ([stats_ext.sql#ndistinct](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/stats_ext.sql#L262-L271)) and functional dependencies ([stats_ext.sql#functional_dependencies](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/stats_ext.sql#L572-L597)).
- Foreign-key join estimation is tested through the plan shapes it produces, with `COSTS OFF`: before and after adding a multi-column foreign key, and for outer joins ([join.sql#fkest](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/join.sql#L2755-L2780), [join.sql#fkest-outer](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/join.sql#L2783-L2809)).
- The leakproofness guard on statistics is tested with deliberately leaky operators, also through plan shapes. A second user's leaky operator must print no notice before the query fails for lack of permission, and an estimate degrades without table-wide read permission ([privileges.sql#leaky-selfuncs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/privileges.sql#L312-L345), [privileges.sql#leaky-selfuncs-user2](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/privileges.sql#L347-L359), [privileges.sql#leaky-selfuncs-permission](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/privileges.sql#L380-L391)).
- Support-function row estimates are tested with `test_support_func`, through the join plans chosen for 1,000 and for 10 rows ([misc_functions.sql#support-rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/misc_functions.sql#L215-L225)).
- The `n_distinct` column option is only accepted and followed by an `ANALYZE` in the `ALTER TABLE` tests; no test checks its effect on an estimate ([alter_table.sql#column-options](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/alter_table.sql#L2916-L2921)).
- Gap: the basic single-column estimates are not asserted as numbers. `explain.sql` replaces every number with `N` ([explain.sql#explain_filter](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L13-L35)), and no file in `src/test` mentions the endpoint probe `get_actual_variable_range()`. E4.2 to E4.15 on this page fill that gap for this build.

#### 4.11 Causal summary

1. `ANALYZE` stores a sample's summaries in `pg_statistic` and a page density in `pg_class`.
2. At planning time, the planner multiplies that density by the current file size.
3. Each condition's selectivity comes from an MCV frequency, a histogram fraction, a null fraction or a default.
4. Conditions multiply, unless extended statistics cover them.
5. `clamp_row_est()` rounds the product to at least one row.
6. Join and grouping estimates build on those rows.
7. The executor runs that plan unchanged; only sorts and hash tables adapt to the rows that actually arrive.
8. Only the next `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM` or index build changes the inputs.

### Chapter 5. Estimate costs

#### 5.1 Main idea

A cost is the planner's price for a path, in arbitrary units set by a few base prices, where one sequential page read costs 1.0 by default ([costsize.c:6-14](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6-L14), [cost.h:24](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/cost.h#L24)). Each path carries two prices: `startup_cost`, spent before the first row appears, and `total_cost`, spent to produce every row ([costsize.c:36-49](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L36-L49)). The planner compares candidate paths on these two numbers and keeps the cheap ones.

The recipe is simple and mechanical. Count the pages a step reads and multiply by a page price; count the rows it handles and multiply by per-row CPU prices; add a price for writing temporary files when the data will not fit in memory. Everything else is refinement: a cache model for repeated index lookups, a divisor for parallel workers, and a penalty that makes switched-off methods look terrible without removing them.

Three results surprise most readers. The numbers are not time; they only rank alternatives. `enable_seqscan = off` does not forbid a sequential scan, it adds 10 billion to its price. And the model charges every condition for every row, even when an earlier condition would have rejected the row first. The experiments are E5.1 to E5.9 in [the measurement script](#measurement-script), with E12.1 for the parallel divisor and E8.5 for a rescan.

#### 5.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `seq_page_cost` 1.0, `random_page_cost` 4.0 | price of a sequential and of a random page read | settings, defaults in `cost.h` ([cost.h:24-25](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/cost.h#L24-L25)); a [tablespace](../../../glossary.md#tablespace) may override both ([spccache.c#get_tablespace_page_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/spccache.c#L182-L205)) | parameter | every scan's I/O term |
| `cpu_tuple_cost` 0.01, `cpu_index_tuple_cost` 0.005, `cpu_operator_cost` 0.0025 | price of handling one row, one index entry, one operator call | settings ([cost.h:26-28](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/cost.h#L26-L28)) | parameter | every CPU term |
| `pg_proc.procost` | a function's price in units of `cpu_operator_cost`: 1 for C and internal functions, 100 for other languages unless `COST` says otherwise | the catalog ([functioncmds.c#CreateFunction-defaults](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/functioncmds.c#L1232-L1240)); a support function may answer instead ([plancat.c#add_function_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2094-L2137)) | stored parameter | condition and projection costs |
| [effective_cache_size](../../../glossary.md#effective_cache_size) (default 524,288 pages, 4 GB) | pages the planner assumes the OS and PostgreSQL cache together | setting ([cost.h:34](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/cost.h#L34)) | parameter; it reserves no memory and is used only for estimates ([config.sgml#guc-effective-cache-size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/config.sgml#L6048-L6052)) | the [Mackert-Lohman formula](../../../glossary.md#mackert-lohman-formula) for repeated scans |
| work_mem, `hash_mem_multiplier` | memory one sort, or `work_mem x multiplier` one hash table, may use before spilling | settings; `get_hash_memory_limit()` multiplies them ([nodeHash.c#get_hash_memory_limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeHash.c#L3602-L3613)) | parameter, also read again at run time | sort, hash and materialize spill costs |
| `parallel_setup_cost` 1000, `parallel_tuple_cost` 0.1 | price of starting workers and of passing one row to the leader | settings ([cost.h:29-30](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/cost.h#L29-L30)) | parameter | `Gather` and `Gather Merge` costs |
| [disable_cost](../../../glossary.md#disable_cost) 1.0e10 | penalty added when a penalty-type `enable_*` setting is off; gate-type settings skip the path instead (Step 7) | a constant ([costsize.c:130](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L130)) | parameter compiled into the server | the cost functions of the penalty-type switches |
| `pages`, `tuples`, `rows`, width | size of the input and the output | chapter 4 | estimates | page counts and row counts in every formula |
| `allvisfrac` | fraction of the table's pages marked all-visible | `relallvisible / current pages` ([tableam.c:749-760](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L749-L760)) | stored count against the current size | index-only scan heap fetches ([costsize.c#cost_index-allvisfrac](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L725-L726)) |
| index correlation | how closely index order follows heap order | `pg_stats.correlation` via the index cost estimator ([costsize.c#cost_index-amcostestimate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L617-L622)) | stored statistic | interpolation between random and sequential heap cost |
| `root->total_table_pages` | pages of all base tables in the query | summed once all tables are sized ([allpaths.c#make_one_rel-total_table_pages](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L185-L216)) | estimate | the cache share given to each table |
| `loop_count` | how many times an inner scan will be repeated | the smallest row estimate among the outer relations the path depends on ([indxpath.c#get_loop_count](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L1829-L1871)) | estimate | cache-aware costs of repeated scans |
| `STD_FUZZ_FACTOR` 1.01 | costs within 1 % count as equal | a constant ([pathnode.c:43-47](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L43-L47)) | parameter | `add_path()` comparisons |

The page prices, CPU prices and memory limits are all user-settable settings in the `user` context, so `SET` changes them for the session or transaction only (measured in E16.1; for example [guc_tables.c#seq_page_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3676-L3685), [guc_tables.c#work_mem](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L2448-L2457)). Every forced setting on this page uses that session scope.

#### 5.3 Logic map

```text
For each candidate path (chapters 6 to 13 generate them)
  cost_<kind>(path, sizes from chapter 4, settings)                               [A]
    I/O:  pages read x page price
          sequential scan:  pages x seq_page_cost
          index heap fetches: random..sequential, interpolated by correlation^2       [B]
          bitmap heap:      price per page slides from random toward sequential
                            as sqrt(pages fetched / table pages) grows
          scan repeated by a nested loop (loop_count > 1)?
                -> pages from the Mackert-Lohman formula with a cache share of
                   effective_cache_size x table pages / total_table_pages             [C]
    CPU:  rows x (cpu_tuple_cost + per-row qual cost)
          qual cost = sum over operators and functions of procost x cpu_operator_cost  [D]
          (no credit for short-circuit AND/OR)
    memory: bytes = rows x (aligned width + 24)                                    [E]
          sort bytes > work_mem        -> + page accesses x (0.75 seq + 0.25 random)
          hash-agg entries > hash_mem  -> + batch writes x random_page_cost,
                                          reads x seq_page_cost, 2 x cpu_tuple_cost per row
    parallel path?  CPU run cost / (workers + leader share)                        [F]
    penalty-type enable_* off?  startup_cost += 1.0e10                              [G]
          (a gate-type enable_* off means this path was never built)
  -> path.startup_cost, path.total_cost, path.rows
        |
add_path: compare with the relation's other paths                                  [H]
  total and startup costs within 1 % count as equal; a path survives if it is
  cheaper on one of them, or better on sort order, parameterization or parallel safety
        |
top of the query: how much of the output is needed? (LIMIT, cursor)                [I]
  fraction f -> cheapest  startup + f x (total - startup)
```

- [A] [costsize.c:36-49](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L36-L49), [costsize.c#cost_seqscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L284-L351)
- [B] [costsize.c#cost_index-io](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L720-L746), [costsize.c#cost_index-interpolate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L781-L787), [costsize.c#cost_bitmap_heap_scan-per-page](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1056-L1070)
- [C] [costsize.c#index_pages_fetched](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L898-L951), [costsize.c#compute_bitmap_pages-loops](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6463-L6481)

#### 5.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: set the prices

Input: the session's settings and the table's tablespace. Each scan asks `get_tablespace_page_costs()` for its page prices, which returns the tablespace's `seq_page_cost` or `random_page_cost` option when set and the setting otherwise ([spccache.c#get_tablespace_page_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/spccache.c#L182-L205), [reloptions.c:2098-2099](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/common/reloptions.c#L2098-L2099)). Temporary files for sorts and materializations never use tablespace overrides ([costsize.c:31-34](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L31-L34)). Output: the unit prices for the formulas below.

##### Step 2: price a scan

A [sequential scan](../../../glossary.md#sequential-scan) reads every page once: `pages x seq_page_cost`. It evaluates the relation's conditions on every stored tuple and projects each output row: `tuples x (cpu_tuple_cost + qual cost per tuple)` plus the target list's cost per output row ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L307-L325)). Its startup cost is zero unless its conditions or output expressions carry a startup part, such as a one-time sub-select ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L319-L325)).

An [index scan](../../../glossary.md#index-scan) first asks the index's access method to price the index work through `amcostestimate` ([costsize.c#cost_index-amcostestimate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L617-L622)). For heap fetches it computes a random-order price and a perfectly ordered price, then interpolates with the square of the index correlation ([costsize.c#cost_index-io](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L720-L746), [costsize.c#cost_index-interpolate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L781-L787)). An [index-only scan](../../../glossary.md#index-only-scan) charges heap fetches only for pages not marked all-visible ([costsize.c#cost_index-allvisfrac](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L725-L726)). The index side is covered in depth by [Planner Penalties for Bloated Indexes in PostgreSQL 17 (unverified)](bloated-indexes-query-planner.md).

A [bitmap scan](../../../glossary.md#bitmap-scan) first estimates the heap pages it touches ([costsize.c#compute_bitmap_pages](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6420-L6461)). It then prices each page between `random_page_cost` and `seq_page_cost` by `sqrt(pages fetched / table pages)`, because reading most of a table in block order is nearly sequential ([costsize.c#cost_bitmap_heap_scan-per-page](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1056-L1070)). It charges its conditions on every fetched tuple, as a recheck ([costsize.c#cost_bitmap_heap_scan-cpu](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1073-L1085)).

##### Step 3: price repeated scans with a cache model

Input: an inner scan that a [nested loop](../../../glossary.md#nested-loop-join) will repeat `loop_count` times. The planner assumes `effective_cache_size` pages of cache, shared among the query's tables in proportion to their size, so each table gets `b = effective_cache_size x T / (total_table_pages + index pages)` ([costsize.c#index_pages_fetched](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L898-L931)).

Calculation: the Mackert-Lohman formula turns `Ns` total tuple fetches over a table of `T` pages into distinct page reads. If the table fits in its share (`T <= b`), pages are `min(2TNs / (2T + Ns), T)`, so repeated fetches of the same pages are free. If not, fetches beyond a limit `2Tb / (2T - b)` start re-reading pages ([costsize.c#index_pages_fetched-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L864-L878), [costsize.c#index_pages_fetched-formula](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L932-L950)). A bitmap scan applies it to `tuples x loop_count` and divides by `loop_count` ([costsize.c#compute_bitmap_pages-loops](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6463-L6481)). Output: fewer pages per loop when the cache is large (E5.9).

Other paths are cheaper to rescan than to scan the first time. `cost_rescan()` charges a `Material` or `Sort` rescan only `cpu_operator_cost` per row, plus a re-read if it spilled; CTE and worktable scans `cpu_tuple_cost` per row; and a single-batch hash join no rebuild of its hash table ([costsize.c#cost_rescan-hashjoin](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4561-L4578), [costsize.c#cost_rescan-materialized](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4579-L4630)). The nested loop adds the first scan once and the rescan cost for every further outer row ([costsize.c#initial_cost_nestloop-rescan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3246-L3288)).

##### Step 4: price the conditions and expressions

Input: a condition or a target-list expression. `cost_qual_eval()` walks the expression tree. Each operator or function adds `procost x cpu_operator_cost`, or whatever its support function reports for `SupportRequestCost` ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-funcs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4769-L4779), [plancat.c#add_function_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2094-L2137)).

Columns, constants, `AND`, `OR` and `NOT` are free, and so is a `NullTest`, which is why E4.5's `note IS NOT NULL` costs the same as no condition. The walker deliberately ignores short-circuit evaluation, so every condition is charged on every row ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-model](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4747-L4767)). A `= ANY (array)` is charged for half the array's elements ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-saop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4819-L4828)), unless it is evaluated through a hash table, which is charged one hash and one comparison per row after a build at startup ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-hashed-saop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4796-L4818)). A pseudoconstant condition, one that uses no column, is charged once as startup cost ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-pseudoconstant](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4729-L4737)).

Consequence at plan creation: `order_qual_clauses()` sorts a node's conditions by security level and then by this per-row cost, cheapest first, so the executor runs cheap tests before expensive ones (E5.5, [createplan.c#order_qual_clauses](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L5315-L5395)). The cost estimate itself still charges all of them.

##### Step 5: price sorts, aggregation and materialization

Input: row count, width and the memory limit. `relation_byte_size()` estimates the bytes as `rows x (MAXALIGN(width) + MAXALIGN(tuple header))`, 24 bytes of header on this build ([costsize.c#relation_byte_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6359-L6362)).

`cost_tuplesort()` picks one of three shapes. If the output does not fit in `work_mem`, it prices `N log2 N` comparisons plus an external merge's page traffic. If a `LIMIT` needs only `k` rows, and either `k` is less than half the input or only the `k` rows fit in memory, it prices a bounded heap sort, `N log2 2k`. Otherwise it prices an in-memory quicksort, `N log2 N` ([costsize.c#cost_tuplesort-shapes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1916-L1960)). Each comparison costs two operator calls, and each output row `cpu_operator_cost` ([costsize.c#cost_tuplesort-comparison](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1901-L1902), [costsize.c#cost_tuplesort-run](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1962-L1970)).

`cost_agg()` prices a plain, sorted or hashed aggregation from the transition functions' costs, one `cpu_operator_cost` per grouping column per input row, and `cpu_tuple_cost` per output row ([costsize.c#cost_agg-strategies](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2692-L2737)). For hashing it predicts spilling from the expected hash-table size and adds disk and CPU costs for each level of recursion ([costsize.c#cost_agg-spill](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2741-L2813)). `cost_material()` adds two `cpu_operator_cost` per row, plus `seq_page_cost` per page when the rows exceed `work_mem` ([costsize.c#cost_material](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2453-L2493)). Output: startup and total costs of the upper node.

##### Step 6: divide the CPU work among parallel workers

Input: a [partial path](../../../glossary.md#partial-path) with `parallel_workers` workers. The scan's CPU cost is divided by `workers + max(0, 1 - 0.3 x workers)`, the second term being the leader's share while `parallel_leader_participation` is on; the disk cost is not divided ([costsize.c#get_parallel_divisor](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6380-L6405), [costsize.c#cost_seqscan-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L326-L346)). The row count shown for the partial scan is per process. A `Gather` adds `parallel_setup_cost` to startup and `parallel_tuple_cost` per row passed up ([costsize.c#cost_gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L436-L461)). Chapter 12 explains how the worker count is chosen.

##### Step 7: penalize or skip switched-off methods

Input: an `enable_*` setting that is off. The switches act in one of two ways, and the difference decides whether a disabled method can still appear in a plan.

A penalty switch keeps the path and adds `disable_cost`, 1.0e10, to its startup cost ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305), [costsize.c#cost_sort](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2124-L2146)). Consequence: the method still wins when it is the only way to run the query (E5.7), which chapter 16 uses to tell a missing alternative from an expensive one.

A gate switch stops the planner from building the path at all. Nothing is left to penalize, so the method cannot appear. Chapter 8 shows both kinds among the join switches.

| Switch turned off | Effect | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `enable_seqscan`; `enable_indexscan` (plain and index-only scans); `enable_bitmapscan`; `enable_tidscan` (TID and TID-range scans) | penalty | [costsize.c:304-305](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305), [costsize.c:606-608](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L606-L608), [costsize.c:1041-1042](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1041-L1042), [costsize.c:1313-1314](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1313-L1314), [costsize.c:1402-1403](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1402-L1403) |
| `enable_sort`, `enable_nestloop`, `enable_gathermerge` | penalty | [costsize.c:2138-2139](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2138-L2139), [costsize.c:3347-3348](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3347-L3348), [costsize.c:493-494](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L493-L494) |
| `enable_hashagg` | penalty on hashed and mixed aggregation; a gate for hashed set operations and semi-join de-duplication, and for hashed `DISTINCT` unless no other path exists | [costsize.c:2708-2712](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2708-L2712), [costsize.c:2726-2727](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2726-L2727), [prepunion.c:1322-1324](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1322-L1324), [initsplan.c:1747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L1747), [planner.c:5262-5267](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5262-L5267) |
| `enable_mergejoin`, `enable_hashjoin` | gate, except for a full join, which still gets the path with the penalty | [joinpath.c:204-217](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L204-L217), [joinpath.c:316-323](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L316-L323), [costsize.c:3794-3795](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3794-L3795), [costsize.c:4224-4225](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4224-L4225) |
| `enable_indexonlyscan` | gate on index-only paths; plain index scans remain | [indxpath.c:1738-1740](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L1738-L1740) |
| `enable_material` | gate on optional Materialize nodes; a merge join still materializes its inner input when correctness requires it | [joinpath.c:1788-1798](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L1788-L1798), [costsize.c:3903-3928](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3903-L3928), [subselect.c:528-534](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L528-L534) |
| `enable_memoize`, `enable_incremental_sort`, `enable_parallel_append`, `enable_parallel_hash`, `enable_partitionwise_join`, `enable_partitionwise_aggregate`, `enable_group_by_reordering`, `enable_presorted_aggregate` | gate | [joinpath.c:591-593](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L591-L593), [allpaths.c:3254-3256](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3254-L3256), [allpaths.c:1319-1320](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1319-L1320), [joinpath.c:2282-2284](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L2282-L2284), [relnode.c:2024-2028](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L2024-L2028), [planner.c:3910-3911](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3910-L3911), [pathkeys.c:485-486](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/pathkeys.c#L485-L486), [planner.c:3299-3301](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3299-L3301) |

##### Step 8: compare and keep paths

`add_path()` compares a new path with the relation's existing ones. `compare_path_costs_fuzzily()` treats totals within 1 % as equal and then looks at startup cost. When the relation cares about fast start (`consider_startup`), a path that is cheaper on startup but dearer in total is "different" and can survive beside the cheaper one ([pathnode.c#compare_path_costs_fuzzily](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L164-L215)). Sort order, parameterization, row count and parallel safety also count, which chapter 8 describes ([pathnode.c#add_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L361-L420)).

##### Step 9: price only the part of the output that will be read

A path's cost assumes all its rows are fetched. When only a fraction `f` is needed, its [tuple fraction](../../../glossary.md#tuple-fraction), the cost of that part is `startup + f x (total - startup)` ([costsize.c:36-49](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L36-L49)). `adjust_limit_rows_costs()` applies this to a `Limit` node, charging the skipped `OFFSET` rows to startup ([pathnode.c#adjust_limit_rows_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3881-L3928)). At the top of the query `get_cheapest_fractional_path()` picks the path whose partial cost is lowest ([planner.c#get_cheapest_fractional_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6534-L6559)). That is why a cursor, planned for 10 % of its rows, can prefer a merge join over index scans (E1.7, chapter 1).

#### 5.5 Eligibility and comparison

Costing makes no path eligible or ineligible by itself; chapters 6 to 13 decide which paths exist. Costs decide which of them survive and win.

| Comparison | What decides it | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Two paths for the same rows | lower total cost wins; within 1 % the lower startup cost wins | `compare_path_costs_fuzzily()` ([pathnode.c#compare_path_costs_fuzzily](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L164-L215)) |
| Fast start against cheap total | both survive when one is cheaper on each; the fraction needed at the top decides | E5.2's `LIMIT` and E1.7's cursor |
| Bitmap heap scan against plain index scan for 9,631 rows | both paths are eligible; `random_page_cost` weights the index scan's random heap reads more heavily than the bitmap scan's block-ordered reads | E5.8: bitmap 513.47 wins at 4.0; E5.8b: the rejected index scan costs 1140.74; E5.8c: the index scan wins at 1.1 with 453.57 (forced settings) |
| Hash against sorted grouping under a small `work_mem` | the predicted hash spill adds about 1,537 to the hash plan's startup, so an index-ordered `GroupAggregate` wins | E5.4 and E5.4b (forced setting) |
| A switched-off method | survives only if nothing else can produce the rows | E5.7 (forced setting) |

Rejected alternatives do not appear in `EXPLAIN`, so their costs are visible only by switching the winner off, as E5.4b, E5.8b and E8.2 do. Section 5.7 works through E5.8 to show the difference between an alternative that exists and one that wins.

#### 5.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Costs are units, not time | no calibration against the hardware ([costsize.c:26-30](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L26-L30)) | cost settings must describe the storage and cache for rankings to be right |
| Several conditions, cheap one first | every condition charged on every row ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-model](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4752-L4767)) | E5.5: `slow_check()` is charged 30,000 times, though at run time it only sees the 3,019 pending rows |
| Estimated rows below one | clamped to 1 ([costsize.c#clamp_row_est](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L202-L218)) | E5.6: `rows=1`, although about 10 rows for `customer_id = 500` times the `cancelled` and `amount < 1` selectivities is far below one row |
| A penalty-type `enable_*` switch off | +1.0e10, path kept ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305)); a gate-type switch builds no path at all (Step 7) | E5.7 |
| Set-returning function in `FROM` | its `procost` is charged once, at startup, not per returned row ([costsize.c#cost_functionscan-eval](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1552-L1566)) | E4.12: 0.25 startup for a 1,000-row PL/pgSQL function; the documentation says per row (Open Questions) |
| Bitmap larger than `work_mem` | some pages become lossy, and all their tuples are rechecked ([costsize.c#compute_bitmap_pages-lossy](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6484-L6510)) | higher CPU cost; E7.8's BRIN scan is lossy by design |
| Rescans of materialized inputs | cheaper than the first scan | E8.5: a `Materialize` rescan costs 0.075 per loop |
| `WHERE CURRENT OF` | `disable_cost` on anything but a TID scan ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-currentof](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4904-L4908)) | the TID scan always wins |
| Displayed costs | rounded to two decimals by `EXPLAIN` ([explain.c:1811](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1811)); comparisons use full precision | derived sums of rounded parts can differ by 0.01 |
| Tablespace page-cost options | apply to relation files only, not temporary files | spill costs always use the session's page costs |

#### 5.7 Formulas and worked examples

Terms: `P` is the relation's pages, `N` its estimated tuples and `R` its estimated output rows (chapter 4). `c_seq`, `c_rand`, `c_tup`, `c_op` are `seq_page_cost`, `random_page_cost`, `cpu_tuple_cost` and `cpu_operator_cost` (E5.1: 1, 4, 0.01, 0.0025). `LOG2(x)` is the natural log divided by 0.693147 ([costsize.c:102](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L102)).

Measured inputs, E5.1:

```text
 relpages | reltuples
      226 |     30000
...
         name         | setting
 cpu_index_tuple_cost | 0.005
 cpu_operator_cost    | 0.0025
 cpu_tuple_cost       | 0.01
 effective_cache_size | 524288
 random_page_cost     | 4
 seq_page_cost        | 1
 work_mem             | 4096
```

Sequential scan: `total = P x c_seq + N x (c_tup + q)`, where `q` is the per-row condition cost.

| Query (E5.1) | `q` | Derived | Estimated by the planner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SELECT * FROM orders` | 0 | 226 + 30000 x 0.01 = 526.00 | `cost=0.00..526.00` |
| `WHERE status = 'pending'` | one `texteq`, 0.0025 | 226 + 30000 x 0.0125 = 601.00 | `cost=0.00..601.00` |
| `WHERE status = 'pending' AND amount < 250` | two operators, 0.0050 | 226 + 30000 x 0.0150 = 676.00 | `cost=0.00..676.00` |

The price does not depend on the selectivity: 3,019 rows or 759 rows cost the same scan.

Limits and sorts, E5.2 and E5.3 (`N` = 30,000, width 40, so bytes = 30000 x (40 + 24) = 1,920,000):

| Plan | Formula | Derived | Estimated |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LIMIT 10` over the scan | `0 + (10 / 30000) x 526` | 0.18 | `Limit (cost=0.00..0.18)` |
| full sort, fits in 4 MB | startup = 526 + 2 x c_op x N x LOG2(N) = 526 + 0.005 x 30000 x 14.8727; run = c_op x N | 526 + 2230.90 = 2756.90; + 75 = 2831.90 | `Sort (cost=2756.90..2831.90)` |
| `LIMIT 10` sort, bounded | startup = 526 + 0.005 x 30000 x LOG2(20) = 526 + 648.29 | 1174.29; Sort total 1249.29; Limit total 1174.29 + (10/30000) x 75 = 1174.31 | `Limit (cost=1174.29..1174.31)` |
| full sort, `work_mem = 64kB` (forced setting) | pages = ceil(1920000 / 8192) = 235; runs = 1920000 / 65536 = 29.3; merge order = 6 (the minimum); passes = ceil(ln 29.3 / ln 6) = 2; accesses = 2 x 235 x 2 = 940, each 0.75 x 1 + 0.25 x 4 = 1.75 | 526 + 2230.90 + 1645 = 4401.90 | `Sort (cost=4401.90..4476.90)` |

The merge order comes from `tuplesort_merge_order()`, which divides the memory by the buffer needs of one input tape and never goes below 6 ([tuplesort.c#tuplesort_merge_order](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/sort/tuplesort.c#L1804-L1847), [tuplesort.c:177-180](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/sort/tuplesort.c#L177-L180)). Measured, E5.2 and E5.3: the executor used `top-N heapsort` for the bounded sort, `quicksort Memory: 2210kB` in 4 MB, and `external merge Disk: 1264kB` in 64 kB, matching the three shapes.

Aggregation, E5.4 (`GROUP BY customer_id`, 2,000 groups, `count(*)` whose transition function costs one `c_op` per row):

| Plan | Formula | Derived | Estimated |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HashAggregate`, default `work_mem` (E5.4c) | startup = 526 + 30000 x 0.0025 (transition) + 30000 x 0.0025 (hashing); total = startup + 2000 x 0.01 | 676.00 and 696.00 | `cost=676.00..696.00` |
| `GroupAggregate` over the index-only scan, `work_mem = 64kB` (E5.4) | 586.29 (scan) + 75 + 75 (comparisons) + 20 | 756.29 | `cost=0.29..756.29` |
| `HashAggregate` forced, 64 kB (E5.4b) | see the spill calculation below | 2213.50 and 2467.88 | `cost=2213.50..2467.88` |

The spill calculation of E5.4b, all from `cost_agg()` and the executor's limit functions:

1. Hash memory: 64 kB x `hash_mem_multiplier` 2 = 131,072 bytes ([nodeHash.c#get_hash_memory_limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeHash.c#L3602-L3613)).
2. Entry size: 92 bytes = 24 for the hash entry + (16-byte chunk header + 16-byte minimal tuple header + 4-byte key) + (16-byte chunk header + 16-byte per-group state) ([nodeAgg.c#hash_agg_entry_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L1694-L1720), [nodeAgg.c:320](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L320), [execnodes.h#TupleHashEntryData](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/execnodes.h#L802-L808), [htup_details.h#MinimalTupleData](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/htup_details.h#L624-L652), [nodeAgg.h#AggStatePerGroupData](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/executor/nodeAgg.h#L250-L267)). 2,000 x 92 = 184,000 bytes > 131,072, so a spill is predicted.
3. Partitions: `1 + 1.5 x 184000 / 131072 = 3.1`, capped at a quarter of memory (3) and raised to the minimum of 4; the limit left for groups is 0.75 x 131072 = 98,304 bytes ([nodeAgg.c#hash_choose_num_partitions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L1991-L2039), [nodeAgg.c#hash_agg_set_limits](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L1798-L1847)).
4. Batches: `ceil(max(184000 / 98304, 2000 / 1068)) = 2`, so the recursion depth is `ceil(log 2 / log 4) = 1` ([costsize.c#cost_agg-spill](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2778-L2789)).
5. Pages: 30000 x (8 + 24) / 8192 = 117.19, written and read once, each doubled as a penalty: 234.38 pages ([costsize.c#cost_agg-spill](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2795-L2806)).
6. Startup = 676 + 234.38 x 4 + 1 x 30000 x 2 x 0.01 = 676 + 937.50 + 600 = 2213.50. Total = 696 + 937.50 + 234.38 x 1 + 600 = 2467.88.

Measured, E5.4b: the executor reported `Batches: 5  Memory Usage: 161kB  Disk Usage: 392kB`. Its batch counter starts at 1 and adds one per spilled partition, which fits the 4 partitions of step 3 ([nodeAgg.c#hashagg_spill_finish-batches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L3110-L3121), [nodeAgg.c:3624](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L3624)).

Condition cost and order, E5.5 (`slow_check()` has `COST 1000`):

```text
Estimated by the planner, E5.5:
 Aggregate  (cost=75603.51..75603.52 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..75601.00 rows=1006 width=0)
         Filter: ((status = 'pending'::text) AND slow_check(amount))
```

Derived: per row 0.01 + 0.0025 + 1000 x 0.0025 = 2.5125; 226 + 30000 x 2.5125 = 75,601.00. The written order `slow_check(amount) AND status = 'pending'` was reversed, cheapest first. The row estimate multiplies 3,019 by the default 0.3333333 for a boolean function, 1,006.

The cache model, E5.9 (forced join methods so that a nested loop is shown; the inner bitmap scan repeats for 21 outer rows and finds 15 rows each time):

| Step | `effective_cache_size` 4 GB (default) | 8 kB (forced setting) |
|---|---|---|
| inputs | `T` = 226 heap pages, `Ns` = 15 x 21 = 315, index pages 34, `total_table_pages` = 22 + 226 = 248 | same |
| cache share `b` | 524288 x 226 / 282 = 420,174.07, rounded up to 420,175 pages, so `T <= b` | 1 x 226 / 282, raised to 1 page, so `T > b` |
| pages for all loops | 2 x 226 x 315 / (452 + 315) = 185.6, rounded up to 186 | limit = 452 / 451 = 1.002; 1 + (315 - 1.002) x 225 / 226 = 313.6, rounded up to 314 |
| pages per loop | 186 / 21 = 8.86, rounded up to 9 | 314 / 21 = 14.95, rounded up to 15 ([costsize.c#compute_bitmap_pages-loops](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6463-L6481)) |
| price per page | 4 - 3 x sqrt(9 / 226) = 3.401 | 4 - 3 x sqrt(15 / 226) = 3.227 |
| heap page cost per loop | 9 x 3.401 = 30.61 | 15 x 3.227 = 48.41 |
| + index scan + 15 x 0.0125 recheck | 3.64 + 30.61 + 0.19 = 34.44 | 4.40 + 48.41 + 0.19 = 53.00, with the unrounded index cost |
| estimated inner cost | `Bitmap Heap Scan ... (cost=3.64..34.44 rows=15)` | `(cost=4.40..53.00 rows=15)` |

The whole nested loop went from 778.42 to 1,168.11. The index-scan part also rises, from 3.64 to 4.40, because the generic index cost estimator applies the same cache model to index pages when a scan repeats ([selfuncs.c#genericcostestimate-repeated](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6740-L6779)); [Planner Penalties for Bloated Indexes in PostgreSQL 17 (unverified)](bloated-indexes-query-planner.md) derives that part.
