Eligibility versus comparison, E5.8 to E5.8c (`WHERE customer_id BETWEEN 100 AND 1000`, 9,631 estimated rows). At the default `random_page_cost` the bitmap scan wins. Switching off bitmap and sequential scans (forced settings) shows that the plain index scan was eligible all along, and what it cost:

```text
Estimated by the planner, E5.8, E5.8b and E5.8c:
 Bitmap Heap Scan on orders  (cost=143.01..513.47 rows=9631 width=40)
...
 Index Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders  (cost=0.29..1140.74 rows=9631 width=40)
...
 Index Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders  (cost=0.29..453.57 rows=9631 width=40)
```

| Term of the index scan | Formula | At `random_page_cost` 4 | At 1.1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| index pages read | `ceil(9631 x 34 / 30000)` = 11 pages x `random_page_cost` ([selfuncs.c#genericcostestimate-numIndexPages](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6729-L6732), [selfuncs.c:6786](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6786)) | 44.00 | 12.10 |
| index entries | 9631 x (`cpu_index_tuple_cost` + 2 index conditions x `cpu_operator_cost`) = 9631 x 0.01 ([selfuncs.c#genericcostestimate-cpu](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6803-L6810)) | 96.31 | 96.31 |
| B-tree descent | `ceil(log2 30000)` = 15 comparisons x 0.0025, plus (tree height 1 + 1) x 50 x 0.0025 ([selfuncs.c#btcostestimate-descent](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7086-L7106)) | 0.2875 | 0.2875 |
| heap pages, uncorrelated | Mackert-Lohman gives min(2 x 226 x 9631 / (452 + 9631), 226) = 226 pages x `random_page_cost` | 904.00 | 248.60 |
| heap pages, perfectly correlated | `ceil(0.32104 x 226)` = 73 pages: one random, 72 sequential | 76.00 | 73.10 |
| heap I/O used | uncorrelated + correlation^2 x (correlated - uncorrelated), correlation 0.014051536 (E4.1) ([costsize.c#cost_index-io](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L720-L746), [costsize.c#cost_index-interpolate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L781-L787)) | 903.84 | 248.57 |
| heap rows | 9631 x `cpu_tuple_cost`; the index conditions are not charged again ([costsize.c#cost_index-qpquals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L598-L604), [costsize.c#cost_index-cpu](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L790-L800)) | 96.31 | 96.31 |
| total (derived) | sum | 1140.74 | 453.57 |

Derived, not measured: the tree height of 1 is inferred from the displayed startup cost 0.29, which the descent terms give as 0.2875.

The table explains the flip. Nearly all of the index scan's cost is 226 random heap reads, so lowering `random_page_cost` from 4 to 1.1 removes 226 x 2.9 = 655.4 from it, while the bitmap scan already reads its pages in block order at a price between the two settings. At 4.0 the ranking is bitmap 513.47, then the sequential scan at 226 + 30000 x 0.015 = 676.00 (derived as in E5.1), then the index scan at 1140.74. The index scan was never ineligible, only more expensive.

A rescan, E8.5: a `Materialize` over 30 rows costs 601.00 + 2 x 0.0025 x 30 = 601.15 on its first scan and 30 x 0.0025 = 0.075 on each of the 1,999 later ones. The nested loop then tests 2,000 x 30 = 60,000 pairs at 0.01 + 0.005 each, giving 42 + 601.15 + 1999 x 0.075 + 900 = 1,693.07, the estimated `Nested Loop (cost=0.00..1693.07)` ([costsize.c#initial_cost_nestloop-rescan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3246-L3288), [costsize.c#final_cost_nestloop-cpu](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3466-L3473)).

The parallel divisor, E12.1 (`events`: 6,819 pages, 600,000 rows, 2 workers): divisor = 2 + (1 - 0.3 x 2) = 2.4. Parallel scan = 6819 + 600000 x 0.01 / 2.4 = 6819 + 2500 = 9,319.00, with 600000 / 2.4 = 250,000 rows per process; the estimated plan shows `Parallel Seq Scan on events (cost=0.00..9319.00 rows=250000)`. The serial scan would cost 6819 + 6000 = 12,819.00 (E12.8).

#### 5.8 Planning versus execution

| Decided while planning | Decided or adapted while running |
|---|---|
| which sort shape the cost assumes ([costsize.c#cost_tuplesort-shapes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1916-L1960)) | tuplesort switches to a bounded heap or to tapes from the rows it actually receives ([tuplesort.c#tuplesort_puttuple_common-switch](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/sort/tuplesort.c#L1261-L1288)) |
| whether hash aggregation is predicted to spill and how deep | the executor enters spill mode when the real table outgrows its limits ([nodeAgg.c#hash_agg_check_limits](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L1856-L1874)); E5.4b reported 5 batches |
| whether a bitmap is predicted lossy | the bitmap turns pages lossy when its entries actually exceed the limit set from `work_mem` ([tidbitmap.c#tbm_add_tuples-lossify](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/tidbitmap.c#L425-L432)) |
| how many parallel workers to plan | fewer may be launched, and the caller must accept that ([parallel.c#LaunchParallelWorkers-fewer](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/parallel.c#L611-L628)); chapter 12 |
| the rows a node will produce | never revised; `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` only reports them |

Costs themselves exist only in the plan. The executor never measures cost units, and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` reports time and rows, not actual costs.

#### 5.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SET` of a cost or memory setting | defaults | session or transaction value (`user` context, E16.1) | only this session's later plans; `EXPLAIN (SETTINGS)` names it (E16.2) |
| `ALTER TABLESPACE ... SET (random_page_cost = ...)` | session page costs | per-tablespace override | scans of relations in that tablespace |
| `ALTER FUNCTION ... COST` | old `procost` | new `procost` | condition order and every plan that evaluates the function |
| Table growth, `VACUUM`, `ANALYZE` | old sizes, `allvisfrac`, correlation | new ones (chapter 4) | page and row terms of every formula |
| Plan cached before the change | old costs frozen in the plan | unchanged until the plan is rebuilt | chapter 14 |

#### 5.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- Hash aggregation spilling at `work_mem = 64kB` is tested in [aggregates.sql#hashagg-spill](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/aggregates.sql#L1470-L1483) and for grouping sets in [groupingsets.sql:492-545](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/groupingsets.sql#L492-L545).
- Bounded sorts are exercised in [tuplesort.sql#bounded-sort](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tuplesort.sql#L50-L52), and in-memory versus disk-based sorts in [tuplesort.sql#in-memory-and-disk](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tuplesort.sql#L159-L176); the in-memory test notes that it cannot show the sort method, because the memory figure is not stable.
- Setting and resetting the tablespace page-cost options is tested in [tablespace.sql:15-32](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tablespace.sql#L15-L32); no test checks their effect on a plan's cost.
- Gap: no regression test asserts a cost number. `explain.sql` masks numbers as `N` ([explain.sql#explain_filter](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L13-L35)), and most plan tests run with `COSTS OFF`. The worked examples in 5.7, reproduced to the cent from E5.1 to E5.9, fill that gap for this build.

#### 5.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: chapter 4's rows, pages and widths, and the session's unit prices.
2. Transformation: each path's cost function turns them into I/O, CPU, memory-spill and parallel terms, plus 1.0e10 when its method is switched off.
3. Output: a startup and a total cost per path.
4. Interaction: `add_path()` keeps the paths that are cheaper by more than 1 % on one of the two, and the top of the query picks the cheapest path for the fraction of rows it will read.
5. Observed result: the executor adapts sorts and hash tables to the real data, but never revisits the choice.
6. Refresh: only a new plan uses changed settings or sizes.

### Chapter 6. Generate scan alternatives

#### 6.1 Main idea

Before the planner can join anything, it must know every way to read each input on its own. For each base [relation](../../../glossary.md#relation) it builds a RelOptInfo, estimates its size, and fills the relation's path list with one candidate path per usable scan method. The kind of range-table entry decides which methods are offered. The kinds are a table, a sampled table, a foreign table, a subquery, a function, a `VALUES` list, a CTE, a transition table, and an empty `FROM`.

The surprising part is how few choices most entries get. Only a plain table gets a real menu: a sequential scan, a parallel sequential scan, index and bitmap scans, and TID scans. Every other entry kind gets exactly one path, whose cost is mostly bookkeeping, and some of them are costed from fixed guesses such as 100 rows for a table function. This chapter's experiments are [E6.1](#measurement-script) to E6.11; the index-based paths are the subject of [chapter 7](#chapter-7-decide-whether-an-index-is-useful).

#### 6.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rte->rtekind`, `rte->relkind`, `rte->inh`, `rte->tablesample` | What the range table entry is | The parser and rewriter ([parsenodes.h#RTEKind](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1023-L1034)) | Fixed for the query | The dispatch in `set_rel_size` and `set_rel_pathlist` ([allpaths.c#set_rel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L359-L381), [allpaths.c:382-458](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L382-L458)) |
| `rel->pages`, `rel->tuples` | Pages to read and rows present before filtering | The live file size scaled by the stored density `reltuples / relpages` ([tableam.c:666](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L666), [tableam.c:711-713](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L711-L713), [tableam.c:747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L747)) | Current page count, stored density | Every scan cost function ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L284-L351)) |
| `rel->allvisfrac` | Fraction of pages the visibility map calls all-visible | Stored `relallvisible` divided by the current page count, never scaled up ([tableam.c:749-760](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L749-L760)) | Stored | Index-only scan cost ([costsize.c:725-726](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L725-L726)) |
| `rel->rows` | Rows after the relation's own quals | `set_baserel_size_estimates()` multiplies tuples by selectivity ([chapter 4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths)) | Estimate | Join sizes and costs above the scan |
| `rel->baserestrictinfo` | Quals that mention only this relation | Qual distribution ([chapter 3](#chapter-3-transform-the-query-safely)) | Fixed for this planning run | Qual cost per row; TID, index and pushdown matching |
| `rel->lateral_relids` | Other relations whose values this entry needs | `LATERAL` references | Fixed | Makes the entry's single path a parameterized path ([allpaths.c:768-773](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L768-L773)) |
| `TsmRoutine` | A sampling method's planning and execution callbacks | The method's handler function ([tsmapi.h#TsmRoutine](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/tsmapi.h#L56-L76)) | Code, plus the `TABLESAMPLE` arguments as parameters | Sample size and cost ([allpaths.c#set_tablesample_rel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L813-L847)) |
| `rte->enrtuples` | Row count of a named tuplestore | Counted from the transition table when a trigger registers it ([spi.c:3369-3383](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/spi.c#L3369-L3383)) | Current at trigger time | `set_namedtuplestore_size_estimates` ([costsize.c:6034-6036](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6034-L6036)) |
| `rel->amflags` | Whether the table AM can scan a TID range | The table AM's callbacks ([plancat.c:555-559](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L555-L559)) | Fixed | TID range eligibility ([tidpath.c#TidRangeQualFromRestrictInfoList](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L386-L404)) |
| `seq_page_cost`, `random_page_cost`, `cpu_tuple_cost`, `cpu_operator_cost`, `enable_seqscan`, `enable_tidscan` | Cost units and method switches | [GUC](../../../glossary.md#guc) settings, all changeable per session | Parameters | Every cost function; a switched-off method gets disable_cost ([costsize.c:304-305](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305)) |

Two of these values look alike but come from different places. `rel->pages` is read from the file on every planning run, while `allvisfrac` divides a stored count by that live number. So after new pages appear, the planner sees them at once but keeps believing the old all-visible count until the next `VACUUM` or `ANALYZE`.

#### 6.3 Logic map

The planner runs two passes over the base relations: first sizes, then paths ([allpaths.c#make_one_rel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L171-L234)). Some entry kinds build their path during the size pass.

```text
make_one_rel
 |
 +-- [A] size pass, per base relation (set_base_rel_sizes -> set_rel_size)
 |     consider_parallel set first, if the query may run in parallel
 |     excluded by constraints, or a constant-false qual? -- yes --> dummy rel, stop
 |     rte->inh (inheritance or partitioned parent)?       -- yes --> append rel (chapter 11)
 |     otherwise by kind:
 |       table, foreign        -> FDW GetForeignRelSize
 |       table, ONLY on a partitioned table -> dummy rel
 |       table, TABLESAMPLE    -> TsmRoutine sample size overrides pages and tuples
 |       table, plain          -> partial-index proofs, then row and width estimates
 |       subquery              -> push safe quals down, plan it, build paths now
 |       function / tablefunc / VALUES -> row estimates only
 |       CTE                   -> self-reference? WorkTableScan : CteScan, paths now
 |       named tuplestore, empty FROM -> path now
 |
 +-- [B] path pass, per base relation (set_base_rel_pathlists -> set_rel_pathlist)
 |       foreign   -> FDW GetForeignPaths
 |       sampled   -> one SampleScan, wrapped in Materialize if a rescan could change it
 |       plain     -> SeqScan; partial SeqScan if parallel-safe; index paths; TID paths
 |       function  -> FunctionScan, ordered only by a referenced ORDINALITY column
 |       tablefunc, VALUES -> one scan path each
 |
 +-- [C] set_rel_pathlist_hook: an extension may add CustomPaths or change paths
 +-- [D] Gather paths over partial paths (not for the top rel or appendrel children)
 +-- [E] set_cheapest: keep the cheapest startup, total and parameterized paths
 |
 later, in create_plan:
 +-- [F] pseudoconstant quals become a gating Result above the scan
 +-- [G] a SubqueryScan that only passes columns through is removed by setrefs
```

- [A] [allpaths.c#set_base_rel_sizes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L289-L324), [allpaths.c#set_rel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L359-L381), [allpaths.c:382-458](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L382-L458), [plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-constant-false](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1602-L1621)
- [B] [allpaths.c#set_rel_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L468-L530), [allpaths.c#set_plain_rel_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L763-L787), [allpaths.c#set_tablesample_rel_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L853-L895)
- [C] [allpaths.c:531-539](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L531-L539)
- [D] [allpaths.c:541-557](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L541-L557)
- [E] [allpaths.c:559-560](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L559-L560)
- [F] [createplan.c#create_gating_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1023-L1068)
- [G] [setrefs.c#trivial_subqueryscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1464-L1524)

#### 6.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: estimate the size of every base relation

`make_one_rel()` first calls `set_base_rel_sizes()`, which visits each base relation once. When parallel mode is allowed for the query, it decides `consider_parallel` for the relation before sizing, because some entry kinds build their paths during this pass ([allpaths.c:312-322](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L312-L322)).

`set_rel_size()` then checks exclusion first. A relation whose quals include a constant `FALSE` or `NULL`, or which constraint exclusion proves empty, becomes a dummy relation with a single empty path ([allpaths.c:363-378](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L363-L378)). The constant-false test runs regardless of `constraint_exclusion` ([plancat.c:1602-1621](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1602-L1621)). Plan creation turns such an empty path into a `Result` whose one-time filter is `false` ([createplan.c:1245-1258](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1245-L1258)).

Measured shape, estimated by the planner, E6.11:

```text
 Result  (cost=0.00..0.00 rows=0 width=0)
   One-Time Filter: false
```

For a plain table, the size step first tests any partial indexes, because a proven unique partial index can change row estimates, and then sets rows and width ([allpaths.c#set_plain_rel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L571-L582)). [Chapter 4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths) explains those estimates.

##### Step 2: offer the paths a plain table allows

`set_plain_rel_pathlist()` always adds a sequential scan. It adds a parallel sequential scan only when the relation may run in workers and has no `LATERAL` dependency. Then it asks for index paths and TID paths ([allpaths.c#set_plain_rel_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L763-L787)). A sequential scan is never parameterized by join clauses; it only inherits `LATERAL` parameterization ([allpaths.c:768-774](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L768-L774)).

The sequential scan cost is one sequential page cost per page plus one CPU charge per row, plus the quals' cost per row ([costsize.c:314-326](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L314-L326)). The worked example in [6.7](#67-formulas-and-worked-examples) reproduces it. The partial path is sized by `compute_parallel_worker()` and is covered in [chapter 12](#chapter-12-plan-parallel-execution-and-jit) ([allpaths.c#create_plain_partial_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L793-L807)).

##### Step 3: TID scans read rows by physical address

`create_tidscan_paths()` looks for quals on the system column `ctid`. Equality, `= ANY (array)`, ORs of such equalities, and `WHERE CURRENT OF` give a TID scan; `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` give a TID range scan ([tidpath.c:5-27](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L5-L27)). It also builds parameterized TID scans from join clauses such as `t1.ctid = t2.ctid` ([tidpath.c#create_tidscan_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L487-L556)).

A TID range path needs a table access method that can scan TID ranges ([tidpath.c:392-393](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L392-L393)). Its cost charges one random page for the first page and sequential pages after it, on purpose, so that an equivalent sequential scan wins ties ([costsize.c:1391-1398](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1391-L1398)).

Measured, E6.5 (estimates beside actual rows):

```text
 Tid Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..4.01 rows=1 width=40) (actual rows=1 loops=1)
   TID Cond: (ctid = '(10,1)'::tid)
...
   ->  Tid Range Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..15.64 rows=664 width=0) (actual rows=664 loops=1)
         TID Cond: (ctid < '(5,0)'::tid)
```

A TID scan can also be a parameterized path. A join equality such as `o.ctid = v.t` usually enters an equivalence class, so `create_tidscan_paths()` regenerates `ctid = <other side>` clauses from the class. It also scans the relation's loose join clauses, which covers outer-join quals ([tidpath.c:530-555](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L530-L555)).

`BuildParameterizedTidPaths()` accepts only plain equalities, not `= ANY` or `CURRENT OF`, and refuses pseudoconstant, security-blocked or unmovable clauses. Each accepted clause yields one TID path whose required outer relations are the clause's other side ([tidpath.c:425-461](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L425-L461)). Measured, E6.5b: each of the two outer rows supplies one TID, so the inner scan runs twice and fetches one row each time.

```text
 Nested Loop  (cost=0.00..8.07 rows=2 width=4) (actual rows=2 loops=1)
   ->  Values Scan on "*VALUES*"  (cost=0.00..0.03 rows=2 width=6) (actual rows=2 loops=1)
   ->  Tid Scan on orders o  (cost=0.00..4.01 rows=1 width=10) (actual rows=1 loops=2)
         TID Cond: (ctid = "*VALUES*".column1)
```

##### Step 4: sampled tables get exactly one path

`TABLESAMPLE` hands sizing to the sampling method. Its `SampleScanGetSampleSize` callback reports how many pages it will visit and how many rows it will return, and those numbers overwrite the table's own `pages` and `tuples` ([allpaths.c:827-843](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L827-L843)). The cost charges a random page per visited page when the method chooses blocks itself (`NextSampleBlock` set), and a sequential page otherwise ([costsize.c:394-402](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L394-L402)).

`SYSTEM` picks blocks, so its pages cost `random_page_cost` ([system.c#tsm_system_handler](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/tablesample/system.c#L66-L82)). `BERNOULLI` reads every page and has no `NextSampleBlock`, so its pages cost `seq_page_cost` ([bernoulli.c#tsm_bernoulli_handler](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/tablesample/bernoulli.c#L64-L80), [bernoulli.c:117-120](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/tablesample/bernoulli.c#L117-L120)). The contrib method `SYSTEM_ROWS` asks for a row count and derives pages from the table's row density ([tsm_system_rows.c#system_rows_samplescangetsamplesize](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/tsm_system_rows/tsm_system_rows.c#L103-L156)).

If a sampling method cannot repeat its sample across rescans and the query may join, the planner wraps the scan in a [Materialize node](../../../glossary.md#materialize-node), so a nested loop cannot scan it twice with different results ([allpaths.c:869-892](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L869-L892)). All three methods measured here declare `repeatable_across_scans = true` ([system.c:72-73](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/tablesample/system.c#L72-L73), [bernoulli.c:70-71](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/tablesample/bernoulli.c#L70-L71), [tsm_system_rows.c:86-87](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/tsm_system_rows/tsm_system_rows.c#L86-L87)).

Measured, E6.1:

```text
   ->  Sample Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..122.00 rows=3000 width=0) (actual rows=3332 loops=1)
         Sampling: system ('10'::real) REPEATABLE ('42'::double precision)
...
   ->  Sample Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..256.00 rows=3000 width=0) (actual rows=2970 loops=1)
         Sampling: bernoulli ('10'::real) REPEATABLE ('42'::double precision)
...
   ->  Sample Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..4.25 rows=25 width=0) (actual rows=25 loops=1)
         Sampling: system_rows ('25'::bigint)
```

##### Step 5: foreign tables ask their foreign data wrapper

For a foreign table, the core planner sets default sizes and then calls the [foreign data wrapper](../../../glossary.md#foreign-data-wrapper)'s `GetForeignRelSize`. It clamps the result so rows never drop to zero ([allpaths.c#set_foreign_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L901-L919)). The path pass calls `GetForeignPaths`, which adds whatever paths the wrapper supports ([allpaths.c#set_foreign_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L925-L930)).

`file_fdw` is the simple case. It reads the file size at plan time; with no statistics it divides the file size by an estimated tuple width to fake a row count ([file_fdw.c#estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L999-L1072)). It charges ten times a sequential scan's CPU per row, to account for parsing ([file_fdw.c#estimate_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L1080-L1106)). [Chapter 15](#chapter-15-extend-and-navigate-the-planner) covers join and aggregate pushdown with `postgres_fdw`.

Estimated by the planner, E6.10 (500 rows are in the file):

```text
 Foreign Scan on products_csv  (cost=0.00..13.51 rows=41 width=36)
   Filter: (id < 10)
...
   Foreign File Size: 7784 b
```

##### Step 6: subqueries are planned first, then wrapped

A subquery in `FROM` that survives subquery pull-up is planned as a separate query level during the size pass. First the planner tries to push the outer quals into it ([allpaths.c:2550-2601](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2550-L2601)). It then calls `subquery_planner()` and makes one `SubqueryScan` path per path the subquery produced, converting each ordering into the outer query's terms ([allpaths.c:2636-2638](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2636-L2638), [allpaths.c:2697-2714](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2697-L2714)).

The pushdown has two gates. The subquery as a whole must be safe: no `LIMIT` or `OFFSET`, no grouping sets, and volatile quals are refused under `DISTINCT`, window functions or set-returning functions ([allpaths.c#subquery_is_pushdown_safe](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3582-L3632)). Each qual must also be safe: no sub-selects, no leaky functions below a security barrier, no whole-row or unsafe output columns ([allpaths.c#qual_is_pushdown_safe-conditions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3832-L3881)).

A qual that stays outside is evaluated by the `SubqueryScan` node itself. E6.7 shows the `OFFSET 0` case, where the whole subquery refuses pushdown:

```text
 Subquery Scan on s  (cost=676.00..721.00 rows=667 width=12)
   Filter: (s.n > 400)
   ->  HashAggregate  (cost=676.00..696.00 rows=2000 width=12)
```

The outer query passes its tuple fraction down only when it has no join, aggregation, grouping, `DISTINCT` or sort of its own; otherwise the subquery plans for full retrieval ([allpaths.c:2617-2630](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2617-L2630)). A subquery that is proved empty yields a dummy relation ([allpaths.c:2643-2654](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2643-L2654)).

##### Step 7: functions, table functions and VALUES get one path each

A function in `FROM` is sized by `expression_returns_set_rows()`, which asks `get_function_rows()` for the support function's estimate or the `prorows` declaration ([clauses.c#expression_returns_set_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L286-L306)); with several functions in `ROWS FROM`, the largest estimate wins ([costsize.c#set_function_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5889-L5915)). The scan is unordered unless the query references a `WITH ORDINALITY` column, which gives it pathkeys on that column ([allpaths.c:2761-2804](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2761-L2804)). The whole function runs before the first row is returned, so its evaluation cost is startup cost ([costsize.c:1554-1567](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1554-L1567)).

A table function, `XMLTABLE` or `JSON_TABLE`, is always sized at 100 rows ([costsize.c:5927-5937](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5927-L5937), [primnodes.h#TableFuncType](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L97-L101)). `JSON_TABLE` was committed in the 17 development cycle (`de3600452b`). A `VALUES` list is sized exactly by its number of rows, and each row is charged one operator evaluation ([costsize.c#set_values_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5949-L5967), [costsize.c:1666-1676](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1666-L1676)).

Estimated by the planner, E6.6:

```text
 Function Scan on generate_series g  (cost=0.00..0.10 rows=10 width=12)
 Function Scan on r  (cost=0.01..0.03 rows=3 width=36)
 Table Function Scan on "json_table" jt  (cost=0.01..1.00 rows=100 width=4)
         ->  Values Scan on "*VALUES*"  (cost=0.00..0.03 rows=2 width=64)
```

##### Step 8: CTEs, worktables and transition tables read tuplestores

A materialized [common table expression](../../../glossary.md#common-table-expression) is planned once as its own subplan. A `CteScan` path then reads its stored rows, sized by the CTE plan's row estimate and ordered like the CTE's own path ([allpaths.c#set_cte_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2859-L2929)). The CTE's own cost is added to the final plan as an initplan cost, not to the scan ([costsize.c:1686-1695](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1686-L1695)). [Chapter 9](#chapter-9-plan-subqueries-and-ctes) explains when a CTE is inlined instead.

The self-reference inside a [recursive CTE](../../../glossary.md#recursive-cte) becomes a `WorkTableScan`. It is sized as `recursive_worktable_factor` times the non-recursive term's rows, because the real size depends on the query's fan-out ([allpaths.c#set_worktable_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2992-L3033), [costsize.c:5991-5998](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5991-L5998)).

A [transition table](../../../glossary.md#transition-table) in a statement trigger is a named tuplestore. When PL/pgSQL registers it, SPI records its current row count as the estimate, so a query planned inside the trigger sees the real count ([spi.c#SPI_register_trigger_data](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/spi.c#L3363-L3401), [costsize.c#set_namedtuplestore_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6019-L6040)). E6.9 captured the plan from inside the trigger after a 10-row insert:

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=0.23..0.24 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Named Tuplestore Scan  (cost=0.00..0.20 rows=10 width=0)
```

An empty `FROM`, as in `SELECT 1 + 1`, is an `RTE_RESULT` entry with a single `Result` path ([allpaths.c#set_result_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2965-L2983)).

##### Step 9: extensions, Gather, and the cheapest path

After the core paths exist, `set_rel_pathlist_hook` may add paths such as a [custom scan](../../../glossary.md#custom-scan) or change the list ([allpaths.c:531-539](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L531-L539)). Only then does the planner add Gather paths over any partial paths, so that a hook's partial paths are included. It skips this for the relation that already holds the whole query, which gets its Gather after the final target list is known ([allpaths.c:541-557](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L541-L557)). Finally `set_cheapest()` records the winners that the join search starts from ([allpaths.c:559-560](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L559-L560)).

##### Step 10: two plan-time adjustments

A pseudoconstant qual, one with no Vars of the current query level and no volatile functions, is marked as a gating qual when quals are distributed ([initsplan.c:2285-2319](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L2285-L2319)). Plan creation lifts it into a gating `Result` node whose one-time filter runs once per execution; the costs are left unchanged ([createplan.c#get_gating_quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1003-L1013), [createplan.c#create_gating_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1023-L1068)). E6.11 shows `now() > '2000-01-01'` gating a bitmap scan:

```text
 Result  (cost=7.84..239.57 rows=458 width=40)
   One-Time Filter: (now() > '2000-01-01 00:00:00+00'::timestamp with time zone)
   ->  Bitmap Heap Scan on orders  (cost=7.84..239.57 rows=458 width=40)
```

A `SubqueryScan` with no filter whose output columns are the subplan's columns in order is removed when references are fixed ([setrefs.c:1395-1413](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1395-L1413), [setrefs.c#trivial_subqueryscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1464-L1524)). The cost model anticipates this: such a path is charged exactly its subpath's cost ([costsize.c:1494-1507](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1494-L1507)).

#### 6.5 Eligibility and comparison

| Path family | Becomes eligible when | Compared how | Typical reason it loses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sequential scan | Always, for a plain table ([allpaths.c:776](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L776)) | Total cost `pages x seq_page_cost + tuples x (cpu_tuple_cost + qual cost)` ([costsize.c:314-326](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L314-L326)) | An index, bitmap or TID path reads far fewer pages |
| Parallel sequential scan | `consider_parallel`, no `LATERAL` parameterization, at least one worker ([allpaths.c:778-780](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L778-L780), [allpaths.c:799-806](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L799-L806)) | Kept in the partial list; competes after a Gather adds setup and transfer costs | Small tables; see [chapter 12](#chapter-12-plan-parallel-execution-and-jit) |
| Index, index-only, bitmap scans | A usable index and a matching qual, useful ordering, a proven partial predicate or an index-only possibility ([chapter 7](#chapter-7-decide-whether-an-index-is-useful)) | `add_path` on cost, ordering and parameterization | Low selectivity makes random heap access dearer than a sequential read |
| TID scan | `ctid = pseudoconstant`, `ctid = ANY(...)`, ORs of those, or `CURRENT OF` ([tidpath.c:5-27](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L5-L27)); a join equality on `ctid` gives a parameterized TID path ([tidpath.c:425-461](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L425-L461), E6.5b) | One random page per requested TID ([costsize.c:1327-1328](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1327-L1328)) | Rarely loses; `CURRENT OF` is forced to use it |
| TID range scan | A `ctid` inequality and a table AM with TID-range callbacks ([tidpath.c#TidRangeQualFromRestrictInfoList](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L386-L404)) | One random page, then sequential pages ([costsize.c:1411-1417](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1411-L1417)) | Deliberately costed above an equivalent sequential scan |
| Sample scan | A `TABLESAMPLE` clause; it is the only path ([allpaths.c:892-894](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L892-L894)) | Nothing to compare within the relation | Not applicable |
| Foreign scan | A foreign table; the FDW decides the paths ([allpaths.c#set_foreign_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L925-L930)) | The FDW's cost estimates | Depends on the FDW |
| Subquery, function, table function, `VALUES`, CTE, worktable, tuplestore, `Result` | The entry kind alone; one path each ([allpaths.c:2748-2809](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2748-L2809), [allpaths.c:2815-2850](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2815-L2850)) | Only against other orderings of the same subquery | The choice moves to the join search |
| Custom scan | A loaded extension adds it through the hook ([custom-scan.sgml#custom-scan-path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/custom-scan.sgml#L34-L58)) | `add_path` like any path | No in-core provider exists to measure |

None of the non-table entry kinds accept join clauses as parameters. Their only parameterization comes from `LATERAL` references, because the planner does not re-plan a subquery or re-evaluate a function once per outer row ([allpaths.c:2470-2479](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2470-L2479), [allpaths.c:2752-2758](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2752-L2758)).

#### 6.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| A qual folds to constant `FALSE` or `NULL` | The relation is proved empty regardless of `constraint_exclusion` ([plancat.c:1602-1621](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1602-L1621)) | A zero-row `Result` replaces the scan (E6.11) |
| `ONLY` on a partitioned table | The relation becomes a dummy, because a partitioned table has no storage ([allpaths.c:394-402](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L394-L402)) | No rows, no scan |
| `enable_seqscan = off` and no other path | The sequential scan still exists, with `disable_cost` added ([costsize.c:304-305](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305)) | The plan keeps a huge cost; see E5.7 in [chapter 5](#chapter-5-estimate-costs) |
| `WHERE CURRENT OF` | `enable_tidscan` is ignored and the qual's built-in `disable_cost` is subtracted ([costsize.c:1301-1314](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1301-L1314)) | A TID scan is always chosen, because only it can execute `CURRENT OF` |
| A table AM without TID-range callbacks | No TID range path ([tidpath.c:392-393](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/tidpath.c#L392-L393)) | A sequential scan filters `ctid` instead |
| Non-repeatable sampling method used where a rescan is possible | A Materialize node wraps the sample scan ([allpaths.c:885-890](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L885-L890)) | A nested loop rescans stored rows, not a new sample |
| `file_fdw` file missing at plan time | Size defaults to ten blocks ([file_fdw.c:1012-1013](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L1012-L1013)) | Estimates are guesses until the file exists or the table is analyzed |
| A foreign table with no statistics | Rows come from file size and width, not from content ([file_fdw.c:1038-1054](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L1038-L1054)) | E6.10: 122 tuples derived for a 500-row file, 41 rows estimated after the filter |
| Subquery with `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` or grouping sets | No qual is pushed down ([allpaths.c:3588-3594](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3588-L3594)) | The outer filter runs after the subquery (E6.7) |
| Subquery from a `security_barrier` view | Leaky quals stay outside ([allpaths.c:2521-2528](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2521-L2528)) | Correct row hiding at some cost; see E3.10 |
| A qual referring to a `PlaceHolderVar` or a lateral Var | Not pushed down ([allpaths.c:3893-3915](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3893-L3915)) | Evaluated at the `SubqueryScan` |
| Table function | Always 100 rows ([costsize.c:5933](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5933)) | E6.6 estimates 100 rows for a two-element `JSON_TABLE` |
| Named tuplestore with no count | 1000 rows ([costsize.c:6034-6036](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6034-L6036)) | Only when the provider leaves the count unset |

#### 6.7 Formulas and worked examples

The terms: `pages` and `tuples` are the relation's size inputs; `seq_page_cost` is 1.0, `random_page_cost` 4.0, `cpu_tuple_cost` 0.01 and `cpu_operator_cost` 0.0025 at the defaults recorded in E5.1. A qual such as `id < 10` costs one operator per row it is evaluated on.

**Sequential scan of `customers`.** E0.1 records 22 pages and 2,000 rows. The cost formula is `pages x seq_page_cost + tuples x cpu_tuple_cost` with no qual ([costsize.c:314-326](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L314-L326)). Derived: `22 x 1.0 + 2000 x 0.01 = 42.00`. Estimated by the planner, E6.6: `Seq Scan on customers c (cost=0.00..42.00 rows=2000 width=9)`.

**Sample scans on `orders`.** E0.1 records 226 pages and 30,000 rows.

| Method | Pages visited | Rows returned | Page cost | Derived total | Estimated, E6.1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SYSTEM (10)` | `rint(226 x 0.10) = 23` ([system.c:119-123](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/tablesample/system.c#L119-L123)) | `30000 x 0.10 = 3000` | random, 4.0 | `23 x 4.0 + 3000 x 0.01 = 122.00` | `122.00` |
| `BERNOULLI (10)` | all 226 ([bernoulli.c:117-120](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/tablesample/bernoulli.c#L117-L120)) | 3000 | sequential, 1.0 | `226 x 1.0 + 3000 x 0.01 = 256.00` | `256.00` |
| `SYSTEM_ROWS (25)` | `25 / (30000 / 226) = 0.19`, clamped to 1 ([tsm_system_rows.c:138-152](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/tsm_system_rows/tsm_system_rows.c#L138-L152)) | 25 | random, 4.0 | `1 x 4.0 + 25 x 0.01 = 4.25` | `4.25` |

The measured row counts differ from the estimates for the two percentage methods: 3,332 and 2,970 rows against 3,000. The planner fixed the estimate; the executor's sampling decided the actual count.

**TID range scan.** Without column statistics, `scalarineqsel()` estimates a `ctid` inequality from the block number and the table's density, giving the last page half weight ([selfuncs.c:592-665](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L592-L665)). For `ctid < '(5,0)'`:

1. Selectivity: `5 / (226 - 0.5) - 1 / 30000 = 0.022173 - 0.000033 = 0.022140`.
2. Rows: `0.022140 x 30000 = 664.2`, shown as 664.
3. Pages: `ceil(0.022140 x 226) = ceil(5.0035) = 6` ([costsize.c:1384-1389](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1384-L1389)).
4. Cost: `4.0 + 5 x 1.0 + 664.2 x 0.01 + 0.0025 = 15.64` ([costsize.c:1413-1439](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1413-L1439)).

Estimated `cost=0.00..15.64 rows=664`; measured `actual rows=664` (E6.5). The single TID scan is simpler: `4.0 x 1 + (0.01 + 0.0025 - 0.0025) x 1 + 0.0025 = 4.0125`, shown as `4.01`, because the TID qual's own cost moves from per-row to startup ([costsize.c:1320-1338](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1320-L1338)).

**Foreign scan with a faked row count.** `file_fdw` estimates the tuple width as `MAXALIGN(36) + MAXALIGN(23) = 40 + 24 = 64` bytes ([file_fdw.c:1050-1053](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L1050-L1053)). Derived, from E6.10:

1. Tuples: `7784 / 64 = 121.6`, clamped to 122.
2. Rows after `id < 10`: `122 x 0.3333 = 40.7`, shown as 41, because the column has no statistics and the default inequality selectivity applies ([selfuncs.h:37](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/selfuncs.h#L37)).
3. Cost: one page at `seq_page_cost` plus `(10 x 0.01 + 0.0025) x 122 = 12.505`, so `13.505`, shown as `13.51` ([file_fdw.c:1100-1105](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L1100-L1105)).

The file holds 500 rows (the stage wrote `generate_series(1, 500)`), so the fake estimate is four times too low.

**Subquery scan with an outside filter.** The subpath, a HashAggregate, costs `676.00..696.00` for 2,000 rows (E6.7). The `SubqueryScan` adds `cpu_tuple_cost + qual cost` per input row ([costsize.c:1509-1520](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1509-L1520)). Derived: `696 + (0.01 + 0.0025) x 2000 = 721.00`. Rows: `2000 x 0.3333 = 667`, because `n` is an aggregate output with no statistics.

**Tuplestore readers.** A `CteScan` charges `cpu_tuple_cost` twice per stored row plus the filter ([costsize.c:1716-1724](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1716-L1724)). Derived, E6.8: `(0.01 + 0.01 + 0.0025) x 308 = 6.93`, matching `CTE Scan on big (cost=0.00..6.93 rows=31)`. The worktable of E6.8 holds `10 x 1 = 10` estimated rows, and `n < 10` keeps a third of them, 3 rows, at `0.0225 x 10 = 0.23`.

#### 6.8 Planning versus execution

| Decision | Made by the planner | Made or adapted by the executor |
|---|---|---|
| Which scan method | Chosen once from the paths above | Never changed; there is no switch of method mid-run |
| Sample contents | Only the estimated pages and rows ([allpaths.c:827-843](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L827-L843)) | `NextSampleBlock` and `NextSampleTuple` pick the actual rows ([tsmapi.h:70-75](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/tsmapi.h#L70-L75)); E6.1 returned 3,332 rows for an estimate of 3,000 |
| Index-only heap visits | Charged using the stored all-visible fraction ([costsize.c:725-726](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L725-L726)) | Each index entry checks the live visibility map and visits the heap when the page is not all-visible ([nodeIndexonlyscan.c:161-169](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeIndexonlyscan.c#L161-L169)) |
| Pseudoconstant quals | Placed in a gating `Result` ([createplan.c:806-814](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L806-L814)) | Evaluated once per execution; a false result skips the scan |
| Named tuplestore size | Read when the query inside the trigger is planned ([spi.c:3379](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/spi.c#L3379)) | The tuplestore is read as it is |
| Foreign-table content | The FDW's estimates only | The FDW reads the data |

E6.3 makes the index-only row concrete. After an `UPDATE` of every 50th row touched every page of the table, `pg_class.relallvisible` still said 163 of 163, so the planner priced almost no heap visits; the executor then made 3,060 heap fetches. Measured, E6.3:

```text
 relpages | relallvisible
      163 |           163
...
 Index Only Scan using ios_pkey on ios  (cost=0.29..93.75 rows=3055 width=4) (actual rows=3000 loops=1)
   Index Cond: (id <= 3000)
   Heap Fetches: 3060
```

The row estimate rose from 3,000 to 3,055 without any `ANALYZE`, because the file grew to 166 pages and `rel->tuples` scales with the live page count ([tableam.c:747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L747)). Derived: `rint(30000 / 163 x 166) = 30552` tuples; the stored selectivity of `id <= 3000`, about 0.1, turns that into the 3,055 estimated rows.

#### 6.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rows inserted or updated, no `VACUUM` yet | `relpages`, `reltuples`, `relallvisible` from the last run | Stored values unchanged; the file may have more pages | Tuples scale with the live file size, while `allvisfrac` uses the stale all-visible count ([tableam.c:747-760](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L747-L760)); E6.3 |
| `VACUUM` | Visibility-map bits cleared by writes | Bits set again and `relallvisible` updated (E6.3: 166 of 166) | Index-only scans cost and run as all-visible again; E6.3 went back to 0 heap fetches |
| New table, never vacuumed or analyzed | `reltuples = -1` | Fewer than 10 pages are treated as 10 pages, and density comes from column widths ([tableam.c:696-699](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L696-L699), [tableam.c:738-745](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L738-L745)) | Estimates are width-based guesses; see E4.10 |
| `ANALYZE` on a foreign table | `reltuples = -1` for the foreign table | Stored density available | `file_fdw` scales density by the current file size instead of guessing ([file_fdw.c:1026-1037](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L1026-L1037)) |
| A transition table is filled | No tuplestore | `enrtuples` holds the real count | Queries planned in the trigger use it (E6.9) |
| `SET enable_seqscan` or `enable_tidscan` | Default on | `disable_cost` added to that method | The method survives but rarely wins ([costsize.c:304-305](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305), [costsize.c:1313-1314](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1313-L1314)) |

#### 6.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- Sample scans, including a view and a partitioned parent: [tablesample.sql:50-54](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tablesample.sql#L50-L54), [tablesample.sql:105-110](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tablesample.sql#L105-L110).
- TID scans with equality, commuted equality, OR lists, `= ANY` and the refused `!= ANY`: [tidscan.sql:10-40](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tidscan.sql#L10-L40). Parameterized TID scans in inner and left joins on `ctid`: [tidscan.sql:42-54](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tidscan.sql#L42-L54). TID range scans: [tidrangescan.sql:1-15](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/tidrangescan.sql#L1-L15).
- Function scans with `ORDINALITY`: [rangefuncs.sql:8-13](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/rangefuncs.sql#L8-L13). `JSON_TABLE` plans: [sqljson_jsontable.sql:206-208](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/sqljson_jsontable.sql#L206-L208).
- A materialized CTE's statistics reaching the outer query: [with.sql:362-372](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/with.sql#L362-L372).
- Volatile quals kept out of a `DISTINCT` subquery: [subselect.sql:789-800](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/subselect.sql#L789-L800).
- A named tuplestore planned inside a trigger, with the same `EXPLAIN` technique as E6.9: [plpgsql.sql:4410-4440](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/plpgsql.sql#L4410-L4440), output [plpgsql.out:5514](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/expected/plpgsql.out#L5514).
- Foreign scans of a file: [file_fdw.sql:155-190](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/sql/file_fdw.sql#L155-L190).
- Constant-false one-time filters: [case.out:272](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/expected/case.out#L272).
- **Gap: custom scans.** No module in the pinned tree defines `CustomPathMethods` or sets `set_rel_pathlist_hook`, so no regression test exercises a custom scan path, and this page could not measure one.
- **Gap: `XMLTABLE`.** The measurement build was configured without `libxml`, so only `JSON_TABLE` was measured; both use the same table-function path.

#### 6.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: the range-table entry kind decides the menu. A plain table's size comes from the live file size and the stored density; other kinds use method callbacks, subplans or fixed guesses.
2. Transformation: only a plain table gets a sequential scan, a parallel sequential scan, index paths and TID paths; every other kind gets exactly one path.
3. Interaction: `set_rel_pathlist_hook` may add custom paths, and Gather paths are added afterwards.
4. Output: `set_cheapest` hands the winners to the join search.
5. Observed result: at run time the executor may see different row counts (samples, visibility) but never switches method.

### Chapter 7. Decide whether an index is useful

#### 7.1 Main idea

An index helps a query only if three separate tests pass, and they happen at different times. First, the index must be usable at all: valid, visible to this transaction, and, if it is a [partial index](../../../glossary.md#partial-index), provably covering the rows the query wants. Second, something in the query must match it. That can be a condition whose operator belongs to the index column's [operator family](../../../glossary.md#operator-class), with the same collation. It can also be an ordering the index delivers, or a column list the index can return by itself. Third, the resulting path must be cheaper than the alternatives.

The surprising part is how literal the matching is. `id + 0 = 42` cannot use the primary key. A comparison under `COLLATE "C"` cannot use an index built under the default collation, even when both collations sort identically. A partial index proven usable for `status = 'pending'` is lost as soon as the value becomes a parameter. Each of these is a failed match, not a cost decision. This chapter's experiments are [E7.1](#measurement-script) to E7.14, with E3.12 and E6.2 to E6.4 from earlier stages.

#### 7.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pg_index.indisvalid`, `indcheckxmin` | Whether the index may be used, and whether it must wait for older snapshots to end | The [catalog](../../../glossary.md#pg_index), read through the relcache ([plancat.c:256-281](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L256-L281)) | Stored | An [invalid index](../../../glossary.md#invalid-index) is skipped; an [indcheckxmin](../../../glossary.md#indcheckxmin) index is skipped and the plan becomes a [transient plan](../../../glossary.md#transient-plan) |
| `IndexOptInfo` key fields: `indexkeys`, `opfamily`, `indexcollations`, `indexprs` | Which column or expression each index column holds, with its operator family and collation | `get_relation_info()` ([plancat.c:283-310](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L283-L310), [plancat.c:447-452](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L447-L452)) | Stored definition | Clause matching ([indxpath.c#match_index_to_operand](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L3681-L3744)) |
| AM capability flags: `amcanorderbyop`, `amoptionalkey`, `amsearcharray`, `amsearchnulls`, `amhasgettuple`, `amhasgetbitmap`, `amcanparallel` | What the [access method](../../../glossary.md#access-method) can do | Copied from the AM's `IndexAmRoutine` ([plancat.c:318-331](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L318-L331), [amapi.h#IndexAmRoutine](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/amapi.h#L214-L262)) | Fixed by the AM | Which path kinds and clause kinds are allowed |
| `sortopfamily`, `reverse_sort`, `nulls_first` | Whether and how the index is ordered | B-tree opfamilies directly, other `amcanorder` AMs by mapping `<` to B-tree ([plancat.c:340-415](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L340-L415)) | Stored definition | Index pathkeys ([pathkeys.c#build_index_pathkeys-head](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/pathkeys.c#L738-L760)) |
| `canreturn[]` | Whether each column can be returned without the heap | The AM's `amcanreturn` ([plancat.c:298-302](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L298-L302)) | Fixed per AM and opclass | Index-only scan eligibility ([indxpath.c#check_index_only](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L1730-L1800)) |
| `indpred`, `predOK`, `indrestrictinfo` | The partial-index predicate, whether this query implies it, and the quals the index scan must still check | Predicate from the catalog; `predOK` and `indrestrictinfo` computed per query ([indxpath.c:3334-3378](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L3334-L3378)) | Stored predicate, per-query proof | Path generation and the plan's filter |
| `pages`, `tuples`, `tree_height` | Index size and B-tree height | Live file size; tuples equal the table's estimate for a non-partial index ([plancat.c:466-500](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L466-L500)) | Current size | `amcostestimate` ([selfuncs.c#genericcostestimate-head](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L6627-L6700)) |
| [`IndexClause`](../../../glossary.md#indexclause): `rinfo`, `indexquals`, `lossy`, `indexcol` | One query clause matched to one index column, and the index conditions derived from it | `match_clause_to_indexcol()` ([pathnodes.h#IndexClause](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1756-L1766)) | Per planning run | The index scan's conditions; a lossy clause stays as a filter |
| `IndexPath`: `indexclauses`, `indexorderbys`, `indexscandir`, `indexselectivity`, `indextotalcost` | One way to use one index | `create_index_path()` ([pathnodes.h#IndexPath](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1710-L1720)) | Estimate | `add_path`, and reused when the index feeds a bitmap |
| `loop_count` | How often a parameterized inner scan is expected to repeat | The smallest outer relation the path depends on ([indxpath.c#get_loop_count](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L1829-L1872)) | Estimate | Repeated-scan caching in the cost model |
| `enable_indexscan`, `enable_indexonlyscan`, `enable_bitmapscan` | Method switches | Session GUCs | Parameters | `enable_indexonlyscan` removes index-only paths outright ([indxpath.c:1738-1740](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L1738-L1740)); the other two add disable_cost ([costsize.c:606-608](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L606-L608), [costsize.c:1040-1041](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1040-L1041)) |

The index's page count and the table's all-visible fraction come from different clocks. `pages` is read from the index file at every planning run, while the heap's all-visible fraction is a stored count divided by the live page count ([chapter 6](#chapter-6-generate-scan-alternatives)). An index-only scan's estimate therefore reacts to index growth at once, but to lost visibility bits only after `VACUUM`.

#### 7.3 Logic map

```text
get_relation_info, once per table
 +-- [A] each index: invalid? skip.  indcheckxmin not yet safe? skip and mark the plan transient.
 |        copy opfamilies, collations, returnable columns, AM flags, ordering, expressions,
 |        predicate and size into an IndexOptInfo
 +-- [B] get_relation_info_hook may add hypothetical indexes or edit the list
check_index_predicates, size pass
 +-- [C] partial index: do the WHERE clauses (plus movable join and equivalence clauses) imply
 |        the predicate?  yes -> predOK, and drop implied quals from indrestrictinfo
create_index_paths, path pass
 +-- [D] partial index without predOK -> skipped for plain paths
 +-- [E] match each clause to each index column:
 |        pseudoconstant, or blocked by a lower security level? -> no match
 |        index side is the column or an identical expression, other side has no Var of this
 |        table and nothing volatile?
 |          operator in the column's opfamily, collation equal? -> exact IndexClause
 |          otherwise ask the operator's support function     -> derived, usually lossy
 |        also: = ANY(array), row comparisons (B-tree), IS [NOT] NULL (amsearchnulls), booleans
 +-- [F] build_index_paths:
 |        no clause on the first column and !amoptionalkey (hash)?  -> no path
 |        ordered AM -> forward and backward pathkeys; amcanorderbyop -> ORDER BY col <-> const
 |        every needed column returnable -> index-only scan
 |        make a path if: clauses, or useful order, or proven predicate, or index-only possible
 |        amhasgettuple -> add_path; amcanparallel -> partial path; amhasgetbitmap -> bitmap candidate
 +-- [G] join and equivalence clauses -> parameterized index paths, costed with loop_count
 +-- [H] OR clauses -> BitmapOr; bitmap candidates -> choose_bitmap_and -> one BitmapHeapPath
 +-- [I] cost: the AM's amcostestimate plus cost_index's heap part, or cost_bitmap_heap_scan
 +-- [J] add_path keeps the paths no other path beats on cost, order and parameterization
create_plan
 +-- [K] exact index conditions leave the filter; lossy ones and implied ones are handled apart
```

- [A] [plancat.c:256-281](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L256-L281), [plancat.c:283-331](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L283-L331)
- [B] [plancat.c:575-576](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L575-L576)
- [C] [indxpath.c:3272-3316](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L3272-L3316), [indxpath.c:3334-3378](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L3334-L3378)
