No core test triggers the full-join error above. The E8.9 twelve-table comparison is this page's own demonstration.

#### 8.11 Causal summary

1. The collapse limits cut the query's join tree into lists; a `FULL JOIN` keeps its own list.
2. Each list gets its own search: exhaustive below `geqo_threshold` items, genetic at or above it, unless a hook takes over.
3. Each legal pair of relations shares one join relation and one row estimate for its set of tables.
4. For each pair, nested loop, merge and hash paths are built in both input orders, unless a gate switch skips a method, and each is priced from its inputs' estimated rows.
5. `add_path()` keeps the cheapest paths and the usefully sorted ones.
6. The executor runs the chosen tree unchanged. It adapts only hash batch counts, skew handling and Memoize evictions.
7. New statistics, indexes, keys or session settings change these inputs, so the next planning may choose a different tree.

### Chapter 9. Plan subqueries and CTEs

#### 9.1 Main idea

A subquery inside an expression is a [SubLink](../../../glossary.md#sublink). The planner tries hardest to make it disappear: an `IN` or `EXISTS` at the top level of `WHERE` becomes a semi join or anti join, which the join search can then reorder and implement with any join method. Only a subquery that cannot be turned into a join is planned separately, as a SubPlan that runs once per outer row, or as an InitPlan that runs once per execution.

Two things surprise newcomers. `NOT IN` never becomes an anti join, even on `NOT NULL` columns, because its NULL semantics differ from `NOT EXISTS`. And a common table expression is usually not a separate step at all: a CTE referenced once is inlined like a subquery, while `MATERIALIZED`, a second reference, recursion or side effects make it a separately planned subplan. In 17, even a materialized CTE lends its column statistics and sort order to the outer query.

The chapter's evidence is E9.1 to E9.11b in stage s09, plus E3.4b, E6.7, E6.8 and E8.6.

#### 9.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SubLink.subLinkType` | `EXISTS`, `ALL`, `ANY`, row comparison, scalar `EXPR`, `MULTIEXPR`, `ARRAY` or `CTE` ([primnodes.h#SubLinkType](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L995-L1005)) | Parse analysis | Stored in the query tree | `pull_up_sublinks()` and `build_subplan()` branch on it |
| `available_rels` | The outer relations a pulled-up sublink may reference without changing semantics ([subselect.c#convert_ANY_sublink_to_join-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1230-L1234)) | The position of the sublink in `WHERE` or an outer join's `ON` | Current state | The conversion checks |
| `SubPlan.parParam`, `setParam` | Params passed into the subplan from outer rows, and Params it sets as an InitPlan ([primnodes.h#SubPlan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L1044-L1053)) | `build_subplan()` from `root->plan_params` ([subselect.c#build_subplan-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L347-L372)) | Plan-time parameters, filled at execution | InitPlan versus SubPlan decision |
| `SubPlan.useHashTable`, `unknownEqFalse` | Probe a hash of the subquery output; whether UNKNOWN may be treated as FALSE ([primnodes.h:1079-1082](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/primnodes.h#L1079-L1082)) | `build_subplan()`; `isTopQual` from `SS_process_sublinks()` ([subselect.c#SS_process_sublinks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1913-L1928)) | Plan-time decision | Executor's hashed probe |
| `AlternativeSubPlan` | Two plans for one correlated `EXISTS`: per-row and hashed ([subselect.c#make_subplan-alternative](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L243-L307)) | `make_subplan()` | Plan-time candidates | `set_plan_references()` picks one |
| `hash_mem` limit | `work_mem × hash_mem_multiplier` bytes ([nodeHash.c#get_hash_memory_limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeHash.c#L3602-L3613)) | Settings, 4 MB × 2 here (E16.1) | Parameter | Whether a SubPlan may be hashed |
| `CommonTableExpr.ctematerialized`, `cterefcount`, `cterecursive` | The user's `MATERIALIZED` choice, the reference count, and recursion ([parsenodes.h#CTEMaterialize](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1636-L1641), [parsenodes.h:1679-1693](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L1679-L1693)) | Parse analysis | Stored in the query tree | `SS_process_ctes()` |
| `root->cte_plan_ids` and `glob->subplans`, `subpaths`, `subroots` | Which planned subplan implements each CTE, and its Plan, Path and planner state | `SS_process_ctes()` ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-register](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1032-L1045)) | Current state of this planning run | CTE scans read size, statistics and pathkeys from them |
| `recursive_worktable_factor` | Assumed size of the worktable, as a multiple of the non-recursive term's rows; default 10, user-settable ([guc_tables.c#recursive_worktable_factor](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3798-L3808), [cost.h:33](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/cost.h#L33)) | Setting | Parameter | The WorkTable Scan's row estimate |

`parParam` and `setParam` look alike but flow in opposite directions. `parParam` carries values from each outer row into the subplan, so its presence forces a rerun per row. `setParam` carries the one result an InitPlan computes out to the outer plan, which is why an InitPlan must have an empty `parParam`.

#### 9.3 Logic map

The first map follows one SubLink. The second follows one CTE. Keys index the citations under each block.

```text
A SubLink in the query
|
+-- [A] at top level of WHERE or JOIN/ON (only through AND), before pull-up?
|     |
|     +-- ANY (IN):  outer Vars in the sub-select only from available_rels?
|     |              test expression uses outer Vars, none volatile?
|     |                 yes -> JOIN_SEMI with the sub-select as an RTE    (17: correlated allowed)
|     +-- EXISTS / NOT EXISTS:  no WITH, simplifiable, WHERE references the outer
|     |              query and is not volatile?
|     |                 yes -> JOIN_SEMI / JOIN_ANTI with the sub-select's tables
|     +-- NOT IN, ALL, scalar, ARRAY, or conversion refused -> fall through
|
+-- [B] SS_process_sublinks: plan the sub-select as its own query level
      |   (tuple_fraction: EXISTS 1 row, ANY/ALL 50 %, others all rows)
      +-- no outer references (parParam empty) and EXISTS, EXPR, ARRAY, ROWCOMPARE, MULTIEXPR?
      |       yes -> InitPlan: run once, result in a Param
      +-- ANY with no outer references, hashable operators, output fits hash_mem?
      |       yes -> hashed SubPlan
      +-- no outer references otherwise -> SubPlan over a Material node
      +-- correlated -> SubPlan rerun per outer row
      +-- [C] correlated EXISTS -> also plan an IN-style hashed alternative;
              set_plan_references keeps the cheaper for the expected calls

A CTE in WITH
|
+-- [D] unreferenced SELECT -> ignored
+-- [E] NOT MATERIALIZED, or default with one reference; not recursive; plain SELECT
|       without FOR UPDATE; no volatile functions; no outer self-reference when
|       referenced more than once?
|         yes -> inlined as a subquery RTE (then Chapter 3 pull-up rules apply)
|         no  -> planned once for full retrieval as an InitPlan "CTE name"
+-- [F] each reference becomes a CTE Scan: rows, column statistics (17) and
        pathkeys (17) come from the CTE's own plan
```

- [A] [prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L427-L453), [subselect.c#convert_ANY_sublink_to_join-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1275-L1308), [subselect.c#convert_EXISTS_sublink_to_join-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1387-L1439)
- [B] [subselect.c#make_subplan-fraction](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L190-L222), [subselect.c#build_subplan-initplans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L374-L449), [subselect.c#build_subplan-any-all](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L486-L538)
- [C] [subselect.c#make_subplan-alternative](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L243-L307), [setrefs.c#fix_alternative_subplan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L2104-L2139)
- [D] [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-unreferenced](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L900-L908)
- [E] [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-inline](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L910-L955), [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L966-L988)
- [F] [allpaths.c#set_cte_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2860-L2929), [selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable-cte](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5421-L5431)

#### 9.4 Step by step

##### Step 1. Try to turn IN and EXISTS into joins

`pull_up_sublinks()` runs early in `subquery_planner()` (Chapter 3, Step 2). It looks only at the top level of a `WHERE` or `JOIN ... ON` clause, through `AND`, because only there can a FALSE result and a NULL result be treated alike ([prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L427-L453)). The parser has already turned `x IN (SELECT ...)` into `x = ANY (SELECT ...)` ([parse_expr.c#transformSubLink-in](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/parse_expr.c#L1939-L1943)); `EXISTS` and `NOT EXISTS` are recognized directly ([prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks_qual_recurse-any](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L651-L657), [prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks_qual_recurse-not](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L763-L828)).

For `ANY`, `convert_ANY_sublink_to_join()` adds the whole sub-select to the range table as a subquery and builds a `JOIN_SEMI` whose condition is the `IN` comparison ([subselect.c#convert_ANY_sublink_to_join-join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1321-L1362)). The comparison must use outer columns, must not be volatile, and must reference only `available_rels` ([subselect.c#convert_ANY_sublink_to_join-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1275-L1308)). The new subquery entry is then an ordinary candidate for Chapter 3's pull-up, which is why E9.3 shows `orders` scanned directly.

For `EXISTS`, `convert_EXISTS_sublink_to_join()` first drops the sub-select's target list, `GROUP BY`, `WINDOW`, `ORDER BY`, `DISTINCT` and a constant positive `LIMIT`, since none of them changes whether a row exists ([subselect.c#simplify_EXISTS_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1552-L1612)). It then merges the sub-select's tables directly and uses its `WHERE` as the join condition ([subselect.c#convert_EXISTS_sublink_to_join-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1461-L1520)). A sub-select with `WITH`, one whose other clauses reference the outer query, or a volatile `WHERE` is refused ([subselect.c#convert_EXISTS_sublink_to_join-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1387-L1439)).

##### Step 2. Correlated IN is new in 17

Until the 17 cycle, an `IN` sub-select that referenced the outer query could not become a join. Commit `9f13376396` (committed in the 17 development cycle) replaced that refusal: the sub-select is now added as a `LATERAL` subquery, provided its outer references stay within `available_rels` ([subselect.c#convert_ANY_sublink_to_join-lateral](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1275-L1287)). E9.6 shows the result: the correlation `o.amount > c.id * 0.4` ends up as the `Join Filter` of a Hash Semi Join.

Estimated by the planner, E9.6:

```text
 Hash Semi Join  (cost=901.00..1012.37 rows=667 width=56)
   Hash Cond: (c.id = o.customer_id)
   Join Filter: (o.amount > ((c.id)::numeric * 0.4))
   ->  Seq Scan on customers c  (cost=0.00..42.00 rows=2000 width=56)
   ->  Hash  (cost=526.00..526.00 rows=30000 width=10)
         ->  Seq Scan on orders o  (cost=0.00..526.00 rows=30000 width=10)
```

##### Step 3. A semi join is implemented directly or after making one side unique

The semi join gets a `SpecialJoinInfo`, and Chapter 8 plans it. For a semi join, `make_join_rel()` offers two families of paths: a true semi join, and a plain inner join after the inner side is made unique ([joinrels.c#populate_joinrel_with_paths-semi](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinrels.c#L992-L1021), [pathnode.c#create_unique_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L1642-L1654)). Costs decide. In E9.3 the unique-ified form won: a HashAggregate reduces the cancelled orders to an estimated 1,078 distinct customer ids, and a plain Hash Join follows. When the inner side is already unique, `reduce_unique_semijoins()` removes the semi-join constraint altogether (Chapter 3, Step 10).

`NOT EXISTS` becomes `JOIN_ANTI` ([subselect.c:1508](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1508)). E9.4 shows it as a Hash Right Anti Join, which hashes the preserved `customers` side and probes with orders.

##### Step 4. Why NOT IN stays a SubPlan

`pull_up_sublinks()` converts a `NOT` only when its argument is `EXISTS` ([prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks_qual_recurse-not](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L763-L828)). `NOT IN` returns NULL, not TRUE, when the sub-select yields a NULL and nothing matches, and an anti join cannot express that; the hashed SubPlan's executor code returns NULL in exactly that case ([nodeSubplan.c#ExecHashSubPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeSubplan.c#L114-L181)). The code does not look at `NOT NULL` declarations here, so even Q3 over two `NOT NULL` columns keeps the SubPlan (E9.4).

Because the `NOT` sits between the sublink and the top of the qual, the SubPlan is not marked `unknownEqFalse`: it must report UNKNOWN correctly ([subselect.c#process_sublinks_mutator-top-level](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L2003-L2007), [subselect.c#process_sublinks_mutator-not-top](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L2050-L2054)). It is uncorrelated and its `=` is hashable and strict, so it becomes a hashed SubPlan, and the executor tracks NULL rows in the hash table so that the result can be UNKNOWN ([subselect.c#build_subplan-hash](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L509-L520), [subselect.c#hash_ok_operator](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L832-L867)).

Estimated by the planner, E9.4 (Q3), first the `NOT IN` form, then the `NOT EXISTS` form:

```text
 Seq Scan on customers c  (cost=604.77..651.77 rows=1000 width=56)
   Filter: (NOT (ANY (id = (hashed SubPlan 1).col1)))
   SubPlan 1
     ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=1509 width=4)
           Filter: (status = 'cancelled'::text)
```

```text
 Hash Right Anti Join  (cost=67.00..684.63 rows=491 width=56)
   Hash Cond: (o.customer_id = c.id)
...
```

##### Step 5. Plan the remaining sublinks as SubPlans or InitPlans

Every sublink still present during expression preprocessing goes to `make_subplan()` ([planner.c:1227-1229](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1227-L1229)). It plans the sub-select as a new query level with a hint about how much of its output will be read: one row for `EXISTS`, half for `ANY` and `ALL`, all rows otherwise ([subselect.c#make_subplan-fraction](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L190-L222)). References to the outer level become `PARAM_EXEC` Params, recorded in the outer level's `plan_params` ([paramassign.c#overview](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/paramassign.c#L6-L19)).

`build_subplan()` then chooses the form ([subselect.c#build_subplan-initplans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L374-L449), [subselect.c#build_subplan-any-all](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L486-L538)):

1. No outer references and an `EXISTS`, scalar, `ARRAY`, row-comparison or `MULTIEXPR` sub-select: an InitPlan. The outer expression reads its result from a Param. E9.1 shows `Filter: (amount > (InitPlan 1).col1)`.
2. `ANY` or `ALL` can never be an InitPlan, because each outer row compares against the whole output ([subselect.c:509-515](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L509-L515)).
3. An uncorrelated `ANY` with hashable, strict operators whose output fits in `hash_mem` is hashed ([subselect.c#subplan_is_hashable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L712-L728)).
4. Any other uncorrelated SubPlan gets a Material node, unless `enable_material` is off or its top node already materializes ([subselect.c#build_subplan-material](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L522-L534)). E9.5's `ALL` shows `Materialize` under `SubPlan 1`.
5. A correlated SubPlan runs again for each outer row. E9.2 shows `SubPlan 1` with `loops=18`, one per west-region gold customer.

##### Step 6. A correlated EXISTS gets two plans, and the choice waits until setrefs

A correlated `EXISTS` that survives Step 1, for example under an `OR`, first gets its per-row SubPlan. `make_subplan()` then tries to rewrite a second copy as an uncorrelated `IN`. It splits the `WHERE` into `outer = inner` equalities, which become the `ANY` test, and inner-only conditions, which stay in the sub-select ([subselect.c#convert_EXISTS_to_ANY-split](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1702-L1710)). If that works and the result fits in `hash_mem`, both SubPlans go into an `AlternativeSubPlan` ([subselect.c#make_subplan-alternative](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L243-L307)).

The planner cannot choose yet, because the right answer depends on how often the outer query will evaluate the test, and that is unknown this early ([subselect.c:244-250](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L244-L250)). Until then, cost estimation charges the first alternative, the per-row SubPlan ([costsize.c#cost_qual_eval_walker-alternative](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4933-L4944)).

When `set_plan_references()` fixes each finished plan node, it calls `fix_alternative_subplan()`. That function keeps the alternative with the lowest `startup_cost + num_exec × per_call_cost`, and on a tie the later one ([setrefs.c#fix_alternative_subplan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L2104-L2139)). For a qual, `num_exec` is twice the node's estimated output rows, a rough guess that assumes the SubPlan test comes last and passes half the rows ([setrefs.c#NUM_EXEC-rationale](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L100-L116), [setrefs.c#set_plan_refs-seqscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L623-L634)). E9.11 and E9.11b show both outcomes:

Estimated by the planner, E9.11 (up to 2,000 outer rows), then E9.11b (one outer row, `c.id = 42`):

```text
 Seq Scan on customers c  (cost=0.00..106111.07 rows=1100 width=4)
   Filter: ((region = 'west'::text) OR (ANY (id = (hashed SubPlan 2).col1)))
   SubPlan 2
     ->  Seq Scan on orders o  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=1509 width=4)
           Filter: (status = 'cancelled'::text)
```

```text
 Index Scan using customers_pkey on customers c  (cost=0.28..8.87 rows=1 width=4)
   Index Cond: (id = 42)
   Filter: ((tier = 'gold'::text) OR EXISTS(SubPlan 1))
   SubPlan 1
     ->  Index Only Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders o  (cost=0.29..4.55 rows=15 width=0)
           Index Cond: (customer_id = c.id)
```

In E9.11 the kept plan is the hashed `ANY` form (`SubPlan 2`), yet the scan's printed cost still reflects the per-row form: it was computed before the choice. Section 9.7 works through both decisions.

##### Step 7. LATERAL subqueries run once per outer row

A `LATERAL` subquery that pull-up cannot flatten is planned as its own level, and its references to earlier `FROM` items make its path parameterized by those items ([allpaths.c#set_subquery_pathlist-lateral](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2500-L2507), [allpaths.c#set_subquery_pathlist-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2620-L2641)). Merge and hash joins refuse an input parameterized by the other side, so only a nested loop can use this path, and E9.7 is a Nested Loop whose inner `Limit -> Sort -> Bitmap Heap Scan` runs 18 times ([joinpath.c#sort_inner_and_outer-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L1296-L1304), [joinpath.c#hash_inner_and_outer-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L2150-L2157)). The subquery keeps its own `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 2`, because `LIMIT` blocks pull-up (Chapter 3, Step 4). No Subquery Scan node appears: `set_plan_references()` removes a Subquery Scan that only passes rows through ([setrefs.c#trivial_subqueryscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1455-L1470)).

##### Step 8. Decide how each CTE is planned

`SS_process_ctes()` runs first in `subquery_planner()`, before any sublink work ([planner.c#subquery_planner-ctes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L690-L695)). It ignores an unreferenced `SELECT` CTE ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-unreferenced](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L900-L908)). It inlines a CTE only when all of these hold ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-inline](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L910-L955)):

- it is `NOT MATERIALIZED`, or has no option and exactly one reference;
- it is not recursive;
- it is a plain `SELECT` without `FOR UPDATE` anywhere inside it, and calls no volatile function ([subselect.c#contain_dml_walker](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1064-L1079));
- it has no outer self-reference, if it is referenced more than once.

Any other CTE is planned once, for full retrieval, and registered as an InitPlan labelled `CTE name` ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L966-L988), [subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-register](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1032-L1045)). E9.8 shows all four cases on one query. The default single reference and `NOT MATERIALIZED` with two references both produce `orders_pkey` lookups; `MATERIALIZED` and the default with two references both scan all 3,019 pending orders into `CTE p`.

##### Step 9. What the outer query learns from a materialized CTE

Each reference to a planned CTE becomes a CTE Scan. `set_cte_pathlist()` takes the row estimate from the CTE's plan, and in 17 it also converts the CTE path's sort order into the outer query's pathkeys ([allpaths.c#set_cte_pathlist-estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2907-L2928)). Selectivity estimation can now follow a CTE column down to the underlying table's statistics, as it already could for subqueries ([selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable-cte](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5421-L5431), [selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable-cte-subroot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5460-L5503)).

Both changes were committed in the 17 development cycle: `f7816aec23` extracts column statistics from CTE references, and `a65724dfa7` propagates CTE pathkeys to the outer query. The first commit's message argues that the optimization fence only promises that the outer query cannot change the CTE's plan, not that it cannot see the result. E9.9 shows the effect: the CTE Scan for `customer_id = 7` is estimated at 458 rows, exactly the actual count, instead of a default guess.

Measured, E9.9:

```text
   ->  CTE Scan on m  (cost=0.00..675.00 rows=458 width=0) (actual rows=458 loops=1)
         Filter: (customer_id = 7)
         Rows Removed by Filter: 29542
```

##### Step 10. Recursive CTEs

A recursive CTE is a `UNION` planned by `generate_recursion_path()`. It plans the non-recursive term first and publishes its path as `root->non_recursive_path`, then plans the recursive term ([prepunion.c#generate_recursion_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L408-L434)). Inside the recursive term, the self-reference is a WorkTable Scan whose row estimate is `recursive_worktable_factor` times the non-recursive term's rows ([allpaths.c#set_worktable_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3016-L3021), [costsize.c#set_cte_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5990-L5998)). `cost_recursive_union()` then assumes ten iterations ([costsize.c#cost_recursive_union](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1813-L1845)). Section 9.7 works through E9.10.

#### 9.5 Eligibility and comparison

| Construct | Becomes | Eligible when | Chosen by cost? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x IN (SELECT ...)` in top-level `WHERE` | `JOIN_SEMI`, then semi-join or unique-ify paths | Comparison non-volatile, uses outer columns; outer references within `available_rels` ([subselect.c#convert_ANY_sublink_to_join-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1275-L1308)) | Conversion: no. Implementation: yes, `add_path()` ([joinrels.c#populate_joinrel_with_paths-semi](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinrels.c#L992-L1021)) |
| `EXISTS` / `NOT EXISTS` in top-level `WHERE` | `JOIN_SEMI` / `JOIN_ANTI` | Simplifiable, no `WITH`, correlated only in `WHERE`, not volatile ([subselect.c#convert_EXISTS_sublink_to_join-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1387-L1439)) | Implementation only |
| `NOT IN` | Hashed or plain SubPlan | Always a SubPlan | Hashing: by size against `hash_mem`, not by cost |
| Uncorrelated scalar, `EXISTS`, `ARRAY` | InitPlan | Empty `parParam` ([subselect.c#build_subplan-initplans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L374-L449)) | No |
| Correlated scalar | SubPlan per outer row | Outer references present | No |
| Correlated `EXISTS` not converted | `AlternativeSubPlan` | Simplifiable and convertible to `IN` form, hashable ([subselect.c#make_subplan-alternative](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L243-L307)) | Yes: `fix_alternative_subplan()` by expected calls; E9.11 keeps the hashed form, E9.11b the per-row form |
| `LATERAL` subquery | Flattened if simple, else a parameterized subquery path | Chapter 3 pull-up rules | Yes: it competes inside the join search |
| CTE | Inlined subquery, or InitPlan plus CTE Scans | Inlining rules of Step 8 | No: the user's `MATERIALIZED` choice and the reference count decide |

The recurring pattern is that the planner decides the logical form by rule and leaves only the physical implementation to cost comparison. A converted semi join can use hash, merge or nested-loop joins, or a unique-ify step. A SubPlan cannot: its only choices are hashed or not, materialized or not.

#### 9.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `IN` or `EXISTS` inside `OR`, `CASE`, the select list, or under `NOT` (except `NOT EXISTS`) | Not converted ([prepjointree.c#pull_up_sublinks_qual_recurse-and](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L830-L859)) | A SubPlan or `AlternativeSubPlan`; E9.11 |
| Sublink in an outer join's `ON` referencing the preserved side | Not converted: outside `available_rels` ([subselect.c#convert_ANY_sublink_to_join-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1230-L1234)) | Stays a SubPlan |
| `EXISTS` sub-select with aggregates, `HAVING`, `OFFSET`, window functions or `FOR UPDATE` | Not simplified, so not converted ([subselect.c#simplify_EXISTS_query-refusals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1552-L1562)) | SubPlan |
| A subquery in `FROM` with `LIMIT` or `OFFSET`, even `OFFSET 0` | Not pulled up ([prepjointree.c#is_simple_subquery-refusals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L1689-L1700)), and no outer qual is pushed into it ([allpaths.c#subquery_is_pushdown_safe-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3587-L3589)) | An optimization fence: in E3.4b `s.id = 42` stays in a Subquery Scan's Filter over a Seq Scan (`0.00..901.00`) instead of an Index Scan (`0.29..8.30`) |
| `EXISTS (... LIMIT 0)` | Not simplified ([subselect.c:1586-1592](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1586-L1592)) | SubPlan |
| Hashed SubPlan output larger than `hash_mem` | Not hashed ([subselect.c#subplan_is_hashable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L712-L728)) | Plain SubPlan over Material, scanned per outer row |
| Non-hashable or non-strict comparison operator | Not hashed ([subselect.c#hash_ok_operator](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L832-L867)) | Same as above |
| Recursive CTE, CTE with `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`MERGE`, or with volatile functions | Never inlined ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-inline](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L910-L955)) | Planned once; data-modifying CTEs are covered in Chapter 13 |
| Recursive term's size unknown | Fixed guesses: worktable factor and ten iterations ([costsize.c#cost_recursive_union-iterations](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1824-L1831)) | E9.10: 31 rows estimated for a chain that the query limits to 50 levels |
| CTE statistics for a recursive self-reference or appendrel | Not used ([selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable-cte](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5421-L5431)) | Default estimates |
| CTE plan not built yet, as in a side reference from another CTE | Statistics lookup gives up ([selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable-cte-subroot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5460-L5503)) | Default estimates |
| CTE Scan | No parallel paths: a CTE's InitPlan is marked parallel-unsafe ([subselect.c:1005-1009](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L1005-L1009)) | Chapter 12 |

#### 9.7 Formulas and worked examples

Terms: `cpu_tuple_cost` 0.01 and `cpu_operator_cost` 0.0025 (E5.1). `DEFAULT_INEQ_SEL` is 0.3333333333333333 ([selfuncs.h:37](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/selfuncs.h#L37)). A clause the estimator cannot handle gets 0.5, and `NOT` inverts its argument ([clausesel.c:691](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L691), [clausesel.c#clause_selectivity_ext-not](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L798-L806)).

**E9.1: an InitPlan's value is unknown while planning.** The outer filter compares `amount` with a Param, so selectivity falls back to `DEFAULT_INEQ_SEL`: 30,000 × 0.3333 = 10,000 rows estimated, against 14,936 actual. The InitPlan's cost is added to every path of the query level ([subselect.c#SS_charge_for_initplans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L2153-L2164)):

| Input | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| InitPlan total | 601.01 | E9.1 |
| Outer scan total | 601.00 = 226 + 300 + 30,000 × 0.0025 | E9.1; derived as in Chapter 3 |
| `count(*)` transition cost | 10,000 × 0.0025 = 25.00 | derived |
| Aggregate startup, derived | 601.01 + 601.00 + 25.00 = 1,227.01 | matches `cost=1227.01` |

**E9.4: hashing the NOT IN subquery.** Hashing is allowed when `rows × (MAXALIGN(width) + MAXALIGN(heap tuple header))` fits in `hash_mem` ([subselect.c#subplan_is_hashable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L712-L728)). The header is 23 bytes ([htup_details.h:175](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/htup_details.h#L175), [htup_details.h:185](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/htup_details.h#L185)), 24 after 8-byte alignment. So 1,509 × (8 + 24) = 48,288 bytes, far below 4 MB × 2.

The hashed SubPlan costs its whole input once plus one `cpu_operator_cost` per row loaded ([costsize.c#cost_subplan-hashed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4458-L4467)): 601.00 + 1,509 × 0.0025 = 604.77, the scan's startup cost. The scan then adds 22 pages, 2,000 × 0.01 and 2,000 × 0.0025 for the `=` test: 604.77 + 22 + 20 + 5 = 651.77. Its 1,000-row estimate is 2,000 × (1 − 0.5).

**E9.10: the recursive chain.** Inputs from the plan: the non-recursive term returns 1 row at cost 4.29; the recursive term's Nested Loop costs 13.13.

| Step | Default factor 10 | Forced factor 100 |
|---|---|---|
| WorkTable rows = factor × 1 | 10 | 100 |
| After `depth < 50` at 0.3333 | 3 (estimated `rows=3`) | 33 (estimated `rows=33`) |
| Recursive Union rows = 1 + 10 × term rows | 1 + 30 = 31 | 1 + 330 = 331 |
| Total cost = 4.29 + 10 × term cost + 0.01 × rows | 4.29 + 131.30 + 0.31 = 135.90 | 4.29 + 441.50 + 3.31 = 449.10; the plan prints 449.11 because 44.15 is itself rounded |

The formula comes from `cost_recursive_union()` ([costsize.c#cost_recursive_union](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1813-L1845)). The chain really walks 50 levels, so both estimates are guesses; the factor only moves the guess.

**E9.11: why the hashed form wins for many outer rows.** Terms: `num_exec` is the expected number of evaluations; `per_call_cost` and `startup_cost` are the SubPlan's own estimates from `cost_subplan()` ([costsize.c#cost_subplan-hashed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4458-L4467), [costsize.c#cost_subplan-exists](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4489-L4493), [costsize.c#cost_subplan-startup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4508-L4519)).

| Step | Value | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| Output rows: 2,000 × (0.1 + 0.5 − 0.1 × 0.5) | 1,100, printed `rows=1100`. `region = 'west'` is the 0.1 MCV frequency (E4.1); a SubPlan qual gets the default 0.5 ([clausesel.c:691](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L691)); `OR` combines as `s1 + s2 − s1 × s2` ([clausesel.c:415](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L415)) | derived, estimated |
| `num_exec` = 2 × 1,100 | 2,200 ([setrefs.c#NUM_EXEC-rationale](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L100-L116)) | derived |
| Hashed alternative: startup = 601.00 + 1,509 × 0.0025; per call = one `=` test, 0.0025 | 604.77 + 2,200 × 0.0025 = 610.27 | derived from E9.11 |
| Per-row alternative: per-row qual cost implied by the printed total, (106,111.07 − 22 pages − 2,000 × 0.01) / 2,000 | about 53.03 per call, startup 0; for 2,200 calls about 116,670 | derived from E9.11 |
| Kept | hashed `SubPlan 2` | measured, E9.11 |

The printed startup of `0.00` and total of `106111.07` belong to the per-row alternative, which cost estimation charges while the choice is open. With the hashed plan the same scan would be priced near 604.77 + 22 + 2,000 × (0.01 + 0.0025 + 0.0025) = 656.77 (derived, following E9.4's arithmetic).

**E9.11b: why the per-row form wins for one outer row.** The outer scan returns 1 row, so `num_exec` = 2. The per-row SubPlan is an Index Only Scan costing 0.29..4.55 for 15 rows. As an `EXISTS`, one call costs its startup plus the run cost of one row: 0.29 + (4.55 − 0.29) / 15 = 0.57. Two calls cost about 1.15 (derived).

The hashed form would read every order, because its sub-select has no inner-only condition. It still qualifies for hashing, since 30,000 × (8 + 24) = 960,000 bytes fits in `hash_mem`. Assuming the 526.00 sequential scan of E5.1, it would start at 526.00 + 30,000 × 0.0025 = 601.00 (derived). The per-row form is cheaper by a factor of about 500, so `fix_alternative_subplan()` keeps `SubPlan 1`.

**E9.9: a CTE Scan's cost.** `cost_ctescan()` charges `cpu_tuple_cost` twice plus the filter per CTE row ([costsize.c#cost_ctescan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1716-L1724)): 30,000 × (0.01 + 0.01 + 0.0025) = 675.00, as printed.

#### 9.8 Planning versus execution

| The planner fixes | The executor decides |
|---|---|
| Which sublinks become joins, InitPlans, hashed SubPlans or plain SubPlans | When an InitPlan runs: lazily, the first time its Param is read ([nodeSubplan.c#ExecSetParamPlan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeSubplan.c#L1050-L1060), [execExprInterp.c#ExecEvalParamExec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execExprInterp.c#L2517-L2530)) |
| Which alternative of an `AlternativeSubPlan` is kept, at `set_plan_references()` time | Nothing about that choice; only the kept SubPlan exists in the plan |
| That a SubPlan is hashed | Building the hash table on first use and tracking NULL rows so that `NOT IN` returns UNKNOWN correctly ([nodeSubplan.c#ExecHashSubPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeSubplan.c#L114-L181)) |
| That a CTE is materialized once | Each CTE Scan reading a shared tuplestore through its own read pointer, and running the CTE plan only as far as some reader needs ([nodeCtescan.c#ExecInitCteScan-leader](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeCtescan.c#L220-L246), [nodeCtescan.c#CteScanNext-fetch](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeCtescan.c#L87-L109)) |
| An estimate of ten recursive iterations | The real number of iterations: the loop stops when an iteration adds no row to the intermediate table ([nodeRecursiveunion.c#ExecRecursiveUnion](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeRecursiveunion.c#L112-L138)) |
| That a data-modifying CTE is a separate subplan | Running it to completion even if the main query reads none of its rows ([execMain.c#ExecPostprocessPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L1480-L1500)) |

#### 9.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ANALYZE` of a table under a CTE or subquery | Column statistics old | New statistics | The next planning of the outer query sees them through the CTE (17) or subquery |
| `SET recursive_worktable_factor` | Factor 10 | New factor, session scope (`PGC_USERSET`) ([guc_tables.c#recursive_worktable_factor](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3798-L3808)) | New WorkTable estimates; E9.10 |
| `SET work_mem` or `hash_mem_multiplier` | A subplan fits in `hash_mem` | It may no longer fit | Hashing decisions change at the next planning |
| `SET enable_material = off` | Uncorrelated SubPlans get a Material node | No Material node ([subselect.c#build_subplan-material](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L522-L534)) | Rescans rerun the subplan |
| Adding or removing a second reference to a CTE in the query text | Inlined | Materialized (or the reverse) | Different plan shape; `MATERIALIZED`/`NOT MATERIALIZED` pins it |

#### 9.10 Regression coverage and gaps

| Mechanism | Tests at the pin |
|---|---|
| Correlated `ANY` pull-up (17) | [subselect.sql#direct-correlated-any](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/subselect.sql#L1060-L1097) |
| Semi- and anti-join recognition; `NOT IN` is not an anti join | [join.sql#semijoin-antijoin](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/join.sql#L776-L798) |
| `EXISTS` with `LIMIT` simplification | [subselect.sql#exists-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/subselect.sql#L156-L166) |
| Hashed versus plain `EXISTS` SubPlan | [subselect.sql#alternative-subplan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/subselect.sql#L577-L590) |
| Hashed `NOT IN` subplans | [subselect.sql#hashed-subplans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/subselect.sql#L478-L511) |
| CTE inlining rules | [subselect.sql#cte-inlining](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/subselect.sql#L969-L1012) |
| CTE statistics and pathkeys (17) | [with.sql#cte-stats-pathkeys](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/with.sql#L362-L379) |
| Recursive CTEs | [with.sql#recursive](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/with.sql#L17-L25) and the rest of the file |
| `LATERAL` | [join.sql#lateral](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/join.sql#L2435-L2462) and following cases |
| `MULTIEXPR` sublinks in `UPDATE ... SET (a, b) = (SELECT ...)` | [update.sql#multiexpr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/update.sql#L64-L75) |

Gaps: no regression test at the pin sets `recursive_worktable_factor`; E9.10 is the only evidence here. `ARRAY(SELECT ...)` and `MULTIEXPR` InitPlans have no tutorial experiment.

#### 9.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: a sub-select inside an expression, or a `WITH` query.
2. Transformation: at the top level of `WHERE`, `IN` and `EXISTS` become semi joins and `NOT EXISTS` an anti join; in 17 a correlated `IN` qualifies too. `NOT IN` stays a SubPlan because of NULL semantics.
3. Interaction: the join search picks a semi-join or unique-ify implementation by cost.
4. Transformation: every other sub-select becomes an InitPlan when uncorrelated, or a SubPlan rerun per outer row, hashed when it fits in `hash_mem`.
5. Observed result: CTEs referenced once are inlined; others run once and are scanned, passing their statistics and sort order upward in 17. Recursive CTEs rest on the worktable factor and a ten-iteration guess.
6. Refresh: changing `hash_mem`, `recursive_worktable_factor`, `MATERIALIZED` or the underlying statistics changes the outcome at the next planning run.

### Chapter 10. Plan operations above scans and joins

#### 10.1 Main idea

After the scans and joins, a query may still need to compute output expressions, expand set-returning functions, group and aggregate, evaluate [window functions](../../../glossary.md#window-function), remove duplicates, sort, and limit. `grouping_planner()` plans these steps in that fixed order. Each step becomes a new upper relation whose paths are built on the paths of the step below ([planner.c#grouping_planner-upper](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1697-L1766)).

The central idea is ordering. Most of these steps can be done either by hashing or by sorting, and a sort can be avoided when the rows already arrive in a useful order. So the planner decides early which order to ask the scans and joins for, and later compares hashed, fully sorted, incrementally sorted and presorted variants by cost ([planner.c#standard_qp_callback-query_pathkeys](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3651-L3683)).

Three results surprise many readers. An aggregate with its own `ORDER BY` makes the whole grouping sorted, without a cost comparison, and the cheaper-looking alternative never enters the competition (E10.4). A `GROUP BY` may be evaluated in a different key order than written, new in 17 (E10.5). And `UNION` estimates that every input row is distinct (E10.10). The chapter uses E10.1 to E10.12 and E5.2 to E5.4.

#### 10.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `group_pathkeys`, `window_pathkeys`, `distinct_pathkeys`, `sort_pathkeys` | The orderings each upper step would like its input in ([planner.c#standard_qp_callback-group-pathkeys](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3531-L3583), [planner.c#standard_qp_callback-other-pathkeys](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3588-L3627)) | `standard_qp_callback()`, called inside `query_planner()` | current, from the query | the choice of `query_pathkeys` and every sorted variant |
| `query_pathkeys` | The one ordering the scan/join search is asked to produce cheaply: grouping, else the first window, else DISTINCT when it has more keys than ORDER BY, else ORDER BY, else a set operation's order ([planner.c#standard_qp_callback-query_pathkeys](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3651-L3683)) | the same callback | current | which presorted join and scan paths survive (chapter 8) |
| `PathTarget`s: final, sort input, grouping, scan/join | The column lists each stage must output ([planner.c#grouping_planner-targets](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1564-L1622)) | built from the target list after `query_planner()` | current | projection placement and width estimates |
| `limit_tuples`, `tuple_fraction` | How many rows the query will read: an absolute bound for a sort, a fraction for choosing fast-start paths ([planner.c#grouping_planner-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1353-L1367)) | `preprocess_limit()` from constant `LIMIT` and `OFFSET` | estimate; unknown for parameters | bounded sort costs, tuple fraction choices |

#### 10.3 Logic map

```text
grouping_planner(root, tuple_fraction)
 [A] LIMIT/OFFSET constants -> tuple_fraction, limit_tuples
 set operation? --------------------------------------> plan_set_operations   [B]
 otherwise:
 [C] preprocess_targetlist, aggregates, window clauses,
     MIN/MAX rewrite attempt (adds a MinMaxAgg path early)
 [D] query_planner(standard_qp_callback):
     callback sets group/window/distinct/sort pathkeys and query_pathkeys
     -> scan/join relation (unsorted paths, plus presorted ones)
 [E] targets: final, sort-input, window-input, grouping-input, scan/join;
     split around set-returning functions (ProjectSet levels)
 [F] grouping or aggregates?  create_grouping_paths:
       degenerate (HAVING without grouping)? -> special path
       sortable? -> for each input path and each useful GROUP BY key order:
                    presorted | incremental sort | full sort -> Agg/Group
       hashable and no ordered aggregates? -> HashAggregate (priced with spill)
       partial aggregation? -> Partial + Finalize (chapters 11, 12)
       grouping sets? -> sorted rollups, hashed sets, or MixedAggregate
 [G] window functions? create_window_paths: sort per window clause
     (incremental when presorted) -> WindowAgg, run condition on top one
 [H] DISTINCT? create_distinct_paths: Unique over sorted input,
     or HashAggregate unless DISTINCT ON or enable_hashagg is off
 [I] ORDER BY? create_ordered_paths: presorted, incremental or full sort,
     bounded by limit_tuples
 [J] final relation: LockRows, Limit, ModifyTable on each surviving path
     each stage: FDW GetForeignUpperPaths, then create_upper_paths_hook
```

- [A] [planner.c#grouping_planner-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1353-L1367)
- [B] [planner.c#grouping_planner-setops](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1371-L1377)
- [C] [planner.c#grouping_planner-preprocess](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1470-L1517)
- [D] [planner.c#grouping_planner-query_planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1553), [planner.c#standard_qp_callback-query_pathkeys](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3651-L3683)

#### 10.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: decide the useful orderings before the join search

`query_planner()` calls `standard_qp_callback()` once the equivalence classes are known. The callback turns `GROUP BY`, the first window clause, `DISTINCT` and `ORDER BY` into pathkeys, and picks one of them as `query_pathkeys`: grouping first, else the first window, else `DISTINCT` when it needs more sort keys than `ORDER BY`, else `ORDER BY` ([planner.c#standard_qp_callback-query_pathkeys](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3651-L3683)).

The consequence is that an index scan or merge join producing that order can survive the scan and join stages even when it costs more than an unsorted alternative. In 17 the callback also computes `setop_pathkeys` when the query is a branch of a set operation, so that a branch can deliver sorted output for a merged `UNION` ([planner.c#standard_qp_callback-setop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3629-L3649)).

##### Step 2: place projections and set-returning functions

After the join search, `grouping_planner()` builds the target lists each later stage must output ([planner.c#grouping_planner-targets](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1564-L1622)). A projection is usually folded into the node below it; a separate `Result` node appears only when that node cannot project ([pathnode.c#create_projection_path-no-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L2724-L2740)).

A set-returning function in the select list must sit at the top level of a [ProjectSet](../../../glossary.md#projectset) node. `split_pathtarget_at_srfs()` splits the target list into levels, and `adjust_paths_for_srfs()` stacks one ProjectSet per level ([tlist.c#split_pathtarget_at_srfs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/tlist.c#L823-L850), [planner.c#adjust_paths_for_srfs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6577-L6600)). In E10.1, two customers times three series values give the estimated 6 rows.

##### Step 3: group and aggregate

`create_grouping_paths()` first decides what is possible. Sorted grouping needs sortable grouping operators. Hashed grouping needs a `GROUP BY`, hashable operators, and no aggregate with its own `DISTINCT` or `ORDER BY`, because the executor cannot hash those. Partial aggregation needs a combine function for every aggregate ([planner.c#create_grouping_paths-flags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3856-L3896), [prepagg.c#preprocess_aggref-combinefn](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepagg.c#L288-L299)).

For sorted grouping, `add_paths_to_grouping_rel()` walks every input path and every useful key order. An already sorted input is used as is; one sorted on a prefix gets an [incremental sort](../../../glossary.md#incremental-sort); the cheapest input gets a full sort ([planner.c#make_ordered_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7028-L7070), [planner.c#add_paths_to_grouping_rel-sorted](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7094-L7160)). For hashed grouping it adds one `HashAggregate` over the cheapest input, whose cost includes the expected spill to disk ([planner.c#add_paths_to_grouping_rel-hashed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7236-L7265), [costsize.c#cost_agg-spill](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2742-L2760)).

##### Step 4: reorder GROUP BY keys to fit the input (new in 17)

`GROUP BY a, b` does not require input sorted by `a` then `b`; any order of the keys works for sorted grouping. In 17, `get_useful_group_keys_orderings()` offers two orders. The first is the one `preprocess_groupclause()` chose, the written order moved to match `ORDER BY` where possible. The second, when an input path is sorted on some of the keys, reorders the keys to match that path ([pathkeys.c#get_useful_group_keys_orderings](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/pathkeys.c#L465-L515)). Both were committed in the 17 development cycle: `0452b461bc` added the reordering and `505c008ca3` restored `preprocess_groupclause()`, which the first commit had removed.

The reordered path then competes by cost. In E10.5, with hashing switched off to expose the sorted variants (forced setting), the reordered plan groups by `customer_id, status` over the `customer_id` index with an incremental sort: 2746.19. With reordering also switched off, the written order needs a full sort: 3086.90 (Estimated, E10.5).

##### Step 5: presorted aggregates

When aggregates have their own `ORDER BY` or `DISTINCT`, `adjust_group_pathkeys_for_groupagg()` appends the ordering that suits the most aggregates to the grouping pathkeys, and marks those aggregates as presorted ([planner.c#adjust_group_pathkeys_for_groupagg](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3255-L3300), [planner.c#standard_qp_callback-ordered-aggs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3573-L3578)). This is a rule, not a cost choice: once the pathkeys are longer, every sorted grouping path must deliver that order.

##### Step 6: windows

`create_window_paths()` plans one `WindowAgg` per window clause. For each it sorts the input to the window's partition and order keys, incrementally when a prefix is already sorted ([planner.c#create_one_window_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4689-L4730)).

A condition such as `rn <= 2` on the output of `row_number()` in an outer query becomes a run condition. `check_and_push_window_quals()` asks the window function's support function whether it is monotonic; if so, the qual is attached to the `WindowAgg` as its run condition ([allpaths.c#check_and_push_window_quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2407-L2432), [allpaths.c#find_window_run_conditions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2214-L2275), [windowfuncs.c#window_row_number_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/windowfuncs.c#L98-L115)).

The executor uses the run condition to stop work early. Once it fails, a `WindowAgg` with no `PARTITION BY` stops altogether; with one, it passes the rest of the partition through without computing the window functions, and the top `WindowAgg` filters those rows out ([nodeWindowAgg.c#runcondition](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeWindowAgg.c#L2347-L2400)).

##### Step 7: DISTINCT, ORDER BY and LIMIT

`DISTINCT` gets a `Unique` over sorted input and a `HashAggregate`. When a sorted path exists, `DISTINCT ON` or `enable_hashagg = off` removes the hashed one; when none exists, hashing is tried anyway ([planner.c#create_final_distinct_paths-hash](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5250-L5283)). `ORDER BY` keeps any already sorted path and sorts or incrementally sorts the others, passing `limit_tuples` so a bounded top-N sort is priced ([planner.c#create_ordered_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5336-L5384)).

Finally, every surviving path gets `LockRows` if the query locks rows, `Limit` if it has a limit, and `ModifyTable` for a write (chapter 13) ([planner.c#grouping_planner-final](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1766-L1825)). `Limit` charges only the fraction of its input's run cost that the limit reads ([pathnode.c#adjust_limit_rows_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3881-L3924)).

##### Step 8: MIN and MAX

Before the join search, `preprocess_minmax_aggregates()` checks whether every aggregate is a MIN or MAX over a single table, with no `GROUP BY`, window function or CTE ([planagg.c#preprocess_minmax_aggregates-reject](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planagg.c#L90-L140)). For each aggregate it plans `SELECT col FROM tab WHERE col IS NOT NULL ORDER BY col LIMIT 1` and needs a path already sorted on the column, which in practice means an index ([planagg.c#header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planagg.c#L6-L17), [planagg.c#build_minmax_path-sorted](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planagg.c#L436-L446)).

If every aggregate has such a path, a `MinMaxAggPath` joins the grouping relation and competes by cost with the ordinary aggregate ([planagg.c#preprocess_minmax_aggregates-add](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planagg.c#L204-L224)). In E10.7 it becomes two InitPlans with a one-row `Limit` each; for `max(amount)`, which has no index, the plain `Aggregate` remains.

##### Step 9: set operations

`plan_set_operations()` plans each branch as a subquery. `UNION ALL` is an `Append` ([prepunion.c#generate_union_paths-all](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1004-L1011)). `UNION` tries a `HashAggregate` over the `Append`, a sort plus `Unique`, and, when every branch offers rows sorted the right way, a `MergeAppend` plus `Unique` ([prepunion.c#generate_union_paths-hash](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L904-L941), [prepunion.c#generate_union_paths-sort](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L942-L976), [prepunion.c#generate_union_paths-mergeappend](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L977-L1001)). The `MergeAppend` variant was committed in the 17 development cycle (`66c0185a3d`). It was reverted by `7204f35919` on 2024-05-20 and restored by `12933dc604` the next day, whose message says the aim was to ship beta1 with the feature. E10.10's last query uses it.

`INTERSECT` and `EXCEPT` use a [`SetOp`](../../../glossary.md#set-operation) node over an `Append` of flagged branches, hashed or sorted ([prepunion.c#generate_nonunion_paths-order](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1081-L1097), [prepunion.c#generate_nonunion_paths-estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1124-L1144)). For `INTERSECT` the branch with fewer groups goes first, to keep the hash table small, which is why E10.10 lists `*SELECT* 2` first.

#### 10.5 Eligibility and comparison

| Operation | Hashed variant eligible when | Sorted variant eligible when | How they compete |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GROUP BY` | hashable operators, no ordered aggregates, `enable_hashagg` (else `disable_cost`) ([planner.c#create_grouping_paths-hash-flag](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3872-L3890), [costsize.c#cost_agg-hashed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2722-L2738)) | sortable operators | `add_path()`; hash wins for few groups (E10.3 first query), sorted wins when an index delivers the order (E10.3 second) |
| Grouping sets | some sets hashable and the hash tables fit `hash_mem` | rollups of sortable sets | hashed, sorted and mixed (`MixedAggregate`) paths ([planner.c#consider_groupingsets_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4211-L4282)) |
| `DISTINCT` | hashable; when a sorted path exists, also no `DISTINCT ON` and `enable_hashagg` on (a hard switch, not a cost penalty) ([planner.c#create_final_distinct_paths-hash](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5250-L5283)) | sortable | `add_path()` |
| `UNION` | hashable | sortable; `MergeAppend` needs presorted branches | `add_path()` over all variants |
| `INTERSECT`, `EXCEPT` | both hashable and sortable: hashed if the table fits `hash_mem` and costs no more ([prepunion.c#choose_hashed_setop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1290-L1333), [prepunion.c#choose_hashed_setop-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1346-L1365)) | sortable | a cost comparison inside `choose_hashed_setop()`, not `add_path()` |
| `ORDER BY` | not applicable | always | presorted, incremental and full sorts compete |
| MIN/MAX | not applicable | a presorted path per aggregate | `MinMaxAggPath` against the ordinary aggregate |

If neither hashing nor sorting is possible for a set operation, planning fails with "could not implement" ([prepunion.c#choose_hashed_setop-error](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1304-L1320)). Ordered aggregates (Step 5) and DISTINCT ON remove the hashed variant by rule before any cost is compared.

#### 10.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| An aggregate with `ORDER BY` or `DISTINCT` | hashed grouping is not offered ([planner.c#create_grouping_paths-hash-flag](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3872-L3890)); presorted input is required when `enable_presorted_aggregate` is on | E10.4: the chosen plan costs 2666.19 while the forced alternative prints 1665.15, because the per-group sorts inside `Agg` are not priced ([prepagg.c#get_agg_clause_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepagg.c#L560-L617), [nodeAgg.c#aggsortrequired](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L4164-L4182)) |
| Volatile functions in an aggregate's `ORDER BY` | never used for presorting ([planner.c#adjust_group_pathkeys_for_groupagg-volatile](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3268-L3279)) | each aggregate sorts on its own |
| Grouping sets | no partitionwise aggregation ([planner.c#create_grouping_paths-partitionwise](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3910-L3913)); no key reordering ([pathkeys.c#get_useful_group_keys_orderings-gsets](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/pathkeys.c#L488-L492)) | fewer alternatives |
| `UNION` without `ALL` | output groups estimated as all input rows ([prepunion.c#generate_union_paths-groups](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L888-L902)) | E10.10: 1709 estimated; hash tables and later steps are sized for the worst case |
| A LIMIT or OFFSET that is not a constant | `preprocess_limit()` assumes 10 % of the rows are wanted, and `Limit` costs an unknown count or offset as 10 % of its input ([planner.c#preprocess_limit-default](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2536-L2544), [pathnode.c#adjust_limit_rows_costs-default](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3891-L3908)) | fast-start paths are favored by a guess, not by the real value |
| Grouping, aggregates, windows or SRFs present | `limit_tuples` is not passed down to the scan/join stage ([planner.c#grouping_planner-limit_tuples](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1519-L1534)) | a LIMIT above an aggregate cannot bound a sort below it |
| MIN/MAX with `GROUP BY`, a join, a CTE, or any non-MIN/MAX aggregate | no rewrite ([planagg.c#preprocess_minmax_aggregates-reject](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planagg.c#L90-L140)) | ordinary aggregation scans all rows |
| Hash spill underestimated | the executor enters spill mode when memory runs out ([nodeAgg.c#hash_agg_check_limits](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L1849-L1870)) | correct results, more I/O than planned (E5.4b) |

#### 10.7 Formulas and worked examples

##### Aggregation costs (E10.3, E10.5, E10.9)

`cost_agg()` charges, per input row, the aggregates' transition functions and one comparison or hash per grouping column, and per group the final function and one `cpu_tuple_cost` ([costsize.c#cost_agg-sorted](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2703-L2720), [costsize.c#cost_agg-hashed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2722-L2738)). With `cpu_operator_cost` 0.0025 and `count(*)`'s transition function at one operator cost:

| Plan (Estimated) | Input total | + transition 0.0025 x 30000 | + keys x 0.0025 x 30000 | + 0.01 x groups | Derived | Plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E10.3 `GROUP BY status`, hashed | 526.00 | 75 | 1 key: 75 | 3 groups: 0.03 | 676.00..676.03 | 676.00..676.03 |
| E10.3 `GROUP BY customer_id`, index order | 586.29 | 75 | 1 key: 75 | 2000: 20 | 756.29 | 756.29 |
| E10.5 hashed, two keys | 526.00 | 75 | 2 keys: 150 | 3000: 30 | 751.00..781.00 | 751.00..781.00 |
| E10.5 reordered, incremental sort (forced setting) | 2491.19 | 75 | 2 keys: 150 | 3000: 30 | 2746.19 | 2746.19 |
| E10.5 written order, full sort (forced setting) | 2831.90 | 75 | 2 keys: 150 | 3000: 30 | 3086.90 | 3086.90 |
| E10.9 `DISTINCT status`, hashed (no aggregate) | 526.00 | 0 | 1 key: 75 | 3: 0.03 | 601.00..601.03 | 601.00..601.03 |

For hashed aggregation the startup cost carries all the input work, because no group can be emitted before the whole input is read; the sorted form starts with its input ([costsize.c#cost_agg-hashed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2722-L2738)).

##### Why a presorted aggregate looks dearer (E10.4)

`array_agg(amount ORDER BY amount)` grouped by `customer_id` (Estimated, E10.4):

| Setting | Plan | Total cost |
|---|---|---|
| `enable_presorted_aggregate` on (default) | `GroupAggregate` over `Incremental Sort` (customer_id, amount), presorted on customer_id | 2666.19 |
| off (forced setting) | `GroupAggregate` directly over the index scan on customer_id | 1665.15 |

Both totals decompose the same way: 1490.15 (index scan) + 75 (transition) + 75 (key compare) + 5 (final function, 0.0025 x 2000) + 20 (0.01 x 2000) = 1665.15, and 2491.19 + 175 = 2666.19. What the second plan omits is the 2000 small sorts that `Agg` itself runs, one per group, because `aggsortrequired` is set for an aggregate that is not presorted ([nodeAgg.c#aggsortrequired](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L4164-L4182)). The planner never compares the two: the default rule fixes the grouping pathkeys first (Step 5).

##### LIMIT fractions (E10.11)

`ORDER BY ordered_at LIMIT 10 OFFSET 1000` over an index scan costing 0.29..1015.29 for 30000 rows (Estimated, E10.11):

| Term | Formula | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Startup | 0.29 + 1015.00 x 1000 / 30000 | 34.12 |
| Total | 34.12 + 1015.00 x 10 / 30000 | 34.46 |

These match the plan's `Limit (cost=34.12..34.46 rows=10)` ([pathnode.c#adjust_limit_rows_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3881-L3924)). The offset rows count toward startup because they must be read before the first output row.

##### Window cost and the 17 startup charge (E10.8)

`cost_windowagg()` charges per input row each window function's cost, one comparison per partition and order column, and one `cpu_tuple_cost` ([costsize.c#cost_windowagg-cpu](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3120-L3132)). For `row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY amount DESC)`: (0.0025 + 2 x 0.0025 + 0.01) x 30000 = 525, and 2491.19 + 525 = 3016.19, the plan's total.

In 17 the startup cost also includes the rows the WindowAgg must read before its first output ([costsize.c#cost_windowagg-startup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3139-L3151)). With a frame ending at the current row, that is the first row plus one more to confirm the next row is not a peer, so 2 rows ([costsize.c#get_windowclause_startup_tuples](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3033-L3041)). The charge is (3016.19 - 1.33) / 30000 x (2 - 1) = 0.10, the step from the sort's 1.33 to the WindowAgg's 1.43. This was committed in the 17 development cycle (`3900a02c97`).

##### Grouping-set sizes (E10.6)

`ROLLUP (region, tier)` estimates (region, tier) + (region) + () = 12 + 4 + 1 = 17 groups, and `CUBE` adds (tier): 12 + 4 + 3 + 1 = 20 (Estimated, E10.6). Both plans are a single `MixedAggregate`: it hashes the non-empty sets and computes the empty set `()` as a separate unhashed rollup ([planner.c#consider_groupingsets_paths-mixed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4355-L4374)).

##### Set-operation estimates (E10.10)

| Query (Estimated) | Rows | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `UNION` of 1509 cancelled-order customers and 200 western customers | 1709 | all input rows assumed distinct |
| `INTERSECT` | 200 | fewer groups of the two sides ([prepunion.c#generate_nonunion_paths-estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1124-L1144)) |
| `EXCEPT` | 1078 | the left side's estimated groups |
| `UNION` with `ORDER BY` of two presorted index ranges | 200, via `Unique` over `Merge Append` | new in 17 |

#### 10.8 Planning versus execution

| Decided while planning | Decided or adapted while running |
|---|---|
| Sorted or hashed strategy, sort keys, and whether a sort is incremental | incremental sort switches between a full-sort mode and a presorted-prefix mode by group size ([nodeIncrementalSort.c#header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeIncrementalSort.c#L58-L65)); E10.2 shows both group kinds |
| A top-N sort is priced from `limit_tuples` ([planner.c#create_ordered_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5336-L5384)) | `Limit` passes its bound to `Sort` at run time, which switches to a bounded heap ([execProcnode.c#ExecSetTupleBound](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execProcnode.c#L843-L872), [nodeSort.c:123-124](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeSort.c#L123-L124)); E5.2 shows "top-N heapsort" |
| HashAggregate's expected spill is priced | the executor spills when memory runs out ([nodeAgg.c#hash_agg_check_limits](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L1849-L1870)); E5.4b shows 5 batches |
| The window run condition is attached | the WindowAgg stops or passes rows through once the condition fails ([nodeWindowAgg.c#runcondition](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeWindowAgg.c#L2347-L2400)) |
| Ordered aggregates are marked presorted or not | `Agg` sorts per group only for aggregates not marked presorted ([nodeAgg.c#aggsortrequired](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L4164-L4182)) |

#### 10.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ANALYZE` | old distinct counts | new counts | group estimates change hash-versus-sort choices and spill costs |
| New index on grouping, window or sort keys | only explicit sorts | presorted and incremental paths | sorts disappear or shrink (E10.2, E10.3, E10.7) |
| `SET work_mem`, `hash_mem_multiplier` | 4MB, 2 | other memory | spill costs, grouping-set hashing, `choose_hashed_setop()` |
| `SET enable_hashagg`, `enable_sort`, `enable_incremental_sort`, `enable_presorted_aggregate`, `enable_group_by_reordering` | defaults on | a variant penalized or not offered | forced comparisons such as E10.4 and E10.5 |
| Aggregate or window support function changes | installed with the function | different run conditions or window-clause optimizations | only for user-defined functions with `SUPPORT` |

All of these settings have `user` context (E16.1), so `SET` changes them for the session.

| Mechanism | Tests |
|---|---|
| GROUP BY key reordering | [aggregates.sql#group-by-reordering](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/aggregates.sql#L1218-L1250) |
| Presorted aggregates and the off switch | [aggregates.sql#presorted-aggs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/aggregates.sql#L577-L596) |
| MIN/MAX to index scans | [aggregates.sql#minmax](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/aggregates.sql#L346-L352) |
| Window run conditions | [window.sql#run-conditions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/window.sql#L1201-L1240) |
| Grouping sets | [groupingsets.sql#basic](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/groupingsets.sql#L52-L68) |
| UNION with MergeAppend and hashed set operations | [union.sql#hashagg-off](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/union.sql#L141-L152) |
| Incremental sort with LIMIT | [incremental_sort.sql#limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/incremental_sort.sql#L1-L10) |

Gaps: no core test reports the missing cost of per-group aggregate sorts that E10.4 exposes. `create_upper_paths_hook` has no in-core user.

#### 10.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: the query's `GROUP BY`, window, `DISTINCT` and `ORDER BY` clauses.
2. Before the join search, they become the useful orderings, so presorted scan and join paths can survive.
3. For each upper step, the planner builds hashed, fully sorted, incrementally sorted and presorted variants on the step below. Rules remove some before costing: ordered aggregates, `DISTINCT ON`, and `enable_hashagg` for `DISTINCT`.
4. `add_path()` keeps the cheapest per step, and a `LIMIT` charges only the fraction of rows it reads.
5. The executor runs the chosen steps, bounding sorts, spilling hash tables and stopping windows at run time.
6. Refresh: new statistics, indexes or memory settings change the group estimates and orderings, and so the next plan.

### Chapter 11. Handle inheritance and partitioning

#### 11.1 Main idea

A table with children, whether through legacy [inheritance](../../../glossary.md#inheritance) or [declarative partitioning](../../../glossary.md#declarative-partitioning), is planned as an *append relation*. The planner adds one member relation per child, plans each child much like an ordinary table, and puts an [Append or MergeAppend](../../../glossary.md#append-and-mergeappend) node on top that returns the children's rows one after another ([inherit.c#expand_inherited_rtentry](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L61-L84)).

Most of the work is deciding which children not to touch, and when. Declarative partitions are [pruned](../../../glossary.md#partition-pruning) before they are even opened, so pruning also saves planning effort. Legacy children are opened first and then excluded one by one by [constraint exclusion](../../../glossary.md#constraint-exclusion). Values the planner cannot see, such as a prepared statement's parameter or a subquery's result, prune later, in the executor.

The surprising part is how much depends on these rules. A query on one of 256 partitions plans in 29 kB of memory, against 856 kB when every partition stays (Measured, E11.9). A live default partition turns a cheap ordered Append into a MergeAppend (E11.8). And switching on partitionwise join produced a dearer plan than the default in E11.6. This chapter uses experiments E11.1 to E11.9 ([E11.1](#measurement-script)).

#### 11.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RangeTblEntry.inh` | The query names a parent whose children must be read too | parse analysis; `expand_inherited_rtentry()` requires it ([inherit.c#expand_inherited_rtentry-entry](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L85-L104)) | parameter of the query | `add_other_rels_to_query()` ([initsplan.c#add_other_rels_to_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L187-L215)) |
| partition scheme, bounds and `nparts` of a `RelOptInfo` | The partitioning strategy, key and [bounds](../../../glossary.md#partition-bound) of a partitioned table | the table's partition descriptor, read when its `RelOptInfo` is built ([plancat.c#set_relation_partition_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2424-L2446)) | stored in the catalogs, read at planning time | pruning, ordered Append, partitionwise join |
| `live_parts` | Indexes of the partitions that survived plan-time pruning | `prune_append_rel_partitions()` ([inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-prune](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L348-L358)) | estimate-free plan-time result | child creation, `partitions_are_ordered()` |
| `AppendRelInfo` | The column mapping between a parent and one child | built for each child as it is added ([inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-open](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L388-L414)) | current: this query's mapping | translating quals and targets to the child ([allpaths.c#set_append_rel_size-translate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1037-L1076)) |
| `CHECK` constraints of a child | Conditions every row of that child satisfies | `get_relation_constraints()`, immutable ones only ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-constraints](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1688-L1743)) | stored in the catalogs | constraint exclusion |
| `constraint_exclusion` | Which relations constraint exclusion examines: `off`, `partition` (the default) or `on` | a `PGC_USERSET` setting ([guc_tables.c#constraint_exclusion](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4798-L4807)) | parameter | `relation_excluded_by_constraints()` |
| `enable_partition_pruning`, `enable_partitionwise_join`, `enable_partitionwise_aggregate`, `enable_parallel_append`, `enable_async_append` | Switches for the techniques in this chapter; all are `PGC_USERSET` | [guc_tables.c#enable_partition_pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L964-L974), [guc_tables.c#enable_partitionwise_join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L924-L932), [guc_tables.c#enable_partitionwise_aggregate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L934-L942), [guc_tables.c#enable_parallel_append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L944-L952), [guc_tables.c#enable_async_append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L991-L999) | parameter | the functions of steps 11.2 to 11.9 |
| `PartitionPruneInfo` with `initial_pruning_steps`, `exec_pruning_steps`, `execparamids` | Pruning steps the executor runs at startup and on each rescan | `make_partition_pruneinfo()` ([partprune.c#make_partitionedrel_pruneinfo-steps](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L535-L608)) | stored in the plan | `ExecInitPartitionPruning()`, `ExecFindMatchingSubPlans()` |
| parameter values | `$n` values (`PARAM_EXTERN`), and values computed while running (`PARAM_EXEC`: InitPlan results, nested-loop keys) | the caller, or the executor itself ([partprune.c#match_clause_to_partition_key-exec-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L2023-L2050)) | current, known only at run time | initial pruning and execution-time pruning |

Two similar-looking sources of pruning information differ in timing. Partition bounds are stored and read once at planning, so a plan built from them stays valid until a partition is added or removed. Parameter values are current, so the executor must redo the matching whenever they change ([nodeAppend.c#ExecReScanAppend-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L416-L428)).

#### 11.3 Logic map

```text
FROM parent  (RangeTblEntry.inh = true)
|
[A] query_planner: add_other_rels_to_query -> expand_inherited_rtentry
|     partitioned table?
|       yes -> [B] prune on constant quals (prune_append_rel_partitions)
|                  only live partitions: lock, RTE, AppendRelInfo, RelOptInfo (recurse)
```
