```text
|       no  -> legacy inheritance: lock and add every child, the parent as a member too
|
[C] set_append_rel_size, per child
|     constant-false qual?                              -> child is dummy
|     constraint exclusion refutes the quals?           -> child is dummy (excluded)
|     otherwise translate join quals and targets; sum the children's rows
|
[D] set_append_rel_pathlist -> add_paths_to_append_rel
|     Append of cheapest children; Append of cheapest-startup children
|     partial Append / Parallel Append
|     ordered paths: partitions_are_ordered? -> plain Append in bound order
|                    otherwise                -> MergeAppend of ordered children
|     parameterized Appends for nested loops
|
[E] joins: same scheme, equi-join on keys, enable_partitionwise_join
|     -> child joins, then an Append over them
[F] grouping: enable_partitionwise_aggregate, partitioned input
|     GROUP BY covers every partition key -> full: aggregate per partition
|     otherwise, if partial aggregation works -> partial: finalize above the Append
|
[G] create_append_plan: pruning quals left with parameters?
|     -> PartitionPruneInfo: initial steps (stable, PARAM_EXTERN), exec steps (PARAM_EXEC)
|     one child left and no PartitionPruneInfo -> Append removed in setrefs
|
[H] executor
      ExecInitAppend: initial pruning -> "Subplans Removed: N"
      first scan and each rescan with a changed PARAM_EXEC -> execution-time pruning
```

- [A] [planmain.c#query_planner-expand](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planmain.c#L260-L268), [initsplan.c#add_other_rels_to_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L187-L215)
- [B] [inherit.c#expand_inherited_rtentry-partitioned](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L139-L157), [inherit.c#expand_inherited_rtentry-legacy](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L158-L222), [inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-prune](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L348-L358), [inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-open](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L388-L414)
- [C] [allpaths.c#set_append_rel_size-exclusion](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1017-L1036), [plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1602-L1621)
- [D] [allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-simple](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1488-L1502), [allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-partial](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1506-L1552), [allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-parallel-append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1561-L1593), [allpaths.c#generate_orderedappend_paths-partition-order](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1714-L1745)
- [E] [relnode.c#build_joinrel_partition_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L2017-L2052), [joinrels.c#try_partitionwise_join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinrels.c#L1462-L1523)
- [F] [planner.c#create_ordinary_grouping_paths-patype](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4083-L4112)
- [G] [createplan.c#create_append_plan-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1379-L1405), [setrefs.c#set_append_references-single-child](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1760-L1775)
- [H] [nodeAppend.c#ExecInitAppend-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L138-L164), [nodeAppend.c#choose_next_subplan_locally-prune](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L555-L570)

#### 11.4 Step by step

##### Step 11.1: expand the parent late, once its quals are known

Input: a base relation whose range-table entry has `inh` set. Decision: `query_planner()` expands such relations only after it has distributed the quals, so that every restriction on the parent is available for pruning ([planmain.c#query_planner-expand](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planmain.c#L260-L268)).

For a partitioned table, `expand_partitioned_rtentry()` first prunes, then opens and locks only the surviving partitions. It builds a range-table entry, an `AppendRelInfo` and a RelOptInfo for each, and recurses into sub-partitioned children ([inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-prune](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L348-L358), [inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-open](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L388-L414)). The partitioned table itself gets no child entry, because it holds no rows ([inherit.c#expand_inherited_rtentry-no-parent-rte](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L73-L78)).

For legacy inheritance, `find_all_inheritors()` locks every child, and each one, the parent included, becomes a member relation ([inherit.c#expand_inherited_rtentry-legacy](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L158-L222)). Consequence: pruned partitions cost almost nothing to plan, while legacy children are always opened and examined.

##### Step 11.2: prune partitions with constants

Input: the parent's restriction quals. Decision: `prune_append_rel_partitions()` returns every partition when `enable_partition_pruning` is off or there are no quals ([partprune.c#prune_append_rel_partitions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L739-L808)). Otherwise it turns the quals into pruning steps and runs them against the bounds ([partprune.c header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L9-L24)).

At plan time only comparisons with constants qualify. A comparison value that is not a `Const`, and an operator that is not immutable, are rejected for the planner's target ([partprune.c#match_clause_to_partition_key-planner-const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L2008-L2021), [partprune.c#match_clause_to_partition_key-stable-op](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L2052-L2068)). Contradictory quals prune everything.

Output: `live_parts`. In E11.1 the March range left one partition, and `set_append_references()` removed the one-child Append, so the plan scans `orders_r_03` directly ([setrefs.c#set_append_references-single-child](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1760-L1775)). In E11.2 the qual is on `customer_id`, not the key, so all 13 partitions stay and each child gets its own cheapest path.

##### Step 11.3: exclude legacy children by their CHECK constraints

Input: each member relation, after its quals were translated. `set_append_rel_size()` calls `relation_excluded_by_constraints()` for every child and gives an excluded child a dummy path ([allpaths.c#set_append_rel_size-exclusion](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1017-L1036)).

Decision, in order:

1. A constant-false or NULL qual always excludes, whatever the setting ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1602-L1621)).
2. `off` stops there. `partition` continues only for appendrel members. `on` continues for every base relation, and adds a directly named partition's partition constraint ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-mode](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1623-L1657)).
3. Self-contradictory immutable quals exclude ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-self](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1659-L1680)).
4. Otherwise the immutable `CHECK` constraints must refute the quals under strong refutation ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-constraints](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1688-L1743)).

Output: in E11.5, `yr = 2024` refutes `CHECK (yr = 2023)`, so `ledger_2023` disappears under the default `partition` setting and returns when the setting is `off`. The parent `ledger` stays as a member, because it has no such constraint.

##### Step 11.4: build Append paths from the children's paths

Input: every surviving child with its own path list. `add_paths_to_append_rel()` builds these alternatives ([allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-simple](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1488-L1502), [allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-partial](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1506-L1552), [allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-parallel-append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1561-L1593)):

- an Append of each child's cheapest total path, and one of each child's cheapest startup path when fast startup matters, which was added in the 17 development cycle by `a8a968a821` ([allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-startup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1348-L1362));
- a partial Append of partial child paths, and a Parallel Append that may mix partial and non-partial children when `enable_parallel_append` is on (chapter 12);
- ordered Appends and MergeAppends (step 11.5), and parameterized Appends for the inner side of a nested loop.

The Append's cost is the sum of its children plus half a `cpu_tuple_cost` per row ([costsize.c#cost_append-unordered](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2231-L2260), [costsize.c#cost_append-overhead](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2371-L2377)). The alternatives then compete through `add_path()` like any other paths.

##### Step 11.5: keep a sort order without merging when the bounds allow it

Input: the sort orders the query could use. Decision: `generate_orderedappend_paths()` asks `partitions_are_ordered()` whether reading the live partitions in bound order already yields key order ([allpaths.c#generate_orderedappend_paths-partition-order](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1714-L1745)).

`partitions_are_ordered()` says yes for range partitioning unless a default partition is among the live partitions. For list partitioning it says yes unless a live partition interleaves with another. For hash partitioning it always says no ([partbounds.c#partitions_are_ordered](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partbounds.c#L2838-L2886)).

The default partition matters because it may hold keys from anywhere outside the defined ranges, both below the first bound and above the last. So no fixed position for it keeps the output sorted. When the order matches, a plain Append of ordered children is built; otherwise the planner uses a MergeAppend, which merges the children's sorted streams ([allpaths.c#generate_orderedappend_paths-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1760-L1774)).

Output: E11.8 keeps the live default partition and gets a Merge Append at `3.72..1882.83`. E11.8b adds a range that prunes the default, and gets a plain Append at `3.36..1469.36`. E11.8c sorts by `customer_id`, which no partition order provides, so it gets a Merge Append again.

##### Step 11.6: join partition by partition, when forced

Input: a join between two partitioned relations. Eligibility, all of which must hold:

- `enable_partitionwise_join` is on, and no whole-row reference of either table is needed ([allpaths.c#set_append_rel_size-partitionwise](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L960-L969));
- both sides share one partition scheme and are joined by equality on their partition keys ([relnode.c#build_joinrel_partition_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L2017-L2052));
- the bounds are equal, or can be merged so that each partition matches at most one on the other side. Hash partitions merge only when identical ([joinrels.c#compute_partition_bounds](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinrels.c#L1784-L1845), [partbounds.c#partition_bounds_merge-strategy](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partbounds.c#L1103-L1175)).

Calculation: `try_partitionwise_join()` builds one child join per pair and plans it like any join; an Append then collects the child joins ([joinrels.c#try_partitionwise_join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinrels.c#L1462-L1523)).

Consequence: when the partitioned join is the top scan/join relation, `apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths()` throws away its existing paths and rebuilds them from the child relations. That removes the non-partitionwise join paths too ([planner.c#apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths-drop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7754-L7802)). In E11.6 the forced plan is a Parallel Append of four Parallel Hash Joins costing 3519.89, against 3106.56 for the default plan, which joined two Parallel Appends.

##### Step 11.7: aggregate partition by partition, when forced

Input: a grouping step over a partitioned input. Eligibility: `enable_partitionwise_aggregate` is on and the query has no grouping sets ([planner.c#create_grouping_paths-patype](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3904-L3913)).

Decision: full [partitionwise aggregation](../../../glossary.md#partitionwise-aggregation) needs a `GROUP BY` that contains every partition key with the partitioning collation, because then each group lies in one partition. Otherwise partial aggregation is used when every aggregate supports it ([planner.c#create_ordinary_grouping_paths-patype](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4083-L4112), [planner.c#can_partial_agg](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7697-L7722)).

Output: E11.7 groups `orders_h` by its key `id` and gets an Append of four HashAggregates. Grouping by `status` gets four Partial HashAggregates under a Sort and a Finalize GroupAggregate.

##### Step 11.8: hand the executor the pruning it could not do

Input: the chosen Append or MergeAppend and the parent's quals, plus the join quals of a parameterized path. Decision: `create_append_plan()` calls `make_partition_pruneinfo()` only while `enable_partition_pruning` is on and quals remain ([createplan.c#create_append_plan-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1379-L1405), [createplan.c#create_merge_append_plan-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1548-L1561)).

Calculation: the steps are generated twice ([partprune.c#make_partitionedrel_pruneinfo-steps](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L535-L608)):

1. Initial steps are kept only if a usable qual has a stable operator or a non-constant value other than an execution-time parameter, such as `$1`.
2. Execution steps are kept only if a usable qual contains a `PARAM_EXEC` parameter, such as an InitPlan result or a nested-loop key.

If neither kind survives, the plan carries no pruning information ([partprune.c#make_partitionedrel_pruneinfo-none](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L617-L622), [partprune.c#make_partition_pruneinfo-none](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L327-L332)).

##### Step 11.9: prune while starting and while running

Initial pruning is an executor step, not a planner step. It runs once, at executor startup, when `ExecInitAppend()` calls `ExecInitPartitionPruning()`, and only the surviving children are initialized ([nodeAppend.c#ExecInitAppend-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L138-L164), [execPartition.c#ExecInitPartitionPruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execPartition.c#L1790-L1861)). `ExecInitMergeAppend()` does the same for a MergeAppend ([nodeMergeAppend.c#ExecInitMergeAppend-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeMergeAppend.c#L85-L99)). EXPLAIN reports how many were removed as `Subplans Removed` ([explain.c#ExplainMissingMembers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L4398-L4407)).

Plain `EXPLAIN`, without `ANALYZE`, shows this too. `ExplainOnePlan()` always calls `ExecutorStart()`, with `EXEC_FLAG_EXPLAIN_ONLY` when `ANALYZE` is off, and runs the plan only for `ANALYZE` ([explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-executor-start](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L677-L702)). Neither `ExecInitAppend()` nor `ExecInitPartitionPruning()` tests that flag, so startup still prunes ([nodeAppend.c#ExecInitAppend-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L138-L164), [execPartition.c#ExecInitPartitionPruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execPartition.c#L1790-L1861)).

Execution-time pruning runs when the Append first needs a child, and again after a rescan whose changed parameters feed a pruning step ([nodeAppend.c#choose_next_subplan_locally-prune](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L555-L570), [nodeAppend.c#ExecReScanAppend-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L416-L428)). A child pruned every time shows as `(never executed)`.

Output: E11.3b, a plain `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` of the generic plan, already shows `Subplans Removed: 12`, although nothing ran; E11.3c, the same statement with `ANALYZE`, shows the same count and runs only `orders_r_03`. E11.4's InitPlan runs only `orders_r_12` and the default partition. In E11.4b each outer row selects one partition, so March and July run once each and the rest never run.

#### 11.5 Eligibility and comparison

| Alternative | Becomes eligible when | Compared how | Rejected or unavailable when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pruned child set | a partition-key qual compares with a constant through an immutable operator ([partprune.c#match_clause_to_partition_key-planner-const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L2008-L2021)) | not a cost choice: pruned partitions never get a `RelOptInfo` | `enable_partition_pruning` is off, or the qual uses Vars, volatile functions or parameters |
| Excluded legacy child | `constraint_exclusion` covers the relation and immutable `CHECK` constraints refute the quals ([plancat.c#relation_excluded_by_constraints-constraints](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1688-L1743)) | not a cost choice: the child becomes dummy | mutable constraints or quals; `NO INHERIT` constraints when scanning the parent with its children |
| Plain Append | always, from each child's cheapest total path ([allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-simple](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1488-L1502)) | `add_path()` against the other Append paths | a child has only parameterized paths |
| Ordered Append in bound order | `partitions_are_ordered()` holds and the wanted order matches the partition order ([allpaths.c#generate_orderedappend_paths-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1760-L1774)) | cheaper than MergeAppend, since nothing is merged (E11.8b) | a live default partition, interleaved list partitions, hash partitioning (E11.8) |
| MergeAppend | any order some children can provide | against a Sort above an Append | no child provides a useful order |
| Parallel Append | `enable_parallel_append` and a parallel-safe appendrel (chapter 12) | `add_partial_path()`, then Gather | parallel query unavailable |
| Async Append | `enable_async_append`, an unordered and non-parallel-safe Append of more than one child with async-capable children ([createplan.c#create_append_plan-async](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1298-L1301)) | decided while building the plan, not by cost | ordered or parallel Appends; in core, only `postgres_fdw` children qualify |
| Partitionwise join | step 11.6 conditions | the child joins compete inside each child join relation; at the top the non-partitionwise paths are dropped ([planner.c#apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths-drop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7754-L7802)) | setting off (the default), different schemes, no key equi-join, unmergeable bounds |
| Partitionwise aggregation | step 11.7 conditions | `add_path()` inside the grouped relation | setting off (the default), grouping sets, or partial aggregation unsupported for a partial case |

#### 11.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `enable_partition_pruning = off` | plan-time pruning returns every partition, and no `PartitionPruneInfo` is built ([partprune.c#prune_append_rel_partitions-disabled](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L766-L768), [createplan.c:1384](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1384)) | all 256 partitions of `wide_p` are planned: 1,204 kB of planner memory (E11.9) |
| a stable function or `$n` compared with the key | rejected at plan time, kept for initial pruning ([partprune.c#match_clause_to_partition_key-exec-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L2023-L2050)) | a generic plan still reads one partition (E11.3b, E11.3c) |
| a live default partition in range partitioning | `partitions_are_ordered()` returns false ([partbounds.c#partitions_are_ordered-range](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partbounds.c#L2860-L2870)) | a MergeAppend even for the key order (E11.8) |
| a partition dropped after being detached | treated as pruned instead of failing, since `11f1218ce8`, a fix committed in 2024-08 and, per its message, back-patched to 14 ([inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-dropped](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L388-L397)) | a cached plan can still be rebuilt |
| a temporary child of another session | legacy inheritance skips it silently; a partition raises an error ([inherit.c#expand_inherited_rtentry-legacy-temp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L203-L213), [inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-other-temp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L399-L405)) | the query fails for a partitioned table |
| `ONLY partitioned_table` | the relation becomes dummy ([allpaths.c#set_rel_size-excluded](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L394-L401)) | no rows, since the parent holds none |
| a whole-row reference to a partitioned table | partitionwise join is not considered ([allpaths.c#set_append_rel_size-partitionwise](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L960-L969)) | the join is planned over the whole Appends |
| partitionwise join forced on for the top join | the parent's other paths are discarded ([planner.c#apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths-drop-pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7754-L7775)) | the plan can cost more than the default one (E11.6) |
| partitions pruned only at executor startup | their locks are still taken, because a cached plan's range-table relations are locked before it runs ([plancache.c#AcquireExecutorLocks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1780-L1825), [ddl.sgml#ddl-partition-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ddl.sgml#L4985-L4997)) | a generic plan over many partitions still locks all of them |
| an `IS NOT NULL` step combined with another step on a range table with a default partition | before 17.11 the default partition could be pruned wrongly; `31f2acde53`, first in 17.11, marks it in both representations ([partprune.c#get_matching_range_bounds-all-bounds](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c#L2984-L2997)) | the pinned 17.11 returns the rows; 17.10 and earlier could miss them |

#### 11.7 Formulas and worked examples

**Planning cost of partitions (E11.9).** `plan_summary()` reports the planner's memory for `SELECT count(*)` over `wide_p`, which has 256 hash partitions (Measured, E11.9):

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=704.00..704.01 rows=1 width=8) | 256 scan nodes | Memory: used=856kB  allocated=1032kB
 Aggregate  (cost=1.92..1.93 rows=1 width=8) | 1 scan nodes | Memory: used=29kB  allocated=40kB
 Aggregate  (cost=577.92..577.93 rows=1 width=8) | 256 scan nodes | Memory: used=1204kB  allocated=2056kB
 Aggregate  (cost=4.31..4.32 rows=1 width=8) | 1 scan nodes | Memory: used=14kB  allocated=16kB
```

The lines are, in order: no qual; `id = 42` with pruning; `id = 42` with pruning forced off; and `orders WHERE id = 42` as a plain-table baseline. Derived: each extra partition costs about (856 - 29) / 255 = 3.2 kB of planner memory without a qual, and (1204 - 29) / 255 = 4.6 kB when a qual must be copied into every child. Pruning at expansion time avoids that work, because pruned partitions never get a `RelOptInfo` (step 11.1).

**What an excluded child saves (E11.5).** The Append cost adds each child's total cost plus `0.5 x cpu_tuple_cost` per output row ([costsize.c#cost_append-overhead](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2371-L2377), [costsize.c#APPEND_CPU_COST_MULTIPLIER](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L104-L109)). Each 5,000-row child with a filter costs 28 x 1.0 + 5000 x 0.01 + 5000 x 0.0025 = 90.50, the figure printed for both children; `ledger_2024` has 28 pages (Measured, E0.1).

| Plan | Children kept | Append total (Estimated, E11.5) | Derived check |
|---|---|---|---|
| default `partition` | `ledger`, `ledger_2024` | 115.50 | 0 + 90.50 + 0.005 x 5001 = 115.505 |
| `off` (forced setting) | all three | 206.01 | 0 + 90.50 + 90.50 + 0.005 x 5002 = 206.01 |

**Parallel Append workers (E11.6).** With `enable_parallel_append` on, a partial Append asks for at least ⌊log2(children)⌋ + 1 workers, capped by `max_parallel_workers_per_gather` ([allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-workers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1520-L1537)). Derived for four hash partitions: ⌊log2 4⌋ + 1 = 3, then min(3, 2) = 2. That matches `Workers Planned: 2` in both E11.6 plans.

**Partitionwise join forced on (E11.6).** Estimated by the planner, first the default plan, which joins two Parallel Appends:

```text
 Finalize Aggregate  (cost=3106.55..3106.56 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Gather  (cost=3106.33..3106.54 rows=2 width=8)
...
               ->  Parallel Hash Join  (cost=622.22..2012.58 rows=37500 width=0)
...
                     ->  Parallel Append  (cost=0.00..1291.91 rows=37500 width=4)
...
                           ->  Parallel Append  (cost=0.00..465.97 rows=12500 width=4)
```

Then the forced plan (forced setting), a Parallel Append of four Parallel Hash Joins, one per partition pair:

```text
 Finalize Aggregate  (cost=3519.88..3519.89 rows=1 width=8)
...
               ->  Parallel Append  (cost=156.72..2425.91 rows=37500 width=0)
                     ->  Parallel Hash Join  (cost=156.81..563.07 rows=13308 width=0)
...
                     ->  Parallel Hash Join  (cost=156.72..561.77 rows=13297 width=0)
...
                     ->  Parallel Hash Join  (cost=156.63..561.44 rows=13285 width=0)
...
                     ->  Parallel Hash Join  (cost=153.89..552.14 rows=13052 width=0)
...
```

The forced plan is dearer by 413.33 (Derived). It still wins, because at the top scan/join level the join's earlier paths, including the cheaper non-partitionwise one, are discarded and only child-based paths are rebuilt (step 11.6).

#### 11.8 Planning versus execution

| Decision | Made while planning | Made or adapted while running |
|---|---|---|
| Which partitions can match constant quals | plan-time pruning (E11.1) | none |
| Which legacy children can match | constraint exclusion; there is no execution-time exclusion ([ddl.sgml#ddl-partitioning-constraint-exclusion](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ddl.sgml#L5042-L5049)) | none |
| Which partitions match `$n` or a stable function | the plan stores initial pruning steps | executor startup removes the rest, visible even under plain `EXPLAIN` (E11.3b, E11.3c) |
| Which partitions match an InitPlan result or a nested-loop key | the plan stores execution steps and their parameter ids | re-evaluated whenever those parameters change (E11.4, E11.4b) |
| Plain Append versus MergeAppend | fixed in the plan | none |
| Which worker scans which child of a Parallel Append | the plan fixes the children and marks where partial ones start ([createplan.c#create_append_plan-first-partial](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1408-L1411)) | workers pick the next child while running ([nodeAppend.c#choose_next_subplan_for_worker](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L672-L702)) |
| Asynchronous foreign children | the plan marks them async-capable | the executor interleaves their requests |

#### 11.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| a partition is attached or created | the parent's partition descriptor lists N partitions | `StorePartitionBound()` invalidates the parent's and the default partition's relcache entries ([heap.c#StorePartitionBound-invalidate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/heap.c#L3633-L3648)) | cached plans naming the parent are marked invalid and replanned ([plancache.c#PlanCacheRelCallback-relationOids](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2014-L2023)) |
| a partition is detached and dropped | a cached plan may still name it | expansion skips it as pruned (`11f1218ce8`) | replanning succeeds |
| `CHECK` constraint added to or dropped from a child | constraint exclusion used the old set | the next planning reads the new set | the child may now be excluded, or not |
| `SET constraint_exclusion` or an `enable_*` switch | plans built under the old value | only new planning sees the new value | cached plans keep their old shape until replanned |
| a prepared statement runs with new parameters | generic plan with pruning steps | the executor prunes again at startup | no replanning needed (E11.3c) |

#### 11.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- Plan-time and run-time pruning, including prepared statements and `Subplans Removed`: [partition_prune.sql#runtime-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_prune.sql#L460-L507). Pruning in MergeAppend: [partition_prune.sql#mergeappend-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_prune.sql#L955-L990). Constraint exclusion with pruning off: [partition_prune.sql#constraint-exclusion-on](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_prune.sql#L1172-L1187).
- Constraint exclusion of legacy children through `CHECK` constraints, checked by results rather than by plan shape: [rules.sql#constraint-exclusion](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/rules.sql#L939-L971). Exclusion of a self-contradictory `UNION ALL` branch: [union.sql#constraint-exclusion](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/union.sql#L446-L453).
- Ordered Append and the default-partition rule: [inherit.sql#ordered-append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/inherit.sql#L889-L905).
- Partitionwise join, including bound merging and default partitions: [partition_join.sql#setup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_join.sql#L1-L7), [partition_join.sql#advanced-matching](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_join.sql#L565-L612), [partition_join.sql#default-partitions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_join.sql#L692-L750).
- Partitionwise aggregation, full and partial: [partition_aggregate.sql#full-and-partial](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_aggregate.sql#L186-L200).
- Parallel Append: [select_parallel.sql#parallel-append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L16-L44). Async Append: [postgres_fdw.sql#async](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/sql/postgres_fdw.sql#L3852-L3857).
- Partition sets that change under a cached plan: [plancache.sql#partition-add-remove](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/plancache.sql#L160-L176), and a partition added between planning and execution: [partition-addition.spec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/modules/delay_execution/specs/partition-addition.spec#L1-L38).
- Gaps on this page: async Append is not demonstrated, because the loopback server of chapter 15 is not marked `async_capable`. List partitioning and sub-partitioning are not measured here; the regression tests above cover them.

#### 11.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: a parent with children, expanded late, after its quals are placed.
2. Constant key quals prune partitions before they are opened; `CHECK` constraints exclude legacy children after they are.
3. Each survivor is planned as its own relation, and an Append stacks them, or a MergeAppend when a live default partition or another order prevents bound order.
4. When forced, joins and aggregates move below the Append, and the top join keeps only those paths.
5. Values unknown at plan time become pruning steps, and the executor prunes at startup and on each rescan.
6. Refresh: attaching or detaching a partition invalidates the parent, and the next planning sees the new set.

### Chapter 12. Plan parallel execution and JIT

#### 12.1 Main idea

[Parallel query](../../../glossary.md#parallel-query) splits one scan, join or aggregation across a leader and several worker processes. The planner does not parallelize a finished plan. It builds a second kind of path, the partial path, whose rows are divided among processes, and then puts a Gather or Gather Merge node above it to collect the pieces ([pathnode.c#add_partial_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L707-L745), [allpaths.c#generate_gather_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3035-L3098)).

Two things decide whether that happens. First, safety: every function the workers would run must be marked parallel safe, and one parallel-unsafe function turns parallel query off for the whole statement ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-feasibility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L329-L365)). Second, cost: the partial path divides CPU work among processes, but Gather adds a setup cost of 1,000 and 0.1 per row it passes up, and the cheaper total wins ([costsize.c#cost_gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L436-L461)).

[JIT compilation](../../../glossary.md#jit-compilation) is decided in the same way, only later and more simply. The planner compares the finished plan's total cost with three thresholds and records bit flags in the PlannedStmt; the executor compiles only if a JIT provider library loads ([planner.c#standard_planner-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L564-L587), [jit.c#jit_compile_expr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/jit/jit.c#L145-L178)).

Three results are surprising. With two workers planned, the costing counts the leader as 0.4 of a worker. A parallel-restricted function in a scan's filter keeps that scan serial, while the same function in the output list runs in the leader above Gather. And this build sets JIT flags of 25 and 31 for plans it can never compile. Experiments E12.1 to E12.10 show each point ([E12.1](#measurement-script)).

#### 12.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `glob->parallelModeOK`, `maxParallelHazard` | Whether any parallel plan is possible for this statement, and the worst safety level found | `standard_planner()` scans the query with `max_parallel_hazard()` when the cheap tests pass ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-feasibility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L329-L365), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L715-L740)) | computed for this planning run | every `consider_parallel` decision |
| `proparallel` of a function | `s` safe, `r` restricted to the leader, `u` unsafe | `pg_proc`, set by `CREATE FUNCTION ... PARALLEL` ([parallel.sgml#parallel-safety](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/parallel.sgml#L471-L485)) | stored in the catalog | the hazard walker ([clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_test](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L789-L815)) |
| `RelOptInfo.consider_parallel` | This relation may be scanned or joined inside a worker | `set_rel_consider_parallel()` for base relations; both inputs and the join clauses for joins ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L736-L757), [relnode.c#build_join_rel-consider_parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L828-L845)) | computed during planning | partial-path generation |
| `Path.parallel_workers`, `parallel_aware`, `parallel_safe` | Planned workers, whether the node coordinates with other processes, and whether it may run in a worker | set by each path constructor and cost function ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L327-L346)) | estimate | Gather creation and costing |
| `max_parallel_workers_per_gather` | Cap on workers per Gather; 0 disables parallel plans (default 2, `PGC_USERSET`) | [guc_tables.c#max_parallel_workers_per_gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3420-L3428) | parameter | `compute_parallel_worker()` |
| `min_parallel_table_scan_size`, `min_parallel_index_scan_size` | Minimum size, in 8 kB pages, for a worker: 1,024 pages (8 MB) and 64 pages (512 kB) by default (`PGC_USERSET`) | [guc_tables.c#min_parallel_table_scan_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3521-L3529), [guc_tables.c#min_parallel_index_scan_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3532-L3540) | parameter | worker count |
| `parallel_setup_cost`, `parallel_tuple_cost` | Gather's start-up price (1,000) and price per row passed up (0.1) (`PGC_USERSET`) | [guc_tables.c#parallel_setup_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3742-L3751), [guc_tables.c#parallel_tuple_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3731-L3740) | parameter | `cost_gather()`, `cost_gather_merge()` |
| `parallel_leader_participation` | Whether the leader also runs the partial plan (default on, `PGC_USERSET`) | [guc_tables.c#parallel_leader_participation](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1914-L1922) | parameter | the parallel divisor and Gather at run time |
| `parallel_workers` storage parameter | A per-table override of the size rule | `RelationGetParallelWorkers()` read into `rel_parallel_workers` ([plancat.c:205](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L205)) | stored in the catalog | `compute_parallel_worker()` |
| `max_parallel_workers`, `max_worker_processes` | Instance-wide limits on worker processes; `max_worker_processes` needs a restart (`PGC_POSTMASTER`) | [guc_tables.c#max_parallel_workers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3431-L3439), [guc_tables.c#max_worker_processes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3164-L3173) | current, checked only at run time | worker registration ([bgworker.c#RegisterDynamicBackgroundWorker-parallel-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/postmaster/bgworker.c#L996-L1013)) |
| `jit`, `jit_above_cost`, `jit_optimize_above_cost`, `jit_inline_above_cost`, `jit_expressions`, `jit_tuple_deforming` | Whether and how much to JIT, as cost thresholds (100,000, 500,000, 500,000) and switches; all `PGC_USERSET` | [guc_tables.c#jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1925-L1933), [guc_tables.c#jit_above_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3754-L3762), [guc_tables.c#jit_optimize_above_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3765-L3773), [guc_tables.c#jit_inline_above_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3776-L3784), [guc_tables.c#jit_expressions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1964-L1972), [guc_tables.c#jit_tuple_deforming](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1992-L2000) | parameter | `jitFlags` |
| `jit_provider` | The provider library to load, `llvmjit` by default; needs a restart (`PGC_POSTMASTER`) | [guc_tables.c#jit_provider](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4678-L4686) | parameter | `provider_init()` |
| `PlannedStmt.jitFlags`, `parallelModeNeeded` | The JIT work the executor should attempt, and whether the plan needs parallel mode | `standard_planner()` ([planner.c#standard_planner-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L564-L587)) | stored in the plan | `ExecutorStart()`, workers |
| `nworkers_launched` | Workers actually started for a Gather | `LaunchParallelWorkers()` at the first `ExecGather()` call ([nodeGather.c#ExecGather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L137-L209)) | current, run time | EXPLAIN ANALYZE `Workers Launched` |

`Workers Planned` and `Workers Launched` look alike but come from different moments. The first is an estimate fixed in the plan from sizes and settings; the second is what the instance could start when the Gather first ran, limited by the free worker slots at that moment.

#### 12.3 Logic map

```text
Statement enters standard_planner
|
[A] Parallel possible at all?
|     CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK, not standalone, SELECT, no modifying CTE,
|     max_parallel_workers_per_gather > 0, not inside a worker
|       no  -> parallelModeOK = false: no partial paths anywhere
|       yes -> scan the query: any PARALLEL UNSAFE function, NextValueExpr or FOR UPDATE?
|                yes -> parallelModeOK = false
|                no  -> parallelModeOK = true (worst level SAFE or RESTRICTED)
|
[B] Per base relation: consider_parallel?
|     temp table, CTE, tuplestore, table function, LIMIT subquery -> no
|     restricted qual or restricted output expression             -> no
|     otherwise                                                     -> yes
|
[C] Partial paths (only if consider_parallel)
|     parallel seq scan: workers from pages (log base 3 steps), capped
|     parallel index scan (B-tree only) and parallel bitmap heap scan
|     partial joins (outer partial; inner private or Parallel Hash), partial Append,
|     partial aggregation (chapter 10)
|
[D] Gather placement (generate_useful_gather_paths)
|     Gather: cheapest partial path;  Gather Merge: sorted partial paths
|     at base rels (unless it is the whole query), join levels, grouping,
|     and the final scan/join target
|
[E] Compare with the serial paths: add_path on total cost
|     partial cost = CPU / parallel divisor + I/O
|     Gather cost  = + parallel_setup_cost + parallel_tuple_cost x rows
|
[F] standard_planner, after create_plan:
|     debug_parallel_query and a parallel-safe top plan -> single-copy Gather on top
|     jitFlags from top_plan->total_cost and the jit_* settings
|
[G] Execution
      Gather: launch up to num_workers; 0 launched -> the leader runs the plan alone
      JIT: compile only if flags ask and the provider library loads
```

- [A] [planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-feasibility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L329-L365), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-rules](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L847-L871), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L949-L960)
- [B] [allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-relation](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L606-L660), [allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-kinds](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L661-L735), [allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L736-L757)
- [C] [allpaths.c#create_plain_partial_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L790-L806), [indxpath.c#build_index_paths-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L975-L1003), [allpaths.c#create_partial_bitmap_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4163-L4185), [joinpath.c#hash_inner_and_outer-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L2258-L2320)
- [D] [allpaths.c#set_rel_pathlist-gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L541-L557), [allpaths.c#generate_useful_gather_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3190-L3210), [planner.c#gather_grouping_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7599-L7630)
- [E] [costsize.c#cost_seqscan-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L327-L346), [costsize.c#cost_gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L436-L461)
- [F] [planner.c#standard_planner-debug-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L446-L482), [planner.c#standard_planner-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L564-L587)
- [G] [nodeGather.c#ExecGather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L137-L209), [jit.c#jit_compile_expr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/jit/jit.c#L145-L178)

#### 12.4 Step by step

##### Step 12.1: decide once whether parallelism is possible at all

Input: the query and its `cursorOptions`. Decision: `standard_planner()` first checks cheap conditions: the caller passed `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK`, the server is not in single-user mode, the statement is a `SELECT` without a data-modifying CTE, `max_parallel_workers_per_gather` is above zero, and the planner is not itself running in a worker ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-feasibility](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L329-L365)).

Calculation: only then does `max_parallel_hazard()` walk the whole query. A parallel-unsafe function, a sequence `nextval` or a row lock (`FOR UPDATE`) makes the level unsafe ([clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-functions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L826-L834), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-rules](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L847-L871), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L949-L960)).

Output: `parallelModeOK`. Consequence: a `DECLARE` cursor never gets a parallel plan, because its caller does not pass `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` ([chapter 1](#chapter-1-follow-one-query)). In E12.7 an unsafe function in the `WHERE` clause leaves a plain serial `Seq Scan` costing 162819.00.

##### Step 12.2: mark which relations may run in a worker

Input: each base relation. `set_rel_consider_parallel()` refuses parallelism for a temporary table, a sampled table whose method is not parallel safe, and a foreign table whose wrapper does not declare parallel-safe scans ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-relation](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L606-L660)). It also refuses a subquery with `LIMIT`, a table function, a CTE and a transition table ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-kinds](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L661-L735)).

Decision: a parallel-restricted expression in the relation's quals or outputs also refuses, instead of postponing that qual above the Gather ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L736-L757)). A join relation may run in a worker only when both inputs may and its clauses and outputs are safe ([relnode.c#build_join_rel-consider_parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L828-L845)).

Output: E12.7b's restricted filter gives the same serial plan as the unsafe one. E12.7c moves the restricted function into the output list: the scan runs in two workers, and `Gather` computes `kind_restricted(kind)` in the leader (Estimated, E12.7c).

##### Step 12.3: build partial paths

Input: a relation with `consider_parallel`. The planner adds partial paths with `add_partial_path()`, which compares only total cost and sort order. Row counts and startup cost do not matter, because every partial path of a relation returns the same rows and runs to completion ([pathnode.c#add_partial_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L707-L745)).

The partial paths available in 17:

- A **parallel sequential scan**, with workers from `compute_parallel_worker()` ([allpaths.c#create_plain_partial_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L790-L806)).
- A **parallel index or index-only scan**, only for index types whose `amcanparallel` is true, which in core is B-tree alone ([indxpath.c#build_index_paths-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L975-L1003), [nbtree.c:119](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c#L119), [brin.c:265](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/brin/brin.c#L265)).
- A **parallel bitmap heap scan**, sized by the heap pages the bitmap is expected to fetch ([allpaths.c#create_partial_bitmap_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4163-L4185)). The index part runs once: the first process to arrive builds the shared bitmap while the others wait ([nodeBitmapHeapscan.c#BitmapHeapNext-shared-bitmap](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeBitmapHeapscan.c#L128-L140), [nodeBitmapHeapscan.c#BitmapShouldInitializeSharedState](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeBitmapHeapscan.c#L774-L805)).
- **Partial joins**, whose outer side is partial. A [hash join](../../../glossary.md#hash-join) inner side is either built privately by every process from a parallel-safe path, or built once and shared as a Parallel Hash from a partial path ([joinpath.c#hash_inner_and_outer-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L2258-L2320)).
- A **partial Append or Parallel Append** over children ([chapter 11](#chapter-11-handle-inheritance-and-partitioning)), and partial aggregation ([chapter 10](#chapter-10-plan-operations-above-scans-and-joins)).

Output: E12.3's inner side, `orders`, is small, so each of the three processes hashed all 30,000 rows (`actual rows=30000 loops=3`). E12.3b's inner side is a 600,000-row partial scan, so one Parallel Hash table was built together (Measured, E12.3, E12.3b).

##### Step 12.4: choose the number of workers

Input: pages to scan and settings. `compute_parallel_worker()` uses the `parallel_workers` storage parameter when set. Otherwise a base relation smaller than the minimum sizes gets no workers, and a larger one gets one worker plus one more each time the size triples ([allpaths.c#compute_parallel_worker](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4203-L4250)).

With both heap and index pages, the smaller worker count wins, and the result never exceeds the caller's cap, normally `max_parallel_workers_per_gather` ([allpaths.c#compute_parallel_worker-index](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4252-L4279)). An inheritance child skips the minimum-size test, because its siblings together may be large ([allpaths.c#compute_parallel_worker-inheritance-child](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4217-L4227)).

Output: 2 workers for `events` (worked below). E12.2 sets `parallel_workers = 4` and raises the cap to 4 (forced settings), and the plan shows `Workers Planned: 4`.

##### Step 12.5: price the partial path and the Gather

Input: the partial path's CPU and I/O cost. Calculation: the CPU part is divided by the parallel divisor, workers plus the leader's share. The leader is assumed to contribute 1 - 0.3 x workers of a process while that is positive and `parallel_leader_participation` is on; the disk part is not divided ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L327-L346), [costsize.c#get_parallel_divisor](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6376-L6405)). The row count shown is per process ([chapter 5](#chapter-5-estimate-costs) covers the divisor as part of cost estimation).

Gather adds `parallel_setup_cost` once and `parallel_tuple_cost` per row ([costsize.c#cost_gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L436-L461)). Gather Merge also builds a heap over the workers' streams and charges 5 % more per row ([costsize.c#cost_gather_merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L474-L527)).

Consequence: the Gather path competes with the serial paths in the same `add_path()` comparison (chapter 2). E12.1's parallel count costs 10944.23, and the serial plan of E12.8 costs 14319.01, so the parallel plan wins by default.

##### Step 12.6: place Gather where the rows can be collected

Input: a relation with partial paths. `generate_useful_gather_paths()` puts a Gather over the cheapest partial path and a Gather Merge over each sorted one. It then adds a Sort or Incremental Sort under further Gather Merges for other useful orders ([allpaths.c#generate_useful_gather_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3190-L3210), [allpaths.c#generate_useful_gather_paths-sorted](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3215-L3240)).

It is called for base relations, join levels, partially grouped relations and the final scan/join relation. The relation that covers the whole query waits until its final output list is known, so that the projection can also run in the workers ([allpaths.c#set_rel_pathlist-gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L541-L557), [allpaths.c#standard_join_search-gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3465-L3472), [planner.c#gather_grouping_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7599-L7630)).

Above a partial grouping, or a sort added for Gather Merge, the row estimate is the per-process rows times the number of workers, without the leader's share ([allpaths.c#generate_gather_paths-rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3071-L3078), [planner.c#create_ordered_paths-gather-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5450-L5458)). So E12.4's Gather Merge estimates 500,000 rows for a 600,000-row table.

##### Step 12.7: add test Gathers and JIT flags at the end

Input: the finished plan tree. With `debug_parallel_query` on and a parallel-safe top plan, `standard_planner()` adds a single-copy Gather with one worker. It costs it by hand: the plan's startup cost plus `parallel_setup_cost`, and the total plus 0.1 per row ([planner.c#standard_planner-debug-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L446-L482)). E12.9 shows `Gather (cost=1047.50..1047.61)` over an aggregate costing `47.50..47.51` (forced setting).

Then `jitFlags` is set from `top_plan->total_cost` (step 12.9). Output: the `PlannedStmt` carries `parallelModeNeeded` and `jitFlags` to the executor.

##### Step 12.8: run with the workers that can be obtained

At execution, `ExecGather()` launches workers on its first call, not at plan start. `LaunchParallelWorkers()` may obtain fewer than planned, or none. With none, or when the leader participates, the leader runs the partial plan itself ([nodeGather.c#ExecGather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L137-L209)).

Worker slots are limited by `max_parallel_workers` for parallel query and by `max_worker_processes` overall ([bgworker.c#RegisterDynamicBackgroundWorker-parallel-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/postmaster/bgworker.c#L996-L1013), [parallel.sgml#when-can-parallel-query-be-used-worker-limits](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/parallel.sgml#L204-L227)). The executor also refuses parallel mode for a plan that was already partly run or is asked for a limited number of rows ([execMain.c#ExecutePlan-parallel-mode](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L1661-L1676)).

Output: on the idle test server, every Gather launched all planned workers (`Workers Launched: 2` in E12.1, E12.3 and E12.3b).

##### Step 12.9: JIT, decided while planning and done while running

Input: the finished plan's `total_cost`. Decision: if `jit` is on, `jit_above_cost` is not negative and the cost exceeds it, `standard_planner()` sets `PGJIT_PERFORM`. It adds `PGJIT_OPT3` and `PGJIT_INLINE` when the cost also exceeds the optimize and inline thresholds. It adds `PGJIT_EXPR` and `PGJIT_DEFORM` when `jit_expressions` and `jit_tuple_deforming` are on ([planner.c#standard_planner-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L564-L587), [jit.h#PGJIT](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/jit/jit.h#L18-L24)).

At run time, `standard_ExecutorStart()` copies the flags into the executor state, and workers receive the same flags ([execMain.c:248](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L248), [execParallel.c#ExecInitParallelPlan-jit-flags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execParallel.c#L742-L747)). Expression setup ends in `ExecReadyExpr()`, which first tries `jit_compile_expr()` ([execExpr.c#ExecReadyExpr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execExpr.c#L870-L883)).

`jit_compile_expr()` gives up without the `PERFORM` or `EXPR` flag. Otherwise `provider_init()` looks for the provider library in the package library directory. If the file is missing, it marks JIT as unavailable for the rest of the session ([jit.c#jit_compile_expr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/jit/jit.c#L145-L178), [jit.c#provider_init](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/jit/jit.c#L62-L120)). EXPLAIN prints its JIT section only when functions were created ([explain.c#ExplainPrintJIT](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1007-L1017)).

#### 12.5 Eligibility and comparison

| Alternative | Becomes eligible when | Compared how | Rejected or unavailable when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Serial plan | always | `add_path()` on total cost | never rejected for safety |
| Gather over a partial scan | `parallelModeOK` and the relation's `consider_parallel`, and a nonzero worker count ([allpaths.c#set_plain_rel_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L760-L786)) | partial cost + `parallel_setup_cost` + `parallel_tuple_cost` x rows against the serial total (E12.1: 10944.23 against 14319.01) | small table, unsafe or restricted quals, temp tables, CTE scans, cursors |
| Gather Merge | a sorted partial path, `enable_gathermerge` ([guc_tables.c#enable_gathermerge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L914-L922)) | heap cost plus 5 % more per row than Gather (E12.4) | no useful sort order below |
| Parallel index scan | `amcanparallel`, not a bitmap scan, not parameterized ([indxpath.c#build_index_paths-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L975-L1003)) | as a partial path | every non-B-tree index |
| Parallel bitmap heap scan | enough heap pages for a worker ([allpaths.c#create_partial_bitmap_paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4163-L4185)) | as a partial path (E12.5) | too few pages |
| Private hash in each process | partial outer, parallel-safe inner; not for full, right or right-anti joins ([joinpath.c#hash_inner_and_outer-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L2258-L2320)) | join cost with the inner built per process (E12.3) | those join types |
| Parallel Hash | partial outer and inner, `enable_parallel_hash` ([guc_tables.c#enable_parallel_hash](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L954-L962)) | one shared build (E12.3b) | unique-ification of either side |
| Parallel Append | `enable_parallel_append` ([guc_tables.c#enable_parallel_append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L944-L952)) | partial Append cost (E12.6) | the setting off: plain partial Append only |
| JIT | `jit` on and cost above `jit_above_cost` | not compared with anything: a threshold on the final plan | cost below the threshold; no provider at run time |

#### 12.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| a data-modifying statement, or a modifying CTE | `parallelModeOK` stays false ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-cheap-tests](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L354)) | no parallel plan; `CREATE TABLE AS` and `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` plan a `SELECT` and may still use one ([parallel.sgml#when-can-parallel-query-be-used-writes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/parallel.sgml#L144-L163)) |
| `FOR UPDATE` or `FOR SHARE` anywhere | treated as unsafe ([clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L949-L960)) | serial plan |
| user-defined function without a `PARALLEL` label | defaults to unsafe ([parallel.sgml#when-can-parallel-query-be-used-unsafe-default](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/parallel.sgml#L184-L188)) | serial plan (E12.7) |
| window functions, `PARAM_EXEC` parameters not computed by the leader, domain checks | parallel restricted ([clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-rules](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L847-L871), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L928-L941)) | computed above the Gather, or the relation stays serial |
| a restricted function in a scan qual | the relation is not parallelized; the qual is not postponed ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L736-L757)) | serial scan (E12.7b) |
| partial paths with parameters | never built ([pathnode.c#add_partial_path-no-parameterized](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L719-L731)) | a parameterized inner side of a nested loop stays serial |
| `max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 0` | cheap test fails ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-cheap-tests](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L354)) | serial plan, 14319.01 (E12.8, forced setting) |
| the leader participates with 4 or more workers | the leader's share 1 - 0.3 x workers is not positive, so it adds nothing to the divisor ([costsize.c#get_parallel_divisor](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L6376-L6405)) | E12.2's divisor is exactly 4 |
| Gather Merge row estimate | per-process rows x workers, without the leader's share ([planner.c#create_ordered_paths-gather-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5450-L5458)) | 500,000 estimated for 600,000 rows (E12.4) |
| no free worker slots at run time | fewer or no workers; the leader runs the plan ([nodeGather.c#ExecGather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L137-L209)) | the plan is kept; the run is slower than planned |
| JIT provider missing | `provider_init()` fails once and caches the failure ([jit.c#provider_init-missing-library](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/jit/jit.c#L80-L98)) | flags set, nothing compiled, no JIT section (E12.10b) |

#### 12.7 Formulas and worked examples

**Worker count for `events` (E12.1).** The inputs are Measured: 6,819 pages and 600,000 rows, `min_parallel_table_scan_size` 1,024 pages and `max_parallel_workers_per_gather` 2. The rule of [allpaths.c#compute_parallel_worker-heap](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4228-L4250) gives, Derived:

1. 6,819 is at least 1,024, so the table qualifies for one worker.
2. 6,819 is at least 1,024 x 3 = 3,072, so 2 workers; the threshold becomes 3,072.
3. 6,819 is below 3,072 x 3 = 9,216, so the count stays 2.
4. min(2, 2) = 2, which matches `Workers Planned: 2`.

**Parallel scan, count and Gather (E12.1).** Estimated by the planner:

```text
 Finalize Aggregate  (cost=10944.22..10944.23 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Gather  (cost=10944.00..10944.21 rows=2 width=8)
         Workers Planned: 2
         ->  Partial Aggregate  (cost=9944.00..9944.01 rows=1 width=8)
               ->  Parallel Seq Scan on events  (cost=0.00..9319.00 rows=250000 width=0)
```

Derived, step by step:

| Step | Formula | Result |
|---|---|---|
| parallel divisor | 2 workers + (1 - 0.3 x 2) | 2.4 |
| scan CPU | 600,000 x `cpu_tuple_cost` 0.01 / 2.4 | 2,500 |
| scan total | 6,819 pages x 1.0 + 2,500 | 9,319.00 |
| rows per process | 600,000 / 2.4 | 250,000 |
| partial count | 9,319.00 + 250,000 x `cpu_operator_cost` 0.0025 | 9,944.00 |
| Gather startup | 9,944.00 + `parallel_setup_cost` 1,000 | 10,944.00 |
| Gather total | 10,944.00 + 0.01 + 0.1 x 2 rows | 10,944.21 |

The serial alternative is 6,819 + 6,000 = 12,819.00 for the scan and 14,319.01 with the count (Estimated, E12.8). The parallel plan is cheaper by about 3,375 because the scan's 6,000 of CPU cost shrinks to 2,500, while the Gather adds only about 1,000.

**Four workers (E12.2, forced settings).** With `parallel_workers = 4` and the cap raised to 4, the leader's share is 1 - 1.2 < 0, so the divisor is 4. Derived: 6,819 + 6,000 / 4 = 8,319.00 with 150,000 rows per process; the count adds 150,000 x 0.0025 = 375, giving 8,694.00; the Gather adds 1,000 and 0.1 x 4 rows. The plan shows `Parallel Seq Scan ... (cost=0.00..8319.00 rows=150000)` and `Gather (cost=9694.00..9694.41 rows=4)` (Estimated, E12.2).

**Gather Merge (E12.4).** With N = workers + 1 = 3 streams and a comparison cost of 2 x 0.0025 = 0.005 ([costsize.c#cost_gather_merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L474-L527)), Derived from the Sort below (`14721.41..15346.41`) and 500,000 rows:

| Part | Formula | Result |
|---|---|---|
| heap build | 0.005 x 3 x log2(3) | 0.024 |
| startup | 14,721.41 + 0.024 + 1,000 | 15,721.43 |
| per-row heap work | 500,000 x 0.005 x log2(3) | 3,962.41 |
| heap management | 500,000 x 0.0025 | 1,250.00 |
| rows passed up | 500,000 x 0.1 x 1.05 | 52,500.00 |
| total | 1,000.024 + 3,962.41 + 1,250 + 52,500 + 15,346.41 | 74,058.84 |

The plan prints `Gather Merge (cost=15721.43..74058.84 rows=500000)`. The 52,500 for passing rows up dominates, which is why a `LIMIT 10` above it, reading only a tiny fraction of those rows, still makes the parallel sort worthwhile.

**JIT flags (E12.10).** The flag bits are `PERFORM` 1, `OPT3` 2, `INLINE` 4, `EXPR` 8 and `DEFORM` 16 ([jit.h#PGJIT](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/jit/jit.h#L18-L24)). The query is a serial `count(*)` over `events` with a total cost of 14,319.01 (E12.10 turns parallelism off for it). Measured by `debug_print_plan`, as filtered into `s12-debug.txt` (one marker per statement, then its `PlannedStmt` fields):

```text
marker e12_10_default_costs
plan:
{PLANNEDSTMT
:commandType 1
:canSetTag true
:parallelModeNeeded false
:jitFlags 0
...
marker e12_10_above_cost_10
...
:jitFlags 25
...
marker e12_10_all_thresholds_10
...
:jitFlags 31
...
marker e12_10_jit_off
...
:jitFlags 0
```

| Settings | Test | Bits set | `jitFlags` |
|---|---|---|---|
| defaults: thresholds 100,000 / 500,000 / 500,000 | 14,319.01 is not above 100,000 | none | 0 |
| `jit_above_cost = 10` (forced) | above 10, not above 500,000 | 1 + 8 + 16 | 25 |
| all three thresholds 10 (forced) | above all three | 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16 | 31 |
| `jit = off` (forced), thresholds still 10 | `jit_enabled` is false | none | 0 |

The same statement then ran under `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` with the thresholds at 10 and `jit` back on (E12.10b). Its plan shows no JIT section, because `pg_jit_available()` is false on this build and nothing was compiled.

#### 12.8 Planning versus execution

| Decision | Made while planning | Made or adapted while running |
|---|---|---|
| Whether any part of the plan may run in parallel | safety scan and `consider_parallel` | a plan run under a row limit, or resumed, runs without parallel mode ([execMain.c#ExecutePlan-parallel-mode](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L1661-L1676)) |
| Number of workers | `Workers Planned`, from sizes and settings ([allpaths.c#compute_parallel_worker](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4203-L4250)) | `Workers Launched`, from free slots under `max_parallel_workers` and `max_worker_processes` ([nodeGather.c#ExecGather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L137-L209)) |
| Whether the leader works on the partial plan | assumed in the divisor | decided at the first `ExecGather()` call from the setting and the workers obtained ([nodeGather.c#ExecGather-scan-locally](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L205-L208)) |
| How rows are split among processes | each process's share is an estimate (`rows=250000`) | processes claim the next blocks as they go ([tableam.c#table_block_parallelscan_nextpage](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L483-L494)); in E12.1 the three processes averaged 200,000 rows each (`actual rows=200000 loops=3`) |
| Hash table batching | the planner asks the executor's sizing function how many batches the expected inner rows need, sharing the memory of all participants for Parallel Hash ([costsize.c#initial_cost_hashjoin-batches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4118-L4136)) | the participants add batches together while building when the table outgrows its memory ([nodeHash.c#ExecParallelHashIncreaseNumBatches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeHash.c#L1074-L1080)); E12.3b ran with `Batches: 4` and printed no `(originally N)`, which EXPLAIN adds only when the executor changed the count ([explain.c#show_hash_info-originally](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L3300-L3310)), so no batches were added |
| JIT | `jitFlags` in the plan | compilation, only if the provider loads ([jit.c#jit_compile_expr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/jit/jit.c#L145-L178)); flags are copied to workers ([execParallel.c#ExecInitParallelPlan-jit-flags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execParallel.c#L742-L747)) |

#### 12.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ALTER FUNCTION ... PARALLEL SAFE` (or `RESTRICTED`, `UNSAFE`) | `proparallel` has its old value | the catalog row changes | the next planning sees the new level; cached plans that recorded a dependency on the function are invalidated ([setrefs.c#record_plan_function_dependency](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3464-L3480), [plancache.c#PlanCacheObjectCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2069-L2077)); built-in functions are not tracked; see [chapter 14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans) |
| `ALTER TABLE ... SET (parallel_workers = n)` | the size rule applies | the storage parameter overrides it | the next planning reads `n` with the table's other planner inputs ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-parallel-workers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L196-L205)) (E12.2); the `pg_class` update invalidates the table's relcache entry ([inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-pg_class](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1383-L1391)) |
| `SET max_parallel_workers_per_gather`, the cost settings or `debug_parallel_query` | old values | new values for the session | only new planning sees them (E12.8, E12.9) |
| `SET jit` or a `jit_*` threshold | old flags in cached plans | new flags only for plans built afterwards | a generic plan keeps the JIT decision made when it was built ([jit.sgml#jit-decision](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/jit.sgml#L124-L130)) |
| a table grows past a size step | fewer workers planned | `compute_parallel_worker()` returns more after the size grows | seen at the next planning, since the page count is read from the file each time ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-parallel-workers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L196-L205), chapter 4) |
| other sessions occupy worker slots | all planned workers can start | fewer are launched ([bgworker.c#RegisterDynamicBackgroundWorker-parallel-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/postmaster/bgworker.c#L996-L1013)) | no replanning; only the run changes |

#### 12.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- Parallel plans of many shapes, with the costs lowered to encourage them: [select_parallel.sql#setup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L1-L14). Parallel Append: [select_parallel.sql#parallel-append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L16-L44). A restricted function in the target list prevents parallel aggregation: [select_parallel.sql#restricted-target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L96-L99).
- Parallel index and index-only scans: [select_parallel.sql#parallel-index-scans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L137-L159). Parallel bitmap heap scan: [select_parallel.sql#parallel-bitmap](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L201-L215). Gather Merge: [select_parallel.sql#gather-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L269-L276). `debug_parallel_query`: [select_parallel.sql#debug-parallel-query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select_parallel.sql#L380-L384).
- Parallel Hash against private hash tables: [join_hash.sql#parallel-hash](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/join_hash.sql#L96-L135). Parallel plans under `CREATE TABLE AS`: [write_parallel.sql#ctas](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/write_parallel.sql#L1-L20).
- JIT: no regression test checks `jitFlags`. `aggregates.sql` sets `jit_above_cost = 0` around some aggregation tests so that JIT code paths run on builds that have a provider ([aggregates.sql#jit-above-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/aggregates.sql#L1498-L1506)), and `explain.sql` turns JIT off to keep its output stable ([explain.sql#jit-off](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L54-L56)).
- Gaps on this page: JIT compilation itself cannot be shown, because the build has no LLVM (`pg_jit_available()` is false, E12.10). Worker shortfall at run time is not demonstrated, because the idle test server always had free slots.

#### 12.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: a statement that may run in parallel.
2. The safety scan and the per-relation checks decide where workers may go.
3. Partial paths divide their CPU work by the workers plus the leader's share, and Gather or Gather Merge adds setup and per-row transfer costs.
4. The cheaper of the serial and parallel totals wins: 10944.23 against 14319.01 in E12.1.
5. The finished plan's total cost also sets `jitFlags`.
6. At run time the executor launches the workers it can get, and compiles only if a JIT provider loads.
7. Refresh: settings, storage parameters and function labels change only what the next planning decides.

### Chapter 13. Plan writes and row locking

#### 13.1 Main idea

The planner treats every write as a query that finds rows, with one extra node on top. `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `MERGE` are planned like a `SELECT` that produces the rows to insert or the rows to change. A [ModifyTable](../../../glossary.md#modifytable) node then applies them to the target table ([plannodes.h#ModifyTable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L213-L256)). `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` gets a `LockRows` node instead ([plannodes.h#LockRows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L1247-L1261)).

This matters because the planner's choices stop at the source rows. It chooses scans and joins for those rows by cost, as in chapters 6 to 10, but it adds no cost at all for the write itself ([pathnode.c#create_modifytable_path-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3760-L3770)). Which partition an inserted row lands in, whether a unique key conflicts, which triggers fire and what happens when another session changed the row are all decided by the executor, row by row.

Three results surprise most readers. Q4 carries the physical row address of the `customers` row it joins, although it never changes `customers`. An `INSERT` into a partitioned table shows no partition in its plan at all. And no `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` or `MERGE`, and no `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, ever gets a parallel plan, although `CREATE TABLE AS` can. Experiments E13.1 to E13.11 show each of these ([E13.1](#measurement-script)).

#### 13.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `resultRelation` | range-table index of the target named in the statement | parse analysis, kept in the `Query` ([parsenodes.h#Query-resultRelation](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/parsenodes.h#L138-L143)) | parameter of this planning run | `preprocess_targetlist()`, `ModifyTable` |
| `resultRelations` | the leaf tables the node may change; one entry, or one per surviving partition or child | `grouping_planner()` from `leaf_result_relids` ([planner.c#grouping_planner-inherited-targets](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1836-L1860)) | fixed in the plan | executor opens each ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecInitModifyTable-open](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L4520-L4538)) |
| `processed_tlist` | the target list after the planner added every column the executor needs | `preprocess_targetlist()` ([preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L54-L64)) | plan-time | the scan and join target of the source rows |
| row-identity columns `ctid`, `tableoid`, `wholerow` | junk columns that tell the executor which row, and which table, to change | `add_row_identity_columns()` and inheritance expansion ([appendinfo.c#add_row_identity_columns](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/appendinfo.c#L882-L927), [inherit.c#expand_single_inheritance_child-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L609-L646)) | computed per row at run time | `ModifyTable` |
