| `PlanRowMark` and its `markType` | how each non-target table, or each `FOR UPDATE` table, is re-fetched or locked | `preprocess_rowmarks()` and `select_rowmark_type()` ([planner.c#preprocess_rowmarks-other-rels](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2375-L2400), [planner.c#select_rowmark_type](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2403-L2451)) | plan-time | `LockRows`, `ModifyTable`, EvalPlanQual |
| `epqParam` | a parameter every scan below depends on, used to force re-evaluation of one row | `assign_special_exec_param()` in `grouping_planner()` ([planner.c#grouping_planner-lockrows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1803-L1808)) | parameter | EvalPlanQual |
| `arbiterIndexes` | the unique indexes that decide an `ON CONFLICT` | `infer_arbiter_indexes()` at plan creation ([createplan.c#make_modifytable-arbiter](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7095-L7100)) | read from the catalogs at planning, then stored in the plan | speculative insertion |
| `partColsUpdated` | whether an `UPDATE` assigns a partition-key column | `expand_partitioned_rtentry()` ([inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-partcols](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L338-L346)) | plan-time | the executor's row movement |
| `canSetTag` | whether this `ModifyTable` reports the command's row count | the `Query` ([plannodes.h#ModifyTable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L229-L237)) | fixed in the plan | a data-modifying CTE runs as an auxiliary node |

Two row-identifying values are easy to confuse. The `ctid` of the target table comes from row identity and says which row to update. The `ctid` of another table in the join comes from a [row mark](../../../glossary.md#row-mark) and exists only so that the row can be fetched again if a concurrent update forces a recheck ([plannodes.h#RowMarkType](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L1297-L1335)).

#### 13.3 Logic map

```text
INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / MERGE, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE / SHARE
|
+-- [A] MERGE? -> target JOIN source; join type from the WHEN clauses:
|        NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE and BY TARGET -> FULL, BY SOURCE only -> LEFT,
|        BY TARGET only -> RIGHT, neither -> INNER
+-- [B] row marks: UPDATE / DELETE / MERGE, or FOR UPDATE/SHARE present?
|        no  -> none
|        yes -> every base table except the target gets a PlanRowMark:
|               named in FOR ... -> a lock strength (EXCLUSIVE ... KEYSHARE)
|               other plain table -> REFERENCE (re-fetch by ctid)
|               not a table, or an FDW without a choice -> COPY (whole row)
+-- [C] parallel mode considered only for a SELECT with no modifying CTE and no row marks
+-- [D] preprocess_targetlist:
|        INSERT -> one entry per target column, in column order
|        UPDATE -> update_colnos records which columns are assigned
|        plain target of UPDATE / DELETE / MERGE -> junk "ctid" (FDW: its own columns)
|        row marks -> junk ctidN / wholerowN / tableoidN
|        RETURNING -> Vars of the other tables
+-- [E] target is a partitioned table or an inheritance parent?
|        yes -> expand; prune by the quals; each leaf adds "tableoid" + its row identity
+-- [F] plan the source rows like a SELECT (scans, joins, grouping); target pushed into partitions
+-- [G] final relation, for each surviving path:
|        FOR UPDATE / SHARE -> LockRows    cost + cpu_tuple_cost per row
|        LIMIT / OFFSET     -> Limit
|        not a SELECT       -> ModifyTable cost = input cost; rows only with RETURNING
+-- [H] create_plan -> make_modifytable:
|        ON CONFLICT -> infer_arbiter_indexes (error when nothing matches)
|        foreign target -> PlanDirectModify when eligible, else PlanForeignModify
+-- [I] set_plan_references: RETURNING lists, EXCLUDED and MERGE source columns as inner refs
|
executor: route rows to partitions, speculative insertion, triggers and constraints,
          lock rows, EvalPlanQual rechecks, run CTE writes to completion
```

- [A] [planner.c#subquery_planner-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L697-L700), [prepjointree.c#transform_MERGE_to_join-jointype](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L190-L213), [prepjointree.c#transform_MERGE_to_join-join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L275-L288)
- [B] [planner.c#preprocess_rowmarks-need](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2303-L2333), [planner.c#select_rowmark_type](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2403-L2451)
- [C] [planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-ok](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L329-L365), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-rowmarks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L949-L958)
- [D] [preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-insert-update](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L96-L128), [preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-rowmarks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L214-L285), [preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-returning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L289-L327)
- [E] [inherit.c#expand_single_inheritance_child-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L609-L646)
- [F] [planner.c#apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths-partitioned](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7880-L7886)
- [G] [planner.c#grouping_planner-final-paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1792-L1825), [pathnode.c#create_lockrows_path-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3688-L3695), [pathnode.c#create_modifytable_path-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3760-L3786)
- [H] [createplan.c#make_modifytable-arbiter](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7095-L7100), [createplan.c#make_modifytable-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7183-L7219)
- [I] [setrefs.c#set_plan_refs-modifytable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1065-L1110)
- executor: [nodeModifyTable.c#ExecInitModifyTable-routing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L4667-L4676), [nodeLockRows.c#ExecLockRows-lock](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeLockRows.c#L184-L195), [execMain.c#ExecPostprocessPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L1472-L1502)

#### 13.4 Step by step

##### Step 1. MERGE becomes a join

Input: a `MERGE` query whose join tree holds only the source. Early in `subquery_planner()`, `transform_MERGE_to_join()` rebuilds the join tree so that it joins the target to the source on the `ON` condition ([planner.c#subquery_planner-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L697-L700), [prepjointree.c#transform_MERGE_to_join-join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L275-L288)).

Decision: the `WHEN` clauses fix the join type. A `WHEN NOT MATCHED [BY TARGET]` clause needs every source row, so the target is joined with a right join; `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE` needs every target row, so it becomes a left join; both need a full join ([prepjointree.c#transform_MERGE_to_join-jointype](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L190-L213)). Consequence: from here on, `MERGE` is an ordinary outer join, and chapter 8's join search picks its method by cost. E13.5's `MERGE` has `WHEN MATCHED` and `WHEN NOT MATCHED`, so its plan is a `Hash Right Join` that keeps every `staging` row.

`WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE`, and with it the left and full joins, was committed in the 17 development cycle (`0294df2f1f`); so were `MERGE ... RETURNING` (`c649fa24a4`) and `MERGE` into updatable views (`5f2e179bd3`). That is why the code allows the target to be an expanded view subquery rather than a table ([prepjointree.c#transform_MERGE_to_join-target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepjointree.c#L239-L256)).

##### Step 2. Give every other table a row mark

Input: the command type and any `FOR UPDATE`/`SHARE` clauses. `preprocess_rowmarks()` does nothing for a plain `SELECT` or an `INSERT`. For `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE` and any `FOR ...` clause, it makes a `PlanRowMark` for every base table except the target ([planner.c#preprocess_rowmarks-need](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2303-L2333)).

Decision: `select_rowmark_type()` picks the mark. A table named in `FOR UPDATE` gets a lock strength. Any other plain table gets `ROW_MARK_REFERENCE`, which only re-fetches the row by [TID](../../../glossary.md#tid). A function scan, a `VALUES` list, or a foreign table whose FDW has no preference gets `ROW_MARK_COPY`, which carries the whole row ([planner.c#select_rowmark_type](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2403-L2451)). Output: `root->rowMarks`. Consequence: step 3 adds a junk column for each mark, which is why Q4's plan in E13.3 outputs `c.ctid`.

##### Step 3. Complete the target list

Input: the analyzed target list. `preprocess_targetlist()` makes it what the executor expects ([preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-insert-update](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L96-L128)):

1. For `INSERT`, one entry per target column in column order, so omitted columns get their default. E13.2's `Result` outputs six values, with `NULL::text` for the omitted `note`.
2. For `UPDATE`, the assigned column numbers go to `update_colnos`, and the list is renumbered.
3. For `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `MERGE` on a target that is not expanded for inheritance, a junk `ctid` column for a table, added by `add_row_identity_columns()`; for a foreign table, whatever the FDW's `AddForeignUpdateTargets` asks for. An inherited target gets these per leaf in step 4 instead ([preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-row-identity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L111-L128), [appendinfo.c#add_row_identity_columns](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/appendinfo.c#L882-L927)).
4. For each row mark, junk `ctidN`, `wholerowN` or `tableoidN` columns ([preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-rowmarks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L214-L285)).
5. For `MERGE`, every source column an action or the join condition uses ([preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L130-L186)).
6. For `RETURNING`, any column of another table it mentions ([preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-returning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L289-L327)).

Output: `processed_tlist`, the PathTarget the scans and joins must produce. That is why E13.4's `DELETE` scan outputs only `ctid`, and E13.5's join outputs `o.ctid, s.amount, s.id, s.ctid`.

##### Step 4. Expand an inherited or partitioned target

Input: a target whose range-table entry is marked for inheritance expansion. Only `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `MERGE` can reach this step: parse analysis always opens an `INSERT` target without inheritance, as E13.8 shows below ([analyze.c#transformInsertStmt-target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L668-L669), [analyze.c#transformUpdateStmt-target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L2436-L2438)). As expansion adds each child of the target, it records the child in `all_result_relids`, and a leaf child also in `leaf_result_relids` ([inherit.c#expand_single_inheritance_child-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L609-L646)).

Decision: each leaf adds a junk `tableoid` column, so that the executor can tell which child a row came from, plus its own row identity ([inherit.c#expand_single_inheritance_child-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L628-L646)). A partitioned target is pruned by its quals before this, as chapter 11 describes, so E13.7's March update has a single result relation, `orders_r_03`. When the `UPDATE` assigns a partition-key column, `partColsUpdated` is set ([inherit.c#expand_partitioned_rtentry-partcols](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/inherit.c#L338-L346)). Consequence: the plan lists every surviving leaf as a separate `Update on` target.

##### Step 5. Plan the source rows like a query

Input: the preprocessed query. `query_planner()` and the upper steps plan the source rows exactly as for a `SELECT`; E13.3 plans Q4's join with the same `Hash Join` as Q1. Two differences apply. First, parallel mode is considered only for a `SELECT` without a modifying CTE, and a `FOR UPDATE` anywhere makes the query parallel-unsafe ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-ok](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L365), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-rowmarks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L949-L958)). The comment above that test explains why: workers could not safely see or coordinate the writes ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L329-L345)).

Second, a partial index predicate implied by the query is not dropped from the quals of a target or row-marked table, because an EvalPlanQual recheck must still apply it to a newer row version ([indxpath.c#check_index_predicates-target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L3318-L3355)). For a partitioned target, the target list is computed inside each partition's scan, because `Append` cannot project ([planner.c#apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths-partitioned](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7880-L7886), [createplan.c#is_projection_capable_path-append](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7256-L7262)). A legacy inheritance parent gets no such push-down, so a `Result` computes the new values above the `Append` (E13.9).

##### Step 6. Add LockRows, Limit and ModifyTable on the final relation

Input: every surviving path of the scan/join and upper steps. `grouping_planner()` wraps each one in the upper relation `UPPERREL_FINAL` ([planner.c#grouping_planner-final-paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1792-L1825)):

1. With a `FOR UPDATE`/`SHARE` clause, a `LockRows` path goes first, so it sits below any `Limit`. It costs its input plus `cpu_tuple_cost` per row, and it discards the input's sort order, because locking can replace the sort-key values with newer ones ([pathnode.c#create_lockrows_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3678-L3695)).
2. A `LIMIT` or `OFFSET` adds a `Limit` path.
3. A write adds a `ModifyTable` path. It gets the lists of step 3 and step 4 per result relation ([planner.c#grouping_planner-inherited-targets](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1836-L1860)). The row marks go to `LockRows` when there is one, else to `ModifyTable` ([planner.c#grouping_planner-modify-rowmarks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1998-L2025)).

Consequence: `ModifyTable` keeps its input's cost, and it reports rows only when there is a `RETURNING` list ([pathnode.c#create_modifytable_path-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3760-L3786)).

##### Step 7. Build the ModifyTable plan

Input: the winning `ModifyTablePath`. `make_modifytable()` copies its lists into the plan node and settles two questions that depend on catalogs ([createplan.c#make_modifytable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7029-L7104)).

For `ON CONFLICT`, `infer_arbiter_indexes()` finds every valid unique index whose key columns and expressions exactly match the conflict target, and whose predicate, if any, the conflict clause's `WHERE` implies ([plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L821-L859), [plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-columns](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L862-L927), [plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-predicate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L928-L939)). E13.2's `ON CONFLICT (id)` finds `orders_pkey`.

For a foreign target, the FDW may take over the whole statement. When its direct-modify callbacks exist and no row trigger, stored generated column, `WITH CHECK OPTION` or transition table needs per-row local work, `PlanDirectModify` is asked first. Otherwise `PlanForeignModify` plans a row-by-row modification ([createplan.c#make_modifytable-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7183-L7219)).

##### Step 8. Fix the references of RETURNING, ON CONFLICT and MERGE

[`set_plan_references()`](../../../glossary.md#set_plan_references) rewrites the `RETURNING` lists against the subplan's output and copies the first of them into the node's visible target list, only so that `EXPLAIN` can print it ([setrefs.c#set_plan_refs-returning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1065-L1099)). That is the `Output: id, amount` line of E13.4. It treats `ON CONFLICT` as a pseudo-join whose inner side is the `EXCLUDED` row, and it makes the `MERGE` source columns inner references too ([setrefs.c#set_plan_refs-onconflict-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1103-L1142)).

##### Step 9. Plan a data-modifying CTE as its own subplan

A CTE that contains `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE` or `MERGE` has side effects, so `SS_process_ctes()` never inlines it ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-inline](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L920-L950)). It is planned as a separate subplan with its own `ModifyTable`, as in E13.6. The executor puts every `ModifyTable` that does not set the command tag on a list of auxiliary nodes, and runs each to completion at the end of the statement, even if the outer query read none of its rows ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecInitModifyTable-aux](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L4914-L4925), [execMain.c#ExecPostprocessPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L1472-L1502)).

#### 13.5 Eligibility and comparison

Only the source-row plan is a real choice. Its alternatives become eligible and compete exactly as in chapters 6 to 10, through `add_path()`. The nodes this chapter adds do not change that ranking: `ModifyTable` adds nothing, and the source code says so because "there is no way for the costs to change any higher-level planning choices" ([pathnode.c#create_modifytable_path-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3760-L3767)). `LockRows` adds the same `cpu_tuple_cost` per estimated row to each path it wraps.

| Alternative | How it becomes eligible | How it is compared or rejected |
|---|---|---|
| a parallel source plan | never for a write or a `FOR UPDATE` query: the parallel-mode test requires a `SELECT` without modifying CTEs, and row marks count as parallel-unsafe ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-ok](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L365), [clauses.c#max_parallel_hazard_walker-rowmarks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L949-L958)) | not generated, so never compared |
| `CREATE TABLE AS` or `SELECT INTO` with a parallel source | allowed, because the new table is invisible to workers ([planner.c#standard_planner-parallel-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L336-L343)) | compared by cost as a `SELECT` |
| the join method of a `MERGE` | the join type is fixed by the `WHEN` clauses; any method that supports that outer join is eligible | by cost; E13.5 chose a hash right join |
| an arbiter index | every valid unique index whose columns and predicate match ([plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L821-L859), [plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-columns](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L862-L927), [plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-predicate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L928-L939)) | not cost-based: all matching indexes become arbiters, and no match is an error |
| direct foreign modification | the FDW provides all four direct-modify callbacks and no local per-row work is needed ([createplan.c#make_modifytable-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7183-L7209)) | tried before row-by-row; the FDW decides |
| dropping an implied partial-index qual | only for a table that is neither a target nor row-marked ([indxpath.c#check_index_predicates-target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L3318-L3355)) | kept for targets, so the qual stays in the plan for rechecks |

#### 13.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `ON CONFLICT` target matches no unique index | `infer_arbiter_indexes()` raises "there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification" ([plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-error](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L946-L950)) | the statement fails at planning |
| `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` without a conflict target | no inference; the arbiter list stays empty ([plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-donothing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L730-L737)) | `EXPLAIN` prints no arbiter line, and any unique violation is ignored ([explain.c#show_modifytable_info-conflict](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L4282-L4294)) |
| `ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT` names an exclusion constraint with `DO UPDATE` | error "ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE not supported with exclusion constraints" ([plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-constraint](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L832-L846)) | only `DO NOTHING` works with exclusion constraints |
| an invalid unique index | skipped as an arbiter; `indcheckxmin` is deliberately not checked ([plancat.c#infer_arbiter_indexes-valid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L821-L829)) | an index still being built concurrently does not arbitrate |
| every child target pruned or excluded | a dummy one-relation `ModifyTable` is still built ([planner.c#grouping_planner-all-excluded](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1955-L1980)) | statement triggers still fire |
| `FOR UPDATE` over grouping, after rewriting or pull-up | `CheckSelectLocking()` raises an error ([planner.c#preprocess_rowmarks-need](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2303-L2313)) | no lock on grouped rows |
| `FOR UPDATE` names a subquery that was not flattened | ignored as a lock; the subquery gets a `COPY` mark ([planner.c#preprocess_rowmarks-clauses](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2353-L2361)) | its rows are carried, not locked |
| `MERGE` into a partitioned table with a foreign partition | error "cannot execute MERGE on relation" ([createplan.c#make_modifytable-merge-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7165-L7179)) | `MERGE` has no FDW support |
| a `MERGE` source row with no target, on a partitioned target | its `tableoid` is NULL, and the executor runs the `NOT MATCHED` actions ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecModifyTable-null-tableoid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L4094-L4121)) | the outer join's null side is how "not matched" is detected |
| a locked row was updated concurrently under `REPEATABLE READ` or `SERIALIZABLE` | `LockRows` raises a serialization failure ([nodeLockRows.c#ExecLockRows-updated](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeLockRows.c#L224-L229)) | the transaction must retry |
| `SKIP LOCKED` and the row is locked | `LockRows` skips it ([nodeLockRows.c#ExecLockRows-lock](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeLockRows.c#L184-L195)) | fewer rows than the plan's estimate |

#### 13.7 Formulas and worked examples

Two cost rules cover the nodes of this chapter. Here `S` is the input path's startup cost, `T` its total cost, and `N` its estimated rows.

```text
LockRows:     startup = S     total = T + cpu_tuple_cost x N     rows = N
ModifyTable:  startup = S     total = T                          rows = N with RETURNING, else 0
```

Both come straight from `create_lockrows_path()` and `create_modifytable_path()` ([pathnode.c#create_lockrows_path-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3688-L3695), [pathnode.c#create_modifytable_path-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L3769-L3786)). With the default `cpu_tuple_cost` of 0.01, locking 1,000 estimated rows adds 10.00 (Derived). The experiments of this chapter run with `COSTS OFF`, so they show the shapes these rules produce, not the numbers.

##### Q4: the row identity and the row mark (E13.3)

Estimated by the planner, E13.3:

```text
 Update on public.orders o
   ->  Hash Join
         Output: (o.amount * 1.1), o.ctid, c.ctid
         Inner Unique: true
         Hash Cond: (o.customer_id = c.id)
         ->  Seq Scan on public.orders o
               Output: o.amount, o.ctid, o.customer_id
               Filter: (o.status = 'pending'::text)
         ->  Hash
               Output: c.ctid, c.id
               ->  Seq Scan on public.customers c
                     Output: c.ctid, c.id
                     Filter: (c.region = 'west'::text)
```

The join outputs three things. `o.amount * 1.1` is the new value of the one assigned column. `o.ctid` is the target's row identity from step 3. `c.ctid` is the `ROW_MARK_REFERENCE` mark of step 2: the executor needs it only if a concurrent update of the `orders` row forces an EvalPlanQual recheck, which must re-fetch the same `customers` row ([plannodes.h#RowMarkType](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L1316-L1325)). Run on the copy `orders_w`, the same join produced 290 rows (Measured, E13.11), and `Update` returned 0 rows because Q4 has no `RETURNING`.

##### ON CONFLICT and RETURNING (E13.2, E13.4)

Estimated by the planner, E13.2 and E13.4:

```text
 Insert on public.orders o
   Conflict Resolution: UPDATE
   Conflict Arbiter Indexes: orders_pkey
   ->  Result
         Output: 1, 1, 'pending'::text, '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00'::timestamp with time zone, 1.00::numeric(10,2), NULL::text
...
 Delete on public.orders
   Output: id, amount
   ->  Seq Scan on public.orders
         Output: ctid
         Filter: ((orders.amount < '1'::numeric) AND (orders.status = 'cancelled'::text))
```

The `INSERT` source is a one-row `Result` that lists all six columns, with `NULL` for `note`, which the statement omitted. The arbiter is `orders_pkey`, the only unique index on `id`. The `DELETE` scan needs only `ctid`, because `RETURNING` reads `id` and `amount` from the deleted row itself, not from the scan ([preptlist.c#preprocess_targetlist-returning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/preptlist.c#L289-L313)).

##### MERGE: a right join, then per-row actions (E13.5, E13.11)

Measured, E13.11 (on the copy `orders_w`, rolled back):

```text
 Merge on orders_w o (actual rows=0 loops=1)
   Tuples: inserted=50 updated=300
   ->  Hash Right Join (actual rows=350 loops=1)
         Hash Cond: (o.id = s.id)
         ->  Seq Scan on orders_w o (actual rows=30000 loops=1)
         ->  Hash (actual rows=350 loops=1)
               ->  Seq Scan on staging s (actual rows=350 loops=1)
```

Derived from the fixture: `staging` holds the 300 orders whose `id` is a multiple of 100, plus 50 new ids from 30001 to 30050, so 350 rows. The right join keeps all 350. For the 300 that found a target row, the executor ran `WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE`; for the 50 whose target side is null, it ran `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT`. That split, 300 and 50, is exactly the `Tuples:` line. The planner chose only the join; the executor chose the action per row.

##### A data-modifying CTE (E13.6)

Estimated by the planner, E13.6:

```text
 Insert on public.orders_archive
   CTE moved
     ->  Delete on public.orders
           Output: orders.id, orders.customer_id, orders.status, orders.ordered_at, orders.amount, orders.note
           ->  Seq Scan on public.orders
                 Output: orders.ctid
                 Filter: ((orders.amount < '5'::numeric) AND (orders.status = 'cancelled'::text))
   ->  CTE Scan on moved
         Output: moved.id, moved.customer_id, moved.status, moved.ordered_at, moved.amount, moved.note
```

The `DELETE` runs once, as the CTE's own subplan, and the `INSERT` reads its `RETURNING` rows through a `CTE Scan`. Neither can be inlined into the other, because the CTE contains a write.

##### Partitioned and inherited targets (E13.7, E13.8, E13.9)

Estimated by the planner, E13.7, E13.8 and E13.9 (cut):

```text
 Update on orders_r
   Update on orders_r_03 orders_r_1
   ->  Index Scan using orders_r_03_ordered_at_idx on orders_r_03 orders_r_1
         Index Cond: ((ordered_at >= '2024-03-01 00:00:00+00'::timestamp with time zone) AND (ordered_at < '2024-03-02 00:00:00+00'::timestamp with time zone))
...
 Update on orders_r
   Update on orders_r_01 orders_r_1
   ...
   Update on orders_r_default orders_r_13
   ->  Append
         ->  Seq Scan on orders_r_01 orders_r_1
               Filter: (id = 5)
   ...
 Insert on orders_r
   ->  Result
...
 Update on ledger
   Update on ledger ledger_1
   Update on ledger_2023 ledger_2
   Update on ledger_2024 ledger_3
   ->  Result
         ->  Append
```

The first `UPDATE` constrains the partition key, so pruning left one result relation. The second filters on `id`, which prunes nothing, so all 13 partitions are result relations, and a `SET ordered_at = ...` that crosses a month boundary becomes a delete from one partition and an insert through the root at run time ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecCrossPartitionUpdate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L1743-L1749)). The `INSERT` names no partition, because routing is the executor's job ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecInitModifyTable-routing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L4667-L4676)). The `ledger` update shows the `Result` above an `Append` that step 5 described for legacy inheritance.

##### Row locking (E13.10)

Estimated by the planner, E13.10 (second statement, `FOR UPDATE OF o SKIP LOCKED`):

```text
 LockRows
   Output: o.id, c.name, o.ctid, c.ctid
   ->  Nested Loop
         Output: o.id, c.name, o.ctid, c.ctid
```

Both tables carry a `ctid`, but for different reasons: `o` is locked, while `c` carries a `REFERENCE` mark for rechecks. `LockRows` is the top node, above the join, so it locks each row only after the join has produced it.

#### 13.8 Planning versus execution

| Decided while planning | Decided or adapted while executing |
|---|---|
| the source-row plan, by cost ([planner.c#grouping_planner-final-paths](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1792-L1825)) | which row each `MERGE` action applies to, per row (E13.11) |
| the result relations that survive plan-time pruning (E13.7) | which partition an `INSERT` row goes to ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecInitModifyTable-routing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L4667-L4676)) |
| `partColsUpdated`, which allows row movement | whether an updated row actually moves, and the routing state it needs then ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecCrossPartitionUpdate-routing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L1801-L1811)) |
| the `tableoid` junk column | which result relation a row belongs to, looked up per row ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecModifyTable-tableoid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L4086-L4128)) |
| the arbiter indexes | whether a conflict happens, by speculative insertion ([nodeModifyTable.c#ExecInsert-speculative](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L1038-L1068)) |
| row marks and their junk columns | locking each row, skipping or erroring on a locked one, and rechecking a changed one ([nodeLockRows.c#ExecLockRows-lock](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeLockRows.c#L184-L195), [nodeLockRows.c#ExecLockRows-epq](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeLockRows.c#L254-L275)) |
| that a CTE write is a separate subplan | running it to completion at statement end ([execMain.c#ExecPostprocessPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L1482-L1502)) |
| direct or row-by-row foreign modification | the remote statement or the per-row FDW calls |

EvalPlanQual is the main run-time adaptation. Under `READ COMMITTED`, when an `UPDATE`, `DELETE` or lock finds that another transaction changed the row, the executor re-evaluates the plan's quals against the newest version of that one row, using the junk columns the planner added ([execMain.c#EvalPlanQual](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L2501-L2513), [nodeModifyTable.c#ExecUpdate-epq](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeModifyTable.c#L2436-L2440)).

#### 13.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| a unique index is created on the target | cached plans list the old arbiter set | the relcache invalidation marks every plan that depends on the table invalid ([plancache.c#PlanCacheRelCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1986-L2022)) | the next execution replans and re-runs `infer_arbiter_indexes()`; E14.4 measured the same invalidation for a new index |
| a partition is added or removed | the plan's result relations and pruning information are built from the old partition list | attaching or detaching sends a relcache invalidation for the parent, so its plans are invalidated through the same callback ([heap.c#StorePartitionBound-inval](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/heap.c#L3642-L3647), [tablecmds.c#DetachPartitionFinalize-inval](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/tablecmds.c#L19668-L19672)) | the next planning expands and prunes the new list |
| a row trigger, generated column or view check appears on a foreign target | direct modification was allowed | row-by-row modification is required ([createplan.c#make_modifytable-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7183-L7209)) | decided at the next plan creation |
| a concurrent transaction updates a row the plan is about to change | the snapshot saw the old version | EvalPlanQual rechecks the newest version | none: this is execution only |
| the statement ends | an auxiliary `ModifyTable` in a CTE may be unfinished | `ExecPostprocessPlan()` runs it to completion | none |

#### 13.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- Arbiter inference, with plan shapes: [insert_conflict.sql#explain](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/insert_conflict.sql#L19-L25) and its expected [insert_conflict.out#arbiters](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/expected/insert_conflict.out#L26-L44).
- `MERGE` plans: [merge.sql#explain](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/merge.sql#L247-L262).
- Row movement between partitions: [update.sql#row-movement](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/update.sql#L161-L170).
- Data-modifying CTEs and running them to completion: [with.sql#data-modifying](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/with.sql#L1231-L1240), [with.sql#modifying-in-modifying](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/with.sql#L1416-L1429).
- An inherited `UPDATE` that prunes every child: [inherit.sql#update-where-false](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/inherit.sql#L190-L191); pruning of `UPDATE` and `DELETE` targets: [partition_prune.sql#update-delete](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/partition_prune.sql#L1008-L1009).
- Parallel plans for writes into new tables (`CREATE TABLE AS`, `SELECT INTO`, materialized views): [write_parallel.sql#ctas](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/write_parallel.sql#L13-L30); no regression test asserts that an ordinary `UPDATE` or `FOR UPDATE` query stays serial.
- Partial-index quals kept for a `FOR UPDATE` target: [select.sql#for-update-recheck](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/select.sql#L208-L213).
- Concurrency, which only isolation tests can exercise: [eval-plan-qual.spec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/isolation/specs/eval-plan-qual.spec#L1-L5), [skip-locked.spec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/isolation/specs/skip-locked.spec#L1), [partition-key-update-1.spec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/isolation/specs/partition-key-update-1.spec#L1-L2), [insert-conflict-do-update.spec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/isolation/specs/insert-conflict-do-update.spec#L1-L4), [merge-update.spec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/isolation/specs/merge-update.spec#L1-L7).
- Gaps. This page shows no cost number for `LockRows` or `ModifyTable`, because every write experiment runs with `COSTS OFF`; the formulas above are source-only. No experiment exercises EvalPlanQual, direct foreign modification or row movement under concurrency; those rest on the source and the isolation tests. No regression test asserts the `LockRows` cost charge.

#### 13.11 Causal summary

1. Initial state: a write statement, or a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`.
2. Transformation: `MERGE` becomes a target-to-source join, and every non-target table gets a row mark.
3. Transformation: the target list gains the new values plus junk `ctid`, `tableoid` and row-mark columns; an inherited or partitioned target is expanded and pruned into leaf result relations.
4. Planning: the source rows are planned by cost like a serial `SELECT`.
5. Result: `LockRows`, `Limit` and a zero-cost `ModifyTable` are stacked on each final path, and the arbiter indexes and FDW strategy are fixed at plan creation.
6. Execution: the executor routes, detects conflicts, fires triggers, locks and rechecks each row, and finishes any CTE write at statement end.
7. Refresh: a DDL change on the target invalidates the cached plan, and the next execution plans again.

### Chapter 14. Build, cache, and invalidate plans

#### 14.1 Main idea

Choosing the cheapest path is not the end of planning. Four more steps turn it into something the executor can run. `create_plan()` builds plan tree nodes from the path tree, and `SS_finalize_plan()` works out which parameters each node depends on. `set_plan_references()` rewrites every column reference into executor form and records what the plan depends on. Finally `standard_planner()` wraps the result in a PlannedStmt ([planner.c#standard_planner-core](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L418-L422), [planner.c#standard_planner-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L501-L518), [planner.c#standard_planner-setrefs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L520-L562)).

The dependency lists matter because plans can outlive the moment they were made. A [prepared statement](../../../glossary.md#prepared-statement), a PL/pgSQL function or an SPI caller keeps plans in the plan cache. For each execution, the cache chooses between a [custom plan](../../../glossary.md#custom-and-generic-plan) built for the actual parameter values and a generic plan built once without them. It also throws plans away when the objects they depend on change ([plancache.c header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L6-L20)).

The surprising results are about counts. Measured in E14.5, a PL/pgSQL function called ten times planned its query six times. An SQL function called in five statements planned five times, while the same kind of function called ten times inside one statement planned once. Each number follows from a different caching rule, and this chapter derives all of them. E14.6 adds a lifecycle result: an `ANALYZE` that leaves the table's size figures unchanged keeps a cached generic plan with its old estimates, and one that changes them makes the next execution replan.

#### 14.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CP_*` flags | What a parent node needs from a child's target list: exact, small, labeled or ignored ([createplan.c#CP-flags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L50-L73)) | the parent's `create_*_plan()` call | parameter | the child's target-list choice |
| `glob->finalrtable` | One flat range table for the whole statement, subqueries included ([pathnodes.h#PlannerGlobal-finalrtable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L116-L117)) | `add_rtes_to_flat_rtable()` ([setrefs.c#set_plan_references-flatten](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L294-L299)) | stored in the plan | executor, EXPLAIN |
| `relationOids`, `invalItems` | The relations, user functions and domains the plan depends on ([pathnodes.h#PlannerGlobal-dependencies](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L131-L135)) | `set_plan_references()` and inlining ([setrefs.c#add_rte_to_flat_rtable-relationOids](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L564-L578), [setrefs.c#record_plan_function_dependency](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3464-L3497)) | stored | plan-cache invalidation |
| `extParam`, `allParam` | The `PARAM_EXEC` slots that affect a node, which decide when it must be rescanned ([plannodes.h#Plan-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L159-L171)) | `SS_finalize_plan()` ([subselect.c#SS_finalize_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L2246-L2260)) | stored | executor rescans |
| `transientPlan`, `dependsOnRole`, `jitFlags` | Whether the plan expires when [TransactionXmin](../../../glossary.md#transactionxmin) moves, whether it is valid only for the current role, and which JIT work to do ([plannodes.h#PlannedStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L62-L68)) | `get_relation_info()`, foreign joins and inlining, the plan's total cost ([planner.c#standard_planner-result-flags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L545-L546), [planner.c#standard_planner-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L564-L587)) | stored | plan cache, executor |
| `CachedPlanSource` | One cached statement: raw tree, analyzed queries, their dependencies, the `search_path` and role they were analyzed under, the generic plan, and cost totals ([plancache.h#CachedPlanSource](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/plancache.h#L96-L135)) | `CreateCachedPlan()` and `CompleteCachedPlan()` ([plancache.c#CompleteCachedPlan-deps](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L420-L445)) | stored for the life of the prepared statement | `GetCachedPlan()` |
| `CachedPlan` | One built plan list, with validity, role and `saved_xmin` ([plancache.h#CachedPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/plancache.h#L137-L161)) | `BuildCachedPlan()` ([plancache.c#BuildCachedPlan-flags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1007-L1041)) | stored while referenced | portals |
| `generic_cost`, `total_custom_cost`, `num_custom_plans`, `num_generic_plans` | The running figures for the custom-versus-generic choice ([plancache.h#CachedPlanSource-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/plancache.h#L130-L134)) | `GetCachedPlan()` ([plancache.c#GetCachedPlan-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1226-L1261)) | stored; costs are estimates | `choose_custom_plan()`; shown in `pg_prepared_statements` ([prepare.c#pg_prepared_statement-counters](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L729-L730)) |
| `plan_cache_mode` | `auto`, `force_custom_plan` or `force_generic_plan` ([guc_tables.c#plan_cache_mode](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L5112-L5121)) | setting, `PGC_USERSET`: session or transaction scope | parameter | `choose_custom_plan()` |
| `boundParams` | Actual parameter values given to the planner for a custom plan ([plancache.c#BuildCachedPlan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L897-L912)) | the caller of `GetCachedPlan()` | parameter | constant folding turns them into constants ([clauses.c#eval_const_expressions-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2466-L2524)) |

Two cost figures look alike but are measured differently. `generic_cost` is the generic plan's total cost, while each custom plan adds a charge for planning: `1000 × cpu_operator_cost × (relations in the range table + 1)` ([plancache.c#cached_plan_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1103-L1155)). The comparison therefore asks whether the generic plan beats "run the custom plan plus plan it again".

#### 14.3 Logic map

##### From path to PlannedStmt

```text
best Path (from the final upper relation)
|
+-- [A] create_plan -> create_plan_recurse, one switch arm per path type
|        scans, joins, Append/MergeAppend, Result variants, ProjectSet, Material,
|        Memoize, Unique, Gather, Sort, IncrementalSort, Group, Agg, WindowAgg,
|        SetOp, RecursiveUnion, LockRows, ModifyTable, Limit, GatherMerge
|        each child is built with CP_* flags from its parent;
|        pseudoconstant quals get a gating Result; initPlans attach at the top
|
+-- [B] any PARAM_EXEC Params? -> SS_finalize_plan on subplans, then main plan:
|        compute extParam / allParam for every node
|
+-- [C] set_plan_references on main plan and every subplan:
|        flatten range tables; renumber Vars (scan: flat RT index; join/upper:
|        OUTER_VAR / INNER_VAR); drop trivial SubqueryScan/Append/MergeAppend;
|        look up operator functions; record relationOids and invalItems
|
+-- [D] build PlannedStmt: copy flags (transientPlan, dependsOnRole, parallelModeNeeded),
         lists, and jitFlags from top_plan->total_cost against the jit_* thresholds
```

- [A] [createplan.c#create_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L337-L382), [createplan.c#create_plan_recurse](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L388-L455), [createplan.c#create_plan_recurse-upper](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L456-L526), [createplan.c#create_plan_recurse-end](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L527-L553), [createplan.c#create_scan_plan-gating](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L601-L627)
- [B] [planner.c#standard_planner-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L501-L518)
- [C] [setrefs.c#set_plan_references-steps](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L220-L268)
- [D] [planner.c#standard_planner-plannedstmt-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L537-L587)

##### Getting a plan from the cache

```text
GetCachedPlan(plansource, boundParams)
|
+-- [E] RevalidateCachedQuery
|        one-shot or never-replanned statement? -> use as is
|        search_path differs? / RLS used and role or row_security changed? -> invalid
|        valid -> lock the relations; an invalidation during locking -> invalid
|        invalid -> redo parse analysis and rewrite (new Query list, new dependencies)
|
+-- [F] choose_custom_plan
|        one-shot -> custom          no parameters -> generic
|        plan_cache_mode or cursor options force a choice -> that choice
|        fewer than 5 custom plans so far -> custom
|        generic_cost < average custom cost (incl. planning charge) -> generic, else custom
|
+-- [G] generic wanted: CheckCachedPlan (role? TransactionXmin for a transient plan?
|        lock and recheck) -> reuse; else BuildCachedPlan(NULL params), store
|        generic_cost, and ask choose_custom_plan again
|
+-- [H] custom wanted: BuildCachedPlan(boundParams); add its cost (with planning
         charge) to total_custom_cost; num_custom_plans++   else num_generic_plans++
```

- [E] [plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L602-L662), [plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-reanalyze](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L664-L731)
- [F] [plancache.c#choose_custom_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1053-L1101)
- [G] [plancache.c#CheckCachedPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L829-L895), [plancache.c#GetCachedPlan-generic](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1196-L1247)
- [H] [plancache.c#GetCachedPlan-custom](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1249-L1261)

#### 14.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: build Plan nodes from Paths

Input: the best path. `create_plan()` calls `create_plan_recurse()` with `CP_EXACT_TLIST`, because the top node must return exactly the query's columns ([createplan.c#create_plan-exact-tlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L337-L350)). The recursive function switches on the path's node type. Its case list is also a complete list of what the planner can produce, so it serves as a checklist for chapters 6 to 13 ([createplan.c#create_plan_recurse](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L388-L455), [createplan.c#create_plan_recurse-upper](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L456-L526), [createplan.c#create_plan_recurse-end](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L527-L553)).

Each parent tells each child what target list it needs. `CP_SMALL_TLIST` asks for only the needed columns, because nodes such as Sort and Hash store their input ([createplan.c#CP-flags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L50-L73)). Without such a request, a table scan returns all columns in table order, so that the executor can skip a projection step ([createplan.c#create_scan_plan-physical-tlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L629-L643)).

Two more things happen here. A condition that references no table column, a pseudoconstant, becomes a one-time filter in a gating Result node ([createplan.c#create_scan_plan-gating](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L601-L627)). And the query level's InitPlans are attached to the top node ([createplan.c#create_plan-initplans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L362-L373)). Output: a plan tree whose column references still use the planner's numbering ([createplan.c#create_plan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L322-L331)).

##### Step 2: finalize parameters

Input: the plan tree and any `PARAM_EXEC` slots. If the planner created parameters, `SS_finalize_plan()` runs over every subplan and then the main plan ([planner.c#standard_planner-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L501-L518)). It computes each node's `extParam` and `allParam` sets ([subselect.c#SS_finalize_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L2246-L2260), [plannodes.h#Plan-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L159-L171)). Consequence: when a parameter changes value, the executor knows exactly which nodes must restart.

##### Step 3: fix references and record dependencies

Input: the plan tree. `set_plan_references()` does nine jobs, listed in its header ([setrefs.c#set_plan_references-steps](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L220-L268)). The ones a reader sees most are these:

1. It appends every range-table entry to one flat list and clears the fields the executor does not need, such as a view's subquery ([setrefs.c#set_plan_references-flatten](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L294-L299), [setrefs.c#add_rte_to_flat_rtable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L530-L562)).
2. It turns column references in join nodes into references to the outer or inner input's output columns ([setrefs.c#set_join_references](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L2273-L2282)).
3. It removes a SubqueryScan whose target list only repeats its child's output and which has no filter ([setrefs.c#trivial_subqueryscan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L1438-L1484)).
4. It records the OID of every table and view in `relationOids`. That includes tables no longer in the plan, such as an expanded view or a child removed by constraint exclusion ([setrefs.c#add_rte_to_flat_rtable-relationOids](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L564-L578)).
5. It records user-defined functions and domains in `invalItems`, and ignores built-in objects on the assumption that they never change ([setrefs.c#record_plan_function_dependency](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3464-L3497), [setrefs.c#record_plan_type_dependency](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3499-L3533)). Domain dependencies come from constant folding, which records one when it removes a domain coercion.

Output: an executable plan tree plus the dependency lists.

##### Step 4: assemble the PlannedStmt

Input: the finished tree and `PlannerGlobal`. `standard_planner()` copies the statement type, flags and lists into a new `PlannedStmt` ([planner.c#standard_planner-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L537-L562)). It then compares the top node's total cost with `jit_above_cost`, `jit_optimize_above_cost` and `jit_inline_above_cost` to set `jitFlags`, the plan's request for JIT compilation ([planner.c#standard_planner-jit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L564-L587)). Output: the `PlannedStmt` that the caller runs or caches.

##### Step 5: create a cached plan source

A prepared statement is split in two. `CreateCachedPlan()` stores the raw tree before analysis, and `CompleteCachedPlan()` stores the analyzed and rewritten queries ([plancache.c#CreateCachedPlan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L175-L198)). `CompleteCachedPlan()` also extracts the query tree's dependencies, the role and `row_security` used for rewriting, and the current `search_path` ([plancache.c#CompleteCachedPlan-deps](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L420-L445)). `SaveCachedPlan()` moves the entry into long-lived memory and onto the list that invalidation scans ([plancache.c#SaveCachedPlan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L474-L490), [plancache.c:520](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L520)). No plan exists yet.

##### Step 6: revalidate, choose, build

Each execution calls `GetCachedPlan()` ([plancache.c#GetCachedPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1157-L1194)). First, `RevalidateCachedQuery()` checks the saved `search_path` and the role, locks the tables, and repeats analysis and rewriting if anything invalidated the entry ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L602-L662), [plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-reanalyze](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L664-L731)).

Second, `choose_custom_plan()` decides the kind of plan by the rules in the logic map ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1053-L1101)). Third, the plan is found or built. A generic plan is reused only if `CheckCachedPlan()` finds it valid for the current role and, for a transient plan, for the current `TransactionXmin` ([plancache.c#CheckCachedPlan-validity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L845-L883)). When a generic plan is first built, its cost is stored and the choice is asked again, so a generic plan that turns out worse is never executed ([plancache.c#GetCachedPlan-generic-recheck](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1226-L1245)).

A custom plan is built with the actual values. Those values reach the planner as `boundParams`, and constant folding replaces each `$n` with a constant ([plancache.c#GetCachedPlan-custom](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1249-L1261), [clauses.c#eval_const_expressions-param](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L2466-L2524)). That is why a custom plan's `EXPLAIN` shows the value where a generic plan shows `$1` (E14.1).

##### Step 7: invalidation

The plan cache listens for [invalidation messages](../../../glossary.md#invalidation-message). It registers a [relcache](../../../glossary.md#relcache) callback, and syscache callbacks on functions, types, namespaces, operators, operator-family members, foreign servers, foreign-data wrappers, role membership, roles and databases ([plancache.c#InitPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L159-L173)).

| Callback | What it invalidates |
|---|---|
| relcache callback, for a table or view OID | every saved statement whose query or generic plan lists that OID ([plancache.c#PlanCacheRelCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1985-L2047)) |
| function and type callback | statements whose `invalItems` match the changed object ([plancache.c#PlanCacheObjectCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2069-L2080)) |
| role, membership and database callback | only role-dependent entries: a statement rewritten under row-level security, or a generic plan marked `dependsOnRole` ([plancache.c#PlanCacheRoleCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2179-L2227)) |
| namespace, operator, operator-family, foreign server and wrapper callback | every saved statement, through `ResetPlanCache()` ([plancache.c#PlanCacheSysCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2229-L2274)) |

The role callbacks arrived in the 17.11 release, in commit `1974acf23c` ("Invalidate plan cache after role changes"): it is an ancestor of the `Stamp 17.11.` commit `083ac03341` and not of the `Stamp 17.10.` commit `25c49f3a4a`.

`ANALYZE` reaches the plan cache only through the table's `pg_class` row. It stores its figures with `vac_update_relstats()`, which rewrites the row in place only when `relpages`, `reltuples` or `relallvisible` differ from the stored values ([analyze.c#do_analyze_rel-relstats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L623-L645), [vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-dirty](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1446-L1461), [vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-finish](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1545-L1548)). That in-place update sends the invalidations for the changed `pg_class` row, and a `pg_class` row defines a relcache entry, so a relcache invalidation for the table goes out. `PlanCacheRelCallback` matches it against `relationOids` ([heapam.c#heap_inplace_update_and_unlock-inval](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/heapam.c#L6888-L6907), [inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-relcache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1376-L1392)).

The column statistics take a different path. `ANALYZE` replaces every `pg_statistic` row it computes ([analyze.c#update_attstats-replace](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1709-L1735)). A `pg_statistic` change queues catalog-cache messages but no relcache message, because only `pg_class`, `pg_attribute`, `pg_index` and foreign-key `pg_constraint` rows define relcache entries, and the plan cache registers no callback for the statistics cache ([inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-relcache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1376-L1392), [inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-other-catalogs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1440-L1446), [plancache.c#InitPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L159-L173)). Inserting rows into a user table queues no invalidation at all ([inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTupleCommon-user-tables](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1344-L1350)). So in E14.6 the replan after "insert, then `ANALYZE`" comes from the `ANALYZE`'s `pg_class` update, not from the insert.

When a cached statement is analyzed again, its cost history survives. `RevalidateCachedQuery()` keeps `generic_cost` and `total_custom_cost` on purpose, so the rebuilt plan is chosen by the old five-plan average without five new custom plans ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-keep-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L805-L811)). Another session sees the invalidation when it next locks the table, because taking a new lock processes pending messages ([lmgr.c#LockRelationOid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/storage/lmgr/lmgr.c#L118-L138), [plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-locks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L641-L658)).

##### Step 8: queries embedded in functions and SPI

| Caller | How its queries are planned | Reuse |
|---|---|---|
| SQL-language function (not inlined) | `init_execution_state()` calls `pg_plan_query()` for each statement, with no parameter values ([functions.c#init_execution_state-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/functions.c#L485-L501)) | the plans live in `fn_extra` for the calling query only, and are rebuilt when stale ([functions.c#SQLFunctionCache-lifespan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/functions.c#L76-L90), [functions.c#fmgr_sql-cache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/functions.c#L1078-L1100)) |
| SPI with `SPI_prepare` | `_SPI_prepare_plan()` makes a normal cached plan source ([spi.c#_SPI_prepare_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/spi.c#L2256-L2301)) | plan-cache rules; saved with `SPI_keepplan()` |
| SPI with `SPI_execute`, `SPI_execute_extended` | a one-shot plan source, parsed only; analysis happens at execution ([spi.c#_SPI_prepare_oneshot_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/spi.c#L2309-L2329), [spi.c#_SPI_execute_plan-oneshot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/spi.c#L2506-L2529)) | none: a one-shot plan is always custom and never saved ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-oneshot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1058-L1060), [plancache.c#CreateOneShotCachedPlan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L270-L277)) |
| [PL/pgSQL](../../../glossary.md#plpgsql) static SQL and expressions | `exec_prepare_plan()` calls `SPI_prepare_extended()` and `SPI_keepplan()` on first use; variables become parameters ([pl_exec.c#exec_prepare_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c#L4160-L4191), [pl_exec.c#exec_run_select](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c#L5778-L5811)) | plan-cache rules, per function per session |
| PL/pgSQL simple expressions | an expression with no tables, sub-selects, aggregates or clauses is marked simple ([pl_exec.c#exec_simple_check_plan-rules](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c#L8066-L8105)) | evaluated directly after a cheap validity check ([plancache.c#CachedPlanAllowsSimpleValidityCheck](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1320-L1342)) |
| PL/pgSQL `EXECUTE` | `exec_stmt_dynexecute()` calls `SPI_execute_extended()` ([pl_exec.c#exec_stmt_dynexecute-execute](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/pl/plpgsql/src/pl_exec.c#L4466-L4474)) | none: one-shot, planned every time |

The SQL-function comment says it would someday use `plancache.c` to keep plans longer ([functions.c#SQLFunctionCache-plancache-note](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/functions.c#L80-L82)). In 17 it does not.

#### 14.5 Eligibility and comparison

A statement can use a custom plan only if it has parameters and planning is not a no-op ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-no-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1062-L1067)). Its first five executions are always custom unless a setting or cursor option forces the choice ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-forced-and-five](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1069-L1083)).

From the sixth execution on, the generic plan wins when its cost is below the average custom cost. Because the average includes the planning charge, a generic plan can win even when it is slightly more expensive to run ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-average](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1081-L1100)). The comparison uses estimates only. A generic plan whose estimate is too optimistic for a skewed value still wins, which is what E14.2 shows. The `PREPARE` documentation describes the same five-execution rule ([prepare.sgml#notes-plan-choice](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/prepare.sgml#L142-L152)).

A generic plan also loses capabilities that depend on values. A partial index whose predicate needs `status = 'pending'` cannot be proven usable from `status = $1`, so the generic plan in E7.10 uses a different index than the custom plan.

#### 14.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Statement has no parameters | `choose_custom_plan()` always returns generic ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-no-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1062-L1067)) | planned once, reused until invalidated (E14.5 `sp`) |
| One-shot plan (SPI `execute`, PL/pgSQL `EXECUTE`) | always custom, not saved, no invalidation ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-oneshot](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1058-L1060), [plancache.c#CreateOneShotCachedPlan-comment](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L270-L277)) | planned on every execution |
| First generic plan costs more than the custom average | it is built, costed and kept as the cached generic plan, but not executed; a custom plan runs instead ([plancache.c#GetCachedPlan-generic-recheck](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1226-L1245)) | one extra planning run, and the generic cost is remembered |
| `search_path` changed since analysis | the entry is invalidated and analysis repeats ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-search_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L615-L630)) | a new plan (E14.5: 4 executions, 2 plans) |
| Row-level security was applied and the role or `row_security` changed | re-analysis ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-rls](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L632-L639)) | policies are reapplied for the new role |
| Generic plan depends on the role and the role changed | `CheckCachedPlan()` rejects it ([plancache.c#CheckCachedPlan-role](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L845-L850)) | rebuilt for the new role |
| Transient plan and `TransactionXmin` moved | rejected ([plancache.c#CheckCachedPlan-xmin](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L866-L873)) | the plan can now use an index that was skipped because of indcheckxmin |
| Built-in function or type changes | not tracked ([setrefs.c#record_plan_function_dependency-builtins](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3474-L3483)) | no invalidation for built-ins |
| `ANALYZE` writes new column statistics but leaves `relpages`, `reltuples` and `relallvisible` unchanged | `pg_statistic` changes queue catalog-cache messages, not a relcache message ([inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-relcache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1376-L1392), [inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-other-catalogs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1440-L1446)); the plan cache registers no callback for statistics ([plancache.c#InitPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L159-L173)) | a cached generic plan survives with its old estimates (Measured, E14.6: `plans` stayed at 6) |
| `DISCARD PLANS` | `ResetPlanCache()` invalidates every saved entry ([discard.c#DiscardCommand](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/discard.c#L39-L40), [plancache.c#ResetPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2244-L2274)) | everything replans on next use |
| Transaction-control statements | never invalidated ([plancache.c#ResetPlanCache-transaction-control](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2260-L2269)) | `ROLLBACK` works in an aborted transaction |
| SQL function planned without parameter values | `pg_plan_query(..., NULL)` ([functions.c#init_execution_state-no-params](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/functions.c#L497-L501)) | its queries are always planned like generic plans, with `$n` unknown |

#### 14.7 Formulas and worked examples

##### The choice formula

Define `C_i` as the total cost of custom plan `i`, `n` as the number of range-table entries in its `PlannedStmt`, and `G` as the generic plan's total cost. Then:

```text
custom cost used for averaging  = C_i + 1000 * cpu_operator_cost * (n + 1)
average custom cost             = sum(custom costs) / num_custom_plans
use the generic plan            if num_custom_plans >= 5 and G < average custom cost
```

This is `cached_plan_cost()` and `choose_custom_plan()` ([plancache.c#cached_plan_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1103-L1155), [plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-average](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1081-L1100)). With the default `cpu_operator_cost` of 0.0025 (E5.1) and one table, the planning charge is `1000 × 0.0025 × 2 = 5.00`.

##### E14.1: a unique key

Estimated by the planner and measured, E14.1. The first `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` and four `EXECUTE`s produce five custom plans; the sixth execution switches. In order, the block shows the first custom plan, the `pg_prepared_statements` counters after five and after six executions, and the generic plan of the seventh:

```text
 Index Scan using orders_pkey on orders  (cost=0.29..8.30 rows=1 width=40)
   Index Cond: (id = 1)
...
 by_id |             0 |            5
...
 by_id |             1 |            5
...
 Index Scan using orders_pkey on orders  (cost=0.29..8.30 rows=1 width=40)
   Index Cond: (id = $1)
```

Derived: each custom plan costs `8.30 + 5.00 = 13.30` in the average, so the average is 13.30. The generic plan costs 8.30. Because `8.30 < 13.30`, the generic plan wins, and the `generic_plans` counter moves to 1, then 2 after the next `EXPLAIN EXECUTE`. `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` goes through `GetCachedPlan()` too, so it counts ([prepare.c#ExplainExecuteQuery-GetCachedPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L631)).

##### E14.2: a skewed parameter

Estimated by the planner, E14.2. Customer 7 is one of the twenty large customers; customer 500 is a small one:

In order, the custom plan for 7, the custom plan for 500, and the generic plan chosen at the sixth execution:

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=13.45..13.46 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Index Only Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders  (cost=0.29..12.30 rows=458 width=0)
         Index Cond: (customer_id = 7)
...
 Aggregate  (cost=4.49..4.50 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Index Only Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders  (cost=0.29..4.46 rows=10 width=0)
         Index Cond: (customer_id = 500)
...
 Aggregate  (cost=4.59..4.60 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Index Only Scan using orders_customer_id_idx on orders  (cost=0.29..4.55 rows=15 width=0)
         Index Cond: (customer_id = $1)
```

Derived. The five custom plans were for 7 (four times: one `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` and three `EXECUTE`s) and 500 (once):

| Input | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---|
| custom cost for 7, with planning charge | 13.46 + 5.00 | 18.46 |
| custom cost for 500, with planning charge | 4.50 + 5.00 | 9.50 |
| average over five | (4 × 18.46 + 9.50) / 5 | 16.668 |
| generic cost | from the plan | 4.60 |
| decision | 4.60 < 16.668 | generic |

The generic plan's estimate of 15 rows is the table's 30,000 rows divided by 2,000 distinct customers, because a `$1` of unknown value gets the average frequency (chapter 4). So for customer 7 it plans for 15 rows while 458 exist. The choice is still reasonable here because both plans use the same index; the lesson is that the generic estimate cannot see the skew. E14.3 shows the two forced alternatives: `force_generic_plan` gives the 15-row plan and `force_custom_plan` the 458-row plan.

##### E14.4: invalidation by a new index

Estimated by the planner, E14.4. After five custom plans, the generic plan is a sequential scan. Creating an index sends a relcache invalidation for `orders`, so the next execution replans:

In order, the generic plan before the index, after `CREATE INDEX`, after `DROP INDEX`, and the final counters:

```text
 Aggregate  (cost=604.72..604.73 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=1488 width=0)
         Filter: (note = $1)
...
 Aggregate  (cost=38.05..38.06 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Index Only Scan using orders_note_idx on orders  (cost=0.29..34.33 rows=1488 width=0)
         Index Cond: (note = $1)
...
 Aggregate  (cost=604.72..604.73 rows=1 width=8)
   ->  Seq Scan on orders  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=1488 width=0)
...
 by_note |             3 |            5
```

Each DDL statement invalidated the generic plan, and each following `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` built a new generic plan, which gives three generic uses and still five custom plans.

##### E14.5: planning counts across the boundaries

Measured, E14.5. [`pg_stat_statements`](../../../glossary.md#pg_stat_statements) counts calls and planner invocations per statement; it runs as a `planner_hook` and counts when `track_planning` is on ([pg_stat_statements.c#pgss_planner-track](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L887-L894)):

```text
 toplevel | calls | plans |                                      query
 f        |    10 |     6 | (SELECT /* wiki_pqt_e14_5_plpgsql */ count(*) FROM orders WHERE id = p)
 t        |     4 |     2 | PREPARE /* wiki_pqt_e14_5_prepared */ sp AS SELECT count(*) FROM orders
 f        |     6 |     6 | SELECT /* wiki_pqt_e14_5_dynamic */ count(amount) FROM orders WHERE id = $1
 f        |    10 |     1 | SELECT /* wiki_pqt_e14_5_sqlbatch */ count(customer_id) FROM orders WHERE id = p
 f        |     5 |     5 | SELECT /* wiki_pqt_e14_5_sqlfunc */ count(id) FROM orders WHERE id = p
```

| Row | Caller | Why this many plans |
|---|---|---|
| PL/pgSQL, 10 calls, 6 plans | saved SPI plan with parameters | five custom plans, then one generic plan reused for the last five calls (14.5) |
| `PREPARE sp`, 4 executions, 2 plans | no parameters | one generic plan; `SET search_path` before the fourth execution invalidated it (14.6) |
| `EXECUTE` in PL/pgSQL, 6 calls, 6 plans | one-shot plan | always custom, never saved |
| SQL function, 10 calls in one statement, 1 plan | `fn_extra` cache | planned at the first call and reused by the other nine calls of the same query |
| SQL function, 5 statements, 5 plans | `fn_extra` cache | each statement has a new `FmgrInfo`, so each plans again |

##### E14.6: ANALYZE and a cached generic plan

Measured, E14.6. The experiment runs on `stale_t`, a disposable copy of `orders` with an index on `customer_id`, and on a prepared `sp2(int)` that counts one customer's rows. It executes `sp2(7)` seven times, then runs `ANALYZE` twice with one execution after each. The counters come from `pg_stat_statements` (`calls`, `plans`) and `pg_prepared_statements` (`generic_plans`, `custom_plans`):

```text
        step        | calls | plans | generic_plans | custom_plans
--------------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------------
 after 7 executions |     7 |     6 |             2 |            5
...
ANALYZE /* wiki_pqt_e14_6 */ stale_t;
...
 relpages | reltuples
----------+-----------
      226 |     30000
...
                 step                  | calls | plans | generic_plans | custom_plans
---------------------------------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------------
 after an ANALYZE that changed no size |     8 |     6 |             3 |            5
...
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_e14_6 */ INTO stale_t SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 7;
ANALYZE /* wiki_pqt_e14_6 */ stale_t;
...
 relpages | reltuples
----------+-----------
      229 |     30458
...
                    step                     | calls | plans | generic_plans | custom_plans
---------------------------------------------+-------+-------+---------------+--------------
 after an ANALYZE that changed the row count |     9 |     7 |             4 |            5
```

Derived, from the counters:

| Moment | What the counters say | Why |
|---|---|---|
| after 7 executions | 6 plans: 5 custom, then 1 generic, used twice | executions 1 to 5 are custom; execution 6 builds the generic plan and uses it; execution 7 reuses it (14.5) |
| after `ANALYZE` with 226 pages and 30,000 rows | `plans` unchanged at 6; `generic_plans` 3 | the size figures did not change, so `vac_update_relstats()` sent no relcache message and the existing generic plan ran again ([vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-finish](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1545-L1548)) |
| after 458 inserted rows and `ANALYZE` with 229 pages and 30,458 rows | `plans` 7; `generic_plans` 4; `custom_plans` still 5 | the in-place `pg_class` update invalidated the entry ([heapam.c#heap_inplace_update_and_unlock-inval](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/heapam.c#L6888-L6907)); the next execution re-analyzed and built one new generic plan, and the kept cost history chose it without new custom plans ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-keep-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L805-L811)) |

The first `ANALYZE` still rewrote the column statistics, because it replaces every `pg_statistic` row it computes ([analyze.c#update_attstats-replace](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1709-L1735)). The row count of the query also moved, from 458 to 916 (measured), after the insert added customer 7's 458 rows a second time. So a cached plan keeps its old estimates through statistics refreshes that do not change the table's size figures, and only a change to those figures, or DDL, makes it replan.
