##### E7.10, E11.3 and E12.10: what a generic plan cannot know, and what the PlannedStmt carries

Estimated by the planner, E7.10 (forced settings). The partial index `orders_pending_cust` requires `status = 'pending'`. The custom plan can prove it; the generic plan with `status = $1` cannot. In order, the plan under `force_generic_plan` and the plan under `force_custom_plan`:

```text
 Bitmap Heap Scan on orders  (cost=4.40..53.03 rows=5 width=40)
   Recheck Cond: (customer_id = $2)
   Filter: (status = $1)
...
 Index Scan using orders_pending_cust on orders  (cost=0.28..8.30 rows=1 width=40)
   Index Cond: (customer_id = 700)
```

Measured, E11.3c (the `ANALYZE` run; the plain `EXPLAIN` of E11.3b already shows the same line). A generic plan can still prune partitions, but later: the executor removes the non-matching partitions when it starts the plan, once `$1` is known ([nodeAppend.c#ExecInitAppend-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L138-L164)):

```text
   ->  Append  (cost=0.28..55.14 rows=151 width=0) (actual rows=2626 loops=1)
         Subplans Removed: 12
```

Measured, E12.10. The `jitFlags` field of the `PlannedStmt` follows the cost thresholds even though this build has no JIT provider. The query's plan costs 14319.01, below the default `jit_above_cost` of 100000:

| Settings (forced) | `jitFlags` logged | Flags set ([jit.h#PGJIT](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/jit/jit.h#L19-L24)) |
|---|---|---|
| defaults | 0 | none |
| `jit_above_cost = 10` | 25 | PERFORM 1 + EXPR 8 + DEFORM 16 |
| all three thresholds 10 | 31 | also OPT3 2 + INLINE 4 |
| `jit = off` | 0 | none |

##### E1.3: target lists chosen at plan creation

Estimated by the planner, E1.3. In Q1's hash join, the orders scan returns all six columns and the customers scan returns two:

```text
               ->  Seq Scan on public.orders o  (cost=0.00..601.00 rows=3019 width=14)
                     Output: o.id, o.customer_id, o.status, o.ordered_at, o.amount, o.note
               ->  Hash  (cost=47.00..47.00 rows=200 width=18)
                     Output: c.name, c.id
```

The hash join asks its inner input for a small target list because the Hash node stores it, and asks the outer input for one only when it expects batching ([createplan.c#create_hashjoin_plan-tlists](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L4767-L4778)). With no such request, the orders scan uses the full-row list ([createplan.c#create_scan_plan-physical-tlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L629-L643)).

#### 14.8 Planning versus execution

| Decided while planning | Decided or done while executing |
|---|---|
| Plan shape, target lists and dependency lists | locks: before running a cached plan, `AcquireExecutorLocks()` locks every relation in the plan's range table, including partitions that initial pruning will skip ([plancache.c#AcquireExecutorLocks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1775-L1825)) |
| Pruning steps stored with the Append (chapter 11) | initial pruning at executor startup and further pruning while running ([nodeAppend.c#ExecInitAppend-pruning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAppend.c#L138-L164)) |
| Custom or generic, from estimated costs | whether the plan is still valid: invalidation messages are processed when locks are taken, and a plan invalidated at that moment is rebuilt ([plancache.c#CheckCachedPlan-locks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L856-L895)) |
| `jitFlags` | code generation, only if a JIT provider loads (chapter 12) |
| Row estimates inside a cached generic plan, from the statistics current at planning time | reuse at every execution without reading statistics again; the plan is rebuilt only after an invalidation, such as an `ANALYZE` that changes the table's size figures (Measured, E14.6) |

#### 14.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PREPARE` | no entry | valid `CachedPlanSource`, no plan ([prepare.c#PrepareQuery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L87-L127)) | first execution plans |
| Executions 1 to 5 (with parameters) | `num_custom_plans` 0 to 4 | a custom plan each time, costs accumulated | the average custom cost exists |
| Execution 6 | no generic plan (`generic_cost = -1`) | generic plan built and costed; used if cheaper ([plancache.c#choose_custom_plan-unknown-generic](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1094-L1098)) | later executions reuse it |
| DDL on a referenced table, index or view | valid entry | invalid query tree and generic plan ([plancache.c#PlanCacheRelCallback-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2012-L2046)) | re-analysis and replanning on next use (E14.4) |
| `ANALYZE` that changes `relpages`, `reltuples` or `relallvisible` | stored values | `pg_class` row rewritten in place, which queues a relcache invalidation ([vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-dirty](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1446-L1461), [vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-finish](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1545-L1548), [heapam.c#heap_inplace_update_and_unlock-inval](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/heapam.c#L6888-L6907)) | plans on that table are rebuilt on next use (Measured, E14.6: after 458 inserted rows and `ANALYZE`, 229 pages and 30,458 rows, `plans` rose from 6 to 7) |
| `ANALYZE` that changes only `pg_statistic` | old statistics | new statistics; no relcache message ([inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-relcache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1376-L1392), [inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTuple-other-catalogs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1440-L1446)) | an existing generic plan keeps its old estimates until something else invalidates it (Measured, E14.6: `plans` stayed at 6) |
| Rows inserted, updated or deleted, with no `ANALYZE` | stored size figures | unchanged; user-table rows queue no invalidation ([inval.c#CacheInvalidateHeapTupleCommon-user-tables](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/inval.c#L1344-L1350)) | a cached plan keeps running; a newly built plan would scale its estimates by the current file size (chapter 4) |
| `SET search_path` | entry analyzed under the old path | invalid on next use ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-search_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L615-L630)) | re-analysis (E14.5) |
| `SET ROLE` or `row_security` change with RLS | entry analyzed for the old role | invalid on next use ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-rls](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L632-L639)) | policies reapplied |
| Role, membership or database-owner catalog change | role-dependent entries valid | those entries invalid ([plancache.c#PlanCacheRoleCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2179-L2227)) | replanned for the new rules |
| `TransactionXmin` advances past a transient plan's `saved_xmin` | transient generic plan valid | rejected ([plancache.c#CheckCachedPlan-xmin](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L866-L873)) | replanned, possibly with the new index |
| `DISCARD PLANS`, or a namespace or operator change | valid entries | all invalid ([plancache.c#ResetPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2244-L2274)) | everything replans |
| A new statement calls an SQL function | no `fn_extra` cache | cache built at the first call ([functions.c#fmgr_sql-cache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/functions.c#L1078-L1100)) | reused only within that statement and transaction |

#### 14.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- Plan-cache invalidation on DDL, views, `search_path`, SPI and PL/pgSQL simple expressions, and the `plan_cache_mode` counters: [plancache.sql#invalidation](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/plancache.sql#L1-L56), [plancache.sql#spi-and-simple-expressions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/plancache.sql#L57-L96), [plancache.sql#search_path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/plancache.sql#L97-L127), [plancache.sql#plan_cache_mode](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/plancache.sql#L181-L225).
- `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN)` and its refusal with `ANALYZE`: [explain.sql#generic_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L91-L95).
- Replan counting through `pg_stat_statements`: [planning.sql#replan-counting](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/sql/planning.sql#L10-L27).
- PL/pgSQL behavior that depends on cached plans: [plpgsql_cache.sql](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/pl/plpgsql/src/sql/plpgsql_cache.sql#L1-L30).
- Invalidation that arrives between planning and execution of partitioned plans: the `delay_execution` isolation specs ([delay_execution.c header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/modules/delay_execution/delay_execution.c#L1-L19)).
- Gaps: no regression test covers the role-change callbacks added by `1974acf23c` (the commit changed no test file), and none checks how `ANALYZE` affects a cached generic plan. E14.5 is this page's only evidence for the SQL-function and one-shot planning counts, and E14.6 its only evidence for the `ANALYZE` behavior.

#### 14.11 Causal summary

1. Plan construction: the best path goes to `create_plan()`, which builds nodes with the target lists each parent needs.
2. Finalization: `SS_finalize_plan()` records parameter dependencies, `set_plan_references()` renumbers references and records the plan's dependencies, and `standard_planner()` adds the flags and `jitFlags`.
3. Caching: a cached statement with parameters runs five custom plans, then compares the generic cost with their average plus a planning charge.
4. Invalidation: DDL, `search_path`, role and xmin events, and an `ANALYZE` that changes the table's size figures invalidate entries, so the next execution replans; new column statistics alone do not.
5. Bypass: SQL functions plan once per calling statement, and one-shot SPI calls plan every time, outside the cache.

### Chapter 15. Extend and navigate the planner

#### 15.1 Main idea

The planner is built to be extended without patching it. Extensions can change its behavior at five kinds of boundary. A hook is a global function pointer that core code calls at a fixed point. A foreign data wrapper supplies callbacks that size, cost and plan scans of foreign tables, and may push whole joins and aggregates to a remote server. A custom scan provider adds its own paths. Access methods describe what their indexes and tables can do. Planner support functions teach the planner about individual SQL functions.

This matters because most of what an extension does to planning happens through these boundaries, not through new SQL. The rule that ties them together is simple: an extension adds or edits paths, and `add_path()` compares them with the core paths by the same cost rules as chapter 2 ([allpaths.c#set_rel_pathlist-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L532-L539)).

The surprising part is how few of these interfaces the core tree itself uses. Only two in-core modules set `planner_hook`: `pg_stat_statements`, which counts planning in chapter 14, and a test module. No in-core module sets any other planning hook or provides a custom scan. This chapter also maps the source tree, so that a reader can find each mechanism of the other chapters. Its experiments are E15.1 to E15.4, with E6.10, E7.1 and E14.5 as supporting evidence ([E15.1](#measurement-script)).

#### 15.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hook variables such as `planner_hook` | function pointers, NULL unless a loaded library set them | the library's initialization code ([pg_stat_statements.c#_PG_init-hooks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L460-L472)) | current: process-local state of the backend | the call sites in section 15.4 |
| `FdwRoutine` | a foreign data wrapper's table of callbacks | its handler function ([fdwapi.h#FdwRoutine](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/foreign/fdwapi.h#L203-L281)) | looked up per foreign table while planning | `set_foreign_size()`, `add_paths_to_joinrel()`, `grouping_planner()`, `make_modifytable()` |
| `RelOptInfo.serverid`, `userid`, `fdwroutine` of a join | set only when both sides use one foreign server and one user mapping ([relnode.c#set_foreign_rel_properties](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L585-L619)) | derived while building join relations | plan-time | `GetForeignJoinPaths` and `GetForeignUpperPaths` |
| `CustomPath` and `CustomPathMethods` | a provider's path, with a callback that turns it into a plan ([pathnodes.h#CustomPath](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1904-L1914), [extensible.h#CustomPathMethods](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/extensible.h#L88-L106)) | a hook adds it | plan-time | `create_customscan_plan()` |
| `IndexAmRoutine` capability flags and `amcostestimate` | what an index type can do, and its cost function ([amapi.h#IndexAmRoutine](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/amapi.h#L214-L256), [amapi.h#IndexAmRoutine-functions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/amapi.h#L270-L289)) | the index AM's handler | fixed per access method | copied into each IndexOptInfo ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-am](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L317-L332)) |
| `relation_estimate_size` | the table AM's size estimate for planning ([tableam.h#relation_estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/tableam.h#L767-L780)) | the table AM | estimate from the live file and stored density | `estimate_rel_size()` |
| `TsmRoutine.SampleScanGetSampleSize` | a sampling method's estimate of pages and rows it will read ([tsmapi.h#TsmRoutine](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/tsmapi.h#L56-L76)) | the method's handler | estimate | `set_tablesample_rel_size()` |
| `SupportRequest*` nodes | questions the planner asks a function's support function ([supportnodes.h#header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/supportnodes.h#L3-L24)) | `pg_proc.prosupport` ([pg_proc.h#prosupport](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_proc.h#L55-L56)) | stored catalog link; answers are plan-time estimates | simplification, selectivity, cost, rows, index conditions, windows |
| catalog columns such as `oprrest`, `procost`, `aggcombinefn` | the planner-facing facts about operators, functions and aggregates (E15.2 to E15.4) | `pg_operator`, `pg_proc`, `pg_aggregate` | stored | estimators, cost of quals, parallel aggregation |

Two kinds of extension state behave differently. Hooks and support functions are code: they apply to every query planned after the library is loaded or the function is attached. Catalog columns and FDW options are data: changing them sends an invalidation, and cached plans that depend on them are rebuilt (section 15.9).

#### 15.3 Logic map

```text
standard pipeline                           extension boundary
-----------------                           ------------------
planner()                               [A] planner_hook replaces or wraps standard_planner()
 subquery_planner / grouping_planner
  query_planner
   get_relation_info (catalogs)         [B] get_relation_info_hook edits RelOptInfo / IndexOptInfo
                                        [C] index AM flags + amcostestimate; table AM relation_estimate_size
   set_rel_size                         [D] FDW GetForeignRelSize; tablesample SampleScanGetSampleSize
   selectivity estimates                [E] get_relation_stats_hook / get_index_stats_hook / get_attavgwidth_hook;
                                            operator oprrest/oprjoin; support SupportRequestSelectivity
   expression preprocessing             [F] support SupportRequestSimplify; SupportRequestCost; SupportRequestRows
   set_rel_pathlist                     [G] FDW GetForeignPaths; set_rel_pathlist_hook (CustomPaths)
   join search                          [H] join_search_hook replaces the whole search
    add_paths_to_joinrel                [I] FDW GetForeignJoinPaths; set_join_pathlist_hook
  upper steps (grouping ... final)      [J] FDW GetForeignUpperPaths; create_upper_paths_hook
 create_plan                            [K] FDW GetForeignPlan; CustomPathMethods->PlanCustomPath;
                                            FDW PlanForeignModify / PlanDirectModify
EXPLAIN                                 [L] ExplainOneQuery_hook; explain_get_index_name_hook
```

#### 15.4 Step by step

##### Step 1. Find your way around the source

| `utils/cache/plancache.c` | cached plans, custom versus generic, invalidation ([plancache.c header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L3-L12)) | 14 |

The node definitions sit in `src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h` for the planner's working structures and `plannodes.h` for its output ([pathnodes.h header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L3-L4), [plannodes.h header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L3-L4)). The planner's functions are declared in `src/include/optimizer/`. Code outside the planner is meant to include only `optimizer/optimizer.h`, but FDW planning code counts as a planner module and may use the rest ([optimizer.h header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/optimizer.h#L3-L13)).

##### Step 2. Hooks that replace a stage

Two hooks take over a whole stage. `planner()` calls `planner_hook` instead of `standard_planner()` when it is set, so the hook can run the standard planner and do work around it, or plan in its own way ([planner.c#planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L274-L285), [planner.h#planner_hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/planner.h#L24-L29)). `make_rel_from_joinlist()` calls `join_search_hook` instead of both GEQO and the standard dynamic programming search ([allpaths.c#make_rel_from_joinlist-search](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3372-L3377)).

In the core tree only `pg_stat_statements` and the test module `delay_execution` set `planner_hook`. `pg_stat_statements` times each call and then calls the previous hook or `standard_planner()` ([pg_stat_statements.c#pgss_planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L892-L925)). `delay_execution` plans first and then takes and releases an advisory lock, so that an isolation test can block it there and change the database between planning and execution ([delay_execution.c#header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/modules/delay_execution/delay_execution.c#L3-L12), [delay_execution.c#delay_execution_planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/modules/delay_execution/delay_execution.c#L42-L61), [delay_execution.c#_PG_init](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/modules/delay_execution/delay_execution.c#L93-L94)). Nothing in the core tree sets `join_search_hook`.

One more hook marks the boundary just before planning. At the end of parse analysis, the core computes the query ID when query IDs are enabled, then calls `post_parse_analyze_hook` on the `Query` that the rewriter and planner will receive ([analyze.c#parse_analyze_fixedparams-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L123-L127)). `pg_stat_statements` sets this hook to record the normalized query text early ([pg_stat_statements.c#_PG_init-hooks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L460-L472), [pg_stat_statements.c#pgss_post_parse_analyze](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L855-L870)). Its planner hook counts a planning only when that query ID is not zero ([pg_stat_statements.c#pgss_planner-track](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L892-L895)).

##### Step 3. Hooks that edit a stage's output

Four hooks let an extension edit what a stage produced, and each call site sits right after the core work, so the extension sees the finished list:

| Hook | Called | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `get_relation_info_hook` | at the end of `get_relation_info()`, after sizes and indexes were read ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L569-L576)) | change the assumed size, drop an index, or add a hypothetical index, as the code comment lists |
| `set_rel_pathlist_hook` | after all base-relation paths, before Gather paths are generated ([allpaths.c#set_rel_pathlist-hook-gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L532-L551)) | add `CustomPath`s or partial paths; edit or delete core paths |
| `set_join_pathlist_hook` | last in `add_paths_to_joinrel()`, after nested loop, merge, hash and FDW join paths ([joinpath.c#add_paths_to_joinrel-fdw-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L325-L344)) | custom join paths |
| `create_upper_paths_hook` | after each upper stage: final, grouping, window, `DISTINCT`, partial `DISTINCT`, ordering, and set operations ([planner.c#grouping_planner-final-fdw-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2052-L2065), [planner.c#create_ordinary_grouping_paths-fdw-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4188-L4201), [planner.c#create_window_paths-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4638-L4640), [planner.c#create_distinct_paths-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4881-L4883), [planner.c#create_partial_distinct_paths-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5072-L5074), [planner.c#create_ordered_paths-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5479-L5481), [prepunion.c#create_upper_paths_hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1278-L1280)) | add upper-stage paths |

The upper relation kind tells a `create_upper_paths_hook` which stage called it ([planner.h#create_upper_paths_hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/optimizer/planner.h#L31-L37)). Of the eight kinds ([pathnodes.h#UpperRelationKind](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L69-L81)), the call sites in the pinned tree cover seven; the partial grouping stage calls only the FDW callback, not this hook ([planner.c#create_partial_grouping_paths-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7582-L7593)).

Three more hooks let an extension replace statistics. `examine_simple_variable()` asks `get_relation_stats_hook` before reading `pg_statistic`, and `examine_variable()` asks `get_index_stats_hook` for index expressions. B-tree and BRIN cost estimation ask `get_relation_stats_hook` for an index column that is a plain table column, and `get_index_stats_hook` for an expression column ([selfuncs.c#examine_simple_variable-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5375-L5376), [selfuncs.c#examine_variable-index-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L5203-L5204), [selfuncs.c#btcostestimate-hooks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L7126-L7153), [selfuncs.c#brincostestimate-hooks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L8135-L8167)). `get_attavgwidth()` asks `get_attavgwidth_hook` for a column's width ([lsyscache.c#get_attavgwidth-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/lsyscache.c#L3276-L3278)). None of these seven hooks has an in-core user.

##### Step 4. Foreign data wrappers, callback by callback

An FDW participates in planning through the callbacks below, which the planner calls in this order. `postgres_fdw` implements all of the planning ones except `IsForeignScanParallelSafe`, `GetForeignRowMarkType` and `ReparameterizeForeignPathByChild`, so it can push scans, joins, aggregates and whole writes to the remote server ([postgres_fdw.c#postgres_fdw_handler](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L558-L607)). `file_fdw` does implement `IsForeignScanParallelSafe` ([file_fdw.c:186](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/file_fdw.c#L186)).

| Callback | Called from | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| `GetForeignRelSize` | `set_foreign_size()`, after the core size estimate ([allpaths.c#set_foreign_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L901-L919)) | rows and width; the core then clamps rows and keeps `tuples` at least as large |
| `IsForeignScanParallelSafe` | `set_rel_consider_parallel()` ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-foreign](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L640-L651)) | whether a foreign scan may run in a parallel worker; absent means no |
| `GetForeignPaths` | `set_foreign_pathlist()` ([allpaths.c#set_foreign_pathlist](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L925-L930)) | the `ForeignPath`s for the table |
| `GetForeignJoinPaths` | `add_paths_to_joinrel()`, only when both sides share a server and user mapping ([joinpath.c#add_paths_to_joinrel-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L325-L334), [relnode.c#set_foreign_rel_properties](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L585-L619)) | a path that runs the join remotely |
| `GetForeignUpperPaths` | each upper stage whose input belongs to one FDW ([planner.c#create_ordinary_grouping_paths-fdw-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L4188-L4201)) | a path that runs grouping, sorting or `LIMIT` remotely |
| `GetForeignRowMarkType` | `select_rowmark_type()` ([planner.c#select_rowmark_type-foreign](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L2414-L2423)) | how locked or rechecked foreign rows are re-fetched (chapter 13) |
| `AddForeignUpdateTargets` | `add_row_identity_columns()` ([appendinfo.c#add_row_identity_columns-foreign](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/appendinfo.c#L916-L927)) | the junk columns that identify a remote row |
| `ReparameterizeForeignPathByChild` | reparameterizing a path for a partition ([pathnode.c#reparameterize_path_by_child-foreign](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L4228-L4242)) | partitionwise joins over foreign partitions |
| `GetForeignPlan` | `create_foreignscan_plan()` ([createplan.c#create_foreignscan_plan-GetForeignPlan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L4158-L4168)) | the `ForeignScan` node, including which quals run remotely |
| `IsForeignPathAsyncCapable` | `mark_async_capable_plan()` ([createplan.c#mark_async_capable_plan-foreign](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L1170-L1181)) | whether an `Append` may run the scan asynchronously |
| `PlanDirectModify`, `PlanForeignModify` | `make_modifytable()` ([createplan.c#make_modifytable-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7183-L7219)) | one remote statement, or row-by-row modification |

`postgres_fdw` pushes a join only when `foreign_join_ok()` accepts it: an inner, left, right, full or semi join ([postgres_fdw.c#foreign_join_ok-jointypes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L5801-L5810)). An anti join, the plan for `NOT EXISTS`, therefore stays local, as the regression suite checks ([postgres_fdw.sql#semi-anti-join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/sql/postgres_fdw.sql#L636-L643)). Semi-join push-down was committed in the 17 development cycle (`824dbea3e4`), which deparses the semi join as an `EXISTS` subquery.

##### Step 5. Custom scans

A custom scan provider adds `CustomPath`s from `set_rel_pathlist_hook` or `set_join_pathlist_hook`, using `add_path()` or `add_partial_path()` like core code ([custom-scan.sgml#custom-scan-path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/custom-scan.sgml#L34-L58), [custom-scan.sgml#custom-scan-join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/custom-scan.sgml#L102-L120)). If a custom path wins, `create_customscan_plan()` plans its children, orders its quals, and calls the provider's `PlanCustomPath` to build a `CustomScan` ([createplan.c#create_customscan_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L4277-L4310)). Flags declare whether the scan can run backward, mark and restore, or project ([extensible.h#CUSTOMPATH_SUPPORT](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/extensible.h#L84-L86)).

A `CustomScan` names its methods by `CustomName`, and reading a plan back looks that name up in a registry that the provider fills with `RegisterCustomScanMethods()` ([gen_node_support.pl#custom-methods](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/gen_node_support.pl#L1195-L1213), [extensible.c#RegisterCustomScanMethods](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/extensible.c#L84-L88)). No in-core module registers one.

##### Step 6. Access methods

Index access methods speak to the planner through flags and a few functions in `IndexAmRoutine` ([amapi.h#IndexAmRoutine](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/amapi.h#L214-L256), [amapi.h#IndexAmRoutine-functions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/amapi.h#L270-L289)):

| Field | Planner use |
|---|---|
| `amcanorder`, `amcanorderbyop` | ordered index paths, read in either direction, and nearest-neighbour paths (chapter 7) ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-am](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L317-L332), [plancat.c#get_relation_info-ordering](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L338-L362), [indxpath.c#build_index_paths-backward](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L1005-L1025)) |
| `amcanbackward` | not a path choice: for a scroll cursor the planner adds a `Material` node when `ExecSupportsBackwardScan()`, which reads this flag for index scans, says no ([planner.c#standard_planner-scroll](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L424-L432), [execAmi.c#IndexSupportsBackwardScan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execAmi.c#L602-L618)) |
| `amoptionalkey`, `amsearcharray`, `amsearchnulls` | whether a scan needs a first-column qual, and can take `= ANY` arrays and `IS NULL` |
| `amcanparallel` | parallel index scans (chapter 12) |
| `amgettuple`, `amgetbitmap` | whether plain index scans and bitmap scans are possible at all |
| `amcanreturn` | per-column index-only scans ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-canreturn](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L296-L301)) |
| `amcostestimate` | the index's cost, called from `cost_index()` ([amapi.h#amcostestimate_function](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/amapi.h#L138-L145), [costsize.c#cost_index-amcostestimate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L617-L621)) |

`get_relation_info()` copies the flags it needs into each `IndexOptInfo`, and it allows a bitmap scan only when the table AM also provides `scan_bitmap_next_block` ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-am](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L317-L332)). E7.1 reads the same capabilities from the catalog for all six built-in index types.

A table access method gives the planner one estimate: `relation_estimate_size`, called by `estimate_rel_size()` ([plancat.c#estimate_rel_size-tableam](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L1074-L1078), [tableam.h#table_relation_estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/tableam.h#L1944-L1951)). The heap implements it with the shared block-based helper, whose inputs are a per-tuple overhead and the usable bytes per page ([heapam_handler.c#heapam_estimate_rel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/heapam_handler.c#L2105-L2110), [tableam.c#table_block_relation_estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L634-L658)).

A tablesample method supplies `SampleScanGetSampleSize`, which overwrites the relation's page and row estimates before the ordinary size calculation ([allpaths.c#set_tablesample_rel_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L828-L843)). That is why E6.1's `SYSTEM_ROWS (25)` from the `tsm_system_rows` extension was estimated at exactly 25 rows.

##### Step 7. Support functions and catalog attributes

A support function is attached to an ordinary SQL function through `pg_proc.prosupport`. The planner calls it with a request node, and a NULL result means the support function has nothing to offer, so the planner falls back to its defaults ([supportnodes.h#header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/supportnodes.h#L3-L24)). Each built-in support function answers only the requests it recognizes. So two features that look alike can use different requests: a `LIKE` prefix becomes an index condition, while range containment is rewritten earlier, during constant folding.

| Request | Asked by | Fallback without an answer | Built-in example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SupportRequestSimplify` | `simplify_function()`, during constant folding ([clauses.c#simplify_function-support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4128-L4152)) | try SQL-function inlining ([clauses.c#simplify_function-inline](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/clauses.c#L4154-L4157)) | `elem_contained_by_range_support` rewrites `x <@` a constant range into bound comparisons, which is how E7.12's range condition reached the index; committed in the 17 cycle (`075df6b208`) ([rangetypes.c#elem_contained_by_range_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/rangetypes.c#L2183-L2206), [rangetypes.c#find_simplified_clause-const](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/rangetypes.c#L2786-L2814), [rangetypes.c#find_simplified_clause-bounds](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/rangetypes.c#L2852-L2880)) |
| `SupportRequestSelectivity` | `function_selectivity()` ([plancat.c#function_selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2044-L2060)) | 0.3333333 | `textlike_support`, for `LIKE` written as a function call ([like_support.c#like_regex_support-selectivity](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/like_support.c#L156-L166)) |
| `SupportRequestCost` | `add_function_cost()` ([plancat.c#add_function_cost-support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2105-L2136)) | `procost` × `cpu_operator_cost` | none built in; the regression suite's `test_support_func` answers it ([regress.c#test_support_func-cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/regress.c#L1063-L1072)) |
| `SupportRequestRows` | `get_function_rows()` ([plancat.c#get_function_rows-support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2166-L2193)) | `prorows` | `generate_series_int4_support` and `array_unnest_support`, behind E4.12's 250 and 4 rows ([int.c#generate_series_int4_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/int.c#L1613-L1622), [arrayfuncs.c#array_unnest_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/arrayfuncs.c#L6346-L6354)) |
| `SupportRequestIndexCondition` | `get_index_clause_from_support()` ([indxpath.c#get_index_clause_from_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L2557-L2585)) | no index condition from that clause | `textlike_support` turns E7.12's `name LIKE 'customer 01%'` into a B-tree range ([like_support.c#like_regex_support-indexcond](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/like_support.c#L192-L195)) |
| `SupportRequestWFuncMonotonic` | `find_window_run_conditions()` ([allpaths.c#find_window_run_conditions-support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L2265-L2272)) | no run condition | `window_row_number_support`, behind E10.8's `Run Condition` ([windowfuncs.c#window_row_number_support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/windowfuncs.c#L98-L113)) |
| `SupportRequestOptimizeWindowClause` | `optimize_window_clauses()` ([planner.c#optimize_window_clauses-support](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5807-L5822)) | frame left as written | the same `window_row_number_support` |

The same catalogs carry the other planner-facing facts. Operators name their restriction and join estimators in `oprrest` and `oprjoin`, and say whether they can drive a merge or hash join ([pg_operator.h#FormData_pg_operator](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_operator.h#L47-L75)). Functions carry `procost`, `prorows`, volatility, parallel safety and leakproofness ([pg_proc.h#FormData_pg_proc](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_proc.h#L46-L77)). Aggregates carry the combine and serialize functions that partial aggregation needs, and `aggsortop`, which lets `MIN`/`MAX` become an index probe ([pg_aggregate.h#FormData_pg_aggregate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_aggregate.h#L49-L86)). Tables and indexes carry the sizes and flags of chapters 4 and 7 ([pg_class.h#relpages](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_class.h#L62-L69), [pg_index.h#indisvalid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_index.h#L42-L44)).

##### Step 8. Generated files, and what a change regenerates

Four kinds of planner-relevant source are generated at build time:

| Generated | From | By | Planner consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nodetags.h` and the copy, equal, out, read and query-jumble support files | the node headers, including `pathnodes.h`, `plannodes.h`, `primnodes.h`, `supportnodes.h`, `extensible.h` and `fdwapi.h` ([nodes/Makefile#node_headers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/Makefile#L36-L62)) | `gen_node_support.pl` ([gen_node_support.pl#header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/gen_node_support.pl#L4-L9), [gen_node_support.pl#queryjumble-output](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/gen_node_support.pl#L1246-L1251), [nodes/Makefile#node-support-stamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/nodes/Makefile#L73-L95)) | adding a field to a planner node regenerates its support code; `pg_node_attr(no_copy_equal, no_read, ...)` keeps `PlannerInfo`, `RelOptInfo` and `IndexOptInfo` out of copying and reading ([nodes.h#pg_node_attr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/nodes.h#L34-L69), [pathnodes.h#PlannerInfo-attr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L197), [pathnodes.h#RelOptInfo-attr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L855), [pathnodes.h#IndexOptInfo-attr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L1109)) |
| the catalog headers `*_d.h` and `postgres.bki` | the catalog `.h` and `.dat` files | `genbki.pl` ([catalog/Makefile#bki-stamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/Makefile#L132-L144)) | new catalog columns, such as those the planner reads, appear here |
| `fmgroids.h`, `fmgrprotos.h`, `fmgrtab.c` | `pg_proc.dat` | `Gen_fmgrtab.pl` ([utils/Makefile#fmgr-stamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/Makefile#L48-L53)) | a new estimator or support function needs its `pg_proc` entry |
| `gram.c` and `gram.h` | `gram.y` | `bison` ([parser/Makefile#gram](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/Makefile#L49-L57)) | new SQL syntax for planning features starts here |

The `pathnodes.h` header states the rule behind that attribute: the planner's relations, index descriptions and paths are not meant to be copied ([pathnodes.h#header-no-copy](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/pathnodes.h#L6-L7)).

##### Step 9. Maintenance helpers that call the planner

Some utility commands borrow planner code without planning a query. The last row is the wrapper through which both `EXPLAIN` and ordinary execution plan one:

| Helper | Caller | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_cluster_use_sort()` | `CLUSTER` ([cluster.c:949](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/cluster.c#L949)) | whether a sequential scan plus sort is cheaper than a full index scan, by building both paths and comparing total cost ([planner.c#plan_cluster_use_sort](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6760-L6771), [planner.c#plan_cluster_use_sort-compare](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6860-L6873)) |
| `plan_create_index_workers()` | `index_build()`, for access methods that set `amcanbuildparallel`: B-tree, and BRIN since the 17 cycle (`b437571714`) ([index.c#index_build-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2996-L3005), [nbtree.c:120](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/nbtree/nbtree.c#L120), [brin.c:266](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/brin/brin.c#L266)) | parallel build workers from the table size, capped so each participant gets at least 32 MB of `maintenance_work_mem` ([planner.c#plan_create_index_workers-workers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6991-L7018)); a comment in BRIN questions that cap for BRIN ([brin.c#brinbuild-parallel-note](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/brin/brin.c#L1156-L1159)). No workers for a temporary table, or when `is_parallel_safe()` rejects an index expression or predicate; the table's `parallel_workers` setting replaces the estimate ([planner.c#plan_create_index_workers-safety](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6958-L6986)) |
| `expression_planner()` | `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` defaults, check constraints through `ExecPrepareExpr()`, `COPY` defaults and domain checks, among others ([tablecmds.c:7318](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/tablecmds.c#L7318), [execMain.c:1795](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execMain.c#L1795), [execExpr.c#ExecPrepareExpr](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execExpr.c#L740-L749), [copyfrom.c:1648](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/copyfrom.c#L1648), [typcache.c:1111](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/typcache.c#L1111)) | a standalone expression folded and ready to run, with no dependency tracking ([planner.c#expression_planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L6680-L6701)) |
| `expression_planner_with_deps()` | the plan cache's cached expressions ([plancache.c:1698](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1698)) | the same, plus the dependencies needed for invalidation |
| `pg_plan_query()` | `EXPLAIN`, through `standard_ExplainOneQuery()`, and ordinary statements, through `pg_plan_queries()` ([explain.c:490](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L490), [postgres.c:1001](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L1001)) | nothing itself: it is a thin wrapper around `planner()`, so `EXPLAIN` passes through the same entry point and `planner_hook` as execution ([postgres.c#pg_plan_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L886-L911)) |

#### 15.5 Eligibility and comparison

Extension paths win or lose exactly like core paths. A hook or FDW that adds a path makes it eligible only for the relation it was added to; `add_path()` then keeps it only if no other path dominates it ([allpaths.c#set_rel_pathlist-hook](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L532-L539)). An extension that wants to force its path can also delete the core paths, which the same hook allows.

Remote push-down is eligible only when the whole subtree belongs to one server. A join relation inherits a server, user and FDW routine only when both inputs agree on them ([relnode.c#set_foreign_rel_properties](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/relnode.c#L585-L619)), and an upper relation inherits them from its input ([planner.c#grouping_planner-final-fdw-properties](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L1780-L1787)). Without that, `GetForeignJoinPaths` and `GetForeignUpperPaths` are never called, so the local join is the only alternative.

Once eligible, a remote path competes on its estimated cost. `postgres_fdw` prices a remote scan as a sequential scan plus a fixed startup charge of 100.0 and a transfer charge of 0.2 per row ([postgres_fdw.c#DEFAULT_FDW_COSTS](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L57-L60), [postgres_fdw.c#estimate_path_cost_size-local](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L3448-L3479), [postgres_fdw.c#estimate_path_cost_size-fdw-charges](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L3555-L3564)). With `use_remote_estimate`, it asks the remote server's planner instead, by sending `EXPLAIN` ([postgres_fdw.c:3123](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L3123), [postgres_fdw.c#estimate_path_cost_size-remote](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L3155-L3169)).

#### 15.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| two hooks from different libraries | each library saves the previous pointer and is expected to call it, as `pg_stat_statements` does ([pg_stat_statements.c#pgss_planner-chain](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L913-L921)) | a library that does not chain silently disables the other |
| an FDW without `IsForeignScanParallelSafe` | the foreign scan is parallel-unsafe ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-foreign](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L640-L651)) | no parallel plan over that table |
| an FDW's size estimate of zero rows | `set_foreign_size()` clamps it to at least one ([allpaths.c#set_foreign_size-clamp](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L908-L918)) | no zero-row estimates reach costing |
| a foreign table never analyzed, without remote estimates | `postgres_fdw` assumes 10 pages ([postgres_fdw.c#postgresGetForeignRelSize-default](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L740-L761)) | E15.1's 975-row guess |
| a support function that cannot answer | it must return NULL, and the planner uses the catalog default ([supportnodes.h#header-null-result](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/supportnodes.h#L16-L21)) | defaults such as 0.3333333 selectivity |
| a partitioned index | no AM fields are copied; it has no access method ([plancat.c#get_relation_info-partitioned-index](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L313-L318)) | only its partitions' indexes are scanned |
| a built-in function changed | plans record dependencies only on user functions, with OID at least `FirstUnpinnedObjectId` ([setrefs.c#record_plan_function_dependency](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3472-L3494)) | built-in functions never invalidate plans |
| `MERGE` into a foreign table | not supported by FDWs ([createplan.c#make_modifytable-merge-fdw](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/createplan.c#L7165-L7179)) | error |

#### 15.7 Formulas and worked examples

##### A foreign scan before and after ANALYZE (E15.1)

Measured catalog rows, then Estimated by the planner, E15.1, before the foreign tables were analyzed:

```text
  relname  | relpages | reltuples
 customers |        0 |        -1
 orders    |        0 |        -1
...
 Foreign Scan on remote.orders  (cost=100.00..351.31 rows=975 width=4)
   Output: id
   Remote SQL: SELECT id FROM public.orders WHERE ((amount > 999::numeric))
```

The inputs are the defaults of `postgresGetForeignRelSize()` and the core size estimate. The table has no statistics, so `postgres_fdw` assumes 10 pages and divides them by the row width, in integer arithmetic ([postgres_fdw.c#postgresGetForeignRelSize-default](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L740-L761)). With no statistics for `amount`, the condition gets the default inequality selectivity ([selfuncs.h#DEFAULT_INEQ_SEL](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/selfuncs.h#L36-L37)). The cost is a pessimistic sequential scan plus the FDW's startup and transfer charges ([postgres_fdw.c#estimate_path_cost_size-local](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L3448-L3479), [postgres_fdw.c#estimate_path_cost_size-fdw-charges](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L3555-L3564)):

```text
tuples  = (10 x 8192) / (width 4 + tuple header 24) = 81920 / 28 = 2925   (integer division)
rows    = 2925 x 0.3333333 (no statistics for amount > 999)  = 974.9999, rounded to 975
run     = 10 pages x 1.0 + 2925 x (cpu_tuple_cost 0.01 + one operator 0.0025) = 10 + 36.5625 = 46.5625
total   = 46.5625 + startup 100.0 + transfer 0.2 x 975 + cpu_tuple_cost 0.01 x 975
        = 46.5625 + 100 + 195 + 9.75 = 351.3125  -> printed 351.31
```

All values are Derived, and they match the plan exactly. After `ANALYZE remote.orders` sampled the remote table, the catalog held 226 pages and 30,000 rows (Measured, E15.1b), plus a histogram of `amount`. The estimate became 30 rows and `707.30` (Estimated by the planner, E15.1b), which the same formula reproduces (Derived):

```text
run     = 226 x 1.0 + 30000 x 0.0125 = 601
total   = 601 + 100 + 0.2 x 30 + 0.01 x 30 = 707.30
```

The same query with `use_remote_estimate` also printed `707.30`. In that mode `postgres_fdw` takes the remote `EXPLAIN`'s rows and cost and then adds the same startup and transfer charges ([postgres_fdw.c#estimate_path_cost_size-remote-estimate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L3172-L3177)). Derived: 707.30 − 100 − 0.2 × 30 − 0.01 × 30 = 601.00, the cost of a one-condition sequential scan of `orders`, as in E5.1. The remote planner and the local statistics agreed because both describe the same table.

The join-and-aggregate query shows push-down. Estimated by the planner, E15.1 and E15.1b:

```text
 Foreign Scan  (cost=100.51..295.54 rows=102 width=40)
   Output: c.region, (count(*))
   Relations: Aggregate on ((remote.orders o) INNER JOIN (remote.customers c))
   Remote SQL: SELECT r2.region, count(*) FROM (public.orders r1 INNER JOIN public.customers r2 ON (((r1.customer_id = r2.id)) AND ((r1.status = 'pending')))) GROUP BY 1
...
 Foreign Scan  (cost=791.04..791.92 rows=4 width=13)
```

The `Relations:` line shows that `GetForeignJoinPaths` and `GetForeignUpperPaths` both won: one `Foreign Scan` replaced two scans, a join and a grouping. Without statistics the group count was estimated at 102; with remote estimates it fell to the remote planner's 4, one per region.

##### What the catalogs tell the planner (E15.2 to E15.4)

Measured, E15.2 to E15.4 (cut):

```text
        operator         |   oprrest    |     oprjoin      | oprcanmerge | oprcanhash
 =(integer,integer)      | eqsel        | eqjoinsel        | t           | t
...
 <->(point,point)        | -            | -                | f           | f
...
 <(numeric,numeric)      | scalarltsel  | scalarltjoinsel  | f           | f
...
                   function                   |           prosupport            | procost | prorows | provolatile | proparallel | proleakproof
...
 generate_series(integer,integer)             | generate_series_int4_support    |       1 |    1000 | i           | s           | f
...
 random()                                     | -                               |       1 |       0 | v           | r           | f
 unnest(anyarray)                             | array_unnest_support            |       1 |     100 | i           | s           | f
...
           aggregate           |    aggcombinefn     |      aggserialfn      |                        sortop
...
 max(timestamp with time zone) | timestamptz_larger  | -                     | >(timestamp with time zone,timestamp with time zone)
 count("any")                  | int8pl              | -                     | 0
```

Read with this chapter's tables, each row predicts planner behavior seen elsewhere on this page. Integer `=` can drive merge and hash joins. The distance operator `<->` has no estimator: it returns a `float8` distance, not a boolean, so it orders rows (E7.6) rather than filtering them ([pg_operator.dat#point-distance](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/catalog/pg_operator.dat#L437-L440)).

`generate_series` and `unnest` have support functions, which is why E4.12 estimated 250 and 4 rows instead of their `prorows` of 1000 and 100. `random()` is volatile and parallel-restricted. `max(timestamptz)` names a sort operator, which is what lets E10.7 turn it into an index probe. `count` has a combine function, so partial aggregation can split it across workers.

##### A planning hook at work (E14.5)

`pg_stat_statements` is loaded in the measurement cluster and counts every call of the planner through `planner_hook`, when `pg_stat_statements.track_planning` is on ([pg_stat_statements.c#pgss_planner-track](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L892-L895)). Chapter 14's E14.5 and E14.6 use exactly those counts: for example, 6 plans for 10 calls of a PL/pgSQL function. Every count there is evidence that the hook ran once per planning.

#### 15.8 Planning versus execution

| Interface | Planning side | Execution side |
|---|---|---|
| FDW | size, paths, join and upper push-down, `GetForeignPlan`, modify planning | `BeginForeignScan`, `IterateForeignScan`, `ExecForeignInsert` and the rest of `FdwRoutine` ([fdwapi.h#FdwRoutine-scan-modify](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/foreign/fdwapi.h#L208-L244)) |
| custom scan | `CustomPath`, `PlanCustomPath` | `CreateCustomScanState` and the `CustomExecMethods` ([extensible.h#CustomScanMethods](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/extensible.h#L112-L158)) |
| index AM | flags, `amcostestimate`, `amcanreturn` | `amgettuple` for index and index-only scans, `amgetbitmap` for bitmap scans ([amapi.h#IndexAmRoutine-functions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/amapi.h#L270-L289)) |
| tablesample | `SampleScanGetSampleSize` | `BeginSampleScan`, `NextSampleBlock`, `NextSampleTuple` ([tsmapi.h#TsmRoutine-callbacks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/access/tsmapi.h#L66-L76)) |
| support function | answers at plan time only | none: the target function itself runs |
| `postgres_fdw` remote estimates | an `EXPLAIN` on the remote server while planning | the pushed-down `Remote SQL` while executing |

The last row is the one place in this chapter where planning itself talks to another server: with `use_remote_estimate`, every planning of the query costs a remote round trip.

#### 15.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| a library that sets hooks is loaded, for example through `shared_preload_libraries` | hooks NULL | its initialization code sets them ([pg_stat_statements.c#_PG_init-hooks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L460-L472)) | every later planning in that backend passes through them |
| `ANALYZE` on a foreign table (E15.1b) | `reltuples` -1, no column statistics | local statistics from a sample the FDW's `AnalyzeForeignTable` collects ([postgres_fdw.c#postgres_fdw_handler](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/postgres_fdw.c#L558-L607)) | estimates use them; E15.1's scan went from 975 to 30 rows |
| `ALTER SERVER ... OPTIONS` or `ALTER FOREIGN DATA WRAPPER` | cached plans built with the old options | the plan cache's `FOREIGNSERVEROID` and `FOREIGNDATAWRAPPEROID` callbacks reset every cached plan ([plancache.c#InitPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L162-L172), [plancache.c#PlanCacheSysCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2236-L2239)) | the next execution replans with the new options |
| `ALTER FUNCTION ... COST`, `ROWS` or `SUPPORT` on a user function | plans priced with the old values | plans that recorded the function are invalidated through `PROCOID` ([setrefs.c#record_plan_function_dependency](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/setrefs.c#L3472-L3494), [plancache.c#InitPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L162-L172)) | replanned with the new estimates |
| an operator or operator-class change | cached plans | the `OPEROID` and `AMOPOPID` callbacks reset every cached plan ([plancache.c#InitPlanCache](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L162-L172), [plancache.c#PlanCacheSysCallback](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2236-L2239)) | replanned |

#### 15.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- `postgres_fdw` join and aggregate push-down, with and without remote estimates: [postgres_fdw.sql#join-queries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/sql/postgres_fdw.sql#L498-L512), [postgres_fdw.sql#aggregates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/sql/postgres_fdw.sql#L782-L787), [postgres_fdw.sql#use_remote_estimate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/sql/postgres_fdw.sql#L249). Semi joins pushed and anti joins kept local: [postgres_fdw.sql#semi-anti-join](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/sql/postgres_fdw.sql#L636-L643). A directly modified remote `UPDATE`: [postgres_fdw.sql#direct-update](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/postgres_fdw/sql/postgres_fdw.sql#L1491-L1493).
- `file_fdw` plans: [file_fdw.sql#explain](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/file_fdw/sql/file_fdw.sql#L157); tablesample methods: [tsm_system_rows.sql#explain](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/tsm_system_rows/sql/tsm_system_rows.sql#L14-L25).
- Support functions changing selectivity and row estimates: [misc_functions.sql#support-function](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/misc_functions.sql#L191-L225), using [regress.c#test_support_func](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/regress.c#L1031-L1040). Built-in support functions: range containment simplified in [rangetypes.sql#support-functions](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/rangetypes.sql#L646-L652), `LIKE` prefixes as index conditions in [btree_index.sql#like](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/btree_index.sql#L154-L163), and `row_number()` run conditions in [window.sql#run-condition](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/window.sql#L1201-L1208).
- Index AM properties: [amutils.sql#properties](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/amutils.sql#L1-L10); an index AM with a stub cost function: [dummy_index_am.c#dicostestimate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/modules/dummy_index_am/dummy_index_am.c#L204-L210); a second table AM: [create_am.sql#heap2](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/create_am.sql#L93-L94).
- `planner_hook`: planning counts in [planning.sql](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/sql/planning.sql#L1-L25), and a delay between planning and execution in [partition-addition.spec#s1exec](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/modules/delay_execution/specs/partition-addition.spec#L19-L29).
- Gaps, source-only on this page: no in-core test or module exercises a custom scan, `set_rel_pathlist_hook`, `set_join_pathlist_hook`, `join_search_hook`, `create_upper_paths_hook`, `get_relation_info_hook`, the statistics hooks, `get_attavgwidth_hook` or the two `EXPLAIN` hooks. The page runs no foreign write, so `PlanDirectModify` is covered only by the `postgres_fdw` test above.

#### 15.11 Causal summary

1. **Initial state.** A loaded library has set hook pointers, or a catalog entry names an FDW handler, an access method or a support function (sections 15.2 and 15.9).
2. **Boundary.** Planning reaches a fixed call site: a hook, an FDW callback, an AM flag or cost function, or a support request (section 15.3).
3. **Extension work.** The extension adds, edits or deletes paths, replaces estimates, or takes over a whole stage (steps 2 to 7).
4. **Comparison.** `add_path()` compares extension paths with core paths on cost, like any others (section 15.5).
5. **Plan.** The winner becomes a plan node; a `ForeignScan` can carry a whole pushed-down join and aggregate (E15.1).
6. **Execution.** The extension's run-time callbacks do the work (section 15.8).
7. **Refresh.** `ANALYZE`, option changes and function or operator changes invalidate cached plans; a newly loaded hook affects every later planning in that backend (section 15.9).

### Chapter 16. Diagnose planner decisions

#### 16.1 Main idea

The planner explains itself in one way only: it prints the plan it chose, with the estimates that won. `EXPLAIN` shows those estimates. `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` runs the plan and prints what actually happened beside them ([explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-run](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L690-L706), [explain.c#ExplainNode-actual](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1842-L1860)). Diagnosis is the discipline of comparing the two, node by node, and asking why they differ.

This matters because the planner never sees its own mistakes. The rows a node really returned are counted by the executor, printed, and thrown away. The next plan is built from the same stored statistics as before. So a bad plan stays bad until someone changes an input: the statistics, the schema, a setting, or the query.

The surprising part is how often the cause sits far below the node that looks slow. In E16.5 the planner chose a nested loop over a scan of `customers` that it expected to return 10 rows; the scan found 98. Everything above that node inherits the error. This chapter shows how to find that first divergence, how to tell a missing alternative from an expensive one, and how to probe the planner with forced settings. It uses E16.1 to E16.7 ([E16.1](#measurement-script)) and experiments from earlier chapters.

#### 16.2 Values and structures

| Value or structure | Meaning | Where it comes from | Current state, stored state, estimate or parameter | Used later by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cost=startup..total` | the planner's cost for this node before its first row and for all its rows | the `Plan` node's `startup_cost` and `total_cost`, printed when `COSTS` is on ([plannodes.h#Plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L119-L135), [explain.c#ExplainNode-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1807-L1825)) | estimate | the reader; nothing else reads it after planning |
| `rows=` and `width=` in `cost=(...)` | estimated rows the node emits and their average width | `plan_rows` and `plan_width` of the same node ([plannodes.h#Plan-rows-width](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/nodes/plannodes.h#L131-L135)) | estimate | comparison with the actual row count |
| `actual rows=N loops=L` | rows the node returned, averaged over its `L` executions | instrumentation `ntuples / nloops`, printed only with `ANALYZE` ([explain.c#ExplainNode-actual](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1842-L1860)) | observed during this run | the reader; discarded after the statement |
| `(never executed)` | the node was never started | a node whose instrumentation shows no loops ([explain.c#ExplainNode-never-executed](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1873-L1877)) | observed | pruning and short-circuit diagnosis |
| `Workers Planned` / `Workers Launched` | workers the plan asked for, workers the run got | `Gather.num_workers` and the executor's launch count ([explain.c#ExplainNode-gather](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L2031-L2047), [nodeGather.c:181-183](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L181-L183)) | parameter from the plan; observed at run time | parallel diagnosis ([chapter 12](#chapter-12-plan-parallel-execution-and-jit)) |
| `Sort Method`, `Batches`, `Memory Usage` | how a sort or hash actually ran | executor instrumentation ([explain.c#show_sort_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L2950-L2968), [explain.c#show_hash_info-batches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L3300-L3320)) | observed | spill diagnosis ([chapter 5](#chapter-5-estimate-costs)) |
| `Planning: Memory: used=... allocated=...` | memory the planner used for this statement | a private memory context around `pg_plan_query()` when `MEMORY` is on ([explain.c#standard_ExplainOneQuery-memory](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L469-L499)) | observed during planning | planning-cost diagnosis |
| `Settings:` | planner settings whose current value differs from the built-in default | `get_explain_guc_options()` ([guc.c#get_explain_guc_options](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L5352-L5384)) | current session state | reproducing a plan elsewhere |
| `pg_settings.context` | when and by whom a setting can be changed ([GUC context](../../../glossary.md#guc-context)) | the setting's `GucContext` ([guc.h#GucContext](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/guc.h#L35-L76), [guc_tables.c#GucContext_Names](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L641-L650)) | stored in the server's setting table | choosing how to apply a change |
| `pg_stats`, `pg_class.reltuples`, `relpages` | the stored inputs of the row estimates: MCV lists and histograms and reltuples and relpages | the last `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM` or `CREATE INDEX` ([system_views.sql#pg_stats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/system_views.sql#L189-L211), [vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-dirty](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1446-L1461), [index.c#index_update_stats-write](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2912-L2950)) | stored; stale once the data changes | the next plan ([chapter 4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths)) |

Two numbers on the same line come from different worlds. `rows=` inside `cost=(...)` is what the planner predicted before running anything. `actual rows=` is what one execution of that node produced, on average. When a node runs many times, `actual rows` must be multiplied by `loops` before it is compared with the estimate of the node above.

#### 16.3 Logic map

```text
A statement is slow, or its plan surprises you
|
+-- [A] Get the plan. EXPLAIN shows estimates only; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) runs the
|       statement (wrap writes in BEGIN ... ROLLBACK) and adds what happened.
|
+-- [B] Walk the plan from the leaves up. For each node compare
|       estimated rows with actual rows x loops.
|
+-- first node whose ratio is far from 1?
|     yes --> MISESTIMATE. Which input is wrong?
|       [C] stored statistics stale (reltuples/relpages vs file size,
|           histogram ends)                      --> ANALYZE          (E4.11)
|           correlated columns multiplied as independent
|                                                --> CREATE STATISTICS (E4.6, E16.5)
|           expression or function without statistics
|                                                --> expression index or ROWS (E4.14, E4.12)
|           parameter in a generic plan          --> custom plan or EXPLAIN EXECUTE (E14.2)
|
|     no --> estimates are right, the plan is still slow
|       [D] probe: SET LOCAL enable_<chosen method> = off, EXPLAIN again
|           is that switch a penalty (seqscan, indexscan, bitmapscan, tidscan,
|           sort, nestloop, gathermerge; hashagg for aggregation) or a generation
|           gate (mergejoin, hashjoin, indexonlyscan, memoize, material, ...)?
|           penalty: new plan carries cost 1e10 (disable_cost)?
|             yes --> MISSING ALTERNATIVE: nothing else was eligible
|                     (no index, wrong operator class, a fence)  (E16.6, E5.7)
|             no  --> EXPENSIVE ALTERNATIVE: it existed and cost more;
|                     check cost inputs (random_page_cost, cache size, work_mem) (E5.8b, E5.8c)
|           gate: the method is never built, so no 1e10 can appear; the next
|                 method shows at its ordinary cost (an expensive alternative)
|
+-- [E] plan is fine but planning itself is slow?
|         EXPLAIN (MEMORY, SUMMARY): many joined relations (E8.9), many
|         partitions without pruning (E11.9)
|
+-- [F] fast as ad-hoc SQL, slow as a prepared or PL/pgSQL statement?
|         generic plan: pg_prepared_statements, EXPLAIN EXECUTE,
|         EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN)                                 (E14.2, E16.4)
|
`-- [G] plan changed over time? find the event: ANALYZE, CREATE INDEX,
          a setting, a cached-plan invalidation                  (E14.4, E14.6)
```

- [A] [explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-eflags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L678-L688), [explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-run](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L690-L706), [ref/explain.sgml#analyze-caution](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/explain.sgml#L90-L108)
- [B] [explain.c#ExplainNode-actual](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1842-L1860)
- [C] [tableam.c#table_block_relation_estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L660-L713), [clausesel.c#clauselist_selectivity_ext-extended](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L140-L156), [clausesel.c:263](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L263), [selfuncs.c#var_eq_non_const-average](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L505-L516)
- [D] penalty: [costsize.c:130](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L130), [costsize.c#cost_seqscan-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305); gate: [joinpath.c#add_paths_to_joinrel-mergejoin-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L204-L217), [joinpath.c#add_paths_to_joinrel-hashjoin-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L316-L323); the full lists are in step 4; [ref/set.sgml#LOCAL](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/set.sgml#L110-L120)
- [E] [explain.c#standard_ExplainOneQuery-memory](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L469-L499), [explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-planning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L723-L752)
- [F] [prepare.c#ExplainExecuteQuery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L587-L660), [explain.c#ExplainQuery-generic-check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L299-L303)
- [G] [vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-dirty](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1446-L1461), [index.c#index_update_stats-write](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2912-L2950), [plancache.c#PlanCacheRelCallback-match](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L2012-L2046)

#### 16.4 Step by step

##### Step 1: choose what EXPLAIN should print

Input: the statement and a question. Decision: which options answer it. `EXPLAIN` parses its option list into an `ExplainState`, rejects contradictory combinations, and fills in defaults ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-options](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L200-L225), [explain.c#ExplainQuery-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L278-L306)). Only `COSTS` is on unless you ask for more ([explain.c#NewExplainState](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L372-L381)).

| Option | Default | Needs `ANALYZE` | What it adds | Estimate or observation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ANALYZE` | off | — | runs the plan and prints actual rows and loops per node ([explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-run](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L690-L706)) | observation |
| `VERBOSE` | off | no | output columns per node, qualified names, and the query identifier when one was computed ([explain.c#ExplainPrintPlan-queryid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L914-L929)) | plan structure |
| `COSTS` | on | no | `cost`, `rows`, `width` per node ([explain.c#ExplainNode-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1807-L1825)); also gates the JIT summary ([explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-jit-serialize](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L758-L765)) | estimate |
| `SETTINGS` | off | no | non-default planner settings (E16.2) ([explain.c#ExplainPrintSettings](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L807-L866)) | current state |
| `GENERIC_PLAN` | off | forbidden with it | plans a statement with `$n` placeholders as a generic plan (E16.4) ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-generic-check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L299-L303)) | estimate |
| `BUFFERS` | off | no | buffer counters for planning, and per node with `ANALYZE` ([explain.c#standard_ExplainOneQuery-buffers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L485-L507), [explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-instrument](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L632-L641)) | observation |
| `SERIALIZE` | none | yes | the size of the output converted to text or binary (E16.7); new in 17 ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-serialize](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L226-L250), [explain.c#ExplainPrintSerialize](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1109-L1135)) | observation |
| `WAL` | off | yes, when on | WAL records, full-page images and bytes per node ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-wal-check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L278-L282), [explain.c#show_wal_usage](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L3912-L3933)) | observation |
| `TIMING` | same as `ANALYZE` | yes, when on | per-node startup and total time ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-timing-check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L285-L291)) | observation |
| `SUMMARY` | same as `ANALYZE` | no | planning time, and execution time with `ANALYZE` ([explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-planning-time](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L747-L752), [explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-execution-time](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L789-L797)) | observation |
| `MEMORY` | off | no | planner memory used and allocated (E16.3); new in 17 ([explain.c#show_memory_counters](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L3950-L3968)) | observation of planning |
| `FORMAT` | `TEXT` | no | the same content as TEXT, XML, JSON or YAML ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-format](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L251-L266)) | — |

Two options are new in the 17 cycle. `SERIALIZE` came with `06286709ee` and `MEMORY` with `5de890e361`, and both commits descend from the 17devel stamp `5bcc7e6dc8`. `GENERIC_PLAN` (`3c05284d83`) does not, so it is older than 17 ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-options-generic-memory](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L212-L225)).

Consequence: without `ANALYZE`, every number in the plan is an estimate. `EXPLAIN` still starts the executor with `EXEC_FLAG_EXPLAIN_ONLY`, and executor startup performs initial partition pruning, so its effect is visible, as E11.3b's `Subplans Removed: 12` shows, but no row is read ([explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-eflags](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L678-L688), [execPartition.c#ExecInitPartitionPruning-initial](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execPartition.c#L1820-L1831)).

##### Step 2: read one node

Input: one plan line. `cost=a..b` is the startup and total cost in the planner's units, and `rows`/`width` are its predictions. With `ANALYZE`, `actual rows=N loops=L` follows, where `N` is the rows per execution, rounded, and `L` is the number of executions ([explain.c#ExplainNode-actual](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1842-L1860)).

Calculation: the total rows a node produced is about `N x L`. In E16.5 the inner scan shows `rows=15` estimated and `actual rows=10 loops=98`, so it produced about 980 rows in all. The join above it reports the exact total, 1008, because it ran once. Output: a per-node pair of numbers that can be compared. Consequence: an inner-side estimate looks harmless until it is multiplied by the outer side's error.

##### Step 3: find the first divergence

Input: the pairs from Step 2, read from the leaves up. Decision: the lowest node whose estimate is far from the truth is where the error enters. Every node above it inherits the error, because its own estimate is computed from its children's estimates.

E16.5 shows the pattern (Measured, E16.5):

```text
 Nested Loop  (cost=4.00..492.46 rows=150 width=20) (actual rows=1008 loops=1)
   ->  Seq Scan on customers c  (cost=0.00..52.00 rows=10 width=18) (actual rows=98 loops=1)
         Filter: ((region = 'west'::text) AND (country = 'PT'::text))
         Rows Removed by Filter: 1902
   ->  Bitmap Heap Scan on orders o  (cost=4.00..43.90 rows=15 width=10) (actual rows=10 loops=98)
...
```

The scan of `customers` is the first divergence: 10 estimated, 98 found. The planner multiplied the selectivities of `region = 'west'` and `country = 'PT'` as if the columns were independent ([clausesel.c:263](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L263), [planstats.sgml#independence](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/planstats.sgml#L515-L523)). But `country` determines `region` in this schema. Output: the cause is a statistics gap, not a costing problem. Consequence: the fix is extended statistics, which E4.6 shows raise the estimate to 98 ([chapter 4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths)).

##### Step 4: tell a missing alternative from an expensive one

Input: a plan whose estimates look right but whose method looks wrong. EXPLAIN prints only the winner, because `add_path()` frees each losing path as soon as it is beaten ([pathnode.c#add_path-reject-old](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L585-L592), [pathnode.c#add_path-reject-new](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L615-L621)). The only way to see a loser is to penalize the winner and plan again.

Decision: first check how the switch works, because in 17 the `enable_*` settings work in two different ways.

| Kind of switch | Switches (17) | What `off` does |
|---|---|---|
