| penalty | `enable_seqscan`, `enable_indexscan` (plain and index-only scans), `enable_bitmapscan`, `enable_tidscan`, `enable_sort`, `enable_nestloop`, `enable_gathermerge` | the path is still built, and `disable_cost`, 1.0e10, is added to its startup cost ([costsize.c:130](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L130), [costsize.c#cost_seqscan-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305), [costsize.c#cost_index-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L606-L607), [costsize.c#cost_bitmap_heap_scan-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1041-L1042), [costsize.c#cost_tidscan-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1313-L1314), [costsize.c#cost_sort-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2138-L2139), [costsize.c#final_cost_nestloop-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3347-L3348), [costsize.c#cost_gather_merge-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L493-L494)) |
| both | `enable_hashagg` | a penalty on hashed and mixed aggregation ([costsize.c#cost_agg-mixed-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2708-L2712), [costsize.c#cost_agg-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L2726-L2727)); a gate for hashed set operations, semi-join de-duplication and partial `DISTINCT`, and for final `DISTINCT` unless no other path exists ([prepunion.c#choose_hashed_setop-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L1322-L1324), [initsplan.c:1747](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/initsplan.c#L1747), [planner.c#create_partial_distinct_paths-hashagg-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5038-L5044), [planner.c#create_final_distinct_paths-hashagg](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5262-L5267)) |
| generation gate | `enable_mergejoin` and `enable_hashjoin` (except for a full join), `enable_indexonlyscan`, `enable_memoize`, `enable_material` (optional Materialize nodes only), `enable_incremental_sort`, `enable_parallel_append`, `enable_parallel_hash`, the two partitionwise switches, `enable_group_by_reordering`, `enable_presorted_aggregate` | the planner never builds the path, so it cannot appear at any cost ([joinpath.c#add_paths_to_joinrel-mergejoin-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L204-L217), [joinpath.c#add_paths_to_joinrel-hashjoin-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L316-L323), [indxpath.c#check_index_only-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L1738-L1740), [joinpath.c#get_memoize_path-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L591-L593), [joinpath.c#match_unsorted_outer-material-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L1795-L1796), [allpaths.c#generate_useful_gather_paths-incremental-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3254-L3256), [allpaths.c#add_paths_to_append_rel-parallel-append-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L1320), [joinpath.c#hash_inner_and_outer-parallel-hash-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L2282-L2284), [allpaths.c#set_append_rel_size-partitionwise-join-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L965-L967), [planner.c#create_grouping_paths-partitionwise-aggregate-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3910-L3911), [pathkeys.c#get_useful_group_keys_orderings-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/pathkeys.c#L485-L486), [planner.c#adjust_group_pathkeys_for_groupagg-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L3299-L3301)) |

For a merge or hash full join, the gate is skipped and the penalty applies instead, because that method may be the only way to run the join ([costsize.c#final_cost_mergejoin-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L3794-L3795), [costsize.c#final_cost_hashjoin-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L4224-L4225)). So the reading of the new plan depends on the kind of switch:

| What the new plan shows | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| penalty switch: the same method, with a cost above 10,000,000,000 | no other path was eligible; the alternative you hoped for is **missing** | `amount < 1` has no index: `Seq Scan ... cost=10000000000.00..10000000601.00` (E16.6) |
| penalty switch: a different method at an ordinary cost | the alternative existed and was **more expensive** | `customer_id > 0`: a bitmap scan at 969.79 total, against the sequential scan's 601.00 (E16.6) |
| gate switch: a different method at an ordinary cost | the gated method is gone; the one shown existed and was **more expensive**. A gate cannot show a missing alternative, because no 1e10 path is left behind | with `enable_hashjoin` and `enable_mergejoin` off, E5.9's inner join became a nested loop at an ordinary `3.64..778.42` (forced settings) |

Consequence: a missing alternative sends you to eligibility rules ([chapter 6](#chapter-6-generate-scan-alternatives), [chapter 7](#chapter-7-decide-whether-an-index-is-useful), [chapter 8](#chapter-8-search-join-orders-and-methods)). An expensive one sends you to the cost inputs ([chapter 5](#chapter-5-estimate-costs)).

##### Step 5: check the settings in effect and how to change them

Input: the session. `EXPLAIN (SETTINGS)` lists settings that carry the `GUC_EXPLAIN` flag and differ from their built-in default ([guc.h:215](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/guc.h#L215), [guc.c#get_explain_guc_options](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc.c#L5352-L5384)). In E16.2 it printed `random_page_cost = '1.1', work_mem = '16MB'` and nothing else. The session had also changed `statement_timeout`, `TimeZone` and `compute_query_id`, but their definitions carry no `GUC_EXPLAIN` flag, while `work_mem`'s does ([guc_tables.c#statement_timeout](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L2612-L2620), [guc_tables.c#TimeZone](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4395-L4403), [guc_tables.c#compute_query_id](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4788-L4795), [guc_tables.c#work_mem](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L2448-L2458)).

Decision: how to apply a change depends on the setting's context. The table maps the contexts E16.1 reported (Measured, E16.1) to what a change requires:

| `pg_settings.context` | Requirement | Planner-related settings | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `postmaster` | restart | `jit_provider` (E16.1); also `max_worker_processes` and `shared_preload_libraries` | [guc_tables.c#jit_provider](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4678-L4686), [guc_tables.c#max_worker_processes](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3164-L3173), [guc_tables.c#shared_preload_libraries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4258-L4266) |
| `sighup` | reload | none of the 62 settings in E16.1 | [guc.h#GucContext-sighup](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/guc.h#L46-L51) |
| `superuser` | session or transaction scope, for a role allowed to change it | `compute_query_id` (E16.1); also `log_planner_stats` | [guc_tables.c#compute_query_id](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4788-L4795), [guc_tables.c#log_planner_stats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L1361-L1368) |
| `user` | session or transaction scope with `SET` or `SET LOCAL` | the other 60 rows of E16.1: every `enable_*`, every cost constant, the GEQO settings, `join_collapse_limit`, `from_collapse_limit`, `default_statistics_target`, `plan_cache_mode`, the `jit*` thresholds, the parallel settings, `work_mem`, `hash_mem_multiplier` | [guc_tables.c#plan_cache_mode](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L5112-L5122), [guc_tables.c#default_statistics_target](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L2071-L2079), [guc_tables.c#random_page_cost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3687-L3696) |
| `backend`, `superuser-backend` | new sessions only | none in E16.1 | [guc.h#GucContext-backend](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/utils/guc.h#L53-L60) |
| `internal` | cannot be changed | `block_size`, which fixes how many rows fit a page and so every page count | [guc_tables.c#block_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L3269-L3277) |

Several planner inputs are not settings at all. A tablespace can override `random_page_cost` and `seq_page_cost` ([spccache.c#get_tablespace_page_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/spccache.c#L182-L203)). A table's `parallel_workers` storage parameter overrides the worker formula ([reloptions.c#parallel_workers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/common/reloptions.c#L374-L382), [allpaths.c#compute_parallel_worker-reloption](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L4207-L4213)). A column's `n_distinct` option replaces the computed value, but only at the next `ANALYZE` ([analyze.c#compute-stats-n_distinct-override](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L562-L574)). A function's `COST` and `ROWS` feed its cost and row estimates when it has no support function ([plancat.c#procost](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2133-L2134), [plancat.c#prorows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L2192-L2193)).

Consequence: E16.2 is itself a forced-setting demonstration. With `random_page_cost = 1.1` and `work_mem = 16MB`, Q1 switched plans. The hash join's `Limit` cost `663.46..663.48` (E16.3); the new nested loop over an index scan has a `Limit` at `459.50..459.51` (Estimated by the planner, E16.2). The new plan reads the inner index once per western customer, so it profits from cheaper random reads; that is no evidence that 1.1 suits any real server.

##### Step 6: diagnose planning time

Input: a statement whose plan is fine but whose planning is slow. `EXPLAIN (MEMORY)` creates a private memory context for `pg_plan_query()` and reports what it consumed ([explain.c#standard_ExplainOneQuery-memory](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L469-L499)). Memory is a repeatable proxy for planning effort; `SUMMARY` adds the planning time itself, which this page never records ([explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-planning-time](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L747-L752)).

The measured planner memory across this page (Measured):

| Statement | Planner memory used / allocated | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Q1, two tables | 41 kB / 64 kB | E16.3 |
| one partition of `wide_p` after pruning | 29 kB / 40 kB | E11.9 |
| all 256 partitions of `wide_p` | 856 kB / 1032 kB | E11.9 |
| 256 partitions with pruning switched off (forced setting) | 1204 kB / 2056 kB | E11.9 |
| 12 tables, one `FROM` list, GEQO | 163 kB / 256 kB | E8.9b |
| the same 12 tables, written as `JOIN`s (split by `join_collapse_limit`) | 409 kB / 520 kB | E8.9a |
| the same `FROM` list, exhaustive search (forced setting) | 799 kB / 1040 kB | E8.9c |

Output: the two drivers of planning effort are the number of relations the join search must combine and the number of partitions that survive pruning. Consequence: the remedies are structural, such as partition keys the query can prune on ([chapter 11](#chapter-11-handle-inheritance-and-partitioning)), collapse limits and GEQO ([chapter 8](#chapter-8-search-join-orders-and-methods)), or plan reuse ([chapter 14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans)). For a server-wide view, `pg_stat_statements` with `track_planning` counts plans and planning time per statement, through `planner_hook`, a hook ([pg_stat_statements.c#pgss_planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L880-L895)). `log_planner_stats` writes resource usage around each `planner()` call to the log ([postgres.c#pg_plan_query-log_planner_stats](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L905-L912)).

##### Step 7: diagnose a generic plan

Input: a statement that is fast as ad-hoc SQL and slow as a prepared statement, or inside PL/pgSQL. A generic plan estimates `column = $1` as `(1 - null_frac) / n_distinct` of the rows, the average over all possible values ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_non_const-average](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L505-L516)). For `customer_id` that is 1/2000 of 30,000, so 15 rows, while customer 7 has 458 (Estimated by the planner, E14.2).

Decision tools: `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` shows the plan the cache would use now, with `$1` in its conditions when it is generic. `EXPLAIN (MEMORY) EXECUTE` and `BUFFERS` also measure the cache lookup and any replanning ([prepare.c#ExplainExecuteQuery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L587-L660)). `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN)` shows a generic plan without preparing anything (E16.4). `pg_prepared_statements.generic_plans` and `custom_plans` count which kind each execution used ([prepare.c#pg_prepared_statement-counters](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/prepare.c#L729-L730)). Consequence: `SET LOCAL` [`plan_cache_mode`](../../../glossary.md#plan-cache-mode) `= force_custom_plan` removes the averaging for one transaction ([guc_tables.c#plan_cache_mode_options](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L409-L414)); [chapter 14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans) explains the choice itself.

##### Step 8: capture plans you cannot reproduce by hand

Input: a problem that appears only under production load. `auto_explain` installs executor hooks and writes the plan, with optional `ANALYZE`-style details, for statements slower than `auto_explain.log_min_duration` ([auto_explain.c#_PG_init-hooks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/auto_explain/auto_explain.c#L247-L255), [auto_explain.c#explain_ExecutorEnd-print](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/auto_explain/auto_explain.c#L400-L411)). Its settings, from `log_min_duration` to `sample_rate`, are all `PGC_SUSET` ([auto_explain.c#log_min_duration](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/auto_explain/auto_explain.c#L96-L106), [auto_explain.c#sample_rate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/auto_explain/auto_explain.c#L232-L243)). A superuser can `LOAD` it into one session; server-wide use goes through `session_preload_libraries` or `shared_preload_libraries` ([auto-explain.sgml#loading](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/auto-explain.sgml#L18-L30)).

`pg_stat_statements`, by contrast, only hooks in when it is loaded through `shared_preload_libraries`, a `postmaster` setting, so enabling it needs a restart ([pg_stat_statements.c#_PG_init-preload](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/pg_stat_statements.c#L380-L389), [guc_tables.c#shared_preload_libraries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c#L4258-L4266)). Output: a record of which plan ran and how often each statement was planned. Consequence: these tools observe the planner; they change nothing it decides.

#### 16.5 Eligibility and comparison

A diagnostic probe works only if you know what the planner compared. It compares complete paths for the same relation on total cost, startup cost, sort order, row count, parameterization and parallel safety, and keeps only those no other path beats ([pathnode.c#add_path-header](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/pathnode.c#L361-L373)). A forced setting changes that comparison in one of two ways: a penalty switch adds 1.0e10 to the penalized paths, and a gate switch keeps the gated paths from being built (step 4).

| Probe | What becomes eligible or ineligible | How the result is compared | What it tells you |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enable_<method> = off`, penalty switch | nothing is removed; the method's paths gain `disable_cost` ([costsize.c#cost_seqscan-disable](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L304-L305)) | ordinary `add_path()` dominance | the cheapest alternative's own cost (E5.8b: index scan 1140.74 against the bitmap scan's 513.47) |
| `enable_<method> = off`, gate switch | the method's paths are never built ([joinpath.c#add_paths_to_joinrel-hashjoin-gate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/joinpath.c#L316-L323)) | ordinary `add_path()` dominance among the rest | the next method's own cost; never a 1e10 marker |
| a cost constant (`random_page_cost`, `effective_cache_size`) | nothing; prices change | the same | whether the choice flips at the new value (E5.8c: at 1.1 the index scan wins at 453.57) |
| `CREATE INDEX` in a rolled-back transaction | a new index becomes a candidate ([chapter 7](#chapter-7-decide-whether-an-index-is-useful)) | the same | whether the index would be chosen, without keeping it |
| `CREATE STATISTICS` and `ANALYZE` | nothing; estimates change | the same | whether a better estimate changes the plan (E4.6) |
| `plan_cache_mode` | forces a custom or generic plan | none: the cache follows the setting | whether averaging over parameters is the problem (E14.3) |

The planner rejects alternatives silently. A rejected path leaves no trace in the plan, the log or any statistics view. So "the planner did not consider X" and "the planner considered X and found it dearer" look the same until a probe separates them.

#### 16.6 Exceptions and limitations

| Condition or state | Behavior | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of a write | the statement really runs; its side effects happen ([ref/explain.sgml#analyze-caution](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/explain.sgml#L90-L108)) | wrap writes in `BEGIN` and `ROLLBACK` |
| `GENERIC_PLAN` with `ANALYZE` | rejected with an error ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-generic-check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L299-L303)) | a generic plan can only be inspected, not run, this way |
| `SERIALIZE` without `ANALYZE` | rejected ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-serialize-check](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L294-L297)) | output size is measured only on a real run |
| a utility statement | `EXPLAIN` prints that it has no plan, except for the ones that wrap a query ([explain.c#ExplainOneUtility-no-plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L593-L599)) | see [chapter 1](#chapter-1-follow-one-query) for the ones that do |
| no JIT provider, or nothing compiled | no JIT section, even when the plan's `jitFlags` asked for JIT ([explain.c#ExplainPrintJIT](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1011-L1017)) | E12.10b; the decision is visible only through `debug_print_plan` |
| `VERBOSE` with query identifiers off | no `Query Identifier` line ([explain.c#ExplainPrintPlan-queryid](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L914-L929)) | this page's runs keep `compute_query_id` off, except in `s14` |
| a multi-loop node | `actual rows` is a rounded average ([explain.c#ExplainNode-actual-average](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1847)) | multiply by `loops`; E16.5's 10 x 98 understates the true 1008 |
| no feedback | estimates come only from stored statistics and live file sizes; execution counts are printed and discarded ([tableam.c#table_block_relation_estimate_size](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L660-L713), [explain.c#ExplainOnePlan-run](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L690-L706)) | the same misestimate repeats on every run |
| independence assumption | selectivities of separate clauses are multiplied unless extended statistics cover them ([clausesel.c#clauselist_selectivity_ext-extended](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L140-L156), [clausesel.c:263](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/clausesel.c#L263)) | correlated columns are underestimated (E16.5) |
| sampling | `ANALYZE` reads 300 x the statistics target rows ([analyze.c#std_typanalyze-minrows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L1880-L1894), [ref/analyze.sgml#sampling](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/analyze.sgml#L229-L238)) | on large tables, statistics and estimates change slightly between runs; this page's tables are fully sampled |
| generic plans | a parameter is estimated as an average value ([selfuncs.c#var_eq_non_const-average](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c#L505-L516)) | skewed parameters are misestimated (E14.2) |
| stale statistics | row counts scale with the live file size, but histograms and MCVs do not move ([tableam.c#table_block_relation_estimate_size-scale](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/table/tableam.c#L711-L747)) | new values beyond the histogram are estimated near zero (E4.11: 2 rows against 10,000) |
| `BUFFERS` hit and read counts | depend on what is already cached | this page does not quote them |

#### 16.7 Formulas and worked examples

**Rows per node.** Define `N` as the printed `actual rows`, `L` as `loops`, and `R` as the node's true total. Then `R ≈ N x L`, because `N` is `ntuples / nloops` rounded to an integer ([explain.c#ExplainNode-actual-format](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1847-L1857)). Derived, from E16.5: `10 x 98 = 980`. The join above reports 1008, so the unrounded average was 1008 / 98 ≈ 10.29.

**Where the 10 came from.** Define `T` as the table's rows and `f(v)` as the stored MCV frequency of value `v`. Under independence, `rows = T x f(region = west) x f(country = PT)`. Derived, from E4.1's stored frequencies 0.1 and 0.049: `2000 x 0.1 x 0.049 = 9.8`, printed as 10. The truth is 98, because every `PT` customer is western, so the true selectivity is just `f(PT)`: `2000 x 0.049 = 98`.

**Why the join says 150.** The inner scan's estimate is per outer row: `30000 / 2000 = 15` orders per customer, since `customer_id` has 2,000 distinct values and no parameter-specific statistics. Derived: `10 x 15 = 150`, against 1008 observed. The error came entirely from the outer side.

**A missing alternative's price.** With `enable_seqscan = off` and no index on `amount`, the only path costs `1.0e10 + 601.00`, printed as `10000000000.00..10000000601.00` (E16.6). The 601.00 is the ordinary sequential scan: 226 pages plus 30,000 rows at 0.01 and one operator at 0.0025 each ([chapter 5](#chapter-5-estimate-costs)).

**Planning memory per partition.** Derived from E11.9: `(856 - 29) / 255 ≈ 3.2 kB` of planner memory for each extra partition kept. With pruning off, every partition also carries its filter, and the figure is `(1204 - 29) / 255 ≈ 4.6 kB`.

#### 16.8 Planning versus execution

| Printed item | Decided by | When | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| node types, join order, index choice, `cost`, `rows`, `width` | planner | before execution | [explain.c#ExplainNode-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1807-L1825) |
| `Workers Planned` | planner | before execution | [explain.c#ExplainNode-workers-planned](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L2037-L2038) |
| `Workers Launched` | executor, limited by free worker slots | at run time | [nodeGather.c:181-183](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeGather.c#L181-L183), [parallel.c#LaunchParallelWorkers-fewer](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/transam/parallel.c#L612-L631) |
| `Subplans Removed` | executor startup, from planner-built pruning steps | at `ExecutorStart`, even without `ANALYZE` (E11.3b: `Subplans Removed: 12` in plain `EXPLAIN EXECUTE`), but not under `GENERIC_PLAN` | [explain.c#ExplainMissingMembers](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L4395-L4408), [execPartition.c#ExecInitPartitionPruning-initial](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execPartition.c#L1820-L1831), [execPartition.c#generic-plan-skip](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/execPartition.c#L2055-L2080) |
| `(never executed)`, `actual rows`, `loops` | executor | at run time | [explain.c#ExplainNode-actual-all](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1842-L1877) |
| `Sort Method`, hash `Batches` | executor, adapting to `work_mem` | at run time | [explain.c#show_sort_info](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L2950-L2968), [explain.c#show_hash_info-batches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L3300-L3320) |
| JIT section | planner sets `jitFlags`; executor compiles if a provider loads | both | [explain.c#ExplainPrintJITSummary](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L985-L1003) |
| `Planning: Memory` | planner, measured by EXPLAIN | during planning | [explain.c#standard_ExplainOneQuery-memory](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L469-L499) |
| `Serialization` | the output converter | at run time | [explain.c#ExplainPrintSerialize](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1109-L1135) |

The practical rule follows from the table. A number inside `cost=(...)` changes only when a planner input changes. A number after it describes what the executor did with the plan, and can differ between runs of the same plan. Even the executor's adaptations, such as run-time partition pruning, parallel worker launch and JIT compilation, only act within what the plan already allows.

#### 16.9 Lifecycle

| Event | State before | State after | Effect on later planning |
|---|---|---|---|
| bulk insert, no `ANALYZE` | stored `reltuples`/`relpages` and histogram describe the old data | file larger; statistics unchanged | total rows scale with the file; values past the histogram's end are estimated near zero (E4.11) |
| `ANALYZE` | old statistics | new statistics; `pg_class` sizes rewritten when they changed | new estimates; cached plans replanned only if sizes changed (E14.6) |
| `CREATE STATISTICS` then `ANALYZE` | columns treated as independent | dependency, ndistinct and MCV lists stored | multi-column estimates corrected (E4.6) |
| `CREATE INDEX` | no such path | a new candidate; `pg_class` sizes also rewritten, with a relcache invalidation ([index.c#index_update_stats-write](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/catalog/index.c#L2912-L2950)) | new plans may use it; cached plans are invalidated (E4.11c, E14.4) |
| `SET` / `SET LOCAL` | session defaults | new value for the session or the transaction ([ref/set.sgml#LOCAL](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/set.sgml#L110-L120)) | every later plan in that scope |
| `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... SET (n_distinct = ...)` | computed `n_distinct` | option stored | used at the next `ANALYZE` only ([analyze.c#compute-stats-n_distinct-override](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/analyze.c#L562-L574)) |
| restart with a new `postmaster` setting | old value | new value | e.g. more worker slots for `Workers Launched` |

#### 16.10 Regression coverage and gaps

- `explain.sql` exercises most options: plain, `ANALYZE`, `VERBOSE`, `BUFFERS` in all four formats, `SERIALIZE` ([explain.sql#options](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L64-L71), [explain.sql#serialize](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L166-L171)), `SETTINGS` ([explain.sql#settings](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L79-L88)), `GENERIC_PLAN` including the rejected `ANALYZE` combination ([explain.sql#generic_plan](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L91-L95)), and `MEMORY` including `EXPLAIN EXECUTE` ([explain.sql#memory](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L97-L103)).
- Gap: no core regression test uses the `WAL` option of `EXPLAIN` (grep of `src/test/regress/sql`).
- Those tests replace every number with `N` and drop buffer and "Planning:" lines ([explain.sql#explain_filter](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/explain.sql#L13-L35)), so they assert no cost and no planner-memory figure. Row counts are asserted elsewhere: `stats_ext.sql` compares estimated with actual rows through `check_estimated_rows()` ([stats_ext.sql#check_estimated_rows](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/sql/stats_ext.sql#L10-L27)).
- `pg_stat_statements` tests planning counts with `track_planning` on ([planning.sql#track_planning](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/sql/planning.sql#L5-L6), [planning.sql#plans](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/pg_stat_statements/sql/planning.sql#L22-L26)).
- `auto_explain` has a TAP test that logs plans at `log_min_duration = 0` ([001_auto_explain.pl#settings](../../../../raw/postgres-17/contrib/auto_explain/t/001_auto_explain.pl#L34-L35)). This page's build does not install `auto_explain`, so its behavior is described from source only.
- Gap: the diagnostic decision tree in 16.3 is a procedure, not an engine mechanism; it has no test of its own.

#### 16.11 Troubleshooting exercises

Each exercise runs on the tutorial's disposable database. The expected evidence comes from the measured experiments named with it. Every block sets session-scoped timeouts first, because a diagnostic statement should never wait long on a lock or run away.

##### Exercise 1: why a nested loop?

Question: Q1's cousin below joins western Portuguese customers to their orders with a nested loop. Is the method wrong, or its input?

```sql
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex1 */ statement_timeout = '30s';
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex1 */ lock_timeout = '5s';
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_ex1 */ (ANALYZE, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT c.name, o.amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND c.country = 'PT';
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_ex1 */ attname, most_common_vals, most_common_freqs
  FROM pg_stats
 WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = 'customers' AND attname IN ('region', 'country');
```

Expected evidence: the `customers` scan estimates 10 rows and finds 98, and the join estimates 150 and finds 1008 (E16.5). The stored frequencies are 0.1 for `west` and 0.049 for `PT` (E4.1). Their product explains the 10. Creating `STATISTICS ... (dependencies, ndistinct, mcv) ON region, country` and re-analyzing raises the scan estimate to 98 (E4.6). The input was wrong, not the method.

##### Exercise 2: a table that grew after its last ANALYZE

Question: a range query on a freshly loaded table estimates 2 rows and returns 10,000. Where does the 2 come from?

```sql
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex2 */ statement_timeout = '30s';
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex2 */ lock_timeout = '5s';
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_ex2 */ c.relpages, c.reltuples, pg_relation_size(c.oid) / current_setting('block_size')::int AS current_pages,
       s.n_mod_since_analyze, s.last_analyze, s.last_autoanalyze
  FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_stat_user_tables s ON s.relid = c.oid
 WHERE c.relnamespace = 'public'::regnamespace AND c.relname = 'fresh';
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_ex2 */ (histogram_bounds::text::int[])[99:101] AS last_bounds
  FROM pg_stats WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename = 'fresh' AND attname = 'x';
```

Expected evidence: `relpages` 64 against 108 current pages, and a histogram that ends at 10000 (E4.11, E4.11b). The row total scales with the file, to 16,875, but `x > 10000` falls past the histogram's end, so it is estimated at 2 rows (E4.11). An index on `x` lets the planner probe the real maximum, which raises the estimate to 198 (E4.11c). `ANALYZE` fixes both. In the tutorial database this state lasts only from E4.11's `INSERT` to its `CREATE INDEX`, which rewrote `relpages` to 108 (E4.11c), so rerun those steps to see it.

##### Exercise 3: missing or merely expensive?

Question: why does a query filtering on `amount` never use an index, while one on `customer_id` does not use its index either?

```sql
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex3 */ statement_timeout = '30s';
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex3 */ lock_timeout = '5s';
BEGIN /* wiki_pqt_ex3 */;
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex3 */ LOCAL enable_seqscan = off;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_ex3 */ SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount < 1;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_ex3 */ SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id > 0;
ROLLBACK /* wiki_pqt_ex3 */;
```

Expected evidence: the `amount` plan is still a sequential scan, now priced above 10,000,000,000, so no index path exists: the alternative is missing (E16.6). The `customer_id` plan becomes a bitmap scan at 969.79 total, above the default plan's 601.00, so that alternative exists and is simply dearer (E16.6). `SET LOCAL` confines the probe to the transaction.

##### Exercise 4: a prepared statement that picks the wrong plan for big customers

Question: after five executions a prepared count switches plans. Is the new plan right for customer 7?

```sql
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ statement_timeout = '30s';
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ lock_timeout = '5s';
PREPARE /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ ex4(int) AS SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE customer_id = $1;
EXECUTE /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ ex4(7);
EXECUTE /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ ex4(7);
EXECUTE /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ ex4(7);
EXECUTE /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ ex4(7);
EXECUTE /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ ex4(7);
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ EXECUTE ex4(7);
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ name, generic_plans, custom_plans FROM pg_prepared_statements WHERE name = 'ex4';
DEALLOCATE /* wiki_pqt_ex4 */ ex4;
```

Expected evidence: after five custom plans the cache switches to a generic plan whose condition reads `customer_id = $1` and whose estimate is 15 rows; the custom plans estimated 458 (E14.2). The counters then read 1 generic and 5 custom plans, as in E14.2. E14.2 ran customer 500 once among its five, so this sequence is predicted, not measured.

Derived: each custom plan costs 13.46 plus the planning charge `1000 x 0.0025 x (1 + 1) = 5.00`, which is far above the generic plan's 4.60 ([plancache.c:1150](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L1150)). The generic plan was chosen because it looked cheaper on average, not because it fits customer 7 ([chapter 14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans)). `SET LOCAL plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan`, inside a transaction, restores the value-specific estimate (E14.3).

##### Exercise 5: planning cost of many partitions

Question: a count over a 256-partition table plans slowly. How much planning work does pruning save?

```sql
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex5 */ statement_timeout = '30s';
SET /* wiki_pqt_ex5 */ lock_timeout = '5s';
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_ex5 */ (MEMORY, COSTS OFF) SELECT count(*) FROM wide_p;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_ex5 */ (MEMORY, COSTS OFF) SELECT count(*) FROM wide_p WHERE id = 42;
```

Expected evidence: 256 scans and about 856 kB of planner memory without a key condition, against one scan and about 29 kB with `id = 42` (E11.9). The plan text for the first statement is 256 scan nodes long, which is itself a warning sign ([chapter 11](#chapter-11-handle-inheritance-and-partitioning)).

#### 16.12 Causal summary

1. **Initial state.** The planner builds one plan from stored statistics, live file sizes and settings, and keeps only the cheapest path at each step (sections 16.2 and 16.5).
2. **Observation.** `EXPLAIN` prints that winner's estimates; `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` adds what the executor observed, then discards it (step 1).
3. **Diagnosis.** The lowest node where estimate and observation diverge is where the error enters (steps 2 and 3).
4. **Misestimate.** Fix that input: statistics, extended statistics, or a parameterization (16.3 [C]).
5. **Right estimates, wrong method.** Probe with a forced setting. For a penalty switch, a 1.0e10 cost means the alternative was missing and an ordinary cost means it was dearer; a gate switch can only show the next method at its ordinary cost (step 4).
6. **Refresh.** Every fix works only by changing what the next planning sees: `ANALYZE`, DDL, a setting's scope, or the plan cache's choice (section 16.9).

### Final causal summary

Q1 shows the whole mechanism in one chain. Each step names the chapter that explains it.

1. **Initial state.** `ANALYZE` stored the statistics: `pending` is 10.063 % of `orders`, `west` is 10 % of `customers` (Measured, E4.1). The files hold 226 and 22 pages (Measured, E0.1). Nothing about the query is known yet.
2. **Input.** The SQL text is parsed, analyzed and rewritten into one `Query`; Q1 has no view, so the rewriter changes nothing ([chapter 1](#chapter-1-follow-one-query)).
3. **Transformation.** Each `WHERE` condition is filed on the one table it mentions, and `o.customer_id = c.id` becomes an equivalence class that later supplies the join clause ([chapter 3](#chapter-3-transform-the-query-safely)).
4. **Estimation.** Current file size times stored density gives 30,000 and 2,000 rows; the MCV frequencies give 3,019 and 200 rows ([costsize.c#set_baserel_size_estimates](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5256-L5268)). The foreign key makes the join selectivity `1 / 2000`, so the join estimate is 3,019 × 200 / 2,000 = 301.9, rounded to 302 (Derived; [costsize.c#get_foreign_key_join_selectivity-inner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5741-L5751), [costsize.c#calc_joinrel_size_estimate-inner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5505-L5508), [costsize.c#clamp_row_est](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L202-L217); [chapter 4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths)).
5. **Costing and comparison.** Every scan, join method and join order gets a startup and a total cost from those rows. `add_path()` keeps only paths that nothing else beats, and the hash join survives at `49.50..658.45` (Estimated by the planner, E1.1; [chapters 5 to 8](#chapter-5-estimate-costs)).
6. **Upper steps.** `ORDER BY ... LIMIT 5` makes the planner price a bounded sort and read only 5 rows' share of the Limit input, so the final path is `Limit -> Sort -> Hash Join` ([chapter 10](#chapter-10-plan-operations-above-scans-and-joins)).
7. **Plan construction.** The cheapest final path becomes a `Plan` tree, its references are fixed, and the `PlannedStmt` records which tables it depends on ([chapter 14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans)).
8. **Execution.** The executor runs that tree unchanged. It finds 3,019, 200 and 290 rows and keeps the five largest in a 25 kB top-N heap (Measured, E1.2). The 4 % join misestimate had no effect on the plan's shape, and the executor did not report it back.
9. **Refresh.** Only an event that changes the planner's inputs changes the next plan:

| Event | What it changes | When the planner sees it | Chapter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ANALYZE` | per-column statistics; `relpages`, `reltuples` and `relallvisible` when they differ | the next planning; a cached plan is rebuilt only when one of the three size figures changed, because only then does the in-place `pg_class` update run (Measured, E14.6; [vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-dirty](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1446-L1461), [vacuum.c#vac_update_relstats-write](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/vacuum.c#L1544-L1548)) | [4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths), [14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans) |
| rows added or removed, no `ANALYZE` | the file size, not the statistics | at once: estimates scale with the current page count, while histograms stay stale (Measured, E4.11) | [4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths) |
| `VACUUM` | the visibility map and `relallvisible` | the next planning prices index-only scans with the new all-visible fraction (Measured, E6.3) | [6](#chapter-6-generate-scan-alternatives) |
| `CREATE INDEX`, `DROP INDEX`, other DDL | the relation's index list and definition | invalidates dependent cached plans, so the next execution replans (Measured, E14.4) | [7](#chapter-7-decide-whether-an-index-is-useful), [14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans) |
| `CREATE STATISTICS`, then `ANALYZE` | extended statistics | the next planning corrects correlated estimates (Measured, E4.6) | [4](#chapter-4-estimate-rows-and-widths) |
| `SET` of a planner setting | the session's cost constants or method switches | the next planning; an already cached plan is kept, because revalidation checks `search_path`, the role and `row_security` besides the invalidation messages, and no planner setting ([plancache.c#RevalidateCachedQuery-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L615-L645), [plancache.c#CheckCachedPlan-role-xmin](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c#L844-L873)) | [14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans), [16](#chapter-16-diagnose-planner-decisions) |
| a sixth execution of a prepared statement | nothing in the catalogs | the plan cache compares the generic plan with the custom average and may switch to it (Measured, E14.1, E14.2) | [14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans) |
| `search_path` change | name resolution | the cached statement is re-analyzed and replanned (Measured, E14.5) | [14](#chapter-14-build-cache-and-invalidate-plans) |

The single idea behind all sixteen chapters: the planner is a cost-based search over equivalent plans. It works from stored statistics and live sizes, compares estimates, and hands the executor one fixed plan. The executor can adapt memory, workers, pruning and compilation inside that plan, but only a change to the inputs makes the planner choose again.

## Measurement Script

### Usage

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Purpose | produces every estimated and measured number and every plan on this page: the schema sizes (E0.1), the plans, costs and row counts of E1.1 to E16.7, the statistics behind the worked calculations, the chapter 14 counters, the planner-memory figures, and the `debug_print_*` captures (E1.5, E12.10) |
| Invocation | `bash .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh` from the repository root, after extracting the script with the two commands under this table. `WIKI_ROOT` defaults to `$PWD` and must be this repository: the script checks for `AGENTS.md`, `wiki` and `raw` before it creates anything |
| Stages | `build check cluster schema s01 s03 s04 s05 s06 s07 s08 s09 s10 s11 s12 s13 s14 s15 s16 platform summary stop` by default, plus `clean` on request; the next table describes each. Name stages to run a subset: `bash .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh s04 s05` |
| Failure handling | an unknown stage name, an empty argument or two names passed as one stop the run before anything is created. Every `psql` call runs with `ON_ERROR_STOP`, and a failed call ends the run. An `EXIT` trap stops the server on every path out and checks that no `postmaster.pid` or process from the data directory is left |
| The statement that must fail | E7.14b's `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` runs alone through `pgerr()`, which requires `psql`'s status 3 for a failed script statement under `ON_ERROR_STOP` and the expected error text ([mainloop.c#MainLoop-exit-status](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/bin/psql/mainloop.c#L587-L594), [settings.h:172](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/bin/psql/settings.h#L172)) |
| Environment | `WIKI_ROOT` (`$PWD`), `SRC` (`$WIKI_ROOT/raw/postgres-17`), `SANDBOX` (`$WIKI_ROOT/.wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut`, which must resolve to a directory directly inside `.wiki-runtime/tmp`), `PAGE` (this page), `PORT` (`55441`), `JOBS` (`8`). The pin is a constant in the script |
| Variables the script sets | `TMPDIR=$SANDBOX/tmp` for every stage, and `PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR=$SANDBOX/rs` for the regression suites, so no temporary file or socket directory lands outside the sandbox ([pg_regress.c#make_temp_sockdir](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/pg_regress.c#L499-L526), [pg_regress.c#PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/test/regress/pg_regress.c#L846-L849)). It clears `PGSERVICE`, `PGSERVICEFILE`, `PGHOSTADDR` and `PGOPTIONS` |
| Prerequisites | `bash` 3.2 or later (both macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 and bash 5.3.15 ran the filed text; see [Last run](#last-run)), `git`, a C toolchain, `make`, `flex`, `bison`, `perl`, zlib headers and `pgrep`; about 3 GiB of disk. The build uses `--without-icu --without-readline` and has no LLVM or libxml, so it has neither JIT compilation nor `XMLTABLE`. `initdb` uses `--locale=C --encoding=UTF8` |
| Socket path limit | `$SANDBOX/sock/.s.PGSQL.$PORT` must be shorter than the Unix-socket path limit that the server checks against `UNIXSOCK_PATH_BUFLEN` ([pqcomm.h:60](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/include/libpq/pqcomm.h#L60), [pqcomm.c:453](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/libpq/pqcomm.c#L453)) |
| Output | `$SANDBOX/out/summary.txt`, read first: every stage's statements and results in order, each experiment under its `[ENN.M]` label, then the `debug_print_*` captures and the platform facts. The per-stage files, `server.log` and the build and test logs sit beside it |
| Runtime | about 1.5 minutes for a full run from an empty sandbox on a 10-core machine (1 minute 23 seconds in the last run), mostly the build and the five test suites; about 10 seconds to re-run `schema` and every `sNN` stage while the build is present |
| Cleanup | `bash .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh clean` stops the server and deletes `$SANDBOX`, refusing a directory without the script's `.pqtut-sandbox` mark; then `rm -f .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh`. The default `stop` stage asserts that no server, `postmaster.pid`, process naming the data directory (`pgrep -f -- "$DATA"`) or socket on `$PORT` is left |

| Stage | What it does |
|---|---|
| `build` | checks the pin, configures and installs the checkout out of tree with `pg_stat_statements`, `postgres_fdw`, `file_fdw` and `tsm_system_rows`, and records the pin beside the binaries last; skipped when that record names the pin |
| `check` | runs `make check` and the four contrib suites on the built tree |
| `cluster` | runs `initdb` once and starts the server with `autovacuum` off and `pg_stat_statements` preloaded |
| `schema` | drops and rebuilds the running schema and every fixture, runs `VACUUM (ANALYZE)`, and defines the helpers `h()` and `plan_summary()` |
| `s01`, `s03` to `s16` | the experiments of each chapter; chapter 2 draws on `s01`. Each stage drops and recreates only the objects it owns, and no stage writes to the running schema's tables (`s13` runs its executed writes on the copy `orders_w`), so any stage can be re-run alone after `schema` |
| `platform` | records the server version, block size, alignment, OS, architecture, key settings and test results |
| `summary` | concatenates the stage outputs into `summary.txt` |
| `stop`, `clean` | stop the server and assert the teardown; `clean` also deletes the sandbox |

Extract the script from this page, from the repository root:

```sh
fence=$(printf '\140\140\140')
sed -n "/^${fence}bash\$/,/^${fence}\$/p" wiki/v17/questions/query-planning/query-planner-comprehensive-tutorial.md | sed '1d;$d' > .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh
```

The first `sed` prints the page's only `bash` block with its two fence lines, and the second drops those lines. The fence is assembled with `printf` so that this block does not contain one.

Isolation and settings. The pinned checkout is read only and is checked against the pin with `git --no-optional-locks status`, so the check never rewrites the checkout's index file. The build is out of tree, and the cluster has its own data directory, socket directory and port. Every fixture is disposable. Every statement carries a `/* wiki_pqt_... */` tag after its leading verb, and every session starts with `statement_timeout = 5min` and `lock_timeout = 10s`. The settings the script touches have these scopes in the pinned definitions:

### The script

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Measurements for the wiki page
#   wiki/v17/questions/query-planning/query-planner-comprehensive-tutorial.md
#
# What this measures, and why it is safe to run
# ---------------------------------------------
# Every number and every plan that page reports about a running v17 server
# comes from this script.  It builds the pinned PostgreSQL 17 checkout out of
# tree, starts one isolated cluster, loads the tutorial's running schema
# (customers, orders, items) and a few focused fixtures, and records what the
# planner and the executor do with them: EXPLAIN plans with estimated costs and
# rows, EXPLAIN ANALYZE row counts (with timing turned off, so no wall-clock
# number is ever recorded), catalog statistics, prepared-statement counters,
# pg_stat_statements planning counters, planner-memory figures and the
# PlannedStmt fields that debug_print_plan logs.  Nothing is timed.
#
# The pinned checkout under raw/postgres-17 is read only.  build and check
# refuse to run unless it is at $PIN with no tracked file changed; build
# records $PIN beside the binaries, and every later stage refuses an install
# built from anything else.  Everything this script writes lives under
# $SANDBOX, which must resolve to a directory directly inside this
# repository's .wiki-runtime/tmp.  Every stage that writes points TMPDIR at
# $SANDBOX/tmp, and check points the regression suites' socket directory at
# $SANDBOX/rs instead of a directory under /tmp.  The script marks the sandbox
# when it creates it, and stop and clean touch nothing without that mark.  The
# cluster has its own data directory, its own socket directory and a
# non-default port.  Every fixture is disposable: the script creates and drops
# its own tables, roles and foreign servers in its own cluster, and they are
# not meant for a database anyone cares about.  Stage s07 deliberately runs a
# CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY that fails, to leave an invalid index, and
# drops that index again.
#
# Usage, from the repository root:
#   bash .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh                  # every stage, in order
#   bash .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh s04 s05          # selected stages
#   bash .wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut.sh clean            # stop, delete the sandbox
#
# Stages, in default order:
#   build check cluster schema s01 s03 s04 s05 s06 s07 s08 s09 s10 s11 s12
#   s13 s14 s15 s16 platform summary stop
# and, on request only: clean
# Each sNN stage holds the experiments of tutorial chapter NN (chapter 2 is
# source-only and chapter 1's stage also serves it).  Every experiment is
# labelled [ENN.M] in the output, and the page quotes those labels.
#
# Results.  Each SQL stage writes $SANDBOX/out/<stage>.txt, which holds every
# statement the stage sent (psql --echo-queries) followed by its result.  The
# three debug_print captures of s01 and s12 are filtered into
# $SANDBOX/out/<stage>-debug.txt.  summary concatenates everything, with the
# platform facts, into $SANDBOX/out/summary.txt.
#
# Failure and teardown.  Every psql call that fails ends the run with a
# non-zero status: pg() and pgf() call die themselves, and a psql call made
# inside $(...) is followed by its own || die.  The one statement that must
# fail goes through pgerr(), which requires psql's failed-statement status 3
# and the expected error text.  Every stage name is checked before any stage
# runs.  An EXIT trap stops the server on every path out of the script and
# then checks that no postmaster.pid and no process naming the data directory
# is left.  Every SQL stage starts the server if it is not up, so a selected
# re-run works after a default run has stopped the cluster.
#
# Environment: WIKI_ROOT SRC SANDBOX PAGE PORT JOBS.  WIKI_ROOT must be this
# repository: the script checks for its AGENTS.md, wiki and raw before it
# creates anything.  The script sets TMPDIR and, for the regression suites,
# PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR itself.  It clears PGSERVICE, PGSERVICEFILE and
# PGHOSTADDR, because a service entry's values win over the exported PGHOST,
# PGPORT, PGDATABASE and PGUSER, and a host address sends a session over TCP
# instead of to the sandbox socket.  PGOPTIONS is never inherited: every
# session gets its options passed explicitly.
#
# GUC apply scopes, from the pinned v17 guc_tables.c and pg_stat_statements.c:
#   shared_buffers, port, listen_addresses, unix_socket_directories,
#   shared_preload_libraries
#       -> PGC_POSTMASTER, restart.  Set once on the postmaster command line.
#   autovacuum -> PGC_SIGHUP, reload.  Set once on the postmaster command line.
#   pg_stat_statements.track, pg_stat_statements.track_planning
#       -> PGC_SUSET, session scope for a superuser.  Set once on the
#          postmaster command line so that every session starts with them.
#   compute_query_id
#       -> PGC_SUSET, session scope for a superuser.  Every session starts
#          with it off, so EXPLAIN VERBOSE prints no OID-dependent query
#          identifier; s14 sets it on, because pg_stat_statements needs it.
#   debug_print_parse, debug_print_rewritten, debug_print_plan,
#   client_min_messages, statement_timeout, lock_timeout, TimeZone,
#   application_name, work_mem, hash_mem_multiplier, every enable_* switch,
#   every *_cost constant, effective_cache_size, default_statistics_target,
#   cursor_tuple_fraction, from_collapse_limit, join_collapse_limit,
#   geqo, geqo_threshold, constraint_exclusion, plan_cache_mode, jit,
#   jit_above_cost, max_parallel_workers_per_gather, debug_parallel_query,
#   parallel_setup_cost, parallel_tuple_cost, min_parallel_table_scan_size,
#   recursive_worktable_factor, search_path, row_security
#       -> PGC_USERSET, session or transaction scope, no reload and no restart.
#   Every experiment that changes one of these says so in its [E] label and
#   is a forced-setting demonstration; each stage starts from the defaults.
set -uo pipefail

WIKI_ROOT="${WIKI_ROOT:-$PWD}"
SRC="${SRC:-$WIKI_ROOT/raw/postgres-17}"
SANDBOX="${SANDBOX:-$WIKI_ROOT/.wiki-runtime/tmp/pqtut}"
PAGE="${PAGE:-$WIKI_ROOT/wiki/v17/questions/query-planning/query-planner-comprehensive-tutorial.md}"
PORT="${PORT:-55441}"
JOBS="${JOBS:-8}"

# The commit the page pins.  build and check refuse a checkout at any other
# commit, and every later stage refuses binaries built from any other.
PIN=786db8dcf168bd9df8f55047337525ac19118b1c
MARKER=.pqtut-sandbox
PINFILE=.pqtut-pin
CONTRIB="pg_stat_statements postgres_fdw file_fdw tsm_system_rows"
SANDBOX_OK=0

say()  { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
note() { printf '   %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf '!! %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# check_root: WIKI_ROOT must be this wiki repository.  It runs before anything
# is created, so a run from the wrong directory creates nothing there.
check_root() {
  [ -f "$WIKI_ROOT/AGENTS.md" ] && [ -d "$WIKI_ROOT/wiki" ] && [ -d "$WIKI_ROOT/raw" ] \
    || die "WIKI_ROOT=$WIKI_ROOT is not the wiki repository: run from its root or set WIKI_ROOT"
}

# resolve_sandbox: turn $SANDBOX into its real path, and refuse one that is not
# a directory directly inside this repository's .wiki-runtime/tmp once .. and
# symbolic links are resolved.
resolve_sandbox() {
  local tmp parent base real
  mkdir -p "$WIKI_ROOT/.wiki-runtime/tmp" || die "cannot create $WIKI_ROOT/.wiki-runtime/tmp"
  tmp=$(cd "$WIKI_ROOT/.wiki-runtime/tmp" && pwd -P) || die "cannot resolve $WIKI_ROOT/.wiki-runtime/tmp"
  base=$(basename "$SANDBOX")
  case "$base" in ''|.|..|/) die "refusing sandbox $SANDBOX: it names no directory of its own" ;; esac
  if [ -e "$SANDBOX" ] || [ -L "$SANDBOX" ]; then
    real=$(cd "$SANDBOX" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || die "refusing sandbox $SANDBOX: it is not a directory"
  else
    parent=$(cd "$(dirname "$SANDBOX")" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) \
      || die "refusing sandbox $SANDBOX: its parent directory does not exist"
    real="$parent/$base"
  fi
  [ "$(dirname "$real")" = "$tmp" ] || die "refusing sandbox $SANDBOX: $real is not directly inside $tmp"
  case "$real" in *\'*) die "refusing sandbox $real: it contains a single quote" ;; esac
  SANDBOX="$real"
}

# setup_paths: runs once, after every stage name has been checked.
setup_paths() {
  check_root
  resolve_sandbox
  BUILD="$SANDBOX/build"; INST="$SANDBOX/install"; DATA="$SANDBOX/data"
  SOCK="$SANDBOX/sock"; OUT="$SANDBOX/out"; BIN="$INST/bin"; DB=pqt
  unset PGSERVICE PGSERVICEFILE PGHOSTADDR PGOPTIONS
  export PGPORT="$PORT" PGHOST="$SOCK" PGDATABASE="$DB" PGUSER=postgres
}

use_sandbox_tmp() {
  mkdir -p "$SANDBOX/tmp" || die "cannot create $SANDBOX/tmp"
  export TMPDIR="$SANDBOX/tmp"
}

# check_pin: the build and the regression suites must come from exactly the
# commit the page records, with no tracked file changed.  --no-optional-locks
# keeps git status from refreshing the checkout's index file.
check_pin() {
  local head dirty
  head=$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null) || die "$SRC is not a git checkout"
  [ "$head" = "$PIN" ] || die "$SRC is at $head, not at the pinned $PIN"
  dirty=$(git -C "$SRC" --no-optional-locks status --porcelain --untracked-files=no 2>/dev/null) \
    || die "git status failed in $SRC"
  [ -z "$dirty" ] || die "$SRC has changed tracked files, so a build would not be the pin"
}

check_install_pin() {
  local built
  built=$(cat "$INST/$PINFILE" 2>/dev/null) || die "$INST has no build record: run the build stage"
  [ "$built" = "$PIN" ] || die "$INST was built from $built, not the pinned $PIN: run clean, then build"
}

# claim_sandbox: create $SANDBOX, or accept one this script created before,
# and mark it.  An existing non-empty directory without the mark is refused.
claim_sandbox() {
  if [ -e "$SANDBOX" ] && [ ! -f "$SANDBOX/$MARKER" ] \
     && [ -n "$(ls -A "$SANDBOX" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
    die "refusing sandbox $SANDBOX: it exists, is not empty, and this script did not create it"
  fi
  mkdir -p "$SANDBOX" && : > "$SANDBOX/$MARKER" || die "cannot create $SANDBOX"
  SANDBOX_OK=1
}

own_sandbox() {
  [ -d "$SANDBOX" ] || { note "no sandbox at $SANDBOX"; return 1; }
  [ -f "$SANDBOX/$MARKER" ] || die "refusing: $SANDBOX carries no $MARKER, so this script did not create it"
  SANDBOX_OK=1
}

# Every session: -X ignores ~/.psqlrc, ON_ERROR_STOP stops at the first
# failed statement, and the options below are PGC_USERSET settings applied at
# session scope.  TimeZone is fixed so that timestamptz output is the same on
# every host.
SESSION_OPTS="-c statement_timeout=5min -c lock_timeout=10s -c TimeZone=UTC -c application_name=wiki_pqtut -c compute_query_id=off"
CURRENT_STAGE=""
pg()  { PGOPTIONS="$SESSION_OPTS" "$BIN/psql" -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@" \
          || die "psql failed in stage ${CURRENT_STAGE:-<none>}: psql $*"; }
pgq() { pg -At "$@"; }
# pgf: run one stage's SQL from standard input with every statement echoed,
# into $OUT/<stage>.txt.  psql variables give the SQL the sandbox paths.
pgf() {
  local name="$1"
  PGOPTIONS="$SESSION_OPTS" "$BIN/psql" -X -q -e -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
    -v outdir="$OUT" -v sockdir="$SOCK" -v port="$PORT" -v dbname="$DB" \
    -f - > "$OUT/$name.txt" 2> "$OUT/$name.err" \
    || die "psql failed in stage ${CURRENT_STAGE:-<none>}, see $OUT/$name.txt and $OUT/$name.err"
}
# pgerr runs one statement that must fail: psql reads it from stdin under
# ON_ERROR_STOP and must exit with status 3, psql's status for a failed
# script statement, and its ERROR line must contain the expected text.
pgerr() {
  local sql="$1" want="$2" out st
  out=$(printf '%s\n' "$sql" | PGOPTIONS="$SESSION_OPTS" "$BIN/psql" -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 2>&1)
  st=$?
  [ "$st" = 3 ] || die "expected psql status 3 from a statement that must fail, got $st: $sql: $out"
  # Only the ERROR line is kept: the DETAIL of a failed unique build names
  # whichever duplicate the build met first, which is not part of the result.
  case "$out" in
    *"ERROR:  $want"*) printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E 'ERROR' ;;
    *) die "expected the error \"$want\" from: $sql; got: $out" ;;
  esac
}

running() { [ -x "$BIN/pg_ctl" ] && "$BIN/pg_ctl" -D "$DATA" status >/dev/null 2>&1; }
stop_server() { running && "$BIN/pg_ctl" -D "$DATA" -m fast -w stop >/dev/null 2>&1; return 0; }

# Teardown on every path out of the script.  The trap stops a server only in a
# sandbox this run claimed or verified as its own, and then checks the stop.
on_exit() {
  local st=$?
  trap - EXIT INT TERM
  if [ "$SANDBOX_OK" = 1 ] && [ "$st" -ne 0 ] && running; then
    printf '!! exit status %s with the server still up; stopping it\n' "$st" >&2
  fi
  [ "$SANDBOX_OK" = 1 ] && stop_server
  if [ "$SANDBOX_OK" = 1 ]; then
    if [ -f "$DATA/postmaster.pid" ] \
       || { command -v pgrep >/dev/null 2>&1 && pgrep -f -- "$DATA" >/dev/null 2>&1; }; then
      printf '!! teardown incomplete: stop it with %s -D %s -m fast stop\n' "$BIN/pg_ctl" "$DATA" >&2
      [ "$st" -ne 0 ] || st=1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "$st" -ne 0 ]; then
    if [ "$SANDBOX_OK" = 1 ] && [ -d "$SANDBOX" ]; then
      printf '!! failed with status %s; the sandbox %s was kept\n' "$st" "$SANDBOX" >&2
    else
      printf '!! failed with status %s; nothing was created\n' "$st" >&2
    fi
  fi
  exit "$st"
}
trap on_exit EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM

need_server() {
  running && return 0
  [ -x "$BIN/pg_ctl" ] || die "no built server at $BIN: run the build stage first"
  stage_cluster || die "could not start the measurement server"
}

stage_build() {
  say "build: configure the pinned checkout out of tree, install core and four contrib modules"
  check_pin
  mkdir -p "$BUILD" "$OUT" "$SOCK" || die "cannot create the build directories under $SANDBOX"
  if [ -f "$INST/$PINFILE" ]; then
    check_install_pin
    [ -x "$BIN/postgres" ] || die "$INST has a build record but no postgres binary: run clean, then build"
    note "already built from $PIN: $("$BIN/postgres" --version)"; return 0
  fi
  if [ -e "$INST" ]; then
    note "removing the incomplete install at $INST, which has no build record"
    rm -rf "$INST" || die "cannot remove the incomplete install at $INST"
  fi
  [ -x "$SRC/configure" ] || die "no pinned checkout at $SRC"
  # No --with-llvm: this host has no LLVM, so the server has no JIT provider.
  # s12 records what the planner decides about JIT without one.
  ( cd "$BUILD" && "$SRC/configure" --prefix="$INST" --without-icu --without-readline \
      > "$OUT/configure.log" 2>&1 ) || die "configure failed, see $OUT/configure.log"
  ( cd "$BUILD" && make -s -j "$JOBS" > "$OUT/make.log" 2>&1 \
      && make -s install > "$OUT/install.log" 2>&1 \
      && for m in $CONTRIB; do
           make -s -C contrib/$m install >> "$OUT/install.log" 2>&1 || exit 1
         done ) || die "make failed, see $OUT/make.log and $OUT/install.log"
  printf '%s\n' "$PIN" > "$INST/$PINFILE" || die "cannot record the build's pin in $INST"
  note "$("$BIN/postgres" --version), built from $PIN"
}

stage_check() {
  say "check: core regression suite, then the four contrib suites, on the built tree"
  check_pin
  check_install_pin
  local m rs="$SANDBOX/rs"
  mkdir -p "$rs" || die "cannot create $rs"
  ( cd "$BUILD" && PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR="$rs" make -s check > "$OUT/check.log" 2>&1 ) \
    || die "make check failed, see $OUT/check.log"
  note "core: $(grep -E 'tests passed|tests failed|failed' "$OUT/check.log" | tail -n 1)"
  for m in $CONTRIB; do
    ( cd "$BUILD" && PG_REGRESS_SOCK_DIR="$rs" make -s -C contrib/$m check > "$OUT/check_$m.log" 2>&1 ) \
      || die "contrib/$m check failed, see $OUT/check_$m.log"
    note "$m: $(grep -E 'tests passed|tests failed|failed' "$OUT/check_$m.log" | tail -n 1)"
  done
}

stage_cluster() {
  say "cluster: initdb, start with autovacuum off and pg_stat_statements loaded"
  check_install_pin
  mkdir -p "$OUT" "$SOCK" || die "cannot create $OUT and $SOCK"
  [ -f "$DATA/PG_VERSION" ] || "$BIN/initdb" -D "$DATA" -U postgres --locale=C --encoding=UTF8 \
    > "$OUT/initdb.log" 2>&1 || die "initdb failed, see $OUT/initdb.log"
  running || "$BIN/pg_ctl" -D "$DATA" -l "$OUT/server.log" -w \
    -o "-p $PORT -k '$SOCK' -c listen_addresses='' -c autovacuum=off -c shared_buffers=256MB -c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements -c pg_stat_statements.track=all -c pg_stat_statements.track_planning=on" start \
    >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "server did not start, see $OUT/server.log"
  local have
  have=$(PGDATABASE=postgres pgq -c "SELECT /* wiki_pqt_dbcheck */ count(*) FROM pg_database WHERE datname = '$DB'") \
    || die "could not read pg_database"
  [ "$have" = "1" ] || PGDATABASE=postgres pg -q -c "CREATE /* wiki_pqt_fixture */ DATABASE $DB"
}

# schema: the running schema and the focused fixtures.  Every table is
# disposable and rebuilt from scratch, so the stage can be re-run.  Row values
# come from h(), a deterministic hash of the row number, so the data, and with
# it every statistic, estimate and cost, are the same on every run.  ANALYZE
# samples 300 * statistics target rows; every table here either holds at most
# 30000 rows or has one column's target raised until the sample covers the
# whole table, so ANALYZE reads every row and its statistics are exact and
# repeatable.  VACUUM sets the visibility map, so index-only scans find
# all-visible pages.
stage_schema() {
  say "schema: running schema customers/orders/items and the focused fixtures"
  pgf schema <<'SQL'
SET /* wiki_pqt_schema */ client_min_messages = warning;
-- Objects later stages create are dropped too, so a re-run starts clean.
DROP /* wiki_pqt_schema */ SCHEMA IF EXISTS remote CASCADE;
DROP /* wiki_pqt_schema */ SERVER IF EXISTS loopback CASCADE;
DROP /* wiki_pqt_schema */ SERVER IF EXISTS files CASCADE;
DROP /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE IF EXISTS fresh, products, ios, audit_plans, orders_w, orders_archive, staging,
  j01, j02, j03, j04, j05, j06, j07, j08, j09, j10, j11, j12 CASCADE;
DROP /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE IF EXISTS items, orders, customers, events, places, docs, accounts,
  orders_r, orders_h, items_h, wide_p, ledger CASCADE;
DROP /* wiki_pqt_schema */ FUNCTION IF EXISTS h(int, int);
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ FUNCTION h(k int, salt int) RETURNS int
  LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE
  RETURN ((hashint4(k + salt * 1000003)::int8 + 2147483648) % 100000)::int;

-- customers: region is skewed (40/30/20/10 %), country depends on region
-- (two countries per region), 20 % of emails are NULL.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE customers (
  id int PRIMARY KEY,
  name text NOT NULL,
  region text NOT NULL,
  country text NOT NULL,
  tier text NOT NULL,
  signup date NOT NULL,
  email text
);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO customers
SELECT g, 'customer ' || lpad(g::text, 4, '0'), reg,
       CASE reg WHEN 'north' THEN (ARRAY['NO','SE'])[1 + h(g, 1) % 2]
                WHEN 'south' THEN (ARRAY['ES','IT'])[1 + h(g, 1) % 2]
                WHEN 'east'  THEN (ARRAY['PL','RO'])[1 + h(g, 1) % 2]
                ELSE              (ARRAY['PT','IE'])[1 + h(g, 1) % 2] END,
       CASE WHEN h(g, 2) % 10 = 0 THEN 'gold' WHEN h(g, 2) % 10 < 4 THEN 'silver' ELSE 'bronze' END,
       date '2020-01-01' + h(g, 3) % 1461,
       CASE WHEN h(g, 4) % 5 = 0 THEN NULL ELSE 'user' || g || '@example.com' END
  FROM (SELECT g, CASE WHEN g % 10 < 4 THEN 'north' WHEN g % 10 < 7 THEN 'south'
                       WHEN g % 10 < 9 THEN 'east' ELSE 'west' END AS reg
          FROM generate_series(1, 2000) g) s;

-- orders: 30 % of orders belong to 20 large customers, status is skewed
-- (85/10/5 %), ordered_at rises with id, amount is uniform, note is 95 % NULL.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders (
  id int PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES customers,
  status text NOT NULL,
  ordered_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  amount numeric(10,2) NOT NULL,
  note text
);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO orders
SELECT g,
       CASE WHEN h(g, 11) < 30000 THEN 1 + h(g, 12) % 20 ELSE 21 + h(g, 12) % 1980 END,
       CASE WHEN h(g, 13) < 5000 THEN 'cancelled' WHEN h(g, 13) < 15000 THEN 'pending' ELSE 'shipped' END,
       timestamptz '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' + g * interval '17 minutes',
       (h(g, 14) % 100000) / 100.0,
       CASE WHEN h(g, 15) % 20 = 0 THEN 'gift wrap' END
  FROM generate_series(1, 30000) g;
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INDEX orders_customer_id_idx ON orders (customer_id);
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INDEX orders_ordered_at_idx ON orders (ordered_at);

-- items: three lines per order; half the lines sell one of ten popular products.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE items (
  order_id int NOT NULL REFERENCES orders,
  line_no int NOT NULL,
  product_id int NOT NULL,
  qty int NOT NULL,
  price numeric(10,2) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, line_no)
);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO items
SELECT o, l,
       CASE WHEN h(o * 3 + l, 21) < 50000 THEN 1 + h(o * 3 + l, 22) % 10 ELSE 11 + h(o * 3 + l, 22) % 490 END,
       1 + h(o * 3 + l, 23) % 5,
       1 + (h(o * 3 + l, 24) % 20000) / 100.0
  FROM generate_series(1, 30000) o, generate_series(1, 3) l
 ORDER BY o, l;
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INDEX items_product_id_idx ON items (product_id);
-- 300 * 400 = 120000 sampled rows cover all 90000.
ALTER /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE items ALTER COLUMN line_no SET STATISTICS 400;

-- events: 600000 rows, large enough for a parallel plan at default settings.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE events (
  id bigint NOT NULL,
  order_id int NOT NULL,
  kind smallint NOT NULL,
  at timestamptz NOT NULL,
  payload text NOT NULL
);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO events
SELECT g, 1 + (g - 1) / 20, (h(g, 31) % 10)::smallint,
       timestamptz '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' + g * interval '50 seconds', md5(g::text)
  FROM generate_series(1, 600000) g;
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INDEX events_at_brin ON events USING brin (at);
-- 300 * 2500 = 750000 sampled rows cover all 600000.
ALTER /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE events ALTER COLUMN kind SET STATISTICS 2500;

-- places and docs: geometric and array data for GiST, SP-GiST and GIN.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE places (id int PRIMARY KEY, p point NOT NULL, name text NOT NULL);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO places
SELECT g, point(h(g, 41) % 1000, h(g, 42) % 1000), 'place ' || g FROM generate_series(1, 20000) g;
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE docs (id int PRIMARY KEY, tags text[] NOT NULL);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO docs
SELECT g, ARRAY['t' || (h(g, 51) % 50), 'u' || (h(g, 52) % 500)] FROM generate_series(1, 20000) g;

-- accounts: a small table for row-level security.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE accounts (id int PRIMARY KEY, owner text NOT NULL, balance int NOT NULL);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO accounts
SELECT g, CASE WHEN g % 4 = 0 THEN 'pqt_reader' ELSE 'someone_else' END, g * 10 FROM generate_series(1, 1000) g;

-- orders_r: the orders, range-partitioned by month, plus a default partition.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_r (LIKE orders) PARTITION BY RANGE (ordered_at);
DO /* wiki_pqt_schema */ $do$
BEGIN
  FOR m IN 1..12 LOOP
    EXECUTE format('CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_r_%s PARTITION OF orders_r FOR VALUES FROM (%L) TO (%L)',
                   lpad(m::text, 2, '0'),
                   make_timestamptz(2024, m, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC'),
                   make_timestamptz(2024, m, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC') + interval '1 month');
  END LOOP;
END
$do$;
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_r_default PARTITION OF orders_r DEFAULT;
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO orders_r SELECT * FROM orders;
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INDEX orders_r_customer_id_idx ON orders_r (customer_id);
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INDEX orders_r_ordered_at_idx ON orders_r (ordered_at);
-- The parent's sample is split across partitions; 300 * 200 = 60000 covers all 30000.
ALTER /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_r ALTER COLUMN id SET STATISTICS 200;

-- orders_h and items_h: hash-partitioned four ways on the join key.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_h (LIKE orders) PARTITION BY HASH (id);
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE items_h (LIKE items) PARTITION BY HASH (order_id);
DO /* wiki_pqt_schema */ $do$
BEGIN
  FOR r IN 0..3 LOOP
    EXECUTE format('CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_h%s PARTITION OF orders_h FOR VALUES WITH (MODULUS 4, REMAINDER %s)', r, r);
    EXECUTE format('CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE items_h%s PARTITION OF items_h FOR VALUES WITH (MODULUS 4, REMAINDER %s)', r, r);
  END LOOP;
END
$do$;
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO orders_h SELECT * FROM orders;
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO items_h SELECT * FROM items;
ALTER /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_h ADD PRIMARY KEY (id);
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INDEX items_h_order_id_idx ON items_h (order_id);
ALTER /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE orders_h ALTER COLUMN id SET STATISTICS 200;
ALTER /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE items_h ALTER COLUMN line_no SET STATISTICS 400;

-- wide_p: 256 hash partitions, only for planning-overhead measurements.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE wide_p (id int NOT NULL, v int NOT NULL) PARTITION BY HASH (id);
DO /* wiki_pqt_schema */ $do$
BEGIN
  FOR r IN 0..255 LOOP
    EXECUTE format('CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE wide_p_%s PARTITION OF wide_p FOR VALUES WITH (MODULUS 256, REMAINDER %s)', r, r);
  END LOOP;
END
$do$;
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO wide_p SELECT g, g % 7 FROM generate_series(1, 25600) g;

-- ledger: legacy inheritance with CHECK constraints, for constraint exclusion.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE ledger (yr int NOT NULL, amount numeric NOT NULL);
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE ledger_2023 (CHECK (yr = 2023)) INHERITS (ledger);
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ TABLE ledger_2024 (CHECK (yr = 2024)) INHERITS (ledger);
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO ledger_2023 SELECT 2023, g FROM generate_series(1, 5000) g;
INSERT /* wiki_pqt_schema */ INTO ledger_2024 SELECT 2024, g FROM generate_series(1, 5000) g;

VACUUM /* wiki_pqt_schema */ (ANALYZE) customers, orders, items, events, places, docs, accounts,
  orders_r, orders_h, items_h, wide_p, ledger, ledger_2023, ledger_2024;

-- plan_summary(): EXPLAIN (MEMORY) one statement and keep only its top plan
-- line, the number of scan nodes and the planner-memory line, so that a plan
-- with twelve joins or 256 partitions does not have to be printed in full.
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_schema */ OR REPLACE FUNCTION plan_summary(q text) RETURNS text LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $fn$
DECLARE r record; top text; mem text := ''; scans int := 0;
BEGIN
  FOR r IN EXECUTE 'EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_plan_summary */ (MEMORY) ' || q LOOP
    IF top IS NULL THEN top := btrim(r."QUERY PLAN"); END IF;
    IF r."QUERY PLAN" ~ 'Memory: used=' THEN mem := btrim(r."QUERY PLAN"); END IF;
    IF r."QUERY PLAN" ~ 'Scan( Backward)? (on|using) ' THEN scans := scans + 1; END IF;
  END LOOP;
  RETURN format('%s | %s scan nodes | %s', top, scans, mem);
END $fn$;

\echo [E0.1] Table sizes and row counts after VACUUM (ANALYZE)
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_e0_1 */ c.relname, c.relkind, c.relpages, c.reltuples, c.relallvisible,
       pg_relation_size(c.oid) AS bytes
  FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
 WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname IN ('customers','orders','items','events','places','docs',
       'accounts','orders_pkey','orders_customer_id_idx','orders_ordered_at_idx','items_pkey',
       'items_product_id_idx','customers_pkey','events_at_brin','orders_r_03','ledger_2024')
 ORDER BY c.relname;
SQL
  note "$(grep -c . "$OUT/schema.txt") lines in $OUT/schema.txt"
}

# debug_capture: pull the planner-boundary markers out of a stage's debug_print
# log.  The node dumps are long, so only the markers the page quotes are kept:
# the RAISE LOG markers that name each statement, the three dump headers, the
# plan node types (a trailing blank or line end keeps {AGGREF from matching
# {AGG), range-table kinds, and the PlannedStmt fields.  OIDs are left out, so the capture compares across clusters.
debug_capture() {
  local name="$1"
  grep -E -o 'marker [a-z0-9_]+|(parse tree|rewritten parse tree|plan):|\{QUERY|\{PLANNEDSTMT|\{RANGETBLENTRY|:commandType [0-9]+|:rtekind [0-9]+|:relkind [a-z]|:inh (true|false)|:subquery (<>|\{QUERY)|:jitFlags [0-9]+|:parallelModeNeeded (true|false)|:canSetTag (true|false)|\{(SEQSCAN|INDEXSCAN|INDEXONLYSCAN|BITMAPHEAPSCAN|AGG|GATHER|RESULT|SUBQUERYSCAN)( |$)' \
    "$OUT/$name.err" > "$OUT/$name-debug.txt" || die "no debug_print output in $OUT/$name.err"
}

# s01: chapter 1 (and 2), follow one query through parsing, rewriting,
# planning and execution.
stage_s01() {
  say "s01: follow one query"
  pgf s01 <<'SQL'
\echo [E1.1] Q1, the running query: planner estimates only
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_1 */
SELECT c.name, o.id, o.amount
  FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'pending'
 ORDER BY o.amount DESC
 LIMIT 5;
\echo [E1.2] Q1 executed: the same plan with actual row counts (timing off)
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_2 */ (ANALYZE, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT c.name, o.id, o.amount
  FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'pending'
 ORDER BY o.amount DESC
 LIMIT 5;
\echo [E1.3] Q1 with VERBOSE: the output column list setrefs.c built for every node
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_3 */ (VERBOSE)
SELECT c.name, o.id, o.amount
  FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'pending'
 ORDER BY o.amount DESC
 LIMIT 5;
\echo [E1.4] A view is replaced by its query before planning
CREATE /* wiki_pqt_e1_4 */ OR REPLACE VIEW pending_orders AS
  SELECT id, customer_id, amount FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_4 */ SELECT count(*) FROM pending_orders WHERE amount > 900;
\echo [E1.5] debug_print_parse, debug_print_rewritten and debug_print_plan (captured in s01-debug.txt)
SET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ debug_print_parse = on;
SET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ debug_print_rewritten = on;
SET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ debug_print_plan = on;
SET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ client_min_messages = log;
DO /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ $$ BEGIN RAISE LOG 'marker e1_5_view_query'; END $$;
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ count(*) FROM pending_orders WHERE amount > 900;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ client_min_messages;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ debug_print_parse;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ debug_print_rewritten;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_e1_5 */ debug_print_plan;
\echo [E1.6] A utility statement that contains a query: EXPLAIN of CREATE TABLE AS plans the inner SELECT
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_6 */ CREATE TABLE pending_copy AS SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';
\echo [E1.7] A cursor is planned for its first 10 % of rows (cursor_tuple_fraction = 0.1)
SHOW /* wiki_pqt_e1_7 */ cursor_tuple_fraction;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_7 */ SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.id;
BEGIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_7 */;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e1_7 */ DECLARE c1 CURSOR FOR SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN items i ON i.order_id = o.id;
ROLLBACK /* wiki_pqt_e1_7 */;
SQL
  debug_capture s01
}

# s03: chapter 3, transformations before path search.
stage_s03() {
  say "s03: transform the query safely"
  pgf s03 <<'SQL'
SET /* wiki_pqt_s03 */ client_min_messages = warning;
DROP /* wiki_pqt_s03 */ VIEW IF EXISTS pending_plain, pending_sb;
DROP /* wiki_pqt_s03 */ FUNCTION IF EXISTS big_amount(numeric), big_amount_pinned(numeric), orders_of(int),
  orders_of_plpgsql(int), leaky(int);
DO /* wiki_pqt_s03 */ $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'pqt_reader') THEN
    EXECUTE 'DROP /* wiki_pqt_s03 */ OWNED BY pqt_reader';
    EXECUTE 'DROP /* wiki_pqt_s03 */ ROLE pqt_reader';
  END IF;
END $$;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_s03 */ client_min_messages;

\echo [E3.1] Constant folding: 2 + 3 and abs(-500) are computed at plan time; now() is stable and is not
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e3_1 */ SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = 2 + 3;
```
