```bash
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'pending' ORDER BY o.amount DESC LIMIT 5;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_e16_2 */ random_page_cost;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_e16_2 */ work_mem;

\echo [E16.3] EXPLAIN (MEMORY) reports the memory the planner used for Q1
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e16_3 */ (MEMORY)
SELECT c.name, o.id, o.amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'pending' ORDER BY o.amount DESC LIMIT 5;

\echo [E16.4] EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN) plans a parameterized statement without values
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e16_4 */ (GENERIC_PLAN) SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = $1 AND status = $2;

\echo [E16.5] Finding a misestimate: compare estimated and actual rows node by node
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e16_5 */ (ANALYZE, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF)
SELECT c.name, o.amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.region = 'west' AND c.country = 'PT';

\echo [E16.6] A missing alternative versus an expensive one (forced setting)
SET /* wiki_pqt_e16_6 */ enable_seqscan = off;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e16_6 */ SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount < 1;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e16_6 */ SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id > 0;
RESET /* wiki_pqt_e16_6 */ enable_seqscan;
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e16_6 */ SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id > 0;

\echo [E16.7] EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, SERIALIZE): the cost of producing the output rows
EXPLAIN /* wiki_pqt_e16_7 */ (ANALYZE, SERIALIZE, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF) SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';
SQL
}

# platform: the facts the numbers depend on.  pg_controldata reads the control
# file of the stopped-or-running cluster without touching it.
stage_platform() {
  say "platform: server version, block size, alignment, OS and architecture"
  {
    printf 'script run started %s\n' "$RUN_STARTED"
    printf 'bash %s\n' "$BASH_VERSION"
    printf 'uname %s\n' "$(uname -srm)"
    printf 'pin %s\n' "$PIN"
    printf 'install built from %s\n' "$(cat "$INST/$PINFILE")"
    printf 'checkout at %s\n' "$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
    "$BIN/pg_controldata" -D "$DATA" | grep -E 'Maximum data alignment|Database block size|WAL block size|Blocks per segment'
    grep -E 'tests passed|tests failed' "$OUT/check.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | sed 's/^/make check: /'
    for m in $CONTRIB; do
      grep -E 'tests passed|tests failed' "$OUT/check_$m.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1 | sed "s/^/$m check: /"
    done
  } > "$OUT/platform.txt" || die "could not write $OUT/platform.txt"
  pgq <<'SQL' >> "$OUT/platform.txt" || die "could not read the server settings"
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_platform */ version();
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_platform */ name || ' = ' || setting || coalesce(' ' || unit, '')
  FROM pg_settings
 WHERE name IN ('block_size', 'shared_buffers', 'work_mem', 'max_parallel_workers_per_gather',
                'max_parallel_workers', 'max_worker_processes', 'jit', 'server_encoding',
                'effective_io_concurrency', 'random_page_cost', 'effective_cache_size')
 ORDER BY name;
SELECT /* wiki_pqt_platform */ 'pg_jit_available = ' || pg_jit_available();
SQL
  cat "$OUT/platform.txt" >&2
}

stage_summary() {
  say "summary: written to $OUT/summary.txt"
  local s
  : > "$OUT/summary.txt" || die "cannot write $OUT/summary.txt"
  for s in schema $SQL_EXPERIMENTS; do
    [ -f "$OUT/$s.txt" ] || continue
    printf '\n######## stage %s\n' "$s" >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
    cat "$OUT/$s.txt" >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
    [ -f "$OUT/$s-debug.txt" ] && { printf '\n######## stage %s, debug_print capture\n' "$s"; cat "$OUT/$s-debug.txt"; } >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
  done
  printf '\n######## platform\n' >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
  cat "$OUT/platform.txt" >> "$OUT/summary.txt" 2>/dev/null
  date -u '+run finished %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
  note "$(grep -c . "$OUT/summary.txt") lines"
}

# The teardown is asserted, not assumed: pg_ctl finds no server, there is no
# postmaster.pid, no process whose command line names the data directory, and
# no socket is left on the port.
assert_down() {
  command -v pgrep >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "pgrep is needed to assert that no postgres process is left"
  "$BIN/pg_ctl" -D "$DATA" status >/dev/null 2>&1 && die "pg_ctl still reports a server running from $DATA"
  [ -f "$DATA/postmaster.pid" ] && die "postmaster.pid is still present in $DATA"
  pgrep -f -- "$DATA" >/dev/null 2>&1 && die "a process naming $DATA is still running"
  [ -e "$SOCK/.s.PGSQL.$PORT" ] && die "the socket $SOCK/.s.PGSQL.$PORT is still present"
  return 0
}

stage_stop() {
  say "stop: shut the measurement cluster down"
  own_sandbox || return 0
  stop_server
  assert_down
  note "stopped: no postmaster.pid, no process from $DATA, no socket on port $PORT; $SANDBOX is kept until the clean stage"
}

stage_clean() {
  say "clean: stop the server and delete the sandbox"
  own_sandbox || return 0
  stop_server
  assert_down
  rm -rf "$SANDBOX" || die "could not delete $SANDBOX"
  SANDBOX_OK=0
  note "removed $SANDBOX"
}

# The dispatcher checks every stage name before any stage runs, claims the
# sandbox for the stages that write into it, starts a server for the stages
# that need one, and turns a failed stage into a failed run.
SQL_EXPERIMENTS="s01 s03 s04 s05 s06 s07 s08 s09 s10 s11 s12 s13 s14 s15 s16"
SQL_STAGES="schema $SQL_EXPERIMENTS platform summary"
known_stage() {
  # A stage name is one bare word, so "s04 s05" passed as one argument, or an
  # empty argument, is refused rather than matched as a substring of the list.
  case "$1" in ''|*[!a-z0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
  case " build check cluster stop clean $SQL_STAGES " in *" $1 "*) return 0 ;; esac
  return 1
}
run_stage() {
  local st="$1"
  CURRENT_STAGE="$st"
  case "$st" in
    stop|clean) ;;
    build|check|cluster) claim_sandbox; use_sandbox_tmp ;;
    summary) claim_sandbox; use_sandbox_tmp ;;
    *) claim_sandbox; use_sandbox_tmp; need_server ;;
  esac
  "stage_$st" || die "stage $st failed"
  CURRENT_STAGE=""
}

RUN_STARTED=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
DEFAULT="build check cluster schema $SQL_EXPERIMENTS platform summary stop"
[ $# -eq 0 ] && set -- $DEFAULT
for st in "$@"; do known_stage "$st" || die "unknown stage: $st; nothing was run"; done
setup_paths
for st in "$@"; do run_stage "$st"; done
```

## Context Reviewed

- Pin: `raw/postgres-17/` at `786db8dcf168bd9df8f55047337525ac19118b1c` (PostgreSQL 17.11), read only; the checkout's `git --no-optional-locks status` showed no changed tracked file. The checkout has no release tags, so every "new in 17" statement rests on ancestry from `5bcc7e6dc8` ("Stamp HEAD as 17devel").
- Planner source reviewed as a whole: `src/backend/optimizer/{plan,path,prep,util,geqo}`, `src/backend/utils/adt/selfuncs.c` and the per-type estimators, `src/backend/utils/cache/plancache.c`, `src/backend/partitioning/partprune.c`, `src/include/nodes/{pathnodes,plannodes,primnodes,parsenodes,supportnodes}.h`, `src/include/optimizer/*.h`, `src/backend/tcop/postgres.c`, `src/backend/commands/explain.c`, `src/backend/utils/misc/guc_tables.c`, and the optimizer `README` files.
- Inventory checks behind the chapter audit: every `Path` subtype in `pathnodes.h`, every `Plan` subtype in `plannodes.h`, every case of `create_plan_recurse()`, every setting in the three `QUERY_TUNING_*` groups of `guc_tables.c`, and every planner-related hook in `src/include`.
- Tests: `src/test/regress/sql` and `expected`, `src/test/modules/{delay_execution,test_predtest,test_rls_hooks,dummy_index_am}`, and the regression suites of `pg_stat_statements`, `postgres_fdw`, `file_fdw` and `tsm_system_rows`.
- Empirical: one isolated PostgreSQL 17.11 server built from the pin by the script under [Measurement Script](#measurement-script); its experiments E0.1 to E16.7 are listed per chapter below.
- Wiki context (navigation only, never evidence): `wiki/versions.md`, `wiki/index.md`, `wiki/v17/index.md`, the last twenty `wiki/log.md` entries, the v17 codebase navigation guide, and the v17 planner, partitioning and partial-index pages linked under [Navigation](#navigation). The three v17 common concept pages cover bloat-test protocols, not planner topics, so none is linked.
- Glossary: every entry this page links was checked for a **Checked on:** line that includes PostgreSQL 17.

**Chapter 1.**

- `src/backend/tcop/postgres.c`: `pg_parse_query`, `pg_analyze_and_rewrite_*`, `pg_rewrite_query`, `pg_plan_query`, `pg_plan_queries`, `exec_simple_query`, `exec_parse_message`, `exec_bind_message`.
- `src/backend/parser/analyze.c` (`parse_analyze_fixedparams`, `transformStmt`, `transformExplainStmt`) and `src/backend/parser/gram.y` (`DeclareCursorStmt`).
- `src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c`: `QueryRewrite`, `ApplyRetrieveRule`, `fireRIRrules`.
- `src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c`: `planner`, `standard_planner`, `subquery_planner` outline, `grouping_planner` LIMIT handling, `get_cheapest_fractional_path`; `util/pathnode.c` `compare_fractional_path_costs`; `util/relnode.c` `consider_startup`.
- Utilities that plan inner queries: `commands/explain.c`, `createas.c`, `portalcmds.c`, `copyto.c`, `matview.c`, `prepare.c`; `tcop/utility.c` `ProcessUtility`; `tcop/pquery.c` `PortalStart`, `PortalRunUtility`, `ChoosePortalStrategy`; `executor/execMain.c` `InitPlan`.

## Evidence Map

Each row maps one load-bearing claim to its strongest evidence. "Measured" and "Estimated" rows name the experiment; "derived" rows name the inputs of the arithmetic. The chapters carry the full citations.

| Claim | Evidence | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| Raw parsing reads no catalogs and returns one `RawStmt` per statement | [postgres.c#pg_parse_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L603-L626) | source |
| Parse analysis wraps non-optimizable statements, except DECLARE/EXPLAIN/CTAS/CALL, in `CMD_UTILITY` queries | [analyze.c#transformStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/analyze.c#L340-L416) | source |
| Utility queries skip rewriting; others go through `QueryRewrite()` | [postgres.c#pg_rewrite_query](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L820-L829) | source |
| A view RTE becomes an `RTE_SUBQUERY` but keeps its OID for locking and permissions | [rewriteHandler.c#ApplyRetrieveRule-subquery](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/rewrite/rewriteHandler.c#L1869-L1886) | source |
| The view is gone from the plan: parse tree `relkind v`, rewritten `rtekind 1`, plan `SEQSCAN` | E1.4, E1.5 | measured |
| Utility statements get a wrapper `PlannedStmt` without planning | [postgres.c#pg_plan_queries](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/tcop/postgres.c#L988-L1002) | source |
| `planner()` calls `planner_hook` if set, else `standard_planner()` | [planner.c#planner](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L274-L285) | source |
| Parallel plans need `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK`, a SELECT without modifying CTE, workers above 0, and no unsafe function | [planner.c#standard_planner-parallel](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L349-L365) | source |
| DECLARE always adds `CURSOR_OPT_FAST_PLAN` and never `CURSOR_OPT_PARALLEL_OK` | [gram.y#DeclareCursorStmt](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/parser/gram.y#L12605-L12614) | source |
| Fast-start flag switches `tuple_fraction` to `cursor_tuple_fraction` | [planner.c#standard_planner-tuple-fraction](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L387-L413) | source |

## Open Questions

**Verification gaps of this build.**

- JIT compilation itself is not demonstrated. The server has no LLVM provider (`pg_jit_available()` is false in E12.10), so only the planner's `jitFlags` decision is measured; whether and how the executor compiles expressions is described from source only.
- Nondeterministic collations need ICU, and the build is configured `--without-icu`. Their effect on index eligibility and on pattern matching is described from source only.
- `XMLTABLE` needs libxml, which the build lacks. `JSON_TABLE` stands in for table functions (E6.6).
- No in-core module provides a custom scan, and no in-core module sets `set_rel_pathlist_hook`, `set_join_pathlist_hook`, `join_search_hook`, `create_upper_paths_hook` or `get_relation_info_hook`, so those interfaces are described from source only.
- `auto_explain` was not built. The page describes it only where chapter 16 cites its source.

**Chapter 1.**

- Verification gap: `COPY (query) TO`, `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` and the extended-protocol Parse/Bind path are described from source only; the script uses psql's simple protocol and never runs them.
- Verification gap: no regression test sets `cursor_tuple_fraction` or enables the `debug_print_*` settings; E1.5 and E1.7 are the only evidence on this page.

**Chapter 2.**

- Verification gap: no experiment exposes `PlaceHolderVar`, `varnullingrels` or `SpecialJoinInfo` directly; the chapter describes them from source and the optimizer README only.
- The generated node-support files (`nodetags.h`, `*funcs.funcs.c`, `*funcs.switch.c`) were not inspected in the build tree; the chapter cites only the generator and its Makefile rule.

**Chapter 3.**

- Nondeterministic collations: the measurement build is configured `--without-icu`, so no nondeterministic collation exists in the sandbox. How they limit transformations (for example `LIKE` prefix index conditions and equality under a nondeterministic collation) is described from source only in chapter 7; chapter 3 has no measurement for it.
- No regression test at the pin carries a comment naming plain outer-join reduction (a strict upper qual turning a `LEFT JOIN` into an inner join); `reduce_outer_joins()` is exercised by many plan tests, but a targeted test was not located. E3.5 is the tutorial's only direct evidence.
- No regression test was located that names the `HAVING`-to-`WHERE` move. (The planning-time view permission check is tested by `privileges.sql`; see the coverage matrix.)

**Chapter 4.**

- **Why the never-analyzed `fresh` table had 64 pages.** Its 10,000 rows need 45 pages at the 226 rows per page that the width model predicts, and the next 10,000 inserted rows did take 44 pages (E4.11). Yet `ANALYZE` recorded `relpages 64` (E4.11). The source suggests a cause: `CREATE TABLE AS` inserts through a bulk-insert state ([createas.c#intorel_startup-bistate](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/createas.c#L554-L561)), with which each file extension adds as many pages as all earlier ones together, up to 64 ([hio.c#RelationAddBlocks-sizing](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/hio.c#L300-L307), [hio.c#RelationAddBlocks-remember](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/heap/hio.c#L409-L429)).
- **The 64-page explanation is derived, not measured.** Extensions of 1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 pages give exactly 64, which would leave 19 pages empty and explain the 14,464-row overestimate. The run does not inspect page contents, for example with `pageinspect` or `pg_freespace`.
- **E4.8b is not reproduced by hand.** The self-join estimate of 209,172,402 (actual 209,193,990) comes from `eqjoinsel_inner()`'s MCV-to-MCV matching; the run does not print `items.product_id`'s MCV list, so the arithmetic is not shown.
- **Verification gaps.** The statistics privacy check (leakproofness) and the statistics hooks are covered from source and tests only; this page does not measure them. No file in `src/test` mentions the endpoint probe `get_actual_variable_range()`.

**Chapter 5.**

- **Documentation and source disagree on the cost of set-returning functions.** `CREATE FUNCTION` says that for a set-returning function `COST` is "the cost per returned row" ([create_function.sgml:470-478](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/create_function.sgml#L470-L478)). In a function scan, `cost_functionscan()` charges the function's evaluation cost once, as startup ([costsize.c#cost_functionscan-eval](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L1552-L1566)), and E4.12 measured a 0.25 startup (100 x 0.0025) for a PL/pgSQL function estimated at 1,000 rows. Source wins on this page. Whether a set-returning function in a target list (`ProjectSet`) is charged per row was not examined.
- **E5.9's index-scan costs are not derived.** The inner bitmap index scan costs 3.64 and 4.40 come from `btcostestimate()`/`genericcostestimate()` with a loop count of 21; the page derives only the heap part. The rounded parts, 4.40 + 48.41 + 0.19, do sum to 53.00; that total is consistent with an unrounded index cost between 4.4007 and 4.405, which the page does not derive.
- **E5.8b's tree height is inferred.** The term-by-term derivation of 1140.74 and 453.57 assumes a B-tree height of 1 for the 34-page `orders_customer_id_idx`, inferred from the displayed startup cost 0.29 (0.2875); the run does not print the height.
- **Planned and executed hash-aggregate batches differ.** For E5.4b the cost model predicts 2 batches at recursion depth 1 with 4 partitions; the executor reported `Batches: 5`. The page reads that as 1 initial pass plus 4 spilled partitions from `hash_batches_used` ([nodeAgg.c#hashagg_spill_finish-batches](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L3110-L3121), [nodeAgg.c:3624](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L3624)), but the run does not print the executor's partition count.
- **Verification gaps.** Per-tablespace page costs are covered from source and `tablespace.sql` only; no experiment on this page sets them. Fuzzy path comparison has no direct test or experiment; its effect is visible only in which plans win.

**Chapter 6.**

- **Gap: custom scans.** No module or test in the pinned tree defines `CustomPathMethods` or sets `set_rel_pathlist_hook`. A search of `src/` and `contrib/` finds the API only in `nodes/extensible.[ch]` and `pathnodes.h`, so no custom scan path could be measured. The chapter describes the hook and the API from source and [custom-scan.sgml#custom-scan-path](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/custom-scan.sgml#L34-L58) only.
- **Gap: `XMLTABLE`.** The measurement build was configured without `--with-libxml`, so only `JSON_TABLE` exercised the table-function path (E6.6). Both share `RTE_TABLEFUNC` and the fixed 100-row estimate ([costsize.c:5927-5937](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/costsize.c#L5927-L5937)).
- **Unmeasured: the Materialize wrapper for non-repeatable sampling methods** ([allpaths.c:869-892](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L869-L892)). Every built-in and contrib method in the tree is `repeatable_across_scans`, so the wrapper cannot be triggered without a third-party method.

**Chapter 7.**

- **Code comment versus source (amutils.c).** The comment for `AMPROP_DISTANCE_ORDERABLE` says "at time of writing, only GiST supports it at all" ([amutils.c:284-296](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/amutils.c#L284-L296)). But SP-GiST also sets `amcanorderbyop = true` ([spgutils.c:52](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/access/spgist/spgutils.c#L52)), and E7.1 reports `distance_orderable = t` for the SP-GiST index. Source wins; the comment is stale.
- **Gap: `indcheckxmin` and transient plans.** Not measured. Triggering it needs an index built while an older snapshot can still see broken HOT chains. The chapter cites it from source only ([plancat.c:269-281](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/util/plancat.c#L269-L281)).
- **Verification gap: non-C collations.** The cluster is `--locale=C` and the build has no ICU. The `LIKE` fallback for a non-C index collation, where prefix bounds need a C-collated index or a `*_pattern_ops` opclass ([like_support.c:428-437](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/utils/adt/like_support.c#L428-L437)), is therefore stated from source only. Nondeterministic collations were not measured either. A script cannot rely on any particular libc collation, because the available collations depend on the host OS.
- **Unmeasured: row comparisons and boolean index columns.** B-tree-only `RowCompareExpr` matching and the boolean `col` / `NOT col` rewriting are cited from source only ([indxpath.c:2706-2708](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L2706-L2708), [indxpath.c:2223-2228](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/indxpath.c#L2223-L2228)).

**Chapter 8.**

- The E8.4 Memoize worked example uses the schema's bound of 500 product ids for `ndistinct`, not a measured `n_distinct`; the script does not print `items.product_id` statistics. The derived nested-loop total (16,091) is within 0.02 % of the plan's 16089.13 because the plan prints its inputs to two decimals.
- No core regression test sets `join_collapse_limit`, triggers the "FULL JOIN is only supported with merge-joinable or hash-joinable join conditions" error, or exercises `set_join_pathlist_hook` or `join_search_hook`; this page demonstrates the collapse limit and GEQO (E8.8, E8.9) but not the error or the hooks.
- The planner-memory figures of E8.9 repeated exactly across runs on this platform; whether they are the same on another architecture was not checked.
- The documentation for `geqo_threshold` counts "FROM items involved" ([config.sgml#guc-geqo-threshold](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/config.sgml#L6166-L6169)), while the source counts the items of one join list after the collapse limits ([allpaths.c#make_rel_from_joinlist-search](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L3372-L3377)). The `from_collapse_limit` and `join_collapse_limit` entries note the interaction ([config.sgml#guc-from-collapse-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/config.sgml#L6397-L6399), [config.sgml#guc-join-collapse-limit](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/config.sgml#L6449-L6451)), so this is an incompleteness of the `geqo_threshold` wording rather than a contradiction.

**Chapter 9.**

- Docs versus source: `queries.sgml` says `NOT MATERIALIZED` forces a `WITH` query to be merged into the parent ([queries.sgml#queries-with-cte-materialization](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/queries.sgml#L2520-L2530)). The source still refuses to inline a `NOT MATERIALIZED` CTE that is recursive, uses `FOR UPDATE`/`FOR SHARE` or DML, calls a volatile function, or is multiply referenced with an outer self-reference ([subselect.c#SS_process_ctes-inline](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/subselect.c#L910-L955)). The docs' preceding sentence covers recursion and volatility but not `FOR UPDATE` or outer self-references. Source wins; the tutorial follows it.
- No regression test at the pin sets `recursive_worktable_factor`; E9.10 is the only evidence for its effect.
- `ARRAY(SELECT ...)` and `MULTIEXPR` InitPlans and `EXISTS` simplification with `LIMIT` have no tutorial experiment; they are described from source and `subselect.sql`/`update.sql`.
- The estimate of 667 rows for E9.6's correlated semi join is not derived on the page; its exact composition (semi-join fraction times the join filter's default selectivity) was not traced through `eqjoinsel_semi()`.

**Chapter 10.**

- Presorted ordered aggregates (E10.4): the planner never prices the per-group sorts an ordered aggregate performs inside `Agg` when its input is not presorted ([prepagg.c#get_agg_clause_costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepagg.c#L560-L617), [nodeAgg.c#aggsortrequired](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/executor/nodeAgg.c#L4164-L4182)), so the two plans' costs are not comparable. The script does not run both plans with `ANALYZE`, so no measured comparison is filed.
- `UNION` without `ALL` assumes every input row is distinct ([prepunion.c#generate_union_paths-groups](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/prep/prepunion.c#L888-L902)); the effect of that overestimate on plans above a `UNION` is not measured.
- The E10.8 startup-row count of 2 is derived from `get_windowclause_startup_tuples()` for a frame ending at the current row; EXPLAIN does not print it.
- No experiment triggers the "could not implement" set-operation error or exercises `create_upper_paths_hook`, which has no in-core user.

**Chapter 11.**

- The comment in `apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths()` says that generating the target below the Append is "always the same or cheaper cost", which is its reason for dropping a partitioned relation's existing paths ([planner.c#apply_scanjoin_target_to_paths-drop](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L7754-L7775)). For a partitionwise join, the dropped paths also include the non-partitionwise join paths. In E11.6 the surviving partitionwise plan costs 3519.89, against 3106.56 for the default plan. The comment's cost argument covers target placement, not this comparison. Whether dropping the non-partitionwise paths is intended in this case is not settled by the source or its tests.
- Async Append is described from source only. The loopback server of chapter 15 is not marked `async_capable`, so no plan on this page shows an async Append.
- Planner memory, not planning time, is the only planning-overhead measure here. Planning time is not recorded, because the script records no timings.
- List partitioning, sub-partitioning and partitionwise joins with merged, non-identical bounds are covered by the regression tests cited in chapter 11, not by this page's experiments.

**Chapter 12.**

- JIT compilation itself is not demonstrated: the build has no LLVM, so `pg_jit_available()` is false (E12.10). Only the planner's `jitFlags` decision is measured; the executor's compiled path is described from source.
- A worker shortfall at run time (`Workers Launched` below `Workers Planned`) is described from source and the docs only. The idle test server always had free worker slots.
- The row estimate above a Gather Merge is per-process rows times the planned workers, without the leader's share, while the partial path's own rows were divided by the full divisor including the leader's share (E12.4: 500,000 estimated for 600,000 rows). The source does this deliberately in several places ([planner.c#create_ordered_paths-gather-merge](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/plan/planner.c#L5450-L5458)). No comment states why the leader's share is left out.
- `parallel.sgml` says a parallel-restricted operation "can occur elsewhere in a plan" above Gather. For a restricted qual on a base relation the source does not postpone it; it keeps the whole relation serial ([allpaths.c#set_rel_consider_parallel-quals](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/optimizer/path/allpaths.c#L736-L757), E12.7b). The docs and the source agree on the rule; the docs do not spell out this consequence.

**Chapter 13.**

- The `LockRows` and `ModifyTable` cost rules are source-only on this page: every write experiment runs with `COSTS OFF`, so no measured cost confirms them.
- EvalPlanQual, `SKIP LOCKED`, `NOWAIT`, speculative-insertion conflicts and concurrent row movement need two sessions. The page describes them from source and cites the isolation specs, but runs none of them.
- Direct foreign modification (`PlanDirectModify`) and row-by-row foreign modification are not measured; the loopback `postgres_fdw` server of E15.1 is used only for reads.
- The page does not measure a partitioned `UPDATE` whose partition key changes and actually moves a row; E13.7 shows only the plan, because the script never writes to the running schema.

**Chapter 14.**

- E14.6's first `ANALYZE` rewrote `pg_statistic` with the same values, because the table's data had not changed. That column statistics with different values also leave a cached generic plan in place rests on source: the invalidation messages depend on which catalog row changes, not on its contents, and the plan cache has no callback for `pg_statistic`.
- E14.6 runs in one session. That another session's cached plan is invalidated when it next locks the table is described from source only (`LockRelationOid()` processing pending messages).
- Verification gap: the role-change invalidation callbacks (commit `1974acf23c`, first in 17.11) have no regression test in this checkout; that commit touched no test file.
- Verification gap: transient plans (`saved_xmin`) and the `CheckCachedPlan()` role check are described from source only.
- `EXPLAIN (MEMORY)` figures (E16.3, E8.9, E11.9) come from one platform (Darwin arm64, 8-byte alignment); the chapter uses them only as relative sizes.

**Chapter 15.**

- No in-core module exercises `join_search_hook`, `get_relation_info_hook`, `set_rel_pathlist_hook`, `set_join_pathlist_hook`, `create_upper_paths_hook`, `get_relation_stats_hook`, `get_index_stats_hook`, `get_attavgwidth_hook`, `ExplainOneQuery_hook` or `explain_get_index_name_hook`, and none provides a custom scan. Their behavior on this page rests on the call sites and the `custom-scan.sgml` documentation only.
- The E15.1b remote-estimate result is explained by arithmetic (707.30 minus the FDW charges equals the local one-condition sequential-scan cost of 601.00). The script does not print the remote `EXPLAIN` that `postgres_fdw` ran, so the remote cost itself is derived, not observed.
- Foreign writes (`PlanForeignModify`, `PlanDirectModify`), asynchronous foreign scans (`IsForeignPathAsyncCapable`) and partitionwise joins over foreign partitions (`ReparameterizeForeignPathByChild`) are described from source and, for direct modification, the `postgres_fdw` regression suite only; the page runs none of them.
- The maintenance helpers `plan_cluster_use_sort()` and `plan_create_index_workers()` are not measured; the page does not run `CLUSTER` or a parallel index build.
- `brin.c` carries an XXX comment questioning the 32 MB-per-participant worker cap for BRIN builds; the page records the cap as implemented and the comment as an open design note.

**Chapter 16.**

- Docs versus source, `TIMING` and `WAL`: `ref/explain.sgml` says each "may only be used when ANALYZE is also enabled" ([ref/explain.sgml#WAL](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/explain.sgml#L239-L248), [ref/explain.sgml#TIMING](../../../../raw/postgres-17/doc/src/sgml/ref/explain.sgml#L252-L265)). The code rejects only the enabled form, so `EXPLAIN (TIMING OFF)` and `EXPLAIN (WAL OFF)` without `ANALYZE` are accepted ([explain.c#ExplainQuery-wal-timing-checks](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L278-L291)). The page follows the source.
- "No feedback from execution into later plans" rests on reading the planner's inputs (stored statistics, live relation sizes, settings) and the instrumentation's life cycle. It does not rest on an exhaustive search of every planner input for execution-time data.
- `BUFFERS` counts, planning time and execution time are never recorded on this page, so the buffer and timing parts of the EXPLAIN option table are described from source only.
- `auto_explain` and `log_planner_stats` are described from source only: the build does not install `auto_explain`, and the script never enables `log_planner_stats`.
- Exercise 5 uses `EXPLAIN (MEMORY, COSTS OFF)`; E11.9 measured the same statements with `COSTS` on. The expected figures assume `COSTS` changes only the printed output, not planning, which the option handling supports ([explain.c#ExplainNode-costs](../../../../raw/postgres-17/src/backend/commands/explain.c#L1807-L1825)) but no experiment checks.
